summary: coeff() bounds the angle type range with atom->ndihedraltypes instead of atom->nangletypes, so coefficients are uploaded for the wrong number of types (out-of-bounds writes or silently missing types).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:300-311: `int ilo,ihi;` / `utils::bounds(FLERR,arg[0],1,atom->ndihedraltypes,ilo,ihi,error);` / `for (int i = ilo; i <= ihi; i++) { k_nterms.view_host()[i] = nterms[i]; ... }`. The CPU base uses the angle type count: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_gaussian.cpp:208-209: `int ilo, ihi;` / `utils::bounds(FLERR, arg[0], 1, atom->nangletypes, ilo, ihi, error);`. Every sibling in this group also uses nangletypes, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:284 `utils::bounds(FLERR,arg[0],1,atom->nangletypes,ilo,ihi,error);`. The dual views being indexed are sized nangletypes+1 (src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:65-71, 282-283).
failure_scenario: Any angle-only system (no dihedrals, atom->ndihedraltypes == 0): `angle_style gaussian/kk` + `angle_coeff 1 300.0 2 ...` aborts with the bogus error 'Numeric index 1 is out of bounds (1-0)'. If ndihedraltypes > nangletypes, `angle_coeff * ...` writes k_nterms/k_angle_temperature/k_alpha/k_width/k_theta0 host mirrors past index nangletypes -> heap corruption. If 0 < ndihedraltypes < nangletypes, `angle_coeff * ...` uploads only the first ndihedraltypes types; the remaining types keep nterms==0 on the device, so their Gaussian sum is 0 -> log(0) energy and 0/0 forces.
suggested_fix: Change `atom->ndihedraltypes` to `atom->nangletypes` on line 301 to match AngleGaussian::coeff.

summary: The sin(theta) floor used to regularize the 1/s force prefactor is 1e-12 instead of the base class's SMALL = 0.001, so near-collinear angles get forces up to ~1e9 times larger than the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.cpp:188-189: `KK_FLOAT s = Kokkos::sqrt(static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0) - c*c);` / `if (s < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1e-12)) s = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1e-12);`, and s is then divided into the force at lines 204 (`ff = 0.25*uumin*cssmscc*(2.0+aa*cccpsss)/s;`) and 209 (`ff = 0.5*aa*d_opt1[type]*exp2*cssmscc/s;`). The CPU base uses 0.001: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_cosine_shift_exp.cpp:35 `static constexpr double SMALL = 0.001;` and :118-120 `s = sqrt(1.0 - c*c);` / `if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL;` with the same `ff=...cssmscc/s` at :130 and :138. Every other Kokkos angle style in this group keeps the base value (e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_shift_kokkos.cpp:34,188 use SMALL=0.001; angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:34,198; angle_cross_kokkos.cpp:30,173).
failure_scenario: angle_style cosine/shift/exp/kk with an angle driven close to 0 or 180 degrees (sin(theta) < 1e-3, i.e. within ~0.06 deg of collinear) while theta0 is not collinear: the CPU caps the prefactor at ff <= C/0.001, the KOKKOS kernel allows ff up to C/1e-12, giving forces ~1e9x larger -> 'lost atoms'/blown-up trajectory where the CPU run is stable, and a force/energy mismatch in force-style regression tests.
suggested_fix: Add `static constexpr double SMALL = 0.001;` at the top of the file (as in the sibling styles) and use it for the clamp so the /kk variant reproduces AngleCosineShiftExp exactly.

summary: The sum_g_i underflow guard uses SMALLG = 2.3e-308 cast to KK_FLOAT, which becomes exactly 0.0f in single/mixed-precision KOKKOS builds and therefore never fires.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:31 `static constexpr double SMALLG = 2.3e-308;` and :221-223 `// avoid overflow` / `if (sum_g_i < sum_numerator * static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALLG))` / `sum_g_i = sum_numerator * static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALLG);`. KK_FLOAT is `float` for LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE and LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:399-408), and static_cast<float>(2.3e-308) underflows to 0.0f, so the test degenerates to `if (sum_g_i < 0.0f)`. sum_g_i is then used at :228 `eangle = -kbt * Kokkos::log(sum_g_i);` and :230 `a = -4.0*kbt*(sum_numerator/sum_g_i)*s;`. The CPU base performs the identical guard in double: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_gaussian.cpp:32 and :135-136.
failure_scenario: Build with -DLMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE (or SINGLE_DOUBLE) and run angle_style gaussian/kk with an angle far from every theta0 (all exponents very negative): every g_i underflows, sum_g_i == 0.0f, the guard does not fire, log(0) gives -inf energy and sum_numerator/sum_g_i gives inf/NaN forces -> NaN trajectory. The double-precision default build is unaffected.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the guard in double (or use a KK_FLOAT-appropriate floor such as Kokkos::Experimental::norm_min_v<KK_FLOAT> / std::numeric_limits<KK_FLOAT>::min()) instead of casting a double-denormal constant to KK_FLOAT.

summary: The degenerate-geometry guards compare against SMALL*SMALL with SMALL = 1.0e-100, which underflows to 0 when KK_FLOAT is float, so the zero-length checks that the CPU style relies on become inert.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_dipole_kokkos.cpp:31 `static constexpr double SMALL = 1.0e-100;`, :154-155 `const KK_FLOAT r2 = delx*delx + dely*dely + delz*delz;` / `if (r2 < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)*static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)) return;` and :181-183 `const KK_FLOAT len2 = fx*fx + fy*fy + fz*fz;` / `if (len2 < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)*static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)) return;`. With KK_FLOAT = float (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:399-408, LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE / SINGLE_DOUBLE) static_cast<float>(1.0e-100) is 0.0f, so both tests become `< 0.0f` and never trigger. The CPU base tests the un-squared quantity in double: src/DIPOLE/angle_dipole.cpp:35 `static constexpr double SMALL = 1.0e-100;`, :94-95 `r = sqrt(...); if (r < SMALL) continue;` and :120-121 `len = sqrt(fx*fx+fy*fy+fz*fz); if (len < SMALL) continue;`.
failure_scenario: Single/mixed-precision KOKKOS build, angle_style dipole/kk, with a dipole atom coincident with its reference atom (r == 0) or a dipole exactly parallel to the bond vector (delT == 0 so fx=fy=fz=0): the CPU skips the angle, the /kk kernel divides by rmu == 0 or by sqrt(len2) == 0 and writes inf/NaN into torque and f.
suggested_fix: Do the comparison in double (compare `static_cast<double>(r2) < SMALL*SMALL`) or replace 1.0e-100 with a floor representable in KK_FLOAT.

summary: The device kernel calls the host <cmath> function fmod() instead of Kokkos::fmod(), violating the KOKKOS rule that device kernels use Kokkos:: math functions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.cpp:186-187 inside the KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION operator(): `sgn = (fmod(static_cast<double>(d_N[type]), 2.0) == 0.0) ? static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(-1.0) : static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0);`. Every other math call in the same kernel is namespace-qualified (`Kokkos::sqrt` :154, `Kokkos::acos` :169, `Kokkos::cos` :171, `Kokkos::sin` :178, `Kokkos::fabs` :177). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels (Kokkos::sqrt, Kokkos::exp, Kokkos::pow, Kokkos::log, ...), never std:: -- std::pow and friends fail to compile for GPU targets.' The CPU original is src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_fourier_simple.cpp:132 `sgn = (fmod(N[type], 2.0) == 0.0) ? -1.0 : 1.0;`.
failure_scenario: Backends that do not inject a __device__ overload of the unqualified ::fmod (SYCL/OpenMPTarget, or a build where <cmath> pulls in only the host overload) fail to compile angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.cpp. Where it does compile it forces a double-precision fmod inside an otherwise single-precision kernel.
suggested_fix: Replace `fmod(static_cast<double>(d_N[type]), 2.0)` with `Kokkos::fmod(d_N[type], static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(2.0))`.

summary: 13 of the 16 angle KOKKOS styles in this group have no `action` lines in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, contrary to KOKKOS rule 5.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:37-50 lists only angle_charmm, angle_class2, angle_cosine, angle_table, angle_harmonic, angle_hybrid and angle_spica. Missing: angle_class2_p6_kokkos.{cpp,h} (base src/MOFFF/angle_class2_p6.cpp), angle_class2xe_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/CLASS2/angle_class2xe.cpp), angle_cosine_delta_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_periodic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_shift_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_squared_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_squared_restricted_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cross_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/YAFF/angle_cross.cpp), angle_dipole_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/DIPOLE/angle_dipole.cpp), angle_fourier_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_gaussian_kokkos.{cpp,h}. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 5 requires an action line per new file, with the base file name as second argument when the base lives in an optional package.
failure_scenario: No build breakage today: KOKKOS's action() only does `rm -f ../$1` (install mode is refused outright at Install.sh:216) and CMake finds the files through RegisterStylesExt (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:304). The consequence is that `make no-kokkos`/`make purge` will not remove stale src/ copies of these files left over from an older tree, and the file list drifts out of sync with the documented convention.
suggested_fix: Add the 26 missing `action <file> <base file>` lines to src/KOKKOS/Install.sh in alphabetical order alongside the existing angle_* entries.

summary: Four setflag dual views are allocated as floating-point arrays, filled, and synced to the device on every compute() call, but no kernel ever reads them.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:100-103 syncs `k_setflag`, `k_setflag_a`, `k_setflag_bb`, `k_setflag_ba` each timestep; :339-342 allocates them as `DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d` (integer flags stored as KK_FLOAT); :356-359 and :447-450 assign d_setflag/d_setflag_a/d_setflag_bb/d_setflag_ba; :386-389 and :465-468 fill them. The device views d_setflag* appear nowhere in operator() (:162-308) or ev_tally (:498-603), and the CPU base never reads setflag in compute() either (src/CLASS2/angle_class2.cpp:76-239).
failure_scenario: No wrong results; 4 extra device allocations of (nangletypes+1) KK_FLOATs plus 4 no-op DualView syncs per timestep, and integer flags stored in a float view (silently lossy above 2^24 - irrelevant for 0/1 but wrong typing).
suggested_fix: Delete k_setflag/k_setflag_a/k_setflag_bb/k_setflag_ba, their d_* views, and the corresponding allocate/coeff/read_restart/compute lines.

summary: `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` is duplicated in both allocate() and read_restart(), a copy-paste leftover that likely masks a missing assignment.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:354-356: `d_ba_r1 = k_ba_r1.template view<DeviceType>();` / `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` / `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` and the identical pair at :445-446. All other d_* views are assigned exactly once.
failure_scenario: Harmless as written (the second assignment is idempotent), but it is the classic shape of a dropped `d_theta0`/`d_ba_k2` assignment and confuses future edits.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate line at 355 and at 446.

summary: The per-atom energy/virial arrays are registered with the memory tag 'improper:eatom'/'improper:vatom' inside an angle style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:77 `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"improper:eatom");` and :84 `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_vatom,vatom,maxvatom,"improper:vatom");`. Every sibling uses the correct tag, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:76,81 `"angle:eatom"`, `"angle:vatom"`, matching the CPU base src/angle.cpp:137,144 ("angle:eatom", "angle:vatom").
failure_scenario: No numerical effect; the allocation is attributed to 'improper' in `info memory` / memory-usage output, which misleads anyone tracking KOKKOS memory.
suggested_fix: Change both tags to "angle:eatom" and "angle:vatom".

summary: k_eatom/k_vatom are destroyed and reallocated on every timestep on which per-atom energy/virial is requested, instead of the reuse-and-zero pattern used by the other 13 styles in this group.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:74-87 (with the commented-out size check `//if(k_eatom.extent(0)<maxeatom) { // won't work without adding zero functor`), src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:74-83 and src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_kokkos.cpp:72-81 do an unconditional `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(...)` + `memoryKK->create_kokkos(...)`. The other styles solved the zeroing problem and reuse the buffer, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_class2xe_kokkos.cpp:74-80: `if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { destroy; create; d_eatom = ...; } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);`.
failure_scenario: No wrong results. With `compute pe/atom` or `compute stress/atom` active every output step triggers a device free+malloc of nmax (and 6*nmax) elements per angle style; on GPUs this serializes the step and can dominate the angle cost.
suggested_fix: Adopt the extent-check + Kokkos::deep_copy(...,0.0) pattern already used by angle_class2xe_kokkos.cpp and the other 13 styles in this group.

summary: The energy is rebuilt as cos(theta)cos(theta0)+sin(theta)sin(theta0) using the SMALL-clamped sine, so it differs from the base class's exact cos(theta-theta0) for near-collinear angles.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_delta_kokkos.cpp:189-201: `KK_FLOAT s = Kokkos::sqrt(1.0 - c*c);` / `if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL;` / `const KK_FLOAT cot = c/s;` / ... / `const KK_FLOAT dcostheta = c*c0 + s*s0;` / `const KK_FLOAT tk = d_k[type] * (1.0 - dcostheta);` / `if (eflag) eangle = tk;`. The CPU base clamps s only for the cot term and computes the energy from the unclamped angle: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_cosine_delta.cpp:87-98: `theta = acos(c);` / `s = sqrt(1.0 - c*c); if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL; cot = c/s;` / `dtheta = theta - theta0[type]; dcostheta = cos(dtheta); tk = k[type] * (1.0-dcostheta);`. SMALL is 0.001 in both (kokkos line 34, base line 35). The force terms a11/a12/a22/b11/b12/b22 are identical, so only the energy diverges.
failure_scenario: angle_style cosine/delta/kk with an angle within ~0.06 deg of 0 or 180 degrees: the /kk energy is off by k*(0.001 - sin(theta))*sin(theta0), i.e. up to 1e-3*k per angle, versus the CPU value. Shows up as a small but systematic energy mismatch in force-style regression tests for collapsed/linear angles.
suggested_fix: Compute the energy from the unclamped sine (keep a separate clamped copy for cot), or use Kokkos::cos(Kokkos::acos(c) - theta0) as the base does.

summary: angle_style hybrid/kk dereferences a null cvatom of its sub-styles because it keeps the inherited centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL while every KOKKOS angle sub-style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:144-150 'if (cvflag_atom) { int n = atom->nlocal; ... double **cvatom_substyle = styles[m]->cvatom; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) for (int j = 0; j < 9; j++) cvatom[i][j] += cvatom_substyle[i][j]; }'. AngleHybridKokkos's constructor (src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:33-44) never touches centroidstressflag, and neither does src/angle_hybrid.cpp, so it keeps Angle's default 'centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL' (src/angle.cpp:48). Angle::ev_setup then sets 'cvflag_atom = 1' for the hybrid (src/angle.cpp:128). Every KOKKOS angle sub-style, however, sets 'centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL' in its constructor (e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:48, angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp:48, angle_quartic_kokkos.cpp:44, angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:53, angle_table_kokkos.cpp:49, angle_mwlc_kokkos.cpp:42), so in their ev_setup src/angle.cpp:126-128 takes the 'vflag_atom = 1 / cvflag_atom = 0' branch and their 'cvatom' is never allocated (it stays the nullptr set in Angle's constructor). No CPU angle style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL (grep over src/**/angle_*.cpp returns only KOKKOS files), which is why the CPU angle_hybrid never hits this. PairHybrid does recompute the flag from its sub-styles (src/pair_hybrid.cpp:445-457); AngleHybrid/AngleHybridKokkos do not.
failure_scenario: angle_style hybrid/kk harmonic quartic (or any pair of kk angle styles) together with 'compute centroid/stress/atom' -> the run's ev_set() adds VIRIAL_CENTROID, AngleHybridKokkos::compute sets cvflag_atom = 1, the sub-style leaves cvatom == nullptr, and the accumulation loop segfaults on the first timestep. Even if it did not crash, the per-atom virial the sub-styles wrote into vatom would be silently discarded because the hybrid's own vflag_atom is 0.
suggested_fix: In AngleHybridKokkos::init_style() (after AngleHybrid::init_style()) recompute centroidstressflag from the sub-styles exactly as PairHybrid::init_one does (src/pair_hybrid.cpp:450-457): set CENTROID_NOTAVAIL if any sub-style is CENTROID_NOTAVAIL. Better still, add that loop to the CPU AngleHybrid so all hybrids inherit it.

summary: AngleSPICAKokkos::init_style() unconditionally copies the pair style's lj_type/lj1..lj4/rminsq/emin arrays, but the base class only sets those pointers when repflag is non-zero, so they are still nullptr and the loop dereferences null.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:379-390: 'int ntypes = atom->ntypes; for (int i = 1; i <= ntypes; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= ntypes; j++) { k_lj_type.view_host()(i,j) = lj_type[i][j]; k_lj1.view_host()(i,j) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(lj1[i][j]); ... k_emin.view_host()(i,j) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(emin[i][j]); } }'. The base, src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:294-321, does: 'repflag = 0; for (int i = 1; i <= atom->nangletypes; i++) if (repscale && (repscale[i] > 0.0)) repflag = 1; ... if (repflag) { lj1 = (double **) force->pair->extract("lj1",itmp); ... }' -- i.e. lj1..lj4, lj_type, rminsq and emin are only assigned inside 'if (repflag)'. They are initialised to nullptr in the AngleSPICA constructor (src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:47-52). The kernel itself correctly guards its use with 'if (repflag)' (src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:215), but init_style does not.
failure_scenario: Any input where the 1-3 repulsion is switched off for every angle type, e.g. 'angle_coeff * 50.0 173.0 0.0' (4-argument form sets repscale = 0.0, src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:272) or the legacy 6-argument cg/cmm form with epsilon 0.0. repflag stays 0, lj_type is nullptr, and 'lj_type[1][1]' in init_style segfaults at the start of the run. The plain CPU angle_style spica runs this input fine.
suggested_fix: Wrap the ntypes x ntypes copy loop and the matching modify_host() calls in 'if (repflag) { ... }', mirroring the guard the base class and the device kernel already use.

summary: AngleSPICAKokkos's constructor never sets kokkosable = 1, so angle_style hybrid/kk rejects spica/kk and VerletKokkos turns on auto_sync (a full host/device round trip of x and f) every timestep.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:44-54 is the whole constructor: 'AngleSPICAKokkos<DeviceType>::AngleSPICAKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : AngleSPICA(lmp) { atomKK = (AtomKokkos *) atom; neighborKK = (NeighborKokkos *) neighbor; execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space; datamask_read = X_MASK | F_MASK | TYPE_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK; datamask_modify = F_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK; centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL; }' -- no 'kokkosable = 1;'. Every sibling sets it as the first statement: angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:41, angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp:41, angle_mwlc_kokkos.cpp:35, angle_quartic_kokkos.cpp:37, angle_table_kokkos.cpp:42, angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:35. Consumers: src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:203-204 'if (!styles[m]->kokkosable) error->all(FLERR,"Must use only Kokkos-enabled angle styles with angle_style hybrid/kk");' and src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:473-474 'int prev_auto_sync = lmp->kokkos->auto_sync; if (!force->angle->kokkosable) lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;' (same at dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:247). auto_sync = 1 makes AtomKokkos::sync/modified push everything through the legacy host arrays (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:241-269).
failure_scenario: 'angle_style hybrid/kk spica harmonic' aborts with 'Must use only Kokkos-enabled angle styles with angle_style hybrid/kk' even though spica/kk is a full KOKKOS port. With a plain 'angle_style spica/kk' on a GPU, every step copies x and f device->host->device around the angle compute, so the /kk variant is far slower than intended.
suggested_fix: Add 'kokkosable = 1;' as the first statement of AngleSPICAKokkos's constructor, matching every other KOKKOS angle style.

summary: angle_mm3_kokkos, angle_mwlc_kokkos and angle_quartic_kokkos have no action lines in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, so the traditional make build never installs them and the mm3/kk, mwlc/kk and quartic/kk styles silently do not exist there.
evidence: 'grep "^action angle" src/KOKKOS/Install.sh' returns only lines 37-50 (charmm, class2, cosine, table, harmonic, hybrid, spica). The files src/KOKKOS/angle_mm3_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_mwlc_kokkos.{cpp,h} and angle_quartic_kokkos.{cpp,h} exist and register AngleStyle(mm3/kk,...), AngleStyle(mwlc/kk,...), AngleStyle(quartic/kk,...) (angle_mm3_kokkos.h:16-18, angle_mwlc_kokkos.h:16-18, angle_quartic_kokkos.h:16-18). Their base classes live in optional packages (src/YAFF/angle_mm3.cpp, src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_mwlc.cpp, src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_quartic.cpp), so per .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 5 they need two-argument action lines, e.g. 'action angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp angle_mm3.cpp'.
failure_scenario: 'cd src && make yes-kokkos yes-yaff yes-extra-molecule && make mpi' produces a binary in which 'angle_style mm3/kk' fails with 'Unrecognized angle style'; a CMake build of the same tree has the style, so the two build systems disagree. (The same omission affects several other angle kk styles outside this review group.)
suggested_fix: Add the six missing action lines to src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, each naming both the KOKKOS file and its package base file, and audit the rest of the angle_*_kokkos files for the same omission.

summary: In the Device branch of AtomVecSpinKokkos::sync_pinned the guard for the fm array tests k_sp instead of k_fm, so fm can be left unsynced (or synced spuriously) depending on the state of an unrelated array.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_spin_kokkos.cpp:289-294: 'if ((mask & SP_MASK) && atomKK->k_sp.need_sync_device()) perform_pinned_copy_transform<DAT::ttransform_kkfloat_1d_4>(atomKK->k_sp,space,async_flag); if ((mask & FM_MASK) && atomKK->k_sp.need_sync_device()) perform_pinned_copy_transform<DAT::ttransform_kkacc_1d_3>(atomKK->k_fm,space,async_flag); if ((mask & FML_MASK) && atomKK->k_fm_long.need_sync_device()) ...'. The FM line tests k_sp, not k_fm. The host branch of the same function has it right: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_spin_kokkos.cpp:312-313 'if ((mask & FM_MASK) && atomKK->k_fm.need_sync_host()) perform_pinned_copy_transform<DAT::ttransform_kkacc_1d_3>(atomKK->k_fm,space,async_flag);'. The reference implementation always pairs the guard with the view it copies (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_atomic_kokkos.cpp:165-179).
failure_scenario: Whenever a caller asks for sync_pinned(Device, ... FM_MASK ...) with fm modified on the host and sp already clean, fm is not copied to the device and the following spin kernel reads stale magnetic forces. Today only sync_pinned(HostKK,...)/sync_pinned(Host,...) call sites exist (verlet_kokkos.cpp:448, dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:230, third_order_kokkos.cpp:230), so the defect is latent, but it is armed for the first Device-side caller.
suggested_fix: Change the FM_MASK guard on line 291 to 'atomKK->k_fm.need_sync_device()'.

summary: angle mm3/kk destroys and re-creates the k_eatom/k_vatom dual views on every energy/virial-tally step instead of only when maxeatom/maxvatom grows.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp:72-81: 'if (eflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"angle:eatom"); d_eatom = k_eatom.template view<DeviceType>(); } if (vflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_vatom,vatom); ... }'. The sibling styles use the guarded form, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:74-87 and angle_quartic_kokkos.cpp:68-81: 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { destroy; create; d_eatom = ...; } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);'. maxeatom only grows when atom->nmax grows (src/angle.cpp:133-139).
failure_scenario: A run with 'compute pe/atom' or 'compute stress/atom' and thermo output every step frees and re-allocates two device arrays of atom->nmax (and 6*nmax) elements on every tally step; on a GPU this serialises the step behind an allocation and can dominate the angle time.
suggested_fix: Use the same 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { ... } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);' pattern as angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:74-87.

summary: angle spica/kk destroys and re-creates the k_eatom/k_vatom dual views on every energy/virial-tally step instead of only when maxeatom/maxvatom grows.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:79-88: 'if (eflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"angle:eatom"); d_eatom = k_eatom.template view<DeviceType>(); } if (vflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_vatom,vatom); ... }', versus the guarded form in src/KOKKOS/angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:74-87 / angle_table_kokkos.cpp:75-88 / angle_mwlc_kokkos.cpp:66-79.
failure_scenario: Same as angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp:72 -- per-atom energy/stress output turns every tally step into two device allocations and frees.
suggested_fix: Adopt the extent-guarded reallocation plus Kokkos::deep_copy(...,0.0) used by the other angle kk styles.

summary: k_setflag/d_setflag and k_repscale/d_repscale are allocated, filled, synced and carried into the device functor but are never read by any kernel.
evidence: Allocated at src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:335 and 334 ('k_repscale = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d("AngleSPICA::repscale",nangletypes+1); k_setflag = DAT::tdual_int_1d("AngleSPICA::setflag",nangletypes+1);'), filled in coeff() (lines 416-417) and read_restart() (lines 439-440), synced in compute() (line 92 'k_repscale.template sync<DeviceType>();'), and declared as members at src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.h:92-96. Neither d_setflag nor d_repscale appears anywhere in operator(), ev_tally or ev_tally13 (the whole file contains no other occurrence). The base class likewise only uses repscale to derive repflag (src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:300-301).
failure_scenario: No wrong results; it wastes device memory and one host->device transfer per step, and it misleads a reader into thinking the 1-3 repulsion is per-type scaled on the device when it is not.
suggested_fix: Delete k_setflag/d_setflag and k_repscale/d_repscale (and the sync at line 92), or use d_repscale in the kernel if per-type scaling of the 1-3 term is actually intended.

summary: AngleHybridKokkos::maxangle_all is never initialised, so memory_usage() reads an indeterminate value if it is called before the first re-neighbour step.
evidence: 'int maxangle_all;' is declared at src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.h:43 and is written only inside the 'if (neighbor->ago == 0)' block, src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:85-88 ('maxangle_all = 0; for (int m = 0; m < nstyles; m++) if (h_nanglelist[m] > maxangle_all) maxangle_all = h_nanglelist[m] + EXTRA;'). The constructor (lines 33-44) and allocate() (lines 161-171) do not set it, while memory_usage() reads it at line 220: 'for (int m = 0; m < nstyles; m++) bytes += (double) maxangle_all * 4 * sizeof(int);'. The CPU class initialises the corresponding per-style array in allocate() ('for (int m = 0; m < nstyles; m++) maxangle[m] = 0;', src/angle_hybrid.cpp:161-166).
failure_scenario: 'angle_style hybrid/kk ... ; angle_coeff ... ; info coeffs' (or any memory_usage query issued before a run) reads uninitialised memory and prints a garbage or negative memory figure; it is undefined behaviour reported by valgrind/MSan.
suggested_fix: Initialise maxangle_all = 0 in the AngleHybridKokkos constructor (and/or in allocate()).

summary: AtomVecSpinKokkos::force_clear() ignores its first argument, so it always zeroes fm/fm_long starting at atom 0 instead of at atom n as the base class does.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_spin_kokkos.cpp:166-190: 'void AtomVecSpinKokkos::force_clear(int /*n*/, size_t nbytes) { int nzero = (double)nbytes/sizeof(double); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(nzero, LAMMPS_LAMBDA(int i) { l_fm(i,0) = 0.0; ... l_fm_long(i,2) = 0.0; }); ... }'. The base is src/SPIN/atom_vec_spin.cpp:86-90: 'void AtomVecSpin::force_clear(int n, size_t nbytes) { memset(&fm[n][0], 0, 3 * nbytes); memset(&fm_long[n][0], 0, 3 * nbytes); }' -- it starts at row n. The interface contract is stated in src/atom_vec.h:74 and in the comment 'clear extra forces starting at atom N'.
failure_scenario: Latent today: the only KOKKOS caller, MinKokkos::force_clear (src/KOKKOS/min_kokkos.cpp:602-606), passes n = 0. Any future caller that uses the neighbor->includegroup form (src/verlet.cpp:417 calls 'atom->avec->force_clear(nlocal,nbytes)') would zero the wrong atoms and clobber the magnetic forces of the first nlocal atoms while leaving the ghosts stale.
suggested_fix: Honour the argument: capture n and zero rows [n, n+nzero) (or assert n == 0 with an explicit comment if the offset form is deliberately unsupported).

summary: In single/mixed precision builds the two Boltzmann factors of angle mwlc/kk can both underflow float to zero, making Q = 0 and turning the force and energy into NaN.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_mwlc_kokkos.cpp:170-180: 'const KK_FLOAT kbt = d_temp[type] * boltz; ... const KK_FLOAT q = Kokkos::exp(-d_k1[type] * (1.0 + c) / kbt); const KK_FLOAT qm = Kokkos::exp((-d_k2[type] * (1.0 + c) - d_mu[type]) / kbt); const KK_FLOAT Q = q + qm; ... if (eflag) eangle = -kbt * Kokkos::log(Q) - v_min; const KK_FLOAT a = (d_k1[type] * q + d_k2[type] * qm) / Q;'. With LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE or LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE, KK_FLOAT is float (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:400-408) and expf underflows to 0 below about -88, whereas the CPU version (src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_mwlc.cpp:115-121) works in double and only underflows below about -745. In metal units kbt = 8.617e-5 * T, so at T = 300 K a bending constant k1 of ~0.4 eV already gives an exponent of -88 at c = 1.
failure_scenario: A mwlc/kk run built with -DLMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE, metal units, temp 300 and k1 = k2 = 0.5 (eV): for nearly straight angles q = qm = 0, a = 0/0 = NaN and eangle = -kbt*log(0) = inf, so the whole trajectory becomes NaN while the double-precision build and the CPU style are fine.
suggested_fix: Factor out the larger exponent (compute emin_exp = min of the two exponents and evaluate Q = exp(e1-emin_exp) + exp(e2-emin_exp) with the log shifted accordingly), or evaluate the Boltzmann factors in KK_ACC_FLOAT.

summary: AtomVecKokkos_PackBorderVel drops the non-deform-group velocity branch, so with fix deform + remap v the buffer is short by 3 doubles for every atom outside the deform group and every field packed after v lands at the wrong offset.
failure_scenario: atom_style sphere/kk (or any kk style) + 'fix deform ... remap v' + 'comm_modify vel yes' on a GPU build (forward/exchange comm on device): border atoms not in the deform group get an uninitialized/garbage ghost velocity and every following border-vel field (radius, rmass, omega, q, molecule, mu, angmom, DPD energies) is read from the wrong buffer slot -> wrong forces/energies, potentially NaN.
suggested_fix: Add the missing else branch that writes _v(j,0..2) unshifted (and advances m) when the atom is not in the deform group, exactly as src/atom_vec.cpp:955-959 does.

summary: AtomVecKokkos_PackCommVel never initializes its _mu and _sp views, yet operator() reads them when datamask_comm_vel carries MU_MASK/SP_MASK (atom_style dipole/kk, spin/kk), dereferencing a default-constructed (null) Kokkos view.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style dipole/kk' with 'comm_modify vel yes' on a GPU build -> pack_comm_vel_kokkos launches a kernel that reads _mu(j,0) from an unallocated view: segfault/illegal memory access (or silent garbage dipoles on ghosts with bounds checking off).
suggested_fix: Add _mu(atomKK->k_mu.view<DeviceType>()) and _sp(atomKK->k_sp.view<DeviceType>()) to the AtomVecKokkos_PackCommVel initializer list, in member-declaration order.

summary: unpack_border_vel_kokkos picks the 'x/tag/type/mask/v only' functor based on ncomm_vel instead of nborder_vel, so for atom_style charge/bond/angle/molecular/full the q and molecule values that pack_border_vel_kokkos wrote are never unpacked into ghost atoms.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style full/kk' + 'comm_modify vel yes' (e.g. with fix rigid or a granular/SPH pair style) on a GPU build: every ghost atom keeps a stale or uninitialized charge and molecule ID after each reneighboring -> wrong Coulomb forces and wrong special-bond/molecule-ID-based exclusions.
suggested_fix: Branch on `!nborder_vel` (not `!ncomm_vel`) in unpack_border_vel_kokkos, or give AtomVecKokkos_PackBorderVel the same DEFAULT template parameter so packer and unpacker are selected by the same predicate.

summary: field2size("num_improper") sizes the improper block with atom->dihedral_per_atom instead of atom->improper_per_atom, so size_exchange is too small whenever a system has more impropers per atom than dihedrals per atom, and pack_exchange writes past the end of its buffer row.
failure_scenario: atom_style full/kk or molecular/kk for a molecule with e.g. improper_per_atom=6 and dihedral_per_atom=4: pack_exchange_kokkos writes 10 doubles past the row for every migrating atom, corrupting the next atom's exchange record (and the last row overruns the allocation) -> lost/garbled bonded topology or a crash during atom migration.
suggested_fix: Return 1+5*atom->improper_per_atom for the "num_improper" field.

summary: None of the forward-comm functors handle RADIUS_MASK/RMASS_MASK, so 'atom_style sphere/kk 1' (dynamic radii) silently never forward-communicates radius and rmass to ghost atoms even though size_forward reserves room for them.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style sphere/kk 1' with 'fix adapt ... diameter' on a GPU build: ghost particles keep their radius and rmass from the last borders() call, so pair granular/gran overlap distances and masses are wrong for every ghost contact -> wrong forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Add `if (_datamask & RADIUS_MASK) ...` and `if (_datamask & RMASS_MASK) ...` blocks (in the order used by pack_border) to AtomVecKokkos_PackComm, UnpackComm, PackCommSelf, PackCommSelfFused, PackCommVel and UnpackCommVel, or reject radvary in AtomVecSphereKokkos.

summary: The ellipsoid bonus forward-comm functors always build their buffer view with a row stride of size_forward, but when called from pack_comm_vel_kokkos/unpack_comm_vel_kokkos the buffer stride is size_forward+size_velocity and the offset already includes size_velocity, so the quaternions are written into and read from the wrong buffer rows.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid/kk' with 'comm_modify vel yes' on a GPU build: the ghost quaternions are garbage and the neighbouring atom's communicated x/v are overwritten -> completely wrong aspherical forces, likely blow-up.
suggested_fix: Pass the vel_flag (or the already-computed stride) into the bonus functors and build the buffer view with elements = size_forward + (vel_flag ? size_velocity : 0), matching AtomVecKokkos_PackCommVel.

summary: The Device branch of AtomVecMolecularKokkos::sync_pinned omits k_dihedral_atom4, so that array is never staged to the device while its dual-view sync flag is cleared by the surrounding transfers.
failure_scenario: Any future/existing caller of atomKK->sync_pinned(Device, DIHEDRAL_MASK) after the host modified the topology (data file read, fix bond/react, molecule template insertion) leaves dihedral_atom4 stale on the device -> the 4th atom of every dihedral is wrong on the GPU.  Currently latent: the three call sites (verlet_kokkos.cpp:448, third_order_kokkos.cpp:230, dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:230) all pass Host/HostKK.
suggested_fix: Add the missing k_dihedral_atom4 need_sync_device()/perform_pinned_copy_transform pair to the Device branch.

summary: The Device branch of AtomVecFullKokkos::sync_pinned omits k_dihedral_atom4 (same copy-paste defect as the molecular style).
failure_scenario: Same as the molecular case: a Device-space pinned sync of DIHEDRAL_MASK leaves dihedral_atom4 stale on the GPU for atom_style full/kk.
suggested_fix: Add the missing k_dihedral_atom4 entry to the Device branch.

summary: AtomVecKokkos::~AtomVecKokkos never frees the pinned staging buffer allocated by perform_pinned_copy/perform_pinned_copy_transform, leaking it for the lifetime of the process.
failure_scenario: An input script that changes atom_style (or any run that constructs and destroys several LAMMPS instances / uses the library interface repeatedly) leaks nmax*3*sizeof(double) of page-locked host memory per atom_vec instance; pinned memory is a scarce resource and exhausting it makes further CUDA/HIP allocations fail.
suggested_fix: In ~AtomVecKokkos, `if (buffer) Kokkos::kokkos_free<LMPPinnedHostType>(buffer);` (guarded by the same #ifdef LMP_KOKKOS_GPU as the allocation) and reset buffer/buffer_size.

summary: Source file contains a non-ASCII character (U+2019 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK) in a comment, violating the project's 7-bit US-ASCII rule and failing the style CI check.
failure_scenario: `cd src && make check` / the style-check.yml GitHub workflow fails on this file before the release.
suggested_fix: Replace the typographic apostrophe with a plain ASCII apostrophe (J's).

summary: AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos silently accepts the 'superellipsoid' sub-style argument but is hard-wired to the plain-ellipsoid bonus layout and never allocates atom->radius, so ellipsoid/kk superellipsoid is broken rather than rejected.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:39 hard-codes `size_exchange_bonus = 8;` and the pack/unpack bonus functors move exactly shape[3]+quat[4] (lines 483-489, 557-563, 655-661), matching src/atom_vec_ellipsoid.cpp:46-48 size_border_bonus/size_restart_bonus_one = 8.  AtomVecEllipsoid::process_args (src/atom_vec_ellipsoid.cpp:1095-1114) raises those to 13, switches the bonus storage to bonus_super, and appends "radius" to fields_grow/copy/border/border_vel/exchange/restart/create.  AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos does not override process_args, and its grow() (lines 87-99) grows tag,type,mask,image,x,v,f,rmass,angmom,torque,ellipsoid - never atomKK->k_radius - while set_atom_masks() will put RADIUS_MASK into datamask_border, so AtomVecKokkos_PackBorder (atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:1534-1535) reads _radius(j) from an unallocated view.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid/kk superellipsoid' -> null/empty radius view dereferenced during the first borders() call, and blockiness parameters are never communicated -> crash or silently wrong superquadric shapes.
suggested_fix: Override process_args in AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos to error out on 'superellipsoid' (or implement it: grow k_radius, use the 13-wide bonus layout and the Bonus_Super struct).

summary: AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos_PackExchangeBonus reads the bonus array through _bonus while concurrently writing the same memory through the _bonusw alias in the same parallel_for, so a compacted bonus entry can be read after another thread has overwritten it.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:631-634 aliases the same DualView twice:
      _bonus(bonus.template view<DeviceType>()),
      ...
      _bonusw(bonus.template view<DeviceType>()),
and operator() at lines 655-677 first reads `_bonus(j).shape[0] ... _bonus(j).quat[3]` for j = _ellipsoid[i] and then writes
        _ellipsoidw[_bonus[j_bonus].ilocal] = i_bonus;
        _bonusw[i_bonus] = _bonus[j_bonus];
Nothing orders these across threads.  The authors were aware of the hazard - lines 756-757 say 'must backfill ellipsoid after pack exchange bonus in a separate functor to prevent race conditions' - but the bonus compaction itself was left in the packing kernel.
failure_scenario: Two atoms leaving the sub-domain in the same exchange whose copylist_bonus tail entry for one is the i_bonus slot of the other: the second thread reads a slot the first has already overwritten -> the ellipsoid that stays behind gets the wrong shape/quaternion.  Requires a specific ordering, so it is intermittent.
suggested_fix: Move the bonus compaction (the `_bonusw[i_bonus] = _bonus[j_bonus]` block) into its own parallel_for after the packing kernel, exactly as was done for AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos_BackfillEllipsoid, or verify and document that copylist_bonus can never alias a sent i_bonus.

summary: perform_pinned_copy separates two Kokkos::deep_copy statements with a comma operator instead of a semicolon in both branches.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_kokkos.h:275-276 and 280-281:
      Kokkos::deep_copy(LMPHostType(),tmp_view,src.view_host()),
      Kokkos::deep_copy(LMPHostType(),src.view_device(),tmp_view);
Both calls execute in order so behaviour is currently correct, but the comma makes the pair a single expression statement and will silently swallow the second call if the first is ever wrapped in a conditional.
failure_scenario: No current misbehaviour; a maintenance hazard and a compiler-warning source (-Wcomma).
suggested_fix: Replace the trailing commas with semicolons.

summary: set_atom_masks compares a signed int loop index against std::vector::size(), producing sign-compare warnings in every one of its seven loops.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:2976, 2982, 2988, 2994, 3000, 3006, 3012 all read `for (int i = 0; i < default_xxx.size(); i++)` where default_xxx is a `const std::vector<std::string>` (src/atom_vec.cpp:33-41).  set_size_exchange has the same pattern at line 3023.
failure_scenario: No runtime defect; -Wsign-compare noise that can hide real warnings during the release build.
suggested_fix: Use `std::size_t i` (or a range-for over the vector) in these loops.

summary: AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos::sort_kokkos applies the per-atom bin permutation to the bonus array, which is indexed by ellipsoid[i] rather than by atom index, and it uses the d_bonus member that is never assigned anywhere.
failure_scenario: If the bonus guard in AtomKokkos::sort is ever relaxed, an on-device atom sort scrambles shapes/quaternions and leaves stale bonus.ilocal values -> silently wrong aspherical dynamics.
suggested_fix: Remove the `Sorter.sort(..., d_bonus)` call (and the unused d_bonus/h_bonus members), or implement a proper bonus re-index + ilocal fixup before enabling device sorting for bonus styles.

summary: The ellipsoid border-bonus functors index the communication buffer with the raw view's own extent(1) instead of the packing stride size_border(+size_velocity), which disagrees with AtomVecKokkos_UnpackBorderVel when the receive buffer was allocated with the narrower shape.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid/kk' + 'comm_modify vel yes' with more than one MPI rank: unpack_border_bonus_kokkos reads the bonus flag/shape/quat at row-stride 15 from a buffer that unpack_border_vel_kokkos treated as row-stride 21 -> ghost ellipsoid shapes and orientations come from the wrong atom.
suggested_fix: Build an explicit unmanaged view with elements = size_border + (vel_flag ? size_velocity : 0) inside the bonus border functors (and fix grow_recv_kokkos to allocate the wider row when ghost_velocity is set).

summary: k_brokenflag is written on the device by the kernel but never marked modified, so k_brokenflag.sync_host() is a no-op on GPU builds and bond quartic/kk never breaks any bond.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:124 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_brokenflag,0);' (raw device write, no modify flag), :281 'd_brokenflag(n) = 1;' (device kernel write), :176 'k_brokenflag.sync_host();' with NO preceding 'k_brokenflag.template modify<DeviceType>()' / 'modify_device()'. grep confirms the only k_brokenflag lines in the file are 120,121,122,124,176,182,199,281 - no modify anywhere. Kokkos::DualView::sync_host() only deep-copies when modified_flags(device) > modified_flags(host); both are 0 here, so no D2H copy happens. The host loop then reads h_brokenflag (:182,:199) which stays all-zero. Contrast the correct pattern in the sibling style src/KOKKOS/bond_table_kokkos.cpp:204-205 'k_error_flag.template modify<DeviceType>(); k_error_flag.sync_host();'. CPU base src/MOLECULE/bond_quartic.cpp:102-110 breaks the bond inline (bondlist[n][2]=0 and atom->bond_type[..]=0).
failure_scenario: GPU (CUDA/HIP/SYCL) build, 'bond_style quartic/kk' polymer scission run (e.g. examples/micelle-style FENE/quartic chain scission): a stretched bond with rsq > rc^2 sets d_brokenflag on the device, h_brokenflag stays 0, so h_bondlist(n,2) is never set to 0 and atom->bond_type is never zeroed. No bond is ever broken; the quartic potential silently behaves as an unbreakable bond and the trajectory is wrong. On a CPU-only Kokkos build host and device views alias, so the bug is invisible.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_brokenflag.template modify<DeviceType>();' immediately before the 'k_brokenflag.sync_host();' at line 176 (and mark the deep_copy(d_brokenflag,0) with modify<DeviceType>() as well for consistency).

summary: BondHybridKokkos::compute() calls modify_device() on a subview that shares its DualView modified-flags with the parent, which starves a partial_flag sub-style (quartic/kk) of its host-side bond-type-zero writes and then overwrites them.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:117-119 'auto k_bondlist_m = Kokkos::subview(k_bondlist,m,Kokkos::ALL,Kokkos::ALL); k_bondlist_m.modify_device(); neighborKK->k_bondlist = k_bondlist_m;'. Kokkos DualView subviews share the modified_flags view, so modify_device() sets modified_flags(1) > modified_flags(0) every step. bond quartic/kk marks broken bonds by writing the HOST mirror and calling modify_host: src/KOKKOS/bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:202 'h_bondlist(n,2) = 0;' and :249 'neighborKK->k_bondlist.modify_host();'. On the following step the hybrid's modify_device() at :118 makes modified_device > modified_host, so quartic's 'neighborKK->k_bondlist.template sync<DeviceType>()' (bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:112) performs NO H2D copy and its 'sync_host()' (:180) instead copies device->host, wiping the zeros. Standalone quartic/kk does not hit this because nothing calls modify_device on the neighbor bondlist.
failure_scenario: 'bond_style hybrid/kk quartic/kk harmonic/kk' + chain scission: within one reneighbor interval the bondlist entry of a broken bond is restored to its original type every step, so the 'if (bondlist(n,2) <= 0) return;' skip (bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:266) never fires; if the two atoms relax back inside rc before the next reneighbor the bond is silently re-formed, whereas the CPU bond_hybrid keeps it broken permanently.
suggested_fix: Do not call modify_device() on the shared subview flags; instead give each sub-style bondlist its own DualView (or clear/restore the flags per sub-style) and honour the sub-style's modify_host by syncing the sub-list back to the device before the next step.

summary: BondHybridKokkos::compute() omits the partial_flag / orig_map write-back that the CPU BondHybrid uses to propagate deleted (type 0) bonds from the sub-style bondlist back into the original neighbor bondlist.
evidence: CPU src/bond_hybrid.cpp:85-88 allocates orig_map[m], :99 'if (partial_flag) orig_map[m][n] = i;', and :148-157 'if (partial_flag) { ... if (bondlist[m][i][2] <= 0) { n = orig_map[m][i]; bondlist_orig[n][2] = bondlist[m][i][2]; } }'. The KOKKOS version src/KOKKOS/bond_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:96-103 builds the sub-style lists with no orig_map, and :145-148 restores the original list ('neighbor->nbondlist = nbondlist_orig; neighborKK->k_bondlist = k_bondlist_orig;') without any write-back. partial_flag is set by bond quartic (src/MOLECULE/bond_quartic.cpp:39 'partial_flag = 1;') and bond quartic/kk inherits it, and quartic/kk is a legal hybrid/kk sub-style (bond_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:194-196 only requires kokkosable).
failure_scenario: 'bond_style hybrid/kk quartic/kk ...': after a bond breaks, neighbor->bondlist still carries the old nonzero bond type until the next reneighbor, so 'compute bond/local' / 'compute bond' report a finite energy and length for a bond that the CPU version reports as deleted.
suggested_fix: Port the partial_flag path: keep a per-sub-style orig_map device view filled in the second parallel_for and, when any sub-style has partial_flag, scatter type<=0 entries back into k_bondlist_orig after the sub-style loop.

summary: Non-atomic writes to the shared scalar d_flag can downgrade a fatal 'Bad FENE bond' (flag 2) to a mere warning (flag 1), so the run continues with a clamped rlogarg instead of aborting.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:200-206 'if (rlogarg < 0.1) { if (rlogarg <= -3.0) d_flag() = 2; else d_flag() = 1; rlogarg = 0.1; }' - plain stores to a single scalar from every thread, no Kokkos::atomic_max. src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:140-143 then does 'if (h_flag() == 1) error->warning(...); else if (h_flag() == 2) error->one(FLERR,"Bad FENE bond");'. The CPU base src/MOLECULE/bond_fene.cpp:89-94 raises 'error->one(FLERR, "Bad FENE bond")' immediately for every bond with rlogarg <= -3.0, so it can never be masked.
failure_scenario: One bond has rlogarg <= -3.0 (thread A writes 2) while another has 0.1 > rlogarg > -3.0 (thread B writes 1). If B's store lands last, h_flag()==1 and the run only warns and keeps integrating a catastrophically stretched bond instead of aborting as the CPU style does.
suggested_fix: Use 'Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), 2)' / 'Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), 1)' (or a per-thread reduction into EV/int) so the most severe condition always wins.

summary: Same d_flag race as bond_fene_kokkos: plain stores of 2 (fatal) and 1 (warning) to one shared scalar can hide a 'Bad FENE bond' abort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_expand_kokkos.cpp:191-197 'if (rlogarg < 0.1) { if (rlogarg <= -3.0) d_flag() = 2; else d_flag() = 1; rlogarg = 0.1; }' and :135-138 'if (h_flag() == 1) error->warning(...); else if (h_flag() == 2) error->one(FLERR,"Bad FENE bond");'. CPU base src/MOLECULE/bond_fene_expand.cpp:87-92 aborts per-bond via 'if (rlogarg <= -3.0) error->one(FLERR, "Bad FENE bond");'.
failure_scenario: Two bonds in the same kernel launch, one with rlogarg <= -3.0 and one with -3.0 < rlogarg < 0.1: the fatal flag can be overwritten by the warning flag and the run continues with the bond clamped to rlogarg = 0.1.
suggested_fix: Replace the plain stores with Kokkos::atomic_max on d_flag() so the severity is monotone.

summary: Same d_flag race as bond_fene_kokkos: plain stores of 2 (fatal) and 1 (warning) to one shared scalar can hide a 'Bad FENE bond' abort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_nm_kokkos.cpp:174-180 'if (rlogarg < 0.02) { if (rlogarg <= -0.21) d_flag() = 2; else d_flag() = 1; rlogarg = 0.02; }' and :121-124 'if (h_flag() == 1) error->warning(...); else if (h_flag() == 2) error->one(FLERR,"Bad FENE bond");'. CPU base src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/bond_fene_nm.cpp:86-91 aborts per-bond with 'if (rlogarg <= -.21) error->one(FLERR, "Bad FENE bond");'.
failure_scenario: Concurrent bonds with rlogarg <= -0.21 and -0.21 < rlogarg < 0.02: the fatal marker can be lost and the run continues instead of aborting.
suggested_fix: Use Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), ...) instead of plain assignment.

summary: The spline branch of uf_lookup_kk() reads the pad element d_e(tb,tablength)/d_f(tb,tablength)/d_e2/d_f2 which setup_tables() never fills, and the comment's claim that its weight is exactly zero is false for bond lengths in (hi, hi+delta).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_table_kokkos.cpp:77-86 allocates the 2-D views with 'tablength+1' columns 'so that the spline branch can read itable+1 at the last bin, where its weight is exactly zero', but :95-103 only fills 'for (int i = 0; i < tablength; i++)', leaving column tablength at 0. :249-265: 'const int itable = static_cast<int>((x_in - lo) * invdelta); if (itable >= tablength) { d_error_flag() = 2; return; } ... b = (x_in - d_r(tb,itable)) * invdelta; ... u = a*d_e(tb,itable) + b*d_e(tb,itable+1) + ...'. With r[i] = lo + i*delta and hi = lo + (tablength-1)*delta, itable == tablength-1 corresponds to x in [hi, hi+delta), so b = (x-hi)/delta is in [0,1) and is only zero when x == hi exactly. The CPU src/MOLECULE/bond_table.cpp:611-614 reads tb->e[itable+1] from an array of length tablength (an out-of-bounds read), so the two implementations disagree for hi < r < hi+delta.
failure_scenario: 'bond_style table spline N' with a bond stretched just past the table's outer cutoff (hi < r < hi+delta, still accepted by the itable < tablength test): bond/kk returns u and mdu computed with a zero end point, giving a different (and unphysical) energy/force than the plain bond table style.
suggested_fix: Fill the pad column with the extrapolated end values (or clamp b to 0 at itable == tablength-1) and fix the misleading comment; better yet make itable == tablength-1 raise error flag 2 like the inner cutoff, matching the intent of the table bounds.

summary: coeff() and read_restart() build the coefficient DualViews as function-local temporaries whose host mirrors die at the end of the function, and they copy r0/k2/k3/k4/A/B for ALL types including ones whose coefficients are still uninitialized.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_quartic_exp_kokkos.cpp:243-256 'DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d k_r0("BondQuarticExp::r0",n+1); ... d_r0 = k_r0.template view<DeviceType>();' - the class (src/KOKKOS/bond_quartic_exp_kokkos.h:85-88) only keeps the d_* device views, no k_* members, and compute() (:84-90) syncs nothing. The same pattern is repeated in read_restart() at :292-304. The fill loop at :257-264 runs 'for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++)' over every type, but BondQuarticExp::allocate() (src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/bond_quartic_exp.cpp:129-134) leaves r0/k2/.../B uninitialized until each type's bond_coeff, unlike every other style in this group which loops only ilo..ihi (cf. bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:252).
failure_scenario: 'bond_coeff 1 ...' with nbondtypes = 2 reads uninitialized heap doubles for type 2 and static_cast<KK_FLOAT>s them; harmless today because type 2 is unusable, but it is undefined behaviour and can raise FP exceptions under -ffpe-trap. It also makes the style unmaintainable: the host mirrors are gone, so a later k_*.sync/modify cannot be added.
suggested_fix: Declare k_r0/k_k2/k_k3/k_k4/k_A/k_B as class members allocated in allocate() (as bond_class2_kokkos does), and restrict the coeff() fill loop to ilo..ihi.

summary: compute() copies FixStoreAtom's initial positions for every local+ghost atom through a scalar host loop and a full host-to-device transfer on EVERY timestep.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:100-109 'const int n_sync = atom->nlocal + atom->nghost; auto h_x0 = k_x0.view_host(); for (int i = 0; i < n_sync; i++) { h_x0(i,0) = ...; } k_x0.modify_host(); k_x0.template sync<DeviceType>();' - unconditional, executed once per compute() call.
failure_scenario: Any GPU run with 'bond_style harmonic/restrain/kk': every MD step pays an O(nlocal+nghost) host loop plus a 3*(nlocal+nghost)*sizeof(KK_FLOAT) H2D transfer, which is the same order as the x/f transfer the KOKKOS package exists to avoid; the /kk variant can easily be slower than the plain CPU style.
suggested_fix: Refresh k_x0 only when the atom set changed (neighbor->ago == 0 or a stored update->ntimestep guard), or better, store the initial positions in a device DualView owned by the style and update it in the exchange/border callbacks.

summary: k_eatom/k_vatom are destroyed and re-created on every timestep when per-atom energy/virial is requested, instead of the size-guarded reallocation used by the other bond kokkos styles.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:74-87 'if (eflag_atom) { //if(k_eatom.extent(0)<maxeatom) { ... memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"improper:eatom"); ... //} }' - the guard is commented out. The same unconditional destroy/create appears in src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_kokkos.cpp:80-89, src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_expand_kokkos.cpp:76-85 and src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_nm_kokkos.cpp:73-82. The corrected pattern is src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:74-87 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { ... } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);'.
failure_scenario: 'compute pe/atom' or 'compute stress/atom' with bond class2/kk or fene/kk on a GPU: a device allocation + free per timestep, which serializes with the kernel stream and can dominate the bond time for small systems.
suggested_fix: Restore the 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) {...} else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);' guard in class2, fene, fene/expand and fene/nm, as bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp already does.

summary: Eleven newly added KOKKOS bond styles have no action lines in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, violating KOKKOS rule 5, so 'make no-kokkos' leaves stale copies of them in src/.
evidence: grep '^action bond_' src/KOKKOS/Install.sh returns only class2, fene, table, harmonic, hybrid and quartic_exp (lines 80-91). Missing: bond_fene_expand_kokkos, bond_fene_nm_kokkos, bond_gaussian_kokkos, bond_gromos_kokkos, bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos, bond_harmonic_shift_kokkos, bond_harmonic_shift_cut_kokkos, bond_mm3_kokkos, bond_morse_kokkos, bond_nonlinear_kokkos, bond_quartic_kokkos (.cpp and .h each). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 5 requires 'Register new files in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh with action lines', passing both filenames when the base class lives in an optional package (e.g. bond_gaussian.cpp is in EXTRA-MOLECULE, bond_mm3.cpp in YAFF).
failure_scenario: A tree that once had the KOKKOS package installed under the legacy make build, then 'make no-kokkos': the 22 unregistered files stay behind in src/ and are compiled into the next non-KOKKOS build, producing undefined KOKKOS symbols. (Impact is limited because src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:757 now aborts install mode - the package is CMake-only - so action() is used only for removal.)
suggested_fix: Add the missing 'action bond_<name>_kokkos.cpp bond_<name>.cpp' / '.h' pairs next to the existing bond entries at lines 80-91.

summary: Leftover developer 'FIX:' comment plus redundant re-creation of the coefficient dual views in read_restart(), and per-atom memory tags mislabelled 'improper:' in bond styles.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:264-267 '// FIX: Removed "DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d" to use the class members / // instead of creating local shadowed variables. / k_k = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d("BondHarmonic::k", n+1);' - BondHarmonic::read_restart (src/MOLECULE/bond_harmonic.cpp:169) already calls the virtual allocate(), i.e. BondHarmonicKokkos::allocate() (:213-228), which has just created these very views, so lines 266-270 leak/replace them for nothing (same shape in src/KOKKOS/bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:279-287). Separately, bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:77,84, bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:77,84 and bond_quartic_exp_kokkos.cpp:72,79 pass "improper:eatom"/"improper:vatom" as the memory tag inside a BOND style.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers; the stray 'FIX:' note reads as leftover scratch commentary in a stable release, and the 'improper:' tags make 'info memory' / memory-leak reports attribute bond per-atom arrays to improper styles.
suggested_fix: Delete the 'FIX:' comment and the redundant dual-view (re)construction in read_restart(), and change the memory tags to "bond:eatom"/"bond:vatom" as the other bond kokkos styles already do.

summary: The device minimum_image() applies at most ONE periodic wrap per dimension (if) where Domain::minimum_image loops (while), and it silently drops the 'atoms have moved too far apart' error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:245-263 'if (xperiodic) { if (Kokkos::abs(dx) > xprd_half) { if (dx < 0.0) dx += xprd; else dx -= xprd; } }' (and the same single-if for y, z and for all three triclinic branches at :264-295). CPU src/domain.cpp:1219-1248 and 1250-1290 use 'while (fabs(dx) > xprd_half) {...}' plus 'if (fabs(dx) > (MAXIMGCOUNT * xprd)) error->one(file,line,"Atoms have moved too far apart ({}) for minimum image");'. The CPU base src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/bond_harmonic_restrain.cpp:78 calls exactly that: 'domain->minimum_image(FLERR, delx, dely, delz);'.
failure_scenario: Stored initial positions that are more than 1.5 box lengths apart (box shrunk by fix deform/npt after init_style stored x0, or unwrapped x0 for a stretched molecule) leave a residual image after one wrap, so the reference length r0 - and hence the restraint force - differs from the CPU style; the triclinic branch can also need a second y wrap after the z tilt shift.
suggested_fix: Change each 'if (Kokkos::abs(d?) > ?prd_half)' into a 'while' loop, matching Domain::minimum_image, and optionally set an error flag when the displacement exceeds MAXIMGCOUNT box lengths.

summary: ebond is left uninitialized when eflag == 0 and is then passed by reference into ev_tally(); the CPU base initializes it to 0.0 before the loop.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_class2_kokkos.cpp:180 'KK_FLOAT ebond, fbond, de_bond;' then :186 'if (eflag) ebond = ...;' and :202 'if (EVFLAG) ev_tally(ev,i1,i2,ebond,fbond,delx,dely,delz);'. CPU src/CLASS2/bond_class2.cpp:63 'ebond = 0.0;' before the bond loop. Every other kokkos bond style in this group initializes it (e.g. bond_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:178 'KK_FLOAT ebond = 0;').
failure_scenario: A step with vflag set but eflag clear (e.g. 'compute pressure' without thermo energy) runs the EVFLAG=1 kernel with an indeterminate ebond. ev_tally only reads it under eflag_either, so today it is harmless, but any future eflag_atom/eflag_global refactor turns it into garbage energies, and it trips -Wmaybe-uninitialized / static analysis.
suggested_fix: Initialize as 'KK_FLOAT ebond = 0.0; KK_FLOAT fbond = 0.0;' at line 180, matching the other bond kokkos styles.

summary: uf_lookup_kk() omits the CPU's non-finite bond-length guard, so a NaN/Inf separation produces an undefined int conversion instead of a clean error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_table_kokkos.cpp:241-252 starts straight at 'const int tb = d_tabindex[type]; ... const int itable = static_cast<int>((x_in - lo) * invdelta); if (itable < 0) { d_error_flag() = 1; return; }'. CPU src/MOLECULE/bond_table.cpp:592 begins with 'if (!std::isfinite(x)) { error->one(FLERR, "Illegal bond in bond style table"); }'.
failure_scenario: A blown-up trajectory gives r = NaN: static_cast<int>(NaN) is undefined; on x86 it yields INT_MIN so the code happens to report 'Bond length < table inner cutoff', but on other targets it can produce an in-range itable and silently index the table with garbage instead of aborting.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (!Kokkos::isfinite(x_in)) { d_error_flag() = 1; return; }' (or a third flag value with its own message) at the top of uf_lookup_kk().

summary: A std:: facility (std::numeric_limits<>::min()) is used inside a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION device kernel, which the KOKKOS package rules forbid and which only compiles with --expt-relaxed-constexpr.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:154 'static constexpr KK_ACC_FLOAT SMALL_KK = std::numeric_limits<KK_ACC_FLOAT>::min();' inside 'void BondGaussianKokkos<DeviceType>::operator()(TagBondGaussianCompute<NEWTON_BOND,EVFLAG>, const int &n, EV_FLOAT& ev) const' (:149). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ..., never std::'. Kokkos provides Kokkos::Experimental::norm_min_v / finite_min_v for this.
failure_scenario: Any nvcc/hipcc build without --expt-relaxed-constexpr (or a future toolchain that tightens constexpr host-function use in device code) fails to compile bond_gaussian_kokkos.cpp; today Kokkos enables the flag so it builds.
suggested_fix: Replace with a Kokkos-provided constant (Kokkos::Experimental::norm_min_v<KK_ACC_FLOAT>) or a literal guarded by an if constexpr on sizeof(KK_ACC_FLOAT).

summary: The second-group filter (mask[j] & jgroupbit) is applied only in the single-column template branch, so multi-column 'compute coord/atom cutoff R group <g2> t1 t2 ...' counts neighbours from every group instead of only group2.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_coord_atom_kokkos.cpp:279-280 'if (NCOL == 1)\n        if (!(mask[j] & jgroupbit)) continue;' -- the guard is compiled out for the ncol>1 instantiation TagComputeCoordAtom<CUTOFF,0> launched at :236. The CPU base applies it in BOTH branches: src/compute_coord_atom.cpp:233 'if (mask[j] & jgroupbit) {' (ncol==1) and src/compute_coord_atom.cpp:265 'if (mask[j] & jgroupbit) {' (ncol>1 branch, lines 249-278).
failure_scenario: 'group sub type 1' then 'compute c1 all coord/atom/kk cutoff 3.0 group sub 1 2' gives per-type coordination numbers that include neighbours outside group 'sub'; the non-KOKKOS compute coord/atom returns smaller, correct numbers for the same input.
suggested_fix: Move the jgroupbit test out of the 'if (NCOL == 1)' guard so it runs for every CSTYLE==CUTOFF instantiation (the ORIENT path uses jgroupbit = 'all', so an unconditional test is still equivalent to the CPU ORIENT loop).

summary: compute_local() returns immediately when host_flag is set without falling back to the CPU implementation, so 'compute gaussian/grid/local/kk' computes nothing at all on any host-only KOKKOS build (and for the /kk/host variant on GPU builds).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:130-132 'if (host_flag) {\n    return;\n  }' with host_flag set at :55 'host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK);'. On a CPU-only Kokkos build LMPDeviceType == Kokkos::DefaultExecutionSpace == LMPHostType (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:172-173), so ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<LMPDeviceType>::space resolves to the LMPHostType specialisation, HostKK (kokkos_type.h:220-223) -- host_flag is 1 even for the plain '/kk' style. Contrast the sibling port src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:159-160 'if (host_flag) { ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array();' which does fall back.
failure_scenario: 'lmp -k on t 4 -sf kk' (no GPU) with 'compute g all gaussian/grid/local grid 10 10 10 ...' and 'dump ... local ...' writes zeros in every gaussian column and never sets invoked_local; the non-KOKKOS compute returns the correct densities.
suggested_fix: Replace the bare return with a fallback to the CPU path, e.g. 'if (host_flag) { ComputeGaussianGridLocal::compute_local(); return; }' (syncing x/type to the host first), or port the kernel so it also runs correctly for LMPHostType.

summary: The device kernel drops the compute-group filter, so grid values include atoms outside the compute's group.
failure_scenario: 'group solute type 2' + 'compute g solute gaussian/grid/local/kk grid ...' returns the same densities as a whole-system compute, silently including solvent atoms.
suggested_fix: Add a mask view (sync MASK_MASK in compute_local and store typename AT::t_int_1d_randomread mask) and skip j when '!(mask(j) & groupbit)', matching the CPU loop.

summary: The order parameter is divided by nnn instead of by the actual neighbour count ncount, so 'nnn NULL' (nnn == 0) divides by zero and yields NaN/Inf for every atom; the CPU style divides by ncount.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_hexorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:268-269 'd_qnarray(i,0) = usum/nnn;\n  d_qnarray(i,1) = vsum/nnn;' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:234-235 'qn[0] = usum/ncount;\n      qn[1] = vsum/ncount;'. The CPU style also guards the empty case at :208 'if ((ncount < nnn) || (ncount == 0)) { qn[0] = qn[1] = 0.0; continue; }', while the KOKKOS kernel only tests 'if (ncount < nnn)' (:240). With nnn == 0 the parser sets nnn = 0 for the 'nnn NULL' keyword (compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:70-71).
failure_scenario: 'compute h all hexorder/atom/kk nnn NULL cutoff 1.5' writes 0.0/0.0 = NaN (or usum/0 = +-Inf) into both columns of c_h for every atom, and the same input on the CPU style returns the correctly averaged order parameter.
suggested_fix: Divide by ncount as the CPU style does (ncount already equals nnn when nnn > 0), and add the 'ncount == 0' early-out to the guard at line 240.

summary: The guard that decides whether to call group->inertia_extended() omits finite-size spheres, so the spin moment of inertia of atom_style sphere particles is silently dropped by compute inertia/kk.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_inertia_kokkos.cpp:96-107 comments 'the extended-particle contribution reads the ellipsoid, line, tri and body bonus arrays ... when none of those atom styles is present it adds nothing' and guards with 'if (atom->style_match("ellipsoid") || atom->style_match("line") || atom->style_match("tri") || atom->style_match("body")) { ... group->inertia_extended(igroup,itensor); }'. But Group::inertia_extended -> add_extended_inertia (src/group.cpp:1694-1725) has a sphere fallback that needs none of those atom vecs: ':1721-1722  } else if (radius && radius[i] > 0.0) { ivec[0] = ivec[1] = ivec[2] = SINERTIA * massone * radius[i] * radius[i]; }'. The CPU style calls it unconditionally: src/compute_inertia.cpp:63 'group->inertia_extended(igroup, itensor);'.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style sphere' granular run with 'compute I all inertia/kk': the three diagonal components are short by sum(0.4*m_i*r_i^2) compared to the non-KOKKOS 'compute inertia' on the same configuration.
suggested_fix: Add '|| atom->radius' (or atom->radius_flag) to the condition, or simply always call group->inertia_extended() after syncing the needed host arrays.

summary: d_ncount(ii) is only written for atoms inside the compute group, so atoms outside the group reuse a stale neighbour count from a previous chunk or timestep and get bogus (non-zero) order parameters, where the CPU style memsets their row to zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:243-292: 'if (mask[i] & groupbit) { ... d_ncount(ii) = ncount; ... }' -- there is no else branch, so d_ncount(ii) keeps its previous contents for out-of-group atoms. The follow-up kernels have no mask test: :298-317 'operator()(TagComputeOrientOrderAtomSelect3, ii) { const int ncount = d_ncount(ii); if ((ncount == 0) || (ncount < nnn)) { zero; return; } if (nnn > 0) { select3(nnn, ncount, ii); ...' and :345-354 BOOP2 likewise. The CPU base zeroes the whole array every call: src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp:249 'memset(&qnarray[0][0], 0, sizeof(double) * nmax * ncol);' and only computes inside 'if (mask[i] & groupbit)' (:254).
failure_scenario: 'group core type 1' + 'compute q core orientorder/atom/kk degrees 1 6' on a system with more than 'chunksize' atoms (or on any timestep after the first): rows of c_q belonging to atoms of type 2 contain order parameters computed from another atom's stale d_distsq/d_rlist rows instead of the 0.0 the CPU style writes.
suggested_fix: Add 'else d_ncount(ii) = 0;' in the Neigh kernel (or zero d_ncount/d_qnarray before each chunk) so out-of-group atoms take the zeroing path in Select3.

summary: d_radelem/d_wjelem/d_sinnerelem/d_dinnerelem are allocated with 'nelements' entries but the constructor fills 'ntypes' of them (and sinner/dinner at index i instead of i-1), so any run with more atom types than SNAP elements writes past the end of the host mirrors.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:76-79 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_radelem,"...",nelements); ... d_wjelem ... d_sinnerelem ... d_dinnerelem' followed by :96-103 'for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { h_radelem(i-1) = radelem[i]; h_wjelem(i-1) = wjelem[i]; if (switchinnerflag){ h_sinnerelem(i) = sinnerelem[i]; h_dinnerelem(i) = dinnerelem[i]; } }'. In ComputeSNAGrid radelem/wjelem are per-TYPE arrays of size ntypes+1 (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:62-72) while nelements defaults to 1 and is only changed by the 'chem' keyword (:57 and :115-119). Contrast the correct pattern in src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:484-492 'for (int ielem = 0; ielem < nelements; ielem++) { h_radelem(ielem) = radelem[ielem]; ... }'. The identical code is in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:95-102.
failure_scenario: 'compute g all sna/grid/kk grid 10 10 10 4.0 0.99363 6 0.5 0.7 1.0 1.0' with 2 atom types and no 'chem' keyword: nelements==1, so h_radelem(1) and h_wjelem(1) write one element past a 1-element host allocation -> heap corruption (an immediate abort under KOKKOS_ENABLE_DEBUG_BOUNDS_CHECK).
suggested_fix: Size these views with atom->ntypes (matching the 1-based per-type arrays they mirror) and use consistent i-1 indexing for all four, or switch to genuinely per-element arrays as pair snap/kk does.

summary: The PreUi kernels look up 'type(iatom)' where iatom is a grid-point index, not an atom index, giving a wrong (or out-of-bounds) element for the central site.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:516-524 'const int iatom = iatom_mod + iatom_div * vector_length; if (iatom >= chunk_size) return; int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);' -- iatom indexes grid points in [0,chunk_size), and 'type' is atomKK->k_type (assigned at :190), whose extent is atom->nmax. The same kernel's ComputeNeigh counterpart hard-codes the grid-point type: :429-431 'const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = d_map[itype];', matching the CPU style src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:233-236. Same code in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h (TagCSNAGridLocalPreUi overloads).
failure_scenario: A 500-atom system with a 32x32x32 local grid gives chunk_size = 32768 >> atom->nmax, so type(iatom) reads far past the type array and d_map[itype] is then indexed with arbitrary garbage -> CUDA 'an illegal memory access was encountered' or silently wrong ielem; with 'chem' enabled the central element is wrong even when in bounds.
suggested_fix: Use the grid-point element consistently: 'const int ielem = chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0;' in all three TagCSNAGridPreUi overloads.

summary: max_neighs is hard-coded to 100 and the ComputeNeigh kernel writes snaKK.rij/wj/rcutij/inside at an unbounded offset, so a grid point with more than 100 atoms inside the cutoff overruns the SNA neighbour arrays.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:195-196 '// max_neighs is defined here - think of more elaborate methods.\n  max_neighs = 100;' then :209 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, max_neighs, padding_factor);' while the neighbour loop at :458-487 does 'if (rsq < rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype) && rsq > 1e-20) { snaKK.rij(ii,offset,0) = ...; ... offset++; }' with no 'offset < max_neighs' guard. The CPU style sizes the buffers for every atom: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:220 'snaptr->grow_rij(ntotal);'. Same in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h.
failure_scenario: Any realistic SNAP cutoff (rcutfac*2*radelem ~ 5 A) around a grid point in a dense system holds several hundred atoms; offsets >= 100 write outside snaKK.rij -> device heap corruption, and even without the overrun ComputeCayleyKlein/ComputeUi only iterate jnbor < max_neighs so neighbours past 100 are dropped and the bispectrum is wrong.
suggested_fix: Compute the true maximum neighbour count per chunk (a parallel_reduce over d_ninside, as pair snap/kk does with its neighbour list) and call grow_rij with it, or at minimum clamp 'offset' and raise an error when ninside > max_neighs.

summary: k_cutsq is filled with cutsq[1][1] for every type pair, so multi-type systems use the type-1 cutoff for all neighbours instead of the per-type cutoff the CPU style uses.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:66-73 'cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1];\n  for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= atom->ntypes; j++){ k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cutsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutsq_tmp; ... } }' and the kernel test at :446 'if (rsq >= rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype) || rsq < 1e-20)' with itype fixed at 1. The CPU style selects neighbours with the j-type cutoff: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:258 'if (rsq < cutsq[jtype][jtype] && rsq > 1e-20)', where cutsq[i][i] = (2*radelem[i]*rcutfac)^2 (:79-87). Same in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:65-72.
failure_scenario: A two-type SNAP descriptor with radelem 0.5 and 1.0: the /kk grid compute includes/excludes type-2 neighbours using the type-1 cutoff, producing bispectrum components that differ from 'compute sna/grid' on the same configuration.
suggested_fix: Copy the real cutsq matrix into k_cutsq ('k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = cutsq[i][j]') and test against rnd_cutsq(jtype,jtype) to match the CPU selection rule.

summary: The ComputeNeigh kernel omits the compute-group filter, so grid descriptors include atoms outside the compute's group.
failure_scenario: 'compute g sub sna/grid/kk grid ...' on a subgroup returns the same descriptors as a whole-system compute, silently including atoms the user excluded.
suggested_fix: Sync MASK_MASK, keep a mask view, and 'continue' on '!(mask(j) & groupbit)' in both neighbour loops.

summary: The host_flag fallback calls ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(), which does not exist in that class and resolves to the empty Compute::compute_array(), so compute sna/grid/local/kk computes nothing at all on host-only KOKKOS builds.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:159-162 'if (host_flag) { ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_array(); return; }'. ComputeSNAGridLocal declares only 'void compute_local() override;' (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.h:32) and its base ComputeGridLocal declares 'void compute_local() override = 0;' (src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.h:26); neither declares compute_array(), so the call binds to 'virtual void compute_array() {}' in src/compute.h:129. The sibling GPU-capable style calls the correct method (src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h host branch calls ComputeSNAGrid::compute_array(), which does exist).
failure_scenario: Any KOKKOS build without a GPU backend (LMPDeviceType == LMPHostType, so host_flag==1), or the /kk/host variant on a GPU build: 'compute c sna/grid/local/kk grid ...' + 'dump local' outputs the raw contents of the freshly malloc'd alocal array (uninitialized garbage, including the ix/iy/iz/x/y/z columns) instead of bispectrum components. No error is issued.
suggested_fix: Call ComputeSNAGridLocal::compute_local() in the host_flag branch.

summary: The ComputeNeigh kernel drops the compute-group filter, so every grid descriptor includes atoms outside the compute's group.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:438-452 and :458-487 loop 'for (int j = 0; j < ntotal; j++)' with no mask/groupbit test; the class never reads atom->mask (datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK at :54). The CPU original src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:244-246 has 'if (!(mask[j] & groupbit)) continue;' inside the identical loop.
failure_scenario: 'group solute type 2' + 'compute g solute sna/grid/local/kk grid 10 10 10 ...' -> the /kk result includes all atoms of every type, so the bispectrum components differ from the CPU style for every grid point.
suggested_fix: Add TYPE_MASK|MASK_MASK to datamask_read, capture 'mask = atomKK->k_mask.view<DeviceType>()' in compute_local(), and skip j when '!(mask(j) & groupbit)' in both loops.

summary: k_cutsq is filled with cutsq[1][1] for every type pair, so multi-type systems use the type-1 cutoff for all neighbours instead of the per-type cutoff the CPU style uses.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:65-72: 'cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1]; for (i..ntypes) for (j..ntypes) { k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cutsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutsq_tmp; ... }'. The base class builds a genuinely per-type table: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:80-88 'cut = 2.0*radelem[i]*rcutfac; cutsq[i][i] = cut*cut; ... cutsq[i][j] = cutsq[j][i] = cut*cut;'. The kernel then also queries the wrong element of that table: :446/:466 use 'rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype)' with itype hard-wired to 1 (:429), whereas the CPU uses 'cutsq[jtype][jtype]' (compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:255).
