failure_scenario: Two atom types with different radelem (e.g. radelem 0.5 1.0): all neighbours are cut off at (2*radelem[1]*rcutfac)^2, so type-2 atoms that should be inside the cutoff are dropped (or spurious ones included) and the descriptors are wrong.
suggested_fix: Copy the real cutsq[i][j] table into k_cutsq and index it as rnd_cutsq(jtype,jtype) to match the CPU style.

summary: max_neighs is hard-coded to 100 while the ComputeNeigh kernel writes snaKK.rij/wj/rcutij/inside at an unbounded offset, so a grid point with more than 100 atoms inside the cutoff overruns the SNA neighbour arrays.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:176-177 '// max_neighs is defined here - think of more elaborate methods.  max_neighs = 100;' then :191 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, max_neighs, padding_factor);'. The kernel at :457-486 loops over all ntotal atoms and does 'snaKK.rij(ii,offset,0) = ...; ... offset++;' with no check against max_neighs. The CPU style sizes the arrays for the worst case: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:218 'snaptr->grow_rij(ntotal);'.
failure_scenario: A dense system or a large rcutfac where any grid point has >100 atoms within the cutoff: out-of-bounds device writes -> silent corruption of the SNA views or an illegal-memory-access abort.
suggested_fix: Compute the true maximum neighbour count per grid point (a first counting pass already exists at :438-452; reduce d_ninside to its max) and call grow_rij with that value, or bound offset by max_neighs and error out.

summary: The PreUi kernels look up 'type(iatom)' where iatom is a grid-point index, not an atom index, giving a wrong (or out-of-bounds) element for the central site.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:516-524, :529-536 and :541-549 all do 'int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);' where iatom ranges over [0,chunk_size) grid points. The ComputeNeigh kernel in the same file states the correct convention at :429-431: 'const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = d_map[itype];', matching src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:233-235. type() is also read unconditionally, while d_map is only filled when chemflag is set (:105-109, :117-119).
failure_scenario: Any run: for grid point ii the central element becomes map[type[ii]] instead of map[1]; with chemflag off d_map is uninitialized device memory, so pre_ui writes the self-term into a random element slot. When chunk_size > nlocal+nghost, type(iatom) is an out-of-bounds read.
suggested_fix: Replace the body with the ComputeNeigh convention: 'const int ielem = chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0;'.

summary: d_radelem/d_wjelem/d_sinnerelem/d_dinnerelem are allocated with 'nelements' entries but the constructor fills 'ntypes' of them, and sinner/dinner are written at index i instead of i-1, so any run with more atom types than SNAP elements writes past the end of the host mirrors.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:75-78 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_radelem,...,nelements); ... d_wjelem ... d_sinnerelem ... d_dinnerelem' (nelements defaults to 1, src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:58) versus :95-102 'for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { h_radelem(i-1) = radelem[i]; h_wjelem(i-1) = wjelem[i]; if (switchinnerflag) { h_sinnerelem(i) = sinnerelem[i]; h_dinnerelem(i) = dinnerelem[i]; } }'. Note the inconsistent offset: radelem/wjelem use i-1 but sinnerelem/dinnerelem use i, so even with ntypes == nelements == 1 the sinner/dinner write is one past the end.
failure_scenario: 'compute c all sna/grid/local/kk grid ... switchinnerflag 1 sinner 1.0 dinner 0.5' with a single type: h_sinnerelem(1) is written into a length-1 view -> heap overflow; with 2 types and no chem keyword (nelements==1) radelem/wjelem overflow as well.
suggested_fix: Size the four views with atom->ntypes (or ntypes+1) and use a single consistent offset (i-1) for all four.

summary: setup() calls ComputeGridLocal::setup() (which allocates alocal with plain memory->create) and then overwrites the alocal pointer with a memoryKK allocation, leaking the first array and leaving gridlocal_allocated=1 so the next setup()'s deallocate() calls memory->destroy() on a Kokkos-backed pointer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:108-113 'ComputeGridLocal::setup();\n  // allocate arrays\n  memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_alocal, alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, "grid:alocal");'. ComputeGridLocal::setup() (src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.cpp:70-77) calls deallocate(), allocate() -- which sets gridlocal_allocated = 1 and 'memory->create(alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, ...)' (:110-114) -- and assign_coords(). memoryKK->create_kokkos for a value_type** only smallocs the row-pointer array and points array[i] at &data.view_host()(i,0) (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:103-121), while ComputeGridLocal::deallocate() (:121-130) does 'memory->destroy(alocal)' whose T** overload is 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);' (src/memory.h:208-214). Modify::setup() calls compute[i]->setup() on every run (src/modify.cpp:301). Note the disabled '//gridlocal_allocated = 0;' left in the KOKKOS destructor at :98. The identical pattern is in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:146-149, while compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:152 deliberately avoids calling the base setup for exactly this reason.
failure_scenario: An input with two 'run' commands: the first run leaks the base-class alocal; at the start of the second run deallocate() calls free() on &k_alocal.view_host()(0,0), which is not a malloc base pointer -> glibc 'invalid pointer' abort or heap corruption.
suggested_fix: Follow compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h: call ComputeGridLocal::set_grid_global()/set_grid_local() instead of ComputeGridLocal::setup(), do the memoryKK allocation, and fill columns 0-5 yourself; or override allocate()/deallocate() (making them virtual in the base) so only the Kokkos allocation ever exists.

summary: setup() calls ComputeGridLocal::setup() (which memory->create()s alocal and sets gridlocal_allocated=1) and then overwrites the alocal pointer with a Kokkos allocation, leaking the first array and making the next setup()'s deallocate() call free() on the interior of a Kokkos view.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:143-152: 'ComputeGridLocal::setup(); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_alocal, alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, "grid:alocal"); array_local = alocal;'. src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid_local.cpp:70-77 setup() -> allocate(); allocate() at :108-115 does 'gridlocal_allocated = 1; memory->create(alocal, size_local_rows, size_local_cols, ...)'. deallocate() at :121-130 does 'if (gridlocal_allocated) { gridlocal_allocated = 0; memory->destroy(alocal); }', and Memory::destroy(TYPE **&array) at src/memory.h:208-214 performs 'sfree(array[0]); sfree(array);' - array[0] then points into the Kokkos View host data allocated by MemoryKokkos::create_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:200-217). Compare compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:145-150 which deliberately does NOT call ComputeGrid::setup() but only set_grid_global()/set_grid_local(). The same defect exists in src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:111.
failure_scenario: A second 'run' command (modify->setup() calls compute[i]->setup() every run, src/modify.cpp:301): deallocate() calls free() on a pointer into a Kokkos allocation -> heap corruption / abort. Even a single run leaks size_local_rows*size_local_cols doubles.
suggested_fix: Mirror compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h: call only ComputeGridLocal::set_grid_global()/set_grid_local(), then destroy the previous k_alocal before create_kokkos(); leave gridlocal_allocated at 0.

summary: restore_bias_all_kk() calls the internal temperature compute's host-syncing restore_bias_all() instead of restore_bias_all_kk(), forcing a full device-to-host copy of the velocities on every call.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:148-159 'void ComputeTempDeformKokkos<DeviceType>::restore_bias_all_kk() { if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->restore_bias_all(); ...' versus the matching remove path at :123-134 'void ComputeTempDeformKokkos<DeviceType>::remove_bias_all_kk() { remove_deform_bias_all_kk(); if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->remove_bias_all_kk();'. The _kk-suffixed variants exist precisely to skip the host round trip: e.g. src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_partial_kokkos.cpp:213-217 'void ComputeTempPartialKokkos<DeviceType>::restore_bias_all() { restore_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK); }'.
failure_scenario: 'fix nvt/sllod/kk' with a biased internal temperature compute (src/KOKKOS/fix_nvt_sllod_kokkos.cpp:221 and src/KOKKOS/fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:558,716 drive these paths every timestep): each timestep pays an extra full v device->host transfer. Results are still correct.
suggested_fix: Call temperature->restore_bias_all_kk() in the kokkosable branch, mirroring remove_bias_all_kk().

summary: The /kk variant ignores atom->superellipsoid_flag and always derives the principal moments from bonus.shape, whereas the CPU style uses the pre-computed bonus_super inertia for superellipsoid particles; no guard rejects the unsupported case.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_erotate_asphere_kokkos.cpp:151-158 'auto shape = l_bonus(l_ellipsoid(i)).shape; ... inertia[0] = rmass*(shape[1]^2+shape[2]^2)/5.0' with no superellipsoid test, vs src/compute_erotate_asphere.cpp:114-127 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) { quat = ebonus_super[...].quat; inertia[0] = ebonus_super[...].inertia[0]; ... } else { ...shape based... }'. The sibling KOKKOS style guards explicitly: src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_asphere_noforce_kokkos.cpp:63-64 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot (yet) use superellipsoid particles with ...")'.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid superellipsoid' + 'compute e all erotate/asphere/kk' silently reports a rotational energy computed from an ellipsoid inertia formula (and from a bonus array the KOKKOS ellipsoid atom vec does not populate for superellipsoids) instead of the stored superellipsoid inertia.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (atom->superellipsoid_flag) error->all(FLERR,...)' to ComputeERotateAsphereKokkos::init(), mirroring fix_nve_asphere_noforce_kokkos.cpp:63.

summary: setup() allocates grid, gridall and gridlocal on every call without first deallocating, leaking the whole global grid on each run command.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:150-169 deliberately skips ComputeGrid::setup() (which begins with deallocate(), src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid.cpp:67-73) and then unconditionally does 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_grid, grid, ...); memory->create(gridall, ...); if (...) { gridlocal_allocated = 1; memory->create4d_offset(gridlocal, ...); }'. Modify::setup() calls compute[i]->setup() at the start of every run (src/modify.cpp:301), and Memory::create simply overwrites the pointer.
failure_scenario: A script with N 'run' commands leaks N-1 copies of grid + gridall (2 * nx*ny*nz * size_array_cols doubles) plus gridlocal; a 100x100x100 grid with 60 columns leaks ~1 GB per extra run.
suggested_fix: Call ComputeGrid::deallocate() (or free grid/gridall/gridlocal explicitly) at the top of the KOKKOS setup() before re-creating them.

summary: Neighbour weights, cutoffs and inner-cutoff parameters are looked up by element index while the CPU style looks them up by atom type, so they differ whenever the type-to-element map is not the identity (including every non-chem multi-type run).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:467-479 'int jelem = 0; if (chemflag) jelem = d_map[jtype]; ... snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jelem]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = (2.0*d_radelem[jelem])*rcutfac; ... snaKK.sinnerij(ii,offset) = 0.5*(d_sinnerelem[ielem] + d_sinnerelem[jelem]);' vs src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:263-267 'snaptr->wj[ninside] = wjelem[jtype]; snaptr->rcutij[ninside] = 2.0 * radelem[jtype] * rcutfac; if (switchinnerflag) { snaptr->sinnerij[ninside] = sinnerelem[jelem]; snaptr->dinnerij[ninside] = dinnerelem[jelem]; }'. With chemflag off jelem is always 0, so every neighbour gets wjelem[1] and radelem[1]. The in-source comment at :472-473 records the uncertainty.
failure_scenario: Two atom types with radelem 0.5/1.0 and wjelem 1.0/0.96 and no 'chem' keyword: the /kk grid compute weights every neighbour as type 1, so its bispectrum differs from 'compute sna/grid'.
suggested_fix: Index d_wjelem/d_radelem by jtype (after sizing those views by ntypes, see the allocation finding) and use sinnerelem[jelem] without the 0.5 average, exactly as the CPU loop does.

summary: Neighbour weights and cutoff radii are looked up by element index while the CPU style looks them up by atom type, so they differ whenever the type-to-element map is not the identity.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:467-475 'int jelem = 0; if (chemflag) jelem = d_map[jtype]; ... snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jelem]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = (2.0*d_radelem[jelem])*rcutfac;'. The CPU original uses the type: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:260-261 'snaptr->wj[ninside] = wjelem[jtype]; snaptr->rcutij[ninside] = 2.0 * radelem[jtype] * rcutfac;'. Combined with the i-1 shift at :96-97, even the identity case is off by one relative to the CPU indexing.
failure_scenario: 'chem 2 0 1 1' with three types: types 2 and 3 both map to element 1 and get element 1's weight/radius, while the CPU style gives each type its own wjelem/radelem -> different descriptors.
suggested_fix: Index d_wjelem/d_radelem by jtype (with the same offset used when filling them) as the CPU style does.

summary: remove_deform_bias_all_kk() converts coordinates with DomainKokkos::x2lamda(), which always runs on the device and marks only the device copy modified, while the bias kernel of the LMPHostType instantiation reads the host x view - so 'compute temp/deform/kk/host' on a GPU build computes the bias from Cartesian instead of lamda coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:175-197: 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK|V_MASK|MASK_MASK); ... x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>(); ... domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType, TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias>(0,nlocal),*this); ... domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal);' with no sync between x2lamda and the kernel. src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp x2lamda(int n) is hard-wired to the device: 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view_device(); Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<LMPDeviceType, TagDomain_x2lamda>(0,n),*this); atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK);' (detached_atom_x() is 0 in normal runs, src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:344-347). The style is instantiated for the host too: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.h:18 'ComputeStyle(temp/deform/kk/host,ComputeTempDeformKokkos<LMPHostType>);' and src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:308. The CPU original computes lamda in a local temporary instead: src/compute_temp_deform.cpp:311-321 'domain->x2lamda(atom->x[i], lamda); vbiasall[i][0] = h_rate[0]*lamda[0] + ...'.
failure_scenario: GPU-enabled KOKKOS build + 'compute t all temp/deform/kk/host' (or fix nvt/sllod/kk whose temperature compute is a host-space temp/deform): the kernel at :205-207 uses x in box units (e.g. 0..Lx) where lamda units (0..1) are expected, so the removed streaming velocity is off by a factor of the box length and the reported temperature is wrong.
suggested_fix: After domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal), re-sync and re-fetch the view for the compute's execution space ('atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();'), or compute the lamda transform inline in the kernel from domain->h_inv/boxlo as the CPU style does.

summary: Corrupted GPL license header text: 'the GNU Gdirectoryeneral Public License.'
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_composition_atom_kokkos.cpp:9 '   the GNU Gdirectoryeneral Public License.' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_composition_atom.cpp:9 '   the GNU General Public License.'
failure_scenario: No runtime effect, but the shipped source carries a mangled license notice.
suggested_fix: Restore the standard header line 'the GNU General Public License.'

summary: Local variable 'size_peratom_cols' shadows the Compute base-class member of the same name inside compute_peratom().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_composition_atom_kokkos.cpp:141 'int size_peratom_cols = 1 + atom->ntypes;' shadows Compute::size_peratom_cols, which the base sets in src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_composition_atom.cpp:60 'size_peratom_cols = 1 + ntypes;'; the device kernel at line 226 uses the member, the allocation at line 145 uses the local.
failure_scenario: Harmless today because both hold 1+atom->ntypes, but any future divergence between the two silently allocates a result array of one width and iterates it with another.
suggested_fix: Delete the local declaration and use the inherited member; likewise drop 'int count = 1.0;' (line 197) in favour of 'int count = 1;'.

summary: Device kernel calls the C library exp() instead of Kokkos::exp(), against the KOKKOS package rule on device math functions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:283 'd_alocal(igrid, icol) += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_prefacelem(jtype-1) * exp(-rsq * d_argfacelem(jtype-1)));' inside a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION; .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos::exp in device kernels (compare src/KOKKOS/compute_entropy_atom_kokkos.cpp:300 'Kokkos::exp(...)').
failure_scenario: Compiles today only because ::exp resolves to a CUDA/HIP builtin; it breaks on backends where only the Kokkos wrapper is device-callable.
suggested_fix: Use Kokkos::exp().

summary: d_map is filled by deep-copying an uninitialized host mirror, and d_ninside/max_neighs/inum are allocated or set but never used.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:74 'auto h_map = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_map);' is never written (the loop at :76-81 fills only radelem/sigmaelem/prefacelem/argfacelem) yet :86 does 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_map,h_map);'; d_ninside is reallocated every call at :155 and never read; 'max_neighs = 100;' (:149) and the member 'inum' are dead.
failure_scenario: No wrong results today (d_map is never read), but the copy propagates uninitialized memory and MSan/valgrind will flag it.
suggested_fix: Delete d_map, d_ninside, max_neighs and inum, or initialize h_map before the deep_copy.

summary: Leftover debug scaffolding: an <iostream> include (forbidden by the project style), an unused d_test view, and a deep_copy of a partly uninitialized h_map.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:39 '#include <iostream>'; :81 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_test, "ComputeSNAGridKokkos::test", nelements);' with :92-93 'auto h_test = ...; h_test(0) = 2.0;' and :121 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_test,h_test);' -- d_test is never read; :90 'auto h_map = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_map);' leaves h_map(0) uninitialized before :119 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_map,h_map);'. Compare src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:74/86 for the same h_map issue.
failure_scenario: No wrong results, but <iostream> violates the LAMMPS I/O rules and the uninitialized copy trips memory sanitizers.
suggested_fix: Remove the iostream include and the d_test view; zero h_map (or skip the copy) when chemflag is off.

summary: compute_local() never sets invoked_local, unlike the CPU style and the sibling gaussian/grid/local/kk style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:156-172 has no 'invoked_local = update->ntimestep;'. The CPU original sets it first thing: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid_local.cpp:205-207. The sibling KOKKOS style does too: src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:134.
failure_scenario: Callers that guard on invoked_local (src/library.cpp:2799 lammps_extract_compute, src/REACTION/fix_bond_react.cpp:2413) re-run the whole grid computation on every access in the same timestep.
suggested_fix: Add 'invoked_local = update->ntimestep;' at the top of compute_local().

summary: Leftover debug scaffolding: an <iostream> include (against the project rule banning C++ iostreams), an unused d_test view, and dead grid-coordinate code in the Fill kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:38 '#include <iostream>'; :79-80 '// test\n MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_test, "ComputeSNAGridLocalKokkos::test", nelements);' with :91-92 and :120 filling/copying it, and d_test declared at compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.h:250 but never read; :711-742 in TagCSNAGridLocal2Fill recompute ix/iy/iz and xgrid[] (including the triclinic transform) but never use them, since ComputeNeigh already wrote columns 0-5 at :419-424; :723 leaves a commented-out printf.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers, but the iostream include violates the LAMMPS coding rule and the dead code costs a triclinic matrix-vector product per grid point.
suggested_fix: Delete the <iostream> include, the d_test view and its mirror, and the unused coordinate block in TagCSNAGridLocal2Fill.

summary: Per-atom scratch arrays d_distsq/d_nearest/d_pairs are allocated as full inum x maxneigh / inum x npairs device arrays, so memory grows as O(natoms*maxneigh) where the CPU style uses a single maxneigh-sized buffer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_centro_atom_kokkos.cpp:121-126 'd_distsq = typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d("centro/atom:distsq",inum,maxneigh_kk); d_nearest = ...(inum,maxneigh_kk); d_pairs = ...(inum,npairs)' vs src/compute_centro_atom.cpp:179-180 'memory->create(distsq, maxneigh, ...)' (one row total) and :155 'auto *pairs = new double[npairs];'
failure_scenario: 1e7 local atoms with maxneigh~200 requires ~2e9 KK_FLOAT + 2e9 int of extra device memory (>16 GB) and aborts with a Kokkos allocation failure, while the CPU style needs only a few kB.
suggested_fix: Use per-thread scratch (team scratch memory or a bounded chunked RangePolicy over batches of atoms) instead of a full inum-by-maxneigh global scratch array.

summary: Trapezoid-rule endpoint weighting differs from the CPU style when nbin == 1: the KOKKOS kernel halves the single bin once, the CPU style halves it twice (i.e. weights it 1.0).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_entropy_atom_kokkos.cpp:316-317 'if (k == 0 || k == nbin-1) value += 0.5*integrand; else value += integrand;' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_entropy_atom.cpp:269-273 'for (int k=1;k<nbin-1;++k) value += integrand[k]; value += 0.5*integrand[0]; value += 0.5*integrand[nbin-1];' -- for nbin==1 the CPU adds 0.5*integrand[0] twice, the KOKKOS branch adds it once.
failure_scenario: 'compute e all entropy/atom/kk 1.0 0.5' gives nbin = (int)(0.5/1.0)+1 = 1 and the /kk variant reports exactly half the pair entropy of the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU accumulation exactly (sum k=1..nbin-2 then add 0.5*integrand[0] and 0.5*integrand[nbin-1] separately), or reject nbin < 2 in init().

summary: Per-atom scratch d_distsq/d_nearest is allocated as a full inum x maxneigh device array instead of the single maxneigh-sized buffer used by the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_hexorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:181-184 'd_distsq = typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d("hexorder/atom:distsq",inum,maxneigh_kk); d_nearest = typename AT::t_int_2d(...,inum,maxneigh_kk);' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:182-183 'memory->create(distsq,maxneigh,...); memory->create(nearest,maxneigh,...);' (one row total). Same shape as src/KOKKOS/compute_centro_atom_kokkos.cpp:121-124.
failure_scenario: Large systems with dense neighbour lists need natoms*maxneigh extra device words and can exhaust GPU memory where the CPU style needs a few kB.
suggested_fix: Use team/thread scratch memory or process atoms in bounded chunks.

summary: The rmag <= MY_EPSILON early-out skips only the offending neighbour, whereas the CPU calc_boop returns from the whole atom, leaving all its order parameters at zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:465-468 'const KK_FLOAT rmag = Kokkos::sqrt(...); if (rmag <= MY_EPSILON) { return; }' inside calc_boop1, which handles a single (ii,ineigh) pair, vs src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp:430-432 'double rmag = sqrt(...); if (rmag <= MY_EPSILON) { return; }' inside the 'for (int ineigh...)' loop of calc_boop -- that return abandons the entire atom, and qn[] stays at the memset zeros.
failure_scenario: Two atoms at (numerically) identical coordinates: the CPU style reports Q_l = 0 for the central atom, the /kk style reports Q_l computed from the remaining neighbours.
suggested_fix: Decide which behaviour is intended and make both styles agree; if the CPU 'return' is itself the bug, fix it to 'continue' there rather than diverging silently.

summary: compute_local() advances through the packed buffer with 'j += 2*numbonds + 3' without the store_bonds guard used everywhere else, so the stride would be wrong if it ever ran with store_bonds false.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.cpp:225 'j += 2*numbonds + 3;' vs the same walk in compute_bonds() at :184 'j += (store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3;' and compute_peratom() at :249 'j += (store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3;'. The packer only emits the bond entries under STORE_BONDS (src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4319-4335).
failure_scenario: Currently unreachable because ComputeReaxFFAtom sets 'local_flag = store_bonds' (src/REAXFF/compute_reaxff_atom.cpp:82), but a direct compute_local() call (library/Python interface, or a future caller) with 'bonds no' walks off the packed layout and reads garbage or past the buffer.
suggested_fix: Use the same '(store_bonds ? 2*numbonds : 0) + 3' stride in compute_local(), or assert store_bonds at its entry.

summary: The KOKKOS bias removal round-trips every local atom's coordinates through x2lamda()/lamda2x(), perturbing atom->x by floating-point round-off, whereas the CPU style never modifies atom->x.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_deform_kokkos.cpp:186 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal);' and :195 'domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal);' bracket the bias kernel and operate on all nlocal atoms in place (both call atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK)). The CPU original writes the transformed coordinates to a stack temporary and leaves atom->x untouched: src/compute_temp_deform.cpp:307-321 'double lamda[3]; ... domain->x2lamda(atom->x[i], lamda);'.
failure_scenario: 'fix nvt/sllod' + 'compute temp/deform/kk': coordinates of every atom (including atoms outside the compute group) are rewritten as lamda2x(x2lamda(x)) on every invocation, so trajectories drift from the CPU reference and depend on how often the compute is invoked (thermo frequency).
suggested_fix: Pass domain->h_inv/boxlo (or h/h_rate directly in lamda form) into the kernel and compute the lamda coordinates locally instead of transforming atom->x in place.

summary: ComputeTempSphere::init() detects a temp/region bias with an exact strcmp on tbias->style, which no longer matches once the bias compute is promoted to 'temp/region/kk', so tempbias stays 1 and dof_compute() calls tbias->dof_remove(-1), reading atom->x[-1] out of bounds.
evidence: src/compute_temp_sphere.cpp:106-109 'if (strcmp(tbias->style, "temp/region") == 0) tempbias = 2; else tempbias = 1;'.  src/modify.cpp:1267-1272 rewrites the style string when a suffix is applied: 'std::string estyle = arg[2] + std::string("/") + lmp->non_pair_suffix(); ... compute[ncompute]->style = utils::strdup(estyle);' so the style is literally "temp/region/kk".  src/compute_temp_sphere.cpp:181-182 then takes the tempbias==1 branch: 'if (mode == ALL) dof -= tbias->dof_remove(-1) * natoms_temp;' and src/compute_temp_region.cpp:89-94 'int ComputeTempRegion::dof_remove(int i) { double *x = atom->x[i]; if (region->match(x[0], x[1], x[2])) return 0; return 1; }' dereferences atom->x[-1].  The new src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_region_kokkos.h:16-18 registers temp/region/kk, making this reachable for the first time (there is no /omp or /gpu temp/region).  The identical strcmp appears in ASPHERE/compute_temp_asphere.cpp:122 and BODY/compute_temp_body.cpp:113.
failure_scenario: lmp -sf kk with 'compute b all temp/region myreg' and 'compute t all temp/sphere bias b': the bias compute becomes temp/region/kk, tempbias is set to 1 instead of 2, dof_compute() calls dof_remove(-1) which indexes atom->x[-1] (garbage pointer -> segfault or nonsense), and the per-atom region DOF subtraction is silently skipped so the reported temperature is wrong.
suggested_fix: Compare utils::strip_style_suffix(tbias->style, lmp) with "temp/region" in compute_temp_sphere.cpp (and the same lines in compute_temp_asphere.cpp / compute_temp_body.cpp); optionally also guard dof_remove(-1) in ComputeTempRegion.

summary: In the host/device force-overlap path the forces a non-KOKKOS (legacy Host) force style writes into atom->f are never transferred into the Kokkos host buffer before the merge, so on builds where k_f needs a transform view they are silently dropped.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:421-424 sets 'datamask_exclude = (F_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK)' whenever overlap_possible(), and 438/441 (and 467/470, 502/505) then use only the masked forms '~(~datamask_read|datamask_exclude)', so F_MASK is never passed to atomKK->modified() after the style ran.  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_atomic_kokkos.cpp:210-213 shows modified(Host, mask) only calls 'k_f.modify_host()' when the mask contains F_MASK, so TransformView::modified_legacy_hostkk stays 0.  The merge at verlet_kokkos.cpp:513-514 is 'atomKK->k_f.sync_legacy_to_hostkk(); Kokkos::deep_copy(LMPHostType(),f_merge_copy,atomKK->k_f.view_hostkk());' and src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:955-968 makes sync_legacy_to_hostkk() a no-op unless modified_legacy_hostkk is set.  A non-KOKKOS style has execution_space == Host (src/pair.cpp:128, src/kspace.cpp:98, src/bond.cpp:62) and writes atom->f, which memory_kokkos.h:119 aliases to k_f.view_host() (the legacy view), a different allocation from view_hostkk() whenever TransformView::NEED_TRANSFORM is true (kokkos_type.h:700) -- i.e. single-precision builds (KK_ACC_FLOAT=float, kokkos_type.h:401-402) or LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_DEFAULT builds.  host_force_styles() (verlet_kokkos.cpp:699) deliberately accepts Host as well as HostKK, so the path is taken for such styles.  Contrast the sibling DynamicalMatrixKokkos::update_force (src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:287), which merges from k_f.view_host() (the legacy view) instead.
failure_scenario: GPU backend, single-precision KOKKOS build (or LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_DEFAULT), '-sf kk' with any force style that has no /kk variant (e.g. a non-KOKKOS kspace such as pppm/cg, or an unported pair/bond style): that style's entire force contribution is added to a buffer nobody reads, the merge adds zeros, and the trajectory is silently wrong. In the non-overlap (CPU-only) path datamask_exclude is 0 and F_MASK is claimed normally, which is why CI does not see it.
suggested_fix: Claim the legacy write before the merge (e.g. call atomKK->k_f.modify_legacy_hostkk() in the execute_on_host block when any host force style has execution_space == Host), or merge from k_f.view_host() as DynamicalMatrixKokkos does; note that when both a Host and a HostKK style contributed the two buffers must be added, not deep-copied over each other.

summary: alpha_step() and the x0 snapshot treat xvec as a flat 3*nlocal alias of atom->x, which is only valid for LayoutRight; unlike every other loop in the min/kk styles these three kernels have no F_LAYOUTRIGHT branch, so a KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default GPU build moves the wrong coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:108-109 'if (nvec) xvec = DAT::t_kkfloat_1d(d_x.data(),nvec); if (nvec) fvec = DAT::t_kkacc_1d(d_f.data(),nvec);' aliases the (nmax,3) view k_x as a flat length-3*nlocal view.  The three loops that use it are unguarded: :252-254 'Kokkos::parallel_for(nvec, LAMMPS_LAMBDA(const int& i) { l_x0[i] = l_xvec[i]; });', :391-393 'l_xvec[i] = l_x0[i];' and :410-412 'l_xvec[i] += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(alpha)*l_h[i];'.  Everywhere else the same file and its subclasses do branch, precisely because the flat alias is layout-dependent: min_kokkos.h:27 'static constexpr int F_LAYOUTRIGHT = std::is_same<LMPDeviceLayout,Kokkos::LayoutRight>::value;', min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:191-204 and :286-304, min_cg_kokkos.cpp:68-86, :125-143 and :178-196, min_kokkos.cpp:624-636/661-673/698-711.  src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:177-185 defines LMPDeviceLayout as Kokkos::LayoutRight only for LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_LEGACY; with '-D KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default' (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:33-40) it becomes LMPDeviceType::array_layout, i.e. Kokkos::LayoutLeft on CUDA/HIP.  Under LayoutLeft the flat view of length 3*nlocal covers x(0..3*nlocal-1, 0) -- the x-components of the first 3*nlocal atoms including ghosts -- not (x,y,z) of the first nlocal atoms.
failure_scenario: cmake -D KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default with a CUDA/HIP backend and 'min_style cg/kk': the line search snapshots and restores only x-components (of owned and ghost atoms) and adds alpha*h into those slots, so y and z are never stepped and ghost x-coordinates are corrupted. The minimization silently converges to garbage; with LAYOUT=legacy (the default) the code is correct, which is why CI does not see it.
suggested_fix: Give these three loops the same 'if constexpr (F_LAYOUTRIGHT) ... else' treatment as the fvec loops, indexing atomKK->k_x.view_device()(i,0..2) with j = 3*i in the LayoutLeft branch; do the same for the xvec loops in min_quickmin_kokkos/min_fire_kokkos, or reject KOKKOS_LAYOUT=default in MinKokkos::init().

summary: compute_scalar()/compute_vector() always call the host-facing tbias->remove_bias_all()/restore_bias_all() instead of the kokkosable-guarded *_kk() variants, forcing a device->host->device round trip of v on every invocation even when the bias compute is a KOKKOS style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp:52-58 and 79-84 (and 126-132, 153-158): 'atomKK->sync(tbias->execution_space, tbias->datamask_read); tbias->remove_bias_all(); atomKK->modified(...); atomKK->sync(execution_space, V_MASK);'.  For a kk bias, e.g. src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_ramp_kokkos.cpp:167-171, remove_bias_all() is 'remove_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK);' -- an unconditional full copy of v to the host.  Every other KOKKOS caller uses the guarded form, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:136 'if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->remove_bias_all_kk();' and fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:558, fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:212/371, fix_nvt_sllod_kokkos.cpp:353.
failure_scenario: compute temp/sphere/kk with 'bias' pointing at a temp/ramp/kk or temp/region/kk compute on a GPU build: every thermo evaluation copies the full v array device->host and back, which is exactly the per-step transfer the KOKKOS package policy forbids. Results are still correct, only slow.
suggested_fix: Follow the package pattern: 'if (tbias->kokkosable) tbias->remove_bias_all_kk(); else { atomKK->sync(tbias->execution_space, tbias->datamask_read); tbias->remove_bias_all(); atomKK->modified(...); }' and likewise for restore.

summary: s_KK_double2, the reduction type used for every force dot product in the KOKKOS minimizers, stores its two accumulators as KK_FLOAT, which is 'float' in single- and mixed-precision builds, so the global sums lose precision even when the forces themselves are double.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.h:22-23 'struct s_KK_double2 { KK_FLOAT d0, d1;'.  src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:400-409 'typedef float KK_FLOAT; typedef float KK_ACC_FLOAT;' for LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE and 'typedef float KK_FLOAT; typedef double KK_ACC_FLOAT;' for the mixed setting LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE.  It is used as the parallel_reduce value type over all local degrees of freedom in src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:288-303 (fh in linemin_quadratic), :444-459 (compute_dir_deriv) and src/KOKKOS/min_cg_kokkos.cpp:127-143 (the CG force tolerance and Polak-Ribiere beta), e.g. 'sdot.d0 += static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(l_fvec[i]*l_fvec[i]);' where l_fvec is KK_ACC_FLOAT.  Every other reduction in the same files deliberately accumulates in double: min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:193-195 'LAMMPS_LAMBDA(const int& i, double& fdothme)', :228-230, min_cg_kokkos.cpp:214-216, and min_kokkos.cpp:626-635/663-672/700-710.
failure_scenario: A mixed-precision KOKKOS build (the recommended GPU setting) with min_style cg/kk on a few hundred thousand atoms: dotall[0] and dotall[1] are float sums of ~10^6 terms, so beta = MAX(0.0,(dotall[0]-dotall[1])/gg) and the ftol test lose roughly all digits past 1e-7 relative, degrading or stalling convergence, while the same run in double precision converges.
suggested_fix: Declare d0 and d1 as double (the struct is already named double2) so the reduction accumulates in double regardless of the KK_FLOAT setting.

summary: The per-iteration force dot products of cg/kk, sd/kk and the line-search backtracking loop read the device force view without syncing it, and MinKokkos::energy_force() only pushes host-computed forces to the device when force->newton is set or a min_post_force fix exists.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_kokkos.cpp:524-528 'if (force->newton) { comm->reverse_comm(); timer->stamp(Timer::COMM); atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK); }' and :538-543 'if (modify->n_min_post_force) { ... modify->min_post_force(vflag); atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK); ... }' are the only places energy_force() brings f to the device.  A force style without a /kk variant has execution_space == Host (src/pair.cpp:128) and datamask_modify == ALL_MASK (pair.cpp), so min_kokkos.cpp:469 'atomKK->modified(force->pair->execution_space,force->pair->datamask_modify);' leaves the newest f on the host only.  The consumers then read the device view with no sync: src/KOKKOS/min_cg_kokkos.cpp:125-143 (dotall[0]/dotall[1] -> the ftol test and the Polak-Ribiere beta), src/KOKKOS/min_sd_kokkos.cpp:51-64 (set_search_direction, called at :126 after linemin), and src/KOKKOS/min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:286-304 (the fh reduce inside the backtracking while loop).  The omission is inconsistent inside the same files: min_linesearch_kokkos.cpp:180 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK|F_MASK);' before the loop and :432 'atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK);' in compute_dir_deriv do sync, and the damped-dynamics styles resync every iteration (min_quickmin_kokkos.cpp:116, min_fire_kokkos.cpp:143).
failure_scenario: 'newton off' plus '-sf kk' with a force style that has no KOKKOS version (so f is computed on the host and never reverse-communicated): min_style cg/kk computes beta and the TWO-norm ftol test from a stale device force array, while fnorm_max()/fnorm_sqr() called two lines later do sync and see the correct forces -- the search direction is wrong and the run converges to the wrong configuration or stalls.
suggested_fix: Add atomKK->sync(Device,F_MASK) immediately before the reduce in MinCGKokkos::iterate and MinSDKokkos::set_search_direction and inside the backtracking loop of linemin_quadratic, or make MinKokkos::energy_force() sync F_MASK to the device unconditionally at its end.

summary: The class re-declares 'class AtomKokkos *atomKK;' as a private member, shadowing Pointers::atomKK (a reference bound to lmp->atomKK), unlike every other KOKKOS style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.h:81-82 ' private:\n  class AtomKokkos *atomKK;'.  src/pointers.h:131 declares 'class AtomKokkos *&atomKK;' bound to lmp->atomKK (pointers.h:92).  The constructor's 'atomKK = (AtomKokkos *) atom;' (compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp:36) therefore writes the shadowing member instead of lmp->atomKK.  No other file in src/KOKKOS declares an atomKK member (grep 'AtomKokkos \*atomKK' src/KOKKOS/*.h returns only this one).
failure_scenario: Harmless today because atom and lmp->atomKK are the same object, but the member is uninitialized until the derived constructor body runs and any future base-class code path that runs before it (or that reads Pointers::atomKK) sees a different pointer than this class uses.
suggested_fix: Delete the member declaration and use the inherited Pointers::atomKK like the rest of the package.

summary: VerletKokkos::operator()(const int&) and the 'f' view member are dead code -- the force merge uses the free ForceAdder functor, and nothing ever launches a kernel with *this.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.h:41-49 declares 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator() (const int& i) const {f(i,0) += f_merge_copy(i,0); ...}' and 'DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3 f_merge_copy,f;'.  The only merge in the .cpp is verlet_kokkos.cpp:515-516 'Kokkos::parallel_for(atomKK->k_f.extent(0), ForceAdder<DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3,DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3>(atomKK->k_f.view_device(),f_merge_copy));' using the file-static ForceAdder (verlet_kokkos.cpp:36-48); 'f' is only ever assigned (verlet_kokkos.cpp:512 'f = atomKK->k_f.view_device();') and never read.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; the member keeps a reference to the force view alive and the unused operator() invites confusion about which functor the merge uses.
suggested_fix: Remove the operator() and the 'f' member (and the assignment at verlet_kokkos.cpp:512), keeping only f_merge_copy.

summary: NBinKokkos::c_bincount is declared const and is never initialized (so it is permanently an empty view and makes the class non-copy-assignable), and c_bins is assigned only on a regrow and never read.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_kokkos.h:51 'const typename AT::t_int_1d_const c_bincount;' and :53 'typename AT::t_int_2d_const c_bins;'.  c_bins is written once at src/KOKKOS/nbin_kokkos.cpp:157 'c_bins = bins;' and neither member is read anywhere: the consumers use their own copies, see src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:220-222 and :316 'bincount(_bincount),c_bincount(_bincount),bins(_bins),c_bins(_bins),' fed from src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:104-105 'k_bincount = nbKK->k_bincount; k_bins = nbKK->k_bins;'.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect today; the const member silently deletes NBinKokkos's copy-assignment operator, so any future code that assigns one of these objects fails to compile for a non-obvious reason.
suggested_fix: Delete both members (or, if they are meant to be used, drop the const qualifier and assign them wherever bins/bincount are refreshed, including NBinKokkos::bin_atoms_setup).

summary: The pass that measures the maximum bin occupancy increments k_bincount without zeroing it first, so it counts the previous neighbor build's occupancy on top of the current one and over-allocates the bins array by about a factor of two.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:142-148 'atoms_per_bin = 0; copymode = 1; NPairSSAKokkosBinIDAtomsFunctor<DeviceType> f(*this); Kokkos::parallel_reduce(nlocal, f, atoms_per_bin);' and the kernel at :279-280 'const int ac = Kokkos::atomic_fetch_add(&(bincount[ibin]), (int)1); if (update <= ac) update = ac + 1;'.  Nothing zeroes bincount before this: bin_atoms_setup() (:61-91) only reallocates k_bincount when mbins grows past k_bins.view_host().extent(0) (:63-69), and the only zeroing is the MemsetZeroFunctor at :205-207, which runs AFTER the reduce, right before the real binning pass at :212-215.  bincount is therefore left holding the previous build's final per-bin counts.  Contrast the ghost counting pass at :157-166, which does zero its counter first ('for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) k_gbincount.view_host()(i) = 0; k_gbincount.modify_host(); k_gbincount.sync<DeviceType>();').  The CPU sibling src/DPD-REACT/nbin_ssa.cpp:63-65 likewise clears binhead[] before every build.
failure_scenario: Any run using neigh_modify binsize / pair_style dpd with nbin ssa/kk: from the second neighbor build on, atoms_per_bin reported by the reduce is about 2*max_bin_occupancy, and src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:200-204 allocates k_bins as (mbins, atoms_per_bin), i.e. roughly double the memory it needs. Results stay correct because binAtomsItem() re-counts from a zeroed bincount.
suggested_fix: Run the MemsetZeroFunctor (or Kokkos::deep_copy(bincount,0)) on k_bincount before the binIDAtomsItem reduce as well, mirroring the k_gbincount reset used for the ghost pass.

summary: NBinSSAKokkos allocates and initializes d_resize/h_resize and declares c_binID/c_bins/c_gbins, none of which are ever read by anything.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.h:48 'typename AT::t_int_1d_const c_binID;' (never assigned), :55 'c_bins' and :62 'c_gbins' (assigned only at src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:196 'c_gbins = gbins;' and :224 'c_bins = bins;'), :64-65 'd_resize'/'h_resize' (allocated at nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:38/45 and set at :52 'h_resize() = 1;', then never touched again).  The consumer keeps its own copies: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:87-93 takes only atoms_per_bin, k_bincount, k_bins, ghosts_per_gbin, k_gbincount and k_gbins, and npair_ssa_kokkos.h:136 declares its own c_gbins.  Note also that npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:87/91 copy atoms_per_bin and ghosts_per_gbin into members that are themselves never used.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; dead state that makes the class larger and misleads readers into thinking there is a resize/retry protocol like the one in NBinKokkos.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused members (and the corresponding allocations in the constructor and the two assignments in bin_atoms()).

summary: MinKokkos re-declares the iterate() return-code enum, hiding Min's identical enum in every KOKKOS min style, but omits MAXVDOTF -- so the values only agree by accident and MinFireKokkos silently falls through to the base enumerator.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_kokkos.h:42-44 '// possible return values of iterate() method\n  enum{MAXITER,MAXEVAL,ETOL,FTOL,DOWNHILL,ZEROALPHA,ZEROFORCE,\n       ZEROQUAD,TRSMALL,INTERROR,TIMEOUT};' versus src/min.h:60-74 which declares the same eleven names plus 'MAXVDOTF'.  src/KOKKOS/min_fire_kokkos.cpp:234 'if (max_vdotf_negatif > 0 && vdotf_negatif > max_vdotf_negatif) return MAXVDOTF;' resolves through the derived enum to Min::MAXVDOTF only because MinKokkos has no member of that name.  The codes are consumed positionally by src/min.cpp:1024-1038 'char *Min::stopstrings(int n) { const char *strings[] = {...}; return (char *) strings[n]; }'.
failure_scenario: No wrong behavior today (the eleven shared enumerators happen to be in the same order). If anyone inserts or reorders an entry in Min's enum, the KOKKOS min styles keep the old numbering and Min::run() prints the wrong stop reason, or indexes stopstrings() out of range.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate enum from min_kokkos.h and use the inherited Min enum.

summary: AtomKokkos::map_set_device() reallocates sametag BEFORE the map_init(0) call that may free it, so for MAP_HASH the kernel writes into a destroyed, zero-extent k_sametag view.
failure_scenario: Run with the Kokkos device atom map (default, kokkos atom/map not legacy) and atom_modify map hash (or >1e6 atom IDs so hash is auto-selected).  When this rank's nlocal+nghost grows past map_nhash (load imbalance, ghost growth), map_init(0) recreates the hash, which calls map_delete() and destroys k_sametag / sets max_same=0.  The following parallel_for then writes d_sametag(i) for i in [0,nall) into a zero-extent view: out-of-bounds device write / memory corruption (Kokkos bounds-check abort in a debug build), and k_sametag.sync_host() at line 267 leaves sametag == nullptr for all later host users (Domain::closest_image, Special).
suggested_fix: Move the 'if (nall > max_same) {...}' sametag (re)allocation block below the 'if (map_style == MAP_HASH) { if (nall > map_nhash) map_init(0); }' block, matching src/atom_map.cpp:196-201 and AtomKokkos::map_set_host().

summary: CommTiledKokkos::forward_comm_device(): in the generic (non comm_x_only, non ghost_velocity) branch the self-send case packs the buffer but never unpacks it, so the ghost atoms this rank sends to itself never receive their forward-communicated data.
failure_scenario: comm_style tiled with the KOKKOS device forward comm (package kokkos comm device, the GPU default) and either (a) an atom style whose forward comm is not x-only -- atom_style dipole (mu), spin (sp), dpd/react (dpdTheta,uCond,uMech,uChem) -- or (b) any atom style in a single/mixed-precision KOKKOS build, where atomKK->k_x.NEED_TRANSFORM is true and even plain x takes this branch.  Whenever a rank is its own neighbour for a swap (sendself[iswap] != 0, normal with periodic boundaries and few tiles), the self ghosts keep the values from the last borders() call for the whole reneighbouring interval -> wrong forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Add 'atomKK->avecKK->unpack_comm_kokkos(recvnum[iswap][nrecv],firstrecv[iswap][nrecv],k_buf_send);' after the pack_comm_kokkos call in the sendself block, matching the ghost_velocity branch and CommTiled::forward_comm().

summary: PPPMKokkos shadows PPPM::gc and never overrides PPPM::reset_grid(), so a load-balance rebalance runs the CPU reset_grid on the KOKKOS style: it calls the non-virtual PPPM::compute_rho_coeff(), which writes the base rho_coeff array that a KOKKOS run never allocates (nullptr), and dereferences the base gc, which is also nullptr.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:103-108:
  // same name but different than base class
  gc = nullptr; fft1 = nullptr; fft2 = nullptr; remap = nullptr;
(these assign the PPPMKokkos members declared in src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h:449, which shadow PPPM::gc etc.; PPPM's own gc is set to nullptr at src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:80 and never re-assigned in a KOKKOS run).  'grep -rn reset_grid src/KOKKOS' finds nothing, so PPPM::reset_grid (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:637-668) is inherited unchanged; it runs
  allocate();                                   // virtual -> PPPMKokkos::allocate, which creates only k_rho_coeff (pppm_kokkos.cpp:865) and never memory->create2d_offset(rho_coeff,...) as PPPM::allocate does at pppm.cpp:913
  if (!overlap_allowed && !gc->ghost_adjacent()) // base gc == nullptr
  compute_rho_coeff();                          // NOT virtual (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:142) -> PPPM::compute_rho_coeff writes 'rho_coeff[l][m] = a[l][k];' (pppm.cpp:2930) with rho_coeff == nullptr
reset_grid() is called on every rebalance: src/fix_balance.cpp:341 'if (force->kspace) force->kspace->reset_grid();'.
failure_scenario: 'fix balance ... rcb' (or shift) in a run with kspace_style pppm/kk: the rebalance calls kspace->reset_grid(), which segfaults in PPPM::compute_rho_coeff (null rho_coeff); with 'kspace_modify overlap no' it segfaults one line earlier on the null base gc.  Even if the pointers were valid, the KOKKOS device copies (k_rho_coeff / d_rho_coeff, re-created uninitialized by PPPMKokkos::allocate) would never be filled or synced, since PPPMKokkos::init() is the only place that does compute_rho_coeff() + k_rho_coeff.modify_host()/sync (pppm_kokkos.cpp:277-281).
suggested_fix: Give PPPMKokkos an override of reset_grid() that mirrors PPPM::reset_grid but uses the KOKKOS gc and calls PPPMKokkos::compute_rho_coeff() followed by k_rho_coeff.modify_host()/sync<DeviceType>(); alternatively make PPPM::compute_rho_coeff virtual and stop shadowing gc.  NOTE: pppm_kokkos.cpp is outside this reviewer's assigned file list (found while tracing Grid3dKokkos callers).

summary: DynamicalMatrixKokkos::setup() is never called: the base DynamicalMatrix::setup() is not virtual and DynamicalMatrix::command() calls it non-virtually, so the KOKKOS setup (auto_sync bracketing plus the synced pair->compute) is dead code.
evidence: src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h:23 declares 'void setup();' with no 'virtual'.  src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.h:35 declares 'void setup();' with no 'override' (it cannot have one).  src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.cpp, DynamicalMatrix::command(): 'if (style == REGULAR) { setup(); ...' -- an unqualified call inside a DynamicalMatrix member, statically bound to DynamicalMatrix::setup().  The KOKKOS version (src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:91-134) sets 'lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;' for the duration of the domain/comm/neighbor setup, adds an atomKK->sync()/modified() wrapped force->pair->compute(), and clears auto_sync to 0 at the end -- none of which runs.  This is the exact shape of rule 2 in .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md ('Declare virtual void allocate() in the base-class header ... without virtual, the base version is silently called').  src/KOKKOS/third_order_kokkos.cpp:91 has the identical dead override against src/PHONON/third_order.h:23.
failure_scenario: 'dynamical_matrix/kk all regular 0.000001' on a GPU build: the base setup() runs, so lmp->kokkos->auto_sync is left at its default 1 for the whole calculateMatrix() loop and every atomKK->modified() call forces a full host<->device copy of the per-atom arrays -- the KOKKOS command runs at roughly host speed.  Any future correctness fix put into the KOKKOS setup() would also be silently ignored.
suggested_fix: Make DynamicalMatrix::setup() (and ThirdOrder::setup()) virtual in src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h / third_order.h and mark the KOKKOS versions 'override'.

summary: norm_functor stores the FFT normalization factor in an 'int' member, so the 1/(nfast*nmid*nslow) scaling is truncated to 0 and a scaled backward FFT would zero the whole output array.
failure_scenario: Any FFT3dKokkos created with scaled=1 (the constructor argument) returns an all-zero backward transform.  Currently latent because the only in-tree caller, src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:879-887, passes scaled=0 and does its own scaling; a new KOKKOS kspace style (or a fix to PPPM) that requests scaling silently gets zeros instead of an error.
suggested_fix: Change the functor member and constructor parameter to FFT_SCALAR (matching plan->norm / src/KSPACE/fft3d.cpp).

summary: GroupKokkos::angmom_kk() uses the raw atom velocity instead of the deformation-corrected velocity, so with 'fix deform ... remap v' the angular momentum differs from Group::angmom() by the h_rate image term.
failure_scenario: 'fix deform ... remap v' together with 'fix momentum N group angular' (src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp:135 calls angmom_kk) or 'fix addtorque/group' (src/KOKKOS/fix_addtorque_group_kokkos.cpp:98): for any atom of the deform group with a nonzero image flag the velocity used is the peculiar velocity instead of the streaming-corrected one, so the removed/applied angular momentum is wrong and the /kk run silently disagrees with the same input run without -k on.
suggested_fix: Add a DomainKokkos::unmap overload that also returns the corrected velocity (taking h_rate, deform_vremap and deform_groupbit as captured scalars) and use it in angmom_kk, matching Domain::unmap(x,v,image,mask,y,u).

summary: With the device atom map and MAP_ARRAY, the global->local map array is never cleared: exchange_device() skips map_clear() and map_set_device() only clears the hash, so map() returns stale local indices for atom IDs that have migrated off this rank instead of -1.
failure_scenario: GPU run with the defaults (ngpus>0 => atom_map_legacy=0, exchange_comm_legacy=0) and an atom-ID range small enough that map_style is MAP_ARRAY.  An atom whose ID once lived on this rank migrates away; a bonded partner lookup for that ID then returns the stale local index instead of -1, so 'Bond/Angle atom missing' is not detected and neigh_bond builds a bond to an unrelated atom -> silently wrong forces instead of a hard error.
suggested_fix: Either drop the atom_map_legacy guard around map_clear() in exchange_device()/CommTiledKokkos, or add a device-side clear of k_map_array (deep_copy(view_device(),-1)) at the start of AtomKokkos::map_set_device() the way the hash branch already clears d_map_hash.

summary: k_exchange_copylist_bonus is marked modified on the host and synced to the device on every dimension of every exchange, even when there is no bonus data (bonus_flag == 0).
failure_scenario: Any non-bonus atom style: three needless host->device copies of k_exchange_copylist_bonus per exchange() call (once per dimension), plus a modify/sync flag toggle on a view nothing reads.
suggested_fix: Move the modify_host()/sync<DeviceType>() pair inside the 'if (bonus_flag)' block.

summary: DomainKokkos::pbc() drops the base class check that owned-atom coordinates are finite, so a blown-up KOKKOS run silently continues with NaN/Inf positions instead of aborting with the documented error.
failure_scenario: A KOKKOS GPU run whose pair style produces an infinite force (two atoms at the same position, bad initial configuration).  On the CPU (or with 'package kokkos comm no') LAMMPS stops with 'Non-numeric atom coords - simulation unstable'; on the device path the NaNs propagate silently and the run ends with garbage output or a much later, unrelated failure.
suggested_fix: Add a Kokkos::parallel_reduce over nlocal that ORs !isfinite(x(i,d)) into a flag (it can be folded into the existing PBC functor as a reduction) and call error->one() with the same message when the flag is set.

summary: DomainKokkos declares 'int closest_image(const int, int) const;' which is never defined anywhere and hides the three Domain::closest_image() overloads for anyone holding a DomainKokkos*.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.h:50: 'int closest_image(const int, int) const;'.  'grep -rn "DomainKokkos::closest_image" src' finds no definition; src/domain.h:143-145 declares the three non-virtual base overloads 'int closest_image(int, int); int closest_image(const double *const, int); void closest_image(const double *const, const double *const, double *const);' which name lookup in DomainKokkos would hide.  The KOKKOS callers (fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp:1031, fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:2388, neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp) each define their own closest_image member instead.
failure_scenario: Any new code that calls domain->closest_image(...) through a DomainKokkos pointer gets either an undefined-symbol link error (two-int form) or a compile error (the other overloads are hidden).
suggested_fix: Delete the declaration, or implement it and mark it as an explicit using-declaration of the base overloads.

summary: update_force() allocates a fresh f_merge_copy device view on every force evaluation, although the code further down already grows it on demand.
failure_scenario: dynamical_matrix does 6*N force evaluations; each one performs (and frees) a 3*nmax device allocation, which serialises against the device stream and dominates the runtime for large systems on a GPU.
suggested_fix: Drop the line 152 allocation and rely on the size check at lines 282-285 (same as VerletKokkos does).

summary: The KISS FFT path allocates a fresh 'fft_3d:tmp' device view for each of the three 1d FFT stages on every fft_3d_kokkos() call instead of keeping a scratch view in the plan.
failure_scenario: KISS FFT is the default when no vendor FFT library is enabled; pppm/kk performs 4 FFTs per timestep, so this is 12 device allocate/free pairs per timestep, each of which serialises the device stream.
suggested_fix: Add a persistent tmp view to fft_plan_3d_kokkos (allocated once in fft_3d_create_plan_kokkos, sized like d_scratch) and reuse it in all three stages.

summary: The KOKKOS_ENABLE_CUDA (and SYCL) FFT-library fallback blocks forget to undefine FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL, unlike the HIP block, so a CUDA+NVPL build ends up with both NVPL and KISS defined and fails to compile instead of falling back to KISS.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fftdata_kokkos.h:43-55 (CUDA) undefines FFT_KOKKOS_FFTW, FFT_KOKKOS_FFTW3 and FFT_KOKKOS_MKL and then '#if !defined(FFT_KOKKOS_CUFFT) && !defined(FFT_KOKKOS_KISS) / #define FFT_KOKKOS_KISS'; the HIP block at lines 56-71 additionally does '# if defined(FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL)\n#  undef FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL\n# endif'.  The SYCL block (lines 72-84) also omits it.  With CUDA + -DFFT_KOKKOS_NVPL both FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL and FFT_KOKKOS_KISS are then defined: the typedef chain at lines 145-153 picks the fftw_complex FFT_KOKKOS_DATA, while line 268 still includes kissfft_kokkos.h, whose kernels use the '.re'/'.im' members of the KISS struct.
failure_scenario: 'make' with the traditional build (or any non-CMake configuration) using the Kokkos CUDA backend and -DFFT_KOKKOS_NVPL: a confusing compile error inside kissfft_kokkos.h instead of the intended silent fallback to KISS.  CMake blocks this combination (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:224-226 FATAL_ERROR), which is why it has not been seen.
suggested_fix: Add the '#if defined(FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL) / #undef FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL / #endif' stanza to the CUDA and SYCL blocks, matching the HIP block.

summary: vcm_kk() forms the momentum products in KK_FLOAT (float in single/mixed precision) before widening to the double accumulator, unlike every other reduction in the same file and unlike Group::vcm().
failure_scenario: A mixed-precision KOKKOS build (KOKKOS_PRECISION=mixed) running 'fix momentum linear' or 'compute temp/com' (src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_com_kokkos.cpp:57): each term of the center-of-mass velocity is rounded to float before summation, so the removed drift and the temperature bias carry single-precision error even though the accumulator is double.
suggested_fix: Cast d_v(i,*) and massone to double before multiplying, as the other kernels in this header do.

summary: grow_send_kokkos() sizes the send buffer with the constant Comm::BUFEXTRA instead of the Comm::bufextra member, so the extra headroom the legacy CommBrick::exchange() relies on (maxexchange + BUFEXTRA) is not provided.
failure_scenario: Legacy exchange path (package kokkos comm no, or gpu/aware off with >1 rank) with a style whose per-atom exchange size is large (many bonds/angles per atom, or fixes contributing a large maxexchange_fix): AtomVec::pack_exchange writes past the end of k_buf_send's host allocation.
suggested_fix: Use the Comm::bufextra member (kept up to date by Comm::init_exchange()) instead of Comm::BUFEXTRA, and round the row count up rather than down when dividing by size_border.

summary: Grid3dKokkos::forward_comm()/reverse_comm() select the brick vs tiled path from the live comm->layout, while the matching data structures were built from the snapshot Grid3d::layout_grid taken at construction, so a layout change during a run makes the two disagree.
failure_scenario: Any sequence where comm->layout flips to LAYOUT_TILED after this Grid3dKokkos was set up but before it is destroyed (e.g. a balance/rcb between the grid setup and the next kspace comm): forward_comm() then takes the tiled branch while nsend/nrecv/ncopy are all still 0 from setup_comm_brick(), so no ghost grid data is exchanged at all and PPPM silently uses stale/zero ghost planes.  Currently masked because fix balance calls kspace->reset_grid() immediately after changing comm->layout.
suggested_fix: Use the inherited layout_grid member in both dispatchers (and fix the misleading indentation of the if/else while there).

summary: The MEAM pair scale factor is stored in an INTEGER Kokkos view, so every non-integral 'fix adapt ... pair meam scale' value is truncated (0.5 becomes 0, 1.9 becomes 1) before it reaches the device kernels.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_kokkos.h:65 'typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale;' and src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.h:108 'typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale;'. It is filled from the CPU double array by an implicit narrowing conversion at src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.cpp:303-307: 'for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) { h_map[i] = map[i]; for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++) h_scale(i,j) = scale[i][j]; }' where PairMEAM::scale is 'double **' (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:170 'memory->create(scale, np1, np1, "pair:scale");'). It is then read as a floating-point factor: src/KOKKOS/meam_dens_final_kokkos.h:63 'scaleii = d_scale(type[i],type[i]);' followed by ':182 Fl *= scaleii;', and src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:186-187 'KK_FLOAT scaleij = d_scale(type[i], type[i]);'. 'scale' is a documented fix adapt target for pair meam (doc/src/fix_adapt.rst:243: '| :doc:`meam <pair_meam>` | scale | type pairs |'), and PairMEAM::extract exposes it (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:895-898 'if (strcmp(str, "scale") == 0) return (void *) scale;').
failure_scenario: 'pair_style meam/kk ...' plus 'fix adapt 1 pair meam scale 1 1 v_ramp' with v_ramp going 1.0 -> 0.0: the CPU style scales the MEAM energy smoothly, while the /kk style sees d_scale = 1 until the value drops below 1.0 and then 0, so the embedding energy of every atom of that type jumps discontinuously to zero. Any fractional scale (the normal case for a thermodynamic-integration ramp) is silently wrong.
suggested_fix: Declare d_scale as a floating-point view ('typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d') in both src/KOKKOS/meam_kokkos.h:65 and src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.h:108 (and in the meam_dens_final signature at meam_dens_final_kokkos.h:25 / meam_kokkos.h:89), and re-copy scale[][] to the device whenever fix adapt can have changed it, not only in coeff().

summary: The KOKKOS MEAM force kernel never applies the pair scale factor to the forces or the virial: the whole 'if (!isone(scaleij)) { dUdrij *= scaleij; ... }' block of the CPU version is missing.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:692-702 reads 'dUdrij = phip * sij + d_frhop[i] * drhodr1 + d_frhop[j] * drhodr2; dUdsij = 0.0; if (!iszero_kk(d_dscrfcn[fnoffset + jn])) { dUdsij = phi + d_frhop[i] * drhods1 + d_frhop[j] * drhods2; } for (m = 0; m < 3; m++) { dUdrijm[m] = d_frhop[i] * drhodrm1[m] + d_frhop[j] * drhodrm2[m]; }' and then goes straight to 'force = dUdrij * recip + dUdsij * d_dscrfcn[fnoffset + jn];'. The CPU original has five more lines between them, src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:622-627: 'if (!isone(scaleij)) { dUdrij *= scaleij; dUdsij *= scaleij; dUdrijm[0] *= scaleij; dUdrijm[1] *= scaleij; dUdrijm[2] *= scaleij; }'. Nothing else in meam_force_kokkos.h uses scaleij -- 'grep -c scaleij src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h' returns 2, both inside the eflag_either block at :186-187.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style meam/kk' with 'fix adapt 1 pair meam scale 1 2 2.0': the CPU style doubles both energy and force of the 1-2 MEAM interaction, the /kk style doubles only the energy and leaves the force (and the virial and pressure computed from it) at the unscaled value, so the trajectory is wrong and the reported energy is inconsistent with the forces.
suggested_fix: Insert the scaling block after line 699, using the correct per-pair factor: 'if (!isone_kk(scaleij)) { dUdrij *= scaleij; dUdsij *= scaleij; dUdrijm[0] *= scaleij; dUdrijm[1] *= scaleij; dUdrijm[2] *= scaleij; }' with scaleij hoisted out of the eflag_either block.

summary: The block that undoes the 'pair/only' sort/atom-map overrides is guarded by 'if (lmp->pair_only_flag)' instead of 'if (!lmp->pair_only_flag)', so 'package kokkos pair/only on' never actually moves atom sorting and the atom map back to the host.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:776-785 sets 'if (lmp->pair_only_flag) { if (sort_legacy == 0) { sort_legacy = 1; sort_changed = 1; } if (atom_map_legacy == 0) { atom_map_legacy = 1; atom_map_changed = 1; } }'; then src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:824-833 immediately does 'if (lmp->pair_only_flag) { if (sort_changed) { sort_legacy = 0; sort_changed = 0; } if (atom_map_changed) { atom_map_legacy = 0; atom_map_changed = 0; } }'. The analogous 'change them back' block for the comm flags at line 789 is correctly guarded with 'if (gpu_aware_flag && !lmp->pair_only_flag)'. As written the second block is only reachable when pair_only_flag is true, i.e. exactly when the first block has just set the flags, so the two cancel and the settings never change; and when pair/only is later switched off the stale sort_changed/atom_map_changed flags can never be undone (they were already cleared).
failure_scenario: GPU build, 'package kokkos pair/only on': the intent is that with only pair styles accelerated the atom sort and atom map run on the host (sort_legacy = atom_map_legacy = 1). Instead both stay 0 and sorting/atom map keep running on the device while all non-pair styles are plain CPU styles, costing extra host/device transfers (and exercising the device sort/map path that pair/only is meant to avoid).
suggested_fix: Change the condition at line 824 to 'if (!lmp->pair_only_flag)' so the sort/atom-map overrides are undone only when pair/only is turned off again, matching the comm-flag block at line 789.

summary: The SLURM_LOCALID branch of the '-k on g N' parser is missing the 'if (ngpus > 0)' guard that all six other MPI-launcher branches have, so 'g 0' divides by zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:223-228: 'if ((str = getenv("SLURM_LOCALID"))) { int local_rank = std::stoi(str); device = local_rank % ngpus; if (device >= skip_gpu) device++; set_flag = 1; }' -- no ngpus check, while FLUX_TASK_LOCAL_ID (229), MPT_LRANK (237), MV2_COMM_WORLD_LOCAL_RANK (245), OMPI_COMM_WORLD_LOCAL_RANK (253), PMI_LOCAL_RANK (261) and PALS_LOCAL_RANKID (269) all wrap the identical body in 'if (ngpus > 0) { ... }'. ngpus comes straight from the user at line 208 and is only rejected later (line 316) for LMP_KOKKOS_GPU builds, and 'ngpus > 0' is not required at all for host-only builds (line 209-212 only errors for ngpus > 0).
failure_scenario: Run under SLURM (SLURM_LOCALID set) with 'lmp -k on g 0 ...' (e.g. a host-only Kokkos build where the user disables GPUs explicitly, or a typo): 'local_rank % 0' is integer division by zero -> SIGFPE/undefined behavior before any of the later argument validation runs.
suggested_fix: Wrap the SLURM_LOCALID body in 'if (ngpus > 0) { ... }' exactly like the other launcher branches, or validate ngpus >= 1 right after parsing it.

summary: A leftover debugging printf() sits in MemoryKokkos::create4d_offset_kokkos(), which the project rules forbid in LAMMPS code.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:142: 'printf("^^^^^ memoryKK->create_4d_offset_kokkos\n");' inside create4d_offset_kokkos(), with a commented-out sanity check right above it at line 140 ('//if (n1 <= 0 || n2lo > n2hi || ...) array = nullptr;'). The project instructions state 'There should not be any printf() statements or fprintf(screen,...) ... in new code' and 'Any output statements that were added for the obvious purpose of aiding in debugging should be removed entirely'.
failure_scenario: The first caller of this helper makes every MPI rank print '^^^^^ memoryKK->create_4d_offset_kokkos' to stdout, outside the log file and unguarded by comm->me == 0.
suggested_fix: Delete the printf and the commented-out guard line; restore the real dimension check ('if (n1 <= 0 || n2lo > n2hi || n3lo > n3hi || n4lo > n4hi) return ...') that Memory::create4d_offset has at src/memory.h:742.

summary: create4d_offset_kokkos() never applies the n2lo/n3lo/n4lo index offsets its name and comment promise, so every access through the returned pointer array is shifted, and there is no matching destroy for the pointer levels it smallocs.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:151-172 builds the pointer levels with 'array[i][j][k] = &data.view_host()(i,j,k,0);' and returns without any offset arithmetic. The CPU original, Memory::create4d_offset (src/memory.h:739-755), ends with 'bigint m = ((bigint) n1) * n2 * n3; for (bigint i = 0; i < m; i++) array[0][0][i] -= n4lo; m = ((bigint) n1) * n2; for (bigint i = 0; i < m; i++) array[0][i] -= n3lo; for (int i = 0; i < n1; i++) array[i] -= n2lo;'. It also drops the 'if (n1 <= 0 || n2lo > n2hi || n3lo > n3hi || n4lo > n4hi) return nullptr;' guard of src/memory.h:742 (commented out at line 140), and no destroy4d_offset_kokkos exists to free the per-i and per-i,j smalloc'ed pointer blocks (src/memory.h:769-778 has destroy4d_offset for the CPU version). grep confirms the function currently has no callers.
failure_scenario: The first style that ports a create4d_offset() array to KOKKOS and calls this with a non-zero n2lo/n3lo/n4lo (the usual case, e.g. type arrays starting at 1) reads and writes at index-lo instead of index, silently corrupting data or running off the end of the view; freeing the array leaks the two inner pointer levels.
suggested_fix: Either delete this unused helper, or add the three offset loops and the dimension guard mirroring src/memory.h:742-753 and provide a matching destroy4d_offset_kokkos().

summary: The 3d create_kokkos() overload that also builds a host mirror allocates the view with only two of the three extents and then indexes it in three dimensions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:319-351: 'TYPE create_kokkos(TYPE &data, HTYPE &h_data, typename TYPE::value_type ***&array, int n1, int n2, int n3, const char *name) { ... data = TYPE(std::string(name),n1,n2); h_data = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(data); ... array[i][j] = &data.view_host()(i,j,0); ... }'. The n3 argument is never used in the allocation, while the sibling overload without the host mirror (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:287-317) correctly writes 'data = TYPE(std::string(name),n1,n2,n3);'. The body is also internally inconsistent: it makes h_data with Kokkos::create_mirror_view(data) (i.e. TYPE is a plain View, as in the working 2d overload at line 177-197 which uses '&h_data(i,0)'), yet indexes 'data.view_host()', a DualView member. grep over src/KOKKOS shows no caller passes seven arguments, so the template is never instantiated today.
failure_scenario: The first caller of this overload either fails to compile (no view_host() on a plain View) or, for a DualView TYPE, gets a view whose third extent is 0 and then takes '&data.view_host()(i,j,0)' on a zero-size view -- out-of-bounds pointers handed back to the caller as a legacy 3d array.
suggested_fix: Fix the allocation to 'data = TYPE(std::string(name),n1,n2,n3);' and index the host mirror consistently ('array[i][j] = &h_data(i,j,0);'), or delete the unused overload.

summary: kf_bfly_generic() uses the single per-plan scratch view st.d_scratch that every concurrently running 1d FFT of the same parallel_for shares, where the CPU original allocates a private scratch buffer per call.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kissfft_kokkos.h:387 'typename FFT_AT::t_FFT_DATA_1d_um d_scratch = st.d_scratch;' then :392-393 'd_scratch(q1).re = d_Fout(Fout_count + k).re; ...' and :407 'C_MUL(t,d_scratch,q,d_twiddles,twidx);'. st.d_scratch is allocated once per plan in kiss_fft_alloc_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/kissfft_kokkos.h:520 'st.d_scratch = typename FFT_AT::t_FFT_DATA_1d("kissfft:scratch",p_max);'). The state is copied by value into kiss_fft_functor (src/KOKKOS/fft3d_kokkos.cpp:183-193 'kiss_fft_state_kokkos<DeviceType> st;'), but a Kokkos::View member copies by reference-counted handle, so all threads of 'Kokkos::parallel_for(total/length,f);' (src/KOKKOS/fft3d_kokkos.cpp:261, and the mid/slow equivalents) write the same memory. The CPU original gives every call its own buffer: src/KSPACE/kissfft.h:340 'auto *scratch = (FFT_DATA *) KISS_FFT_TMP_ALLOC(sizeof(FFT_DATA) * p);' ... :362 'KISS_FFT_TMP_FREE(scratch);'.
failure_scenario: Any FFT grid dimension with a prime factor larger than 5 (e.g. nfast = 7) routes kf_work's default switch case to kf_bfly_generic; every one of the total/length concurrent 1d FFTs then reads and writes the same p_max-element scratch view, so the transformed data is garbage (nondeterministic, differs run to run). Today this is latent for PPPM only because PPPM::set_grid_global boosts every grid dimension until PPPM::factorable() accepts it and factors[] is only {2,3,5} (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:92-96,1170-1172) -- any future user of FFT3dKokkos with an arbitrary grid size hits it immediately.
suggested_fix: Give each FFT its own scratch slice: size st.d_scratch as p_max*(number of concurrent FFTs) and index it with the functor's 'i' (or the offset/length), or use Kokkos scratch (team) memory instead of a plan-wide view.

summary: The five MS-MEAM per-atom arrays and their duplicated scatter views are allocated unconditionally, where the CPU base allocates them only when msmeamflag is set, wasting 23 KK_FLOATs per atom (times the thread count under a duplicated scatter view) in every plain pair_style meam/kk run.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_dens_init_kokkos.h:148-168 allocates k_arho2mb (nmax), k_arho1m (nmax x 3), k_arho2m (nmax x 6), k_arho3m (nmax x 10) and k_arho3mb (nmax x 3) with no msmeamflag test, and :222-226 / :237-241 unconditionally build dup_/ndup_ scatter views over them ('dup_arho2mb = Kokkos::Experimental::create_scatter_view<...ScatterDuplicated>(d_arho2mb);' etc.), with :261-265 contributing them back. The CPU original guards every one of these: src/MEAM/meam_dens_init.cpp:74-81 'if (msmeamflag) { memory->create(arho1m, nmax, 3, "pair:arho1m"); memory->create(arho2m, nmax, 6, ...); memory->create(arho3m, nmax, 10, ...); memory->create(arho2mb, nmax, ...); memory->create(arho3mb, nmax, 3, ...); }' (and the matching destroy at :47-53). Every consumer of these arrays in the KOKKOS kernels is itself behind 'if (msmeamflag)' (meam_dens_init_kokkos.h:47-63, :516-523, :561-570, :578-598), so the storage is provably dead for a non-MS-MEAM potential.
failure_scenario: pair_style meam/kk (not meam/ms/kk) on a GPU with 10 million owned+ghost atoms permanently holds an extra 23 * 8 bytes/atom = ~1.8 GB of device memory that is never read or written; on a threaded host backend where lmp->kokkos->need_dup<DeviceType>() is true the duplicated scatter views multiply that waste by the thread count, so a 16-thread run over 1M atoms burns ~2.9 GB.
suggested_fix: Wrap the msmeam allocations at :148-168, the scatter-view creation at :221-226 / :236-241, and the contribute calls at :260-265 in 'if (msmeamflag)', mirroring src/MEAM/meam_dens_init.cpp:74-81.

summary: The pair scale factor is looked up as d_scale(type[i], type[i]) instead of d_scale(type[i], type[j]), so a per-type-pair 'fix adapt pair meam scale' uses the i-i factor for every i-j pair.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:186 'KK_FLOAT scaleij = d_scale(type[i], type[i]);'. The CPU original indexes both types: src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:92 'scaleij = scale[type[i]][type[j]];' (inside the jn loop, after 'j = firstneigh[jn]'). The name 'scaleij' in the KOKKOS code confirms the intent. The other lookup in the port, src/KOKKOS/meam_dens_final_kokkos.h:63 'scaleii = d_scale(type[i],type[i]);', is correct because the base uses scale[type[i]][type[i]] there (src/MEAM/meam_dens_final.cpp:34 and :138).
failure_scenario: A two-element MEAM system with 'fix adapt 1 pair meam scale 1 2 0.5' (only the cross interaction scaled, so scale[1][1] = scale[2][2] = 1.0): the CPU style halves the 1-2 pair energy while the /kk style applies scale[1][1] = 1.0 and leaves it unscaled -- and conversely, scaling only 1 1 wrongly rescales the 1-2 pairs of every type-1 atom.
suggested_fix: Change to 'd_scale(type[i], type[j])' and hoist the lookup out of the 'if (eflag_either)' block so the same value can also scale dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm as the CPU version does.

summary: The per-atom pair energy tally uses the unscaled phi while the global energy tally on the line above uses the scaled phi_sc, so eatom no longer sums to the global energy when a scale factor is set.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:188-192: 'if (eflag_global) ev.evdwl += static_cast<KK_ACC_FLOAT>(phi_sc * sij); if (eflag_atom) { a_eatom[i] += static_cast<KK_ACC_FLOAT>(static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.5) * phi * sij); a_eatom[j] += static_cast<KK_ACC_FLOAT>(static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.5) * phi * sij); }'. The CPU original uses phi_sc in both places, src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:116-121: 'if (eflag_global != 0) *eng_vdwl = *eng_vdwl + phi_sc * sij; if (eflag_atom != 0) { eatom[i] = eatom[i] + 0.5 * phi_sc * sij; eatom[j] = eatom[j] + 0.5 * phi_sc * sij; }'.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style meam/kk' with any scale != 1 and 'compute pe/atom': the sum of the per-atom energies differs from the thermo pe by the unscaled pair contribution, and a 'compute reduce sum c_pe' sanity check that passes on the CPU style fails on /kk.
suggested_fix: Use phi_sc in the eflag_atom branch, matching src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:119-120.
