summary: The 't'/'threads' command-line option reads arg[iarg+1] without the 'if (iarg+2 > narg)' bounds check that the 'd'/'device' and 'g'/'gpus' options perform.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:282-289: '} else if (strcmp(arg[iarg],"t") == 0 || strcmp(arg[iarg],"threads") == 0) { nthreads = utils::inumeric(FLERR, arg[iarg+1], false, lmp);' -- compare src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:200-202 ('if (iarg+2 > narg) error->all(FLERR,"Invalid Kokkos command-line args");') and :207. narg here is kklast-kkfirst computed in src/lammps.cpp:302-304, so arg[iarg+1] can be one past the delimited range.
failure_scenario: 'lmp -k on t' as the final command-line arguments passes narg=1; arg[1] is read out of the delimited range (it is argv's terminating nullptr for a main()-provided argv, but an arbitrary pointer for a library caller of lammps_open() whose argv is not nullptr-terminated) -> out-of-bounds read instead of the intended 'Invalid Kokkos command-line args' error.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (iarg+2 > narg) error->all(FLERR,"Invalid Kokkos command-line args");' as the first statement of the 't'/'threads' branch.

summary: The 'Kokkos package already initialized' check tests a freshly default-constructed InitializationSettings object, so the branch is dead and the warning can never fire.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:297-310: 'Kokkos::InitializationSettings args;' immediately followed by 'if (args.has_num_threads()) { ... error->warning(FLERR,"Kokkos package already initalized. Cannot change parameters"); nthreads = args.get_num_threads(); ... }'. 'args' is a local object that has just been default constructed and no setter has been called, so has_num_threads() is always false and only the else branch (set_num_threads/set_device_id) ever executes. The comment above it ('we cannot change any Kokkos library parameters after the first initalization') shows the intent was to detect an already-initialized Kokkos runtime, which is what KokkosLMP::initialize() tests with Kokkos::is_initialized() at line 496.
failure_scenario: A library user calls lammps_open() twice with different '-k on t N g M' settings: the second instance silently reports and uses the newly requested nthreads/ngpus in its log while Kokkos keeps the settings from the first initialization (KokkosLMP::initialize skips Kokkos::initialize), and no warning is printed.
suggested_fix: Test 'Kokkos::is_initialized()' (and query the live execution space / init_ngpus) instead of args.has_num_threads(), or drop the dead branch.

summary: Member 'neighflag_qeq_set' is declared but never initialized nor used anywhere in the source tree.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.h:29 'int neighflag_qeq_set;'; 'grep -rn neighflag_qeq_set src/' returns only this declaration. It is not set in the KokkosLMP constructor (src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:116-490, which initializes neigh_thread_set, threads_per_atom_set, pair_team_size_set, ... but not this one) and never read.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect today, but the uninitialized member is a trap for anyone who later adds a 'if (neighflag_qeq_set)' test analogous to neigh_thread_set.
suggested_fix: Remove the member, or initialize it in the constructor and use it to distinguish an explicit 'neigh/qeq' setting like neigh_thread_set does.

summary: memset_kokkos() keeps its zeroing functor in a function-local static and zeroes only floor(bytes/4) bytes; the helper is dead code (no caller anywhere in src/).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1421-1427: 'template<class ViewType> void memset_kokkos (ViewType &view) { static MemsetZeroFunctor<typename ViewType::execution_space> f; f.ptr = view.data(); Kokkos::parallel_for(view.span()*sizeof(typename ViewType::value_type)/4, f); ... }'. The functor object is shared by every call for a given execution space, and 'f.ptr' is written before the launch, so two host threads calling this for different views race on 'f.ptr'. The trip count 'span()*sizeof(value_type)/4' truncates: a view whose byte size is not a multiple of 4 leaves its last 1-3 bytes untouched. 'grep -rn memset_kokkos src/' finds only this definition -- there is no caller.
failure_scenario: If a future caller uses it on a view whose byte size is not a multiple of 4 (e.g. a char or a 2-byte value type), the tail bytes stay uninitialized; if two threads call it concurrently one view is zeroed twice and the other not at all.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused helper, or replace its body with 'Kokkos::deep_copy(view, typename ViewType::value_type());' which is correct for any value type and has no shared state.

summary: Two blocks of commented-out code left in the header, which the project coding rules ask to remove.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:185 '//typedef Kokkos::LayoutLeft LMPDeviceLayout;' inside the '#else' of the layout selection, and src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1465 '//typedef struct { SNAreal re, im; } SNAcomplex;' just above the SNAComplex template.
failure_scenario: None at runtime; the review checklist in .github/copilot-instructions.md ('Commented out code ... should be removed entirely') flags these.
suggested_fix: Delete both commented-out typedefs.

summary: ModifyKokkos declares a member function pre_decide() that is never defined and never called, and it does not override anything in Modify.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.h:34 'void pre_decide();' -- it carries no 'override' (Modify has no such virtual, see src/modify.h:58-104) and 'grep -rn pre_decide src/' finds only this one line: there is no definition in src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp and no caller.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; any future call to it would be an undefined-reference link error rather than the intended behavior.
suggested_fix: Remove the declaration, or implement it if a pre-decide hook is actually wanted.

summary: ModifyKokkos::energy_atom() is a byte-for-byte copy of Modify::energy_atom(), adding no KOKKOS sync/modify handling, so the override serves no purpose.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp:504-514 and src/modify.cpp:514-524 have identical bodies ('eatom = fix[list_energy_atom[i]]->eatom; if (!eatom) continue; for (j = 0; j < nlocal; j++) energy[j] += eatom[j];'). Unlike every other wrapper in modify_kokkos.cpp it contains no atomKK->sync/modified and no auto_sync bracket. (This is currently harmless because no fix in src/KOKKOS sets energy_peratom_flag, so list_energy_atom only ever holds non-KOKKOS fixes whose eatom is plain host memory.)
failure_scenario: None today; but the empty override hides the fact that the first KOKKOS fix to provide a device-resident per-atom energy would be read here without a sync.
suggested_fix: Delete the override and let Modify::energy_atom() be used, or make it actually sync the fix's per-atom energy when the fix is kokkosable.

summary: MathSpecialKokkos::factorial() is declared extern in the header but is defined nowhere and called nowhere, so any use would be a link error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/math_special_kokkos.h:34 'extern double factorial(const int n);' with the doc comment promising a table lookup for 0 <= n <= 167. src/KOKKOS/math_special_kokkos.cpp defines only 'double MathSpecialKokkos::erfcx_y100(const double y100)' (line 61) -- the nfac_table[] and the factorial() definition that src/math_special.cpp:10-199 carries were not ported. 'grep -rn "MathSpecialKokkos::factorial" src/' finds nothing; the KOKKOS styles that need factorials use their own copies (src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:1910, and compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:38 which pulls in the non-KOKKOS MathSpecial::factorial).
failure_scenario: A future KOKKOS style that calls MathSpecialKokkos::factorial() compiles cleanly and then fails at link time with an undefined reference.
suggested_fix: Remove the declaration, or port the nfac_table[] lookup from src/math_special.cpp into math_special_kokkos.cpp.

summary: The header defines the object-like macro FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE and never undefines it, leaking it into every translation unit that includes math_special_kokkos.h.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/math_special_kokkos.h:59 '#define FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE  1.4426950408889634074'. The non-KOKKOS original keeps the same constant out of the header and as a typed constant in the implementation file: src/math_special.cpp has 'static constexpr double FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE = 1.4426950408889634074;'.
failure_scenario: Any translation unit that includes both math_special_kokkos.h and a file declaring an identifier named FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE (e.g. src/math_special.cpp's static constexpr, were it ever pulled in) fails to compile with a confusing macro-expansion error.
suggested_fix: Replace the macro with 'static constexpr double FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE = 1.4426950408889634074;' inside the MathSpecialKokkos namespace.

summary: Three device-callable functions use unqualified sqrt()/cos()/sin() instead of the Kokkos:: math functions the rest of the file (and the KOKKOS package rules) use.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/math_extra_kokkos.h:526 (qnormalize) 'double norm = 1.0 / sqrt(q[0] * q[0] + ...);'; :722,:727,:732,:737 (exyz_to_q) 'q[0] = sqrt(q0sq);' etc.; :824-825 (no_squish_rotate) 'c_phi = cos(static_cast<double>(dt) * phi); s_phi = sin(static_cast<double>(dt) * phi);'. Every other function in the same header uses the qualified form, e.g. :108 'Kokkos::sqrt(v[0]*v[0]+...)', :207, :571-572 'Kokkos::sin(halfa) / Kokkos::cos(halfa)'. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels (Kokkos::sqrt, Kokkos::exp, Kokkos::pow, Kokkos::log, ...), never std::'. All three are reached from device kernels: src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:854 'MathExtraKokkos::richardson(...)' (which calls qnormalize) and :1476 'MathExtraKokkos::qnormalize(quatatom);', src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_nh_small_kokkos.cpp:665-669 'MathExtraKokkos::no_squish_rotate(...)'.
failure_scenario: Compiles today because CUDA/HIP inject ::sqrt/::cos/::sin device overloads for double via math.h, but the same construct is what rule 4 was written for; a backend that does not (or a KK_FLOAT=float build, where the unqualified call silently promotes to double) either fails to compile or costs double-precision transcendentals in a single-precision kernel.
suggested_fix: Replace with Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::cos / Kokkos::sin like the rest of the header.

summary: MEAMKokkos::G_gam() is missing the 'gamma == 0.0' division-by-zero guard that was added to the CPU MEAM::G_gam(), so the two implementations can return different values for the same input.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_funcs_kokkos.h:47-52 'if (gamma < gsmooth_switchpoint) { KK_FLOAT G = 1 / (gsmooth_factor_kk + 1) * Kokkos::pow((gsmooth_switchpoint / gamma), gsmooth_factor_kk); return Kokkos::sqrt(G); }'. The CPU original has one extra line at src/MEAM/meam_funcs.cpp:43-49: 'if (gamma < gsmooth_switchpoint) { ... if (gamma == 0.0) return 0.0; // avoid division by zero. For gamma = 0.0 => G = 1 / inf   double G = 1 / (gsmooth_factor + 1) * pow((gsmooth_switchpoint / gamma), gsmooth_factor); return sqrt(G); }'. git log -L on those lines shows the guard came from the 'static-analysis-updates' merge (63fcdb6e5) and was never propagated to the KOKKOS copy; MEAMKokkos::G_gam is otherwise a line-by-line transliteration.
failure_scenario: A potential file with a negative gsmooth_factor puts gsmooth_switchpoint = -gsf/(gsf+1) above zero, so gamma == 0.0 enters the branch: the CPU pair style returns 0.0 while pair_style meam/kk evaluates gsmooth_switchpoint/0.0 and feeds the infinity to pow, so the /kk run can disagree with the CPU run (0/0 -> NaN when gsmooth_switchpoint is also 0). With the usual positive gsmooth_factor the branch requires gamma < -0.99 and the guard is unreachable, so this is a latent divergence rather than an observed wrong answer.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (gamma == static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.0)) return 0.0;' before the pow, mirroring src/MEAM/meam_funcs.cpp:47 (and consider the same for dG_gam, which divides by gamma at line 99 and has no guard in either version).

summary: The 'if (SINGLE_DEVICE) modify_legacy_device();' branch inside TransformView::sync_hostkk_to_legacy() is unreachable, because a single-device Kokkos DualView always reports need_sync_host()/need_sync_device() as false.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1041-1049: 'if (modified_hostkk_legacy) { Kokkos::deep_copy(h_view,h_viewkk); modified_hostkk_legacy = 0; if (k_view.need_sync_host() || k_view.need_sync_device()) { if (SINGLE_DEVICE) modify_legacy_device(); } else modified_legacy_device = 0; }'. SINGLE_DEVICE is defined at line 714 as 't_dev::device_type == t_host::device_type', which is exactly Kokkos' impl_dualview_is_single_device; for such a DualView Kokkos' need_sync<Device>() returns false unconditionally, so the guarded call can never execute and the else branch always runs under SINGLE_DEVICE.
failure_scenario: No wrong results today; the intent of the branch (record that the legacy host is now ahead of the device) is silently never carried out, so a later change to the surrounding logic will behave differently from what the code reads as.
suggested_fix: Drop the dead 'if (SINGLE_DEVICE)' branch, or if the intent was the non-single-device case, change it to 'if (!SINGLE_DEVICE) modify_legacy_device();' and re-verify the sync state machine.

summary: ModifyKokkos::post_run() is the only fix-calling wrapper that omits the auto_sync bracketing used around every other non-KOKKOS fix callback.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp:522-528: 'for (int i = 0; i < nfix; i++) { atomKK->sync(fix[i]->execution_space, fix[i]->datamask_read); fix[i]->post_run(); atomKK->modified(fix[i]->execution_space, fix[i]->datamask_modify); }'. Every other wrapper in the file (e.g. end_of_step at :446-449, post_force at :379-382, min_post_force at :745-748, and energy_couple/energy_global as of commit 9ba00b501) wraps the call as 'int prev_auto_sync = lmp->kokkos->auto_sync; if (!fix[...]->kokkosable) lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1; fix[...]->hook(); lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = prev_auto_sync;'. The purpose (documented in src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:425-428) is that a non-KOKKOS style running inside a KOKKOS run needs auto_sync on so that any sync()/modified() it triggers indirectly (e.g. through the DomainKokkos x2lamda/lamda2x overrides) writes through to the legacy host arrays it reads.
failure_scenario: A non-KOKKOS fix whose post_run() goes through a KOKKOS-overridden helper that syncs to the device (DomainKokkos::x2lamda/lamda2x, AtomKokkos::sort) leaves the legacy host arrays behind, so anything the fix reads afterwards in post_run() (or a later 'run' command that re-reads them) sees stale coordinates.
suggested_fix: Add the same 'prev_auto_sync' save/force/restore around 'fix[i]->post_run();' that all the other ModifyKokkos wrappers use.

summary: Few's initializer_list constructor neither bounds-checks nor default-initializes: a list longer than n writes past the fixed buffer, a shorter one leaves elements uninitialized.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos_few.h:113 'alignas(T) char array_[n * sizeof(T)];' and :117-122 'Few(std::initializer_list<T> l) { std::size_t i = 0; for (auto it = l.begin(); it != l.end(); ++it) { new (data() + (i++)) T(*it); } }'. There is no 'i < n' guard and no loop to construct the remaining n - l.size() elements, while the destructor at :132-134 unconditionally runs '(data()[i]).~T()' for all n. The sibling constructors at :124-130 correctly cover all n slots.
failure_scenario: 'Few<double,3> f = {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0};' constructs a fourth double past the end of array_ (stack/object corruption); 'Few<double,3> f = {1.0, 2.0};' leaves f[2] holding garbage that is then used as a coordinate or box length. No in-tree caller uses the initializer-list form today, so this is latent.
suggested_fix: Clamp the loop to n and default-construct the remaining slots, e.g. 'std::size_t i = 0; for (auto it = l.begin(); it != l.end() && i < n; ++it) new (data() + (i++)) T(*it); for (; i < n; ++i) new (data() + i) T();'.

summary: With bzeroflag=1, chemflag=1 and wselfallflag=0 the KOKKOS evaluate_bi() subtracts bzero[j] from EVERY diagonal element triple (elem1==elem2==elem3), whereas the CPU SNA::compute_bi() subtracts it only from the one triple built from the central atom's element ielem, so pair snap/kk reports different energies than pair snap.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:1115-1125: 'register_loop<yi_batch>([&] (int n) -> void { bval[n] *= static_cast<accum_type>(2.0); if (bzero_flag) { if (!wselfall_flag) { if (elem1 == elem2 && elem1 == elem3) { bval[n] -= static_cast<accum_type>(bzero[j]); } } else { bval[n] -= static_cast<accum_type>(bzero[j]); } } });' -- evaluate_bi() never receives the central atom's element (its signature at sna_kokkos.h:340 and the caller compute_bi(iatom,jjb) at sna_kokkos_impl.h:1009 carry no ielem). src/ML-SNAP/sna.cpp:696-702: 'if (bzero_flag) { if (!wselfall_flag) { itriple = (ielem*nelements+ielem)*nelements+ielem; for (int jjb = 0; jjb < idxb_max; jjb++) { const int j = idxb[jjb].j; blist[itriple*idxb_max+jjb] -= bzero[j]; } } else { ... every triple ... } }' with ielem = the central atom's element (src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:346 'snaptr->compute_bi(ielem);'). For nelements > 1 the KOKKOS code shifts nelements diagonal triples instead of one. No compensating correction exists elsewhere: 'grep -n bzero src/KOKKOS/*' only matches sna_kokkos{.h,_impl.h}. blist feeds the energy directly (pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:1418 'evdwl += static_cast<accum_type>(d_coeffi[icoeff+1]*snaKK.blist(ii,idx_chem,idxb));').
failure_scenario: A multi-element SNAP potential with 'chemflag 1 bzeroflag 1 wselfallflag 0' (all legal; only wselfallflag differs from the shipped potentials/InP_JCPA2020.snapparam, which uses wselfallflag 1 and therefore hides the bug): every atom's energy is off by the constant -sum_{e != ielem} sum_jjb coeff_ielem[(e,e,e)*idxb_max+jjb+1]*bzero[j], so pair snap/kk and pair snap report different potential energies for the same configuration. Because the offset is position-independent, forces and stresses are unaffected, which is why force-based regression tests do not catch it.
suggested_fix: Pass the central atom's element into compute_bi()/evaluate_bi() (it is already available to the caller as d_map(type(i))) and gate the !wselfall_flag subtraction on 'elem1 == elem2 && elem2 == elem3 && elem1 == ielem', matching sna.cpp:698.

summary: build_topology() syncs the device-built bond/angle/dihedral/improper lists to the host only when the corresponding force style has execution_space == Host, but other host-side consumers read neighbor->bondlist through the plain pointer (fix bond/break, compute stress/cartesian, pair mesocnt, the library's neigh_bondlist export) and so see a never-updated host copy.
evidence: neighbor_kokkos.cpp:435-442: 'if (force->bond && force->bond->execution_space == Host) k_bondlist.sync_host();' (same for angle/dihedral/improper). neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp:288 grow_kokkos(k_bondlist,neighbor->bondlist,...) points the plain pointer at the host view; :305 'k_bondlist.modify<DeviceType>()' after the device build, and nothing else syncs it. Host readers with no KOKKOS variant (none of these exist in src/KOKKOS): src/MC/fix_bond_break.cpp:239-245 'int **bondlist = neighbor->bondlist; ... i1 = bondlist[n][0]; i2 = bondlist[n][1]; type = bondlist[n][2];', src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_stress_cartesian.cpp:374-378, src/library.cpp:2345 'return (void *) lmp->neighbor->bondlist' (lammps_extract_global "neigh_bondlist"). neighbor->nbondlist (the count) IS correct on the host (neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp:284), so these loops run over nbondlist rows of stale/zero host data.
failure_scenario: GPU run with bond_style harmonic/kk (device list) plus 'fix bond/break' on a polymer: the fix iterates nbondlist rows whose host contents are zero-initialized (never synced), 'type != btype' skips every row, so no bond is ever broken and no error is raised. A Python/library driver reading neigh_bondlist gets the same stale data. On CPU-only Kokkos builds host and device views alias, so the problem only appears on GPU.
suggested_fix: Sync the topology lists to the host whenever any non-KOKKOS style may read them (simplest: sync when force->bond exists and either execution_space == Host or any fix/compute in modify is not kokkosable), or provide a Neighbor::get_bondlist-style accessor that syncs on demand and route the host consumers through it.

summary: TuneKokkos opens its log file only on rank 0 and calls the collective error->all() inside that rank-0-only branch, so a failure to open the file makes rank 0 abort collectively while every other rank continues, i.e. a hang or an MPI abort mismatch in parallel runs; the file is also handled with raw fopen/fclose instead of SafeFilePtr.
evidence: tune_kokkos.cpp:96-104: 'if (comm->me == 0) { std::string filename = fmt::format("tuning-{}.log", my_name); tuning_logfile = fopen(filename.c_str(),"w"); if (tuning_logfile == nullptr) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot open tuning logfile {}: {}", ...); } else { tuning_logfile = nullptr; }'. Project rules: error->all() only when all ranks hit the error, error->one() for a single rank; prefer SafeFilePtr for FILE* resources.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank KOKKOS run with 'package kokkos ... tune' in a read-only working directory: rank 0 enters Error::all (MPI_Barrier/abort protocol), the other ranks proceed to allocate() and into the run -> deadlock or an unclean abort instead of the intended error message.
suggested_fix: Use error->one() for the rank-0 failure (or broadcast the failure flag and call error->all on every rank), and hold the FILE* in a SafeFilePtr.

summary: unpack_3d_permute1_n_functor multiplies the fast-index plane stride by nqty ('nqty*fast*nstride_plane'), but the CPU reference src/pack.h advances the destination index by exactly nstride_plane per fast index, so for nqty > 2 the unpack scatters data to wrong (and out-of-range) locations.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h:302-305: 'const int instart = plane + nqty*mid; int in = instart + nqty*fast*nstride_plane; int out = out_orig + nqty*mid*nfast + nqty*fast; for (int iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) d_data[data_offset + in++] = d_buf[buf_offset + out++];'. src/pack.h:175-179 (unpack_3d_permute1_n): 'instart = plane + nqty * mid; for (fast = 0; fast < nfast; fast++, instart += nstride_plane) { in = instart; for (iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) data[in++] = buf[out++]; }' -- i.e. the destination index is plane + nqty*mid + fast*nstride_plane, with NO nqty factor on the stride (nstride_plane is already in units of scalars, remap_kokkos.cpp:524 sets 'nstride_plane = nqty*out.ksize*out.jsize'). The nqty==2 sibling in the same file confirms the correct form: pack_kokkos.h:245 'const int in = in_orig + fast*nstride_plane;' (no factor 2). The buf index 'out' is computed correctly.
failure_scenario: A remap plan created with permute==1 and nqty>=3 (remap_kokkos.cpp:436-437 selects unpack_3d_permute1_n) writes each fast plane nqty times too far apart: with nqty=3 the last plane lands at 3*(nfast-1)*nstride_plane, roughly three times past the end of the receive brick -> silently corrupted FFT/remap output or an out-of-bounds device write. Currently latent: every in-tree caller uses nqty=1 (pppm_kokkos.cpp:891) or nqty=2 (fft3d_kokkos.cpp:473,498,539,567), so the _n variants are never selected today.
suggested_fix: Drop the nqty factor: 'int in = instart + fast*nstride_plane;' (and the same in unpack_3d_permute2_n_functor).

summary: unpack_3d_permute2_n_functor has the same defect as the permute1_n variant: it multiplies the fast-index line stride by nqty ('nqty*fast*nstride_line') where src/pack.h advances by nstride_line only.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h:466-469: 'const int instart = nqty*slow + mid*nstride_plane; int in = instart + nqty*fast*nstride_line; int out = out_orig + nqty*mid*nfast + nqty*fast;'. src/pack.h:257-261 (unpack_3d_permute2_n): 'instart = nqty * slow + mid * nstride_plane; for (fast = 0; fast < nfast; fast++, instart += nstride_line) { in = instart; for (iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) data[in++] = buf[out++]; }' -- destination index is nqty*slow + mid*nstride_plane + fast*nstride_line. The nqty==2 sibling pack_kokkos.h:411 'const int in = in_orig + fast*nstride_line;' has no factor 2, confirming the intended form.
failure_scenario: Same as the permute1_n case: a remap with permute==2 and nqty>=3 (remap_kokkos.cpp:444-445) scatters the unpacked values nqty times too far apart, corrupting the output brick or writing out of bounds. Latent today because no in-tree caller uses nqty>2.
suggested_fix: Change to 'int in = instart + fast*nstride_line;'.

summary: Commented-out debug sync/modified blocks ('// added debug', '// debug') remain in VerletKokkos::run() at lines 350-352, 359-361, 371-373 and 379-381.
evidence: verlet_kokkos.cpp:350-352 '// added debug / //atomKK->sync(Host,ALL_MASK); / //atomKK->modified(Host,ALL_MASK);' and three more identical blocks. Project review rules: commented-out code added for debugging purposes should be removed entirely.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; release-hygiene item flagged by the project's own review checklist.
suggested_fix: Delete the four commented-out debug blocks.

summary: In non-GPU-aware mode remap_3d_kokkos() re-creates the host mirrors of the scratch and send buffers with Kokkos::create_mirror_view() on every call, i.e. a fresh host allocation of the full scratch size for each of the several remaps per FFT per timestep.
evidence: remap_kokkos.cpp:123-128: 'if (!plan->usegpu_aware) { plan->h_scratch = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_scratch); plan->h_sendbuf = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(plan->d_sendbuf); ... }' executed unconditionally at the top of every remap_3d_kokkos() call; on a GPU backend create_mirror_view allocates (d_scratch is not host accessible). The plan struct keeps h_scratch/h_sendbuf as members, so they could be allocated once (or resized when the extents change).
failure_scenario: PPPM/kk on a GPU without GPU-aware MPI: each timestep performs 4 remaps per 3d FFT (2-3 FFTs), each allocating and freeing a host buffer of nqty*out.isize*out.jsize*out.ksize FFT_SCALARs; pure overhead, no wrong results.
suggested_fix: Allocate h_scratch/h_sendbuf once in remap_3d_create_plan_kokkos (or lazily when their extent differs from the device view), not on every call.

summary: The extent check in the TransposeHelperKokkos constructor compares the destination's second extent with itself instead of with the source, so a mismatched extent(1) is never caught.
evidence: transpose_helper_kokkos.h:78: 'assert(d_dst.extent(0) == d_src.extent(0) && d_dst.extent(1) == d_dst.extent(1));' -- the second operand is trivially true; intended is 'd_dst.extent(1) == d_src.extent(1)'.
failure_scenario: A caller passing views whose second extents differ (e.g. after a maxneighs change on only one of them) is not caught in debug builds; the transpose then reads or writes out of bounds instead of asserting. No effect on release builds (assert compiled out).
suggested_fix: Change the second comparison to d_src.extent(1).

summary: All eight pack/unpack functors decompose the flat Kokkos index so that the SLOW index varies fastest across threads, giving fully uncoalesced device loads and stores in every FFT remap.
evidence: pack_kokkos.h:73-76 (and identically at 128-131, 184-187, 238-241, 296-299, 351-354, 405-408, 461-464): 'const int fast = index / (nslow * nmid); const int index_new = index - (fast * nslow * nmid); const int mid = index_new / nslow; const int slow = index_new % nslow;'. Consecutive Kokkos indices therefore differ in 'slow', and the addresses used are 'd_buf[in_orig + mid*nfast + fast]' with in_orig = slow*nmid*nfast and 'd_data[plane + mid*nstride_line + fast]' with plane = slow*nstride_plane (line 77-82): adjacent threads are nmid*nfast resp. nstride_plane elements apart. The contiguous direction is 'fast' (src/pack.h:71 'for (fast = 0; ...) buf[in++] = data[out++]'), which here is the SLOWEST-varying thread index.
failure_scenario: No wrong results. On a GPU backend every remap in every 3d FFT (4 remaps per FFT, several FFTs per PPPM step) runs at a fraction of the achievable bandwidth because neither the read nor the write is coalesced.
suggested_fix: Swap the decomposition so 'fast' is the fastest-varying index (slow = index/(nmid*nfast); mid = (index/nfast)%nmid; fast = index%nfast), or use an MDRangePolicy with the fast index innermost.

summary: pack_kokkos.h has no include guard and includes the guard-less src/pack.h purely for 'struct pack_plan_3d', dragging ten unused static host functions into every translation unit that includes it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h has no '#ifndef LMP_PACK_KOKKOS_H'; line 18 '#include "pack.h"'. src/pack.h likewise has no include guard and, under the default FFT_PACK_ARRAY (pack.h:25-27), defines pack_3d, unpack_3d and the six unpack_3d_permute* functions as file-static (pack.h:55-264). Including either header twice in one translation unit is a redefinition error; today only src/KOKKOS/remap_kokkos.cpp includes pack_kokkos.h, so this is latent.
failure_scenario: A future file including pack_kokkos.h together with pack.h (or including pack_kokkos.h twice through another header) fails to compile; meanwhile every build emits unused-static-function warnings for the ten CPU pack routines.
suggested_fix: Add '#ifndef LMP_PACK_KOKKOS_H' guards to both headers, and move 'struct pack_plan_3d' into its own small header (or forward-declare it) so pack_kokkos.h does not pull in the CPU implementations.

summary: SNAKokkos::compute_dsfac(), a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION, calls unqualified sin()/cos() instead of Kokkos::sin/Kokkos::cos, violating the KOKKOS device-math rule and silently promoting single-precision arguments to double; the function is also dead code.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:2265 'dsfac_outer = -onehalf * sin((r - rmin0) * rcutfac) * rcutfac;', :2283 'sfac_outer = onehalf * (cos((r - rmin0) * rcutfac) + one);', :2290 'sfac_inner = onehalf * (one - cos(static_cast<real_type>(MY_PI2) + (r - sinner) * rcutfac));', :2291 'dsfac_inner = onehalf * rcutfac * sin(...);'. The sibling routines do it correctly: compute_sfac uses 'Kokkos::cos' (:2231) and compute_s_dsfac uses 'Kokkos::sin'/'Kokkos::cos' (:2316-2317, :2328-2329). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ... never std::'. Grepping the package shows compute_dsfac is never called (only compute_sfac at :846 and compute_s_dsfac at :374 and :1832 are used).
failure_scenario: No current runtime effect because the function is unreachable; if it is ever wired back in, a SYCL/HIP build may fail to resolve the unqualified name and a real_type=float build loses precision through double promotion.
suggested_fix: Either delete compute_dsfac (and its declaration at sna_kokkos.h:372) since compute_s_dsfac supersedes it, or qualify the four calls with Kokkos::.

summary: sna_kokkos.h declares three member functions and one data member that have no definition and no caller anywhere in the tree.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos.h:482-486 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void create_team_scratch_arrays(const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team); ... void create_thread_scratch_arrays(const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team);' and :246-247 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION SNAKokkos(const SNAKokkos<DeviceType, real_type, accum_type, vector_length>& sna, const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team);' -- none of the three is defined in sna_kokkos_impl.h nor referenced anywhere ('grep -rn create_team_scratch_arrays src/' matches only this declaration). :409 'int twojmax, diagonalstyle;' -- diagonalstyle is never assigned or read (it is a leftover from the removed 'diagonal' SNAP option).
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; dead declarations mislead readers into thinking there is a team-scratch constructor path, and the uninitialized diagonalstyle member is a false lead when debugging.
suggested_fix: Delete the three declarations and the diagonalstyle member.

summary: memory_usage() selects the GPU vs CPU array set with 'if constexpr (!host_flag)' while grow_rij() allocates them under '!host_flag && !legacy_on_gpu', so with legacy_on_gpu enabled the reported memory omits the two largest arrays and counts five 1x1x1 dummies instead.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:323-339 'if (!host_flag && !legacy_on_gpu) { ...realloc a_gpu/b_gpu/da_gpu/db_gpu/sfac_gpu at full size...; realloc ulist_cpu/dulist_cpu at 1,1,1; } else { ...a_gpu etc at 1,1(,1)...; realloc ulist_cpu/dulist_cpu at natom_pad, nmax, idxu_cache_max; }' versus :2360-2369 'if constexpr (!host_flag) { bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(a_gpu); ... } else { bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(ulist_cpu); bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(dulist_cpu); }'. legacy_on_gpu is a runtime member (sna_kokkos.h:474) initialised from the owner (pair_snap_kokkos.h:87 'static constexpr bool legacy_on_gpu = false;'), so the two conditions only agree while that knob stays false.
failure_scenario: Flip pair_snap_kokkos.h's legacy_on_gpu to true (its documented purpose: 'run the CPU path on the GPU') and 'info memory'/the pair style's memory_usage() under-reports by natom_pad*nmax*idxu_cache_max*sizeof(complex)*4, the dominant allocation. No wrong physics.
suggested_fix: Use the same predicate in memory_usage(): 'if constexpr (!host_flag) if (!legacy_on_gpu) {gpu arrays} else {cpu arrays}', or factor the predicate into a single helper used by both.

summary: sna_kokkos_impl.h redefines MY_PI and MY_PI2 as file-static doubles directly in namespace LAMMPS_NS instead of using MathConst, giving every translation unit its own copy and setting up an ambiguity with MathConst::MY_PI.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:29-30 'static const double MY_PI  = 3.14159265358979323846; // pi' and 'static const double MY_PI2  = 1.57079632679489661923; // pi/2', inside 'namespace LAMMPS_NS {' (line 27). src/math_const.h already provides LAMMPS_NS::MathConst::MY_PI and MY_PI2 with the same values; the CPU counterpart src/ML-SNAP/sna.cpp:23,31 does '#include "math_const.h"' + 'using namespace MathConst;'. Because this header is pulled into pair_snap_kokkos.cpp, compute_sna_grid_kokkos.cpp and compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.cpp, any of those adding 'using namespace MathConst;' would make an unqualified MY_PI ambiguous.
failure_scenario: No current runtime effect. A later edit that adds 'using namespace MathConst;' to any TU including sna_kokkos.h fails to compile with an ambiguous-name error that points at an unrelated line.
suggested_fix: Delete the two definitions and use MathConst::MY_PI / MathConst::MY_PI2 (already available via math_const.h).

summary: get_optimal_combination_idx() seeds opt_perf with the raw sample performance[0][0] instead of the representative value of combination 0, so in AVERAGE/MEDIAN mode opt_perf can be a single outlier sample that no combination's representative value beats; the returned index is then 0 with an inflated opt_perf, and regular_performance_check() later measures every real performance against it and can trigger spurious re-scans.
evidence: tune_kokkos.cpp:465-466 'opt_perf = performance[0][0]; int opt_idx = 0;' followed by the loop computing p_i (max/average/median per combination) and 'if (p_i > opt_perf) { opt_perf = p_i; opt_idx = i; }' (496-499). With mode AVERAGE_VALUE or MEDIAN_VALUE, p_0 <= max sample of row 0, so a large performance[0][0] is never replaced. regular_performance_check(): 'diff = (opt_perf - perf)/opt_perf; if (diff > relative_tolerance) ... re-scan' (543-573).
failure_scenario: tune mode 'average' or 'median' with a noisy first sample of the first combination (e.g. a step right after setup): opt_perf is the outlier, every later check reports the performance as degraded, and the tuner keeps re-scanning instead of settling.
suggested_fix: Initialize opt_perf to the representative value of combination 0 (compute p_0 first) or to -1.0 so the loop always assigns it.

summary: ThirdOrderKokkos::update_force() treats only styles with execution_space == Host as host styles, whereas VerletKokkos::host_force_styles() also treats HostKK (the kk/host variants); a kk/host pair style combined with a device bonded style therefore never gets its forces merged into the device force array.
evidence: third_order_kokkos.cpp:172-207 test 'force->pair->execution_space==Host' (and the same for bond/angle/dihedral/improper/kspace); verlet_kokkos.cpp:697-702 uses '(style->execution_space != HostKK) && (style->execution_space != Host)' to decide. With a HostKK pair style: modified(HostKK,F_MASK) at line 222, then a device bond style does modified(Device,F_MASK) at 243; the DualView's later sync(Host,F_MASK) at 308 copies device -> host and discards the pair forces (no merge, since execute_on_host is false). dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp has the same structure (not in this group).
failure_scenario: GPU build, 'pair_style lj/cut/kk/host' + 'bond_style harmonic/kk' + 'third_order ...': the third-order force constants miss the pair contribution. Unusual combination; the plain Host and plain Device cases are handled.
suggested_fix: Use the same HostKK-or-Host predicate (or reuse VerletKokkos::host_force_styles logic) in ThirdOrderKokkos and DynamicalMatrixKokkos.

summary: dihedral_style hybrid/kk keeps the base class default centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL while every KOKKOS dihedral sub-style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL, so with a centroid/stress/atom compute the hybrid enters its cvflag_atom branch and dereferences styles[m]->cvatom, which the sub-styles never allocate (nullptr).
failure_scenario: 'dihedral_style hybrid/kk harmonic opls' plus 'compute p all centroid/stress/atom NULL' and a thermo/dump referencing it: on the first force evaluation cvatom_substyle is nullptr and the inner loop segfaults. Even without the crash the sub-styles' per-atom virial is silently dropped, because the hybrid's own vflag_atom stays 0 while the sub-styles fill vatom.
suggested_fix: Set centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL in the DihedralHybridKokkos constructor (matching all KOKKOS sub-styles), or make init_style() derive the hybrid's flag from the sub-styles and skip/guard the cvatom accumulation when a sub-style did not produce cvatom. The same shape exists in angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:144 and improper_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:146.

summary: allocate_kokkos() calls DualView::resize() without first forcing the host copy to be the newest, so on a GPU build a dihedral_coeff issued after a run (when the dual views are in the 'device up to date' state) silently zeroes the host mirror and then that zeroed mirror is copied back over the device coefficients.
failure_scenario: GPU build (host and device memory spaces differ). Input: 'dihedral_style fourier/kk; dihedral_coeff 1 2 ...; dihedral_coeff 2 2 ...; run 100; dihedral_coeff 3 4 ... (nterms_max grows from 2 to 4); run 100'. In the second run all dihedral types except type 3 have k/cos_shift/sin_shift/multiplicity = 0, so their dihedral energies and forces silently become zero.
suggested_fix: Call sync_host()/modify_host() (or simply k_*.sync_host() followed by modify_host()) on each dual view before resizing, or pass Kokkos::view_alloc(Kokkos::SequentialHostInit) / reallocate and refill all types after a resize, so the host mirror is authoritative when resize() runs.

summary: Eight of the dihedral KOKKOS styles declare Q_MASK in datamask_read although none of them ever reads atom->q, so VerletKokkos performs a needless charge sync around every dihedral compute.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:44 'datamask_read = X_MASK | F_MASK | Q_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK;' and the same line in dihedral_class2_kokkos.cpp:45, dihedral_class2xe_kokkos.cpp:46, dihedral_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.cpp:46, dihedral_cosine_squared_restricted_kokkos.cpp:48, dihedral_fourier_kokkos.cpp:46, dihedral_helix_kokkos.cpp:49 and dihedral_multi_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:45. Grepping those eight .cpp/.h pairs for 'k_q' or 'q[i' returns zero hits -- only dihedral_charmm_kokkos.cpp (line 109 'q = atomKK->k_q.view<DeviceType>();') and dihedral_charmmfsw_kokkos.cpp:116 actually read charge. src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:173 'atomKK->sync(force->dihedral->execution_space,force->dihedral->datamask_read);' is what consumes the mask. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md requires datamask_read to be 'exactly the per-atom arrays the style reads and writes'.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers; on a GPU build with a charged system the q dual view is considered part of the dihedral's read set every step, which can force extra host/device traffic and masks a genuine mask error if one is ever introduced.
suggested_fix: Drop Q_MASK from datamask_read in the eight styles that do not touch atom->q, keeping it only in dihedral_charmm_kokkos and dihedral_charmmfsw_kokkos.

summary: The neighbor-list error message in dihedral charmmfsw/kk names the wrong style ('charmm/kk'), which will misdirect a user who is running charmmfsw/kk.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_charmmfsw_kokkos.cpp:83-84 'if (lmp->kokkos->neighflag == FULL)\n    error->all(FLERR,"Dihedral_style charmm/kk requires half neighbor list");' -- copy-pasted verbatim from src/KOKKOS/dihedral_charmm_kokkos.cpp:76-77 without renaming the style.
failure_scenario: User runs 'dihedral_style charmmfsw/kk' with '-pk kokkos neigh full' and is told that 'Dihedral_style charmm/kk' is at fault, a style not present in the input.
suggested_fix: Change the message text to 'Dihedral_style charmmfsw/kk requires half neighbor list'.

summary: pair zbl/kk scales the ZBL force and energy by special_lj[sbmask(j)], while the CPU pair zbl (and the /omp and /gpu variants) deliberately ignore the special-bond factors, so the /kk variant gives different forces/energies for 1-2, 1-3 and 1-4 pairs that remain in the neighbor list.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_zbl_kokkos.cpp:148-151 fills `special_lj[0..3] = force->special_lj[...]`, and the generic driver applies it: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:156-166 `const KK_FLOAT factor_lj = c.special_lj[sbmask(j)]; j &= NEIGHMASK; ... const KK_FLOAT fpair = factor_lj*c.template compute_fpair<...>(rsq,i,j,itype,jtype);` and :181 `evdwl = factor_lj * c.template compute_evdwl<...>(...)`.  The CPU base src/pair_zbl.cpp:105-144 does `j = jlist[jj]; j &= NEIGHMASK;` and never reads force->special_lj -- `grep -n 'special_lj\|factor_lj' src/pair_zbl.cpp` returns nothing; the same is true of src/OPENMP/pair_zbl_omp.cpp:114 and lib/gpu/lal_zbl.cu.
failure_scenario: A molecular system with a kspace solver (Neighbor::init then forces special_flag[1..3]=2, so 1-2/1-3/1-4 pairs stay in the list carrying their sbmask bits) and `special_bonds lj 0.0 0.0 0.5`: pair zbl computes the full ZBL repulsion on those pairs, pair zbl/kk multiplies it by 0.0/0.0/0.5, so CPU and KOKKOS runs of the same input give different forces and energies.
suggested_fix: Decide which behaviour is intended and make the two agree: either set `special_lj[1..3] = 1.0` in PairZBLKokkos::compute() to match the CPU style, or add the factor_lj handling to pair_zbl.cpp/pair_zbl_omp.cpp/lib/gpu and document the change.

summary: dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos, dihedral_quadratic_kokkos and dihedral_spherical_kokkos (and ~42 other KOKKOS style files) have no `action` line in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, so a traditional-make `make yes-kokkos` build never installs them and the /kk styles are missing from lmp_serial/lmp_mpi.
evidence: `grep -n 'nharmonic\|quadratic\|spherical' src/KOKKOS/Install.sh` returns nothing, while the sibling styles are registered at src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:150-169 (`action dihedral_fourier_kokkos.cpp dihedral_fourier.cpp`, `action dihedral_table_kokkos.cpp dihedral_table.cpp`, `action dihedral_opls_kokkos.cpp dihedral_opls.cpp`, ...).  A full sweep (`for f in src/KOKKOS/*_kokkos.cpp; do grep -q "^action $(basename $f)" Install.sh || echo $f; done`) lists 45 unregistered files, among them dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_quadratic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, dihedral_spherical_kokkos.{cpp,h}.  This violates rule 5 of .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md.
failure_scenario: `cd src && make yes-kokkos && make serial` then an input with `dihedral_style nharmonic/kk` -> "Unknown dihedral style" (the CMake build is unaffected because it globs the package directory, so CI does not catch this).
suggested_fix: Add the missing `action <file>_kokkos.cpp <base>.cpp` / `.h` lines to src/KOKKOS/Install.sh (base file name given because the bases live in EXTRA-MOLECULE), and audit the other 42 unregistered files at the same time.

summary: allocate_kokkos() grows k_a with DualView::resize() while both sides are in sync, which on a GPU build resizes the device view and re-creates a zero-initialized host mirror, silently wiping the coefficients of all previously defined dihedral types.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos.cpp:345-351 `if (!allocated_kokkos) { k_a = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d(...,n+1,nterms_max); ... } else { k_a.resize(n+1,nterms_max); ... }`; coeff() (lines 364-380) then only re-fills rows ilo..ihi of `k_a.view_host()` and calls `k_a.modify_host()`, so rows outside that range come from the freshly created host mirror.  lib/kokkos/containers/src/Kokkos_DualView.hpp:1027-1030 `if (modified_flags(1) >= modified_flags(0)) resize_on_device(arg_prop);` and :962-973 resize_on_device -> resync_host() -> :1044 `h_view = create_mirror_view(typename t_host::memory_space(), d_view);` (a brand-new, zero-filled host allocation, no copy).  After a `run` the compute() `k_a.template sync<DeviceType>()` (line 96) makes both flags equal, so the very next coeff() that raises nterms_max takes the device branch.
failure_scenario: dihedral_style nharmonic/kk; dihedral_coeff 1 3 a0 a1 a2; run 100; dihedral_coeff 2 5 b0..b4  ->  nterms_max grows 3->5, k_a is resized on the device, the host mirror is replaced by zeros, only row 2 is refilled, and after the following sync<DeviceType>() type 1 has all-zero coefficients: zero dihedral energy and forces for type 1 with no warning.
suggested_fix: Do not rely on resize() to preserve data across the host/device split: after resizing, re-fill the whole host mirror from the CPU-side `a`/`nterms` arrays for all types 1..ndihedraltypes (as read_restart already does), or call k_a.sync_host()/modify_host() before resizing so the host branch is taken.

summary: allocate_kokkos() grows the 2d coefficient DualViews with resize() while host and device are in sync; on a GPU build that resizes the device view and replaces the host mirror with a fresh zero-filled allocation, wiping the coefficients of all previously defined dihedral types.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_spherical_kokkos.cpp:473-485 `} else { k_nterms.resize(n+1); k_Ccoeff.resize(n+1,nterms_max); ... }`; coeff() at :524-538 only refills rows ilo..ihi of the host mirrors before k_*.modify_host() at :540-550.  lib/kokkos/containers/src/Kokkos_DualView.hpp:1027-1029 `if (modified_flags(1) >= modified_flags(0)) resize_on_device(...)` and :1044 `h_view = create_mirror_view(typename t_host::memory_space(), d_view);` -- a new, zero-initialized host allocation with no copy from the old host data.  compute() line 95-105 syncs all views to the device, which equalizes the flags and makes the next resize take the device branch.
failure_scenario: dihedral_style spherical/kk; dihedral_coeff 1 1 <10 args>; run 100; dihedral_coeff 2 2 <20 args>  -> nterms_max grows 1->2, all k_* 2d views resize on device, their host mirrors are zeroed, only row 2 is refilled, and the following sync<DeviceType>() pushes zeros for type 1: type-1 dihedrals silently contribute zero energy and force.
suggested_fix: After a resize, refill the complete host mirror for all types 1..ndihedraltypes from the CPU-side arrays (as read_restart already does), or sync the DualViews to host before resizing so resize takes the host-preserving branch.

summary: setup_tables() unconditionally copies tb->de, tb->df (and tb->f when NOF is used) into device views, but DihedralTable::compute_table() only fills those arrays for tabstyle LINEAR, so for tabstyle spline the copy reads uninitialized heap memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_table_kokkos.cpp:372-379 `for (int i = 0; i < tablength; i++) { k_e.view_host()(m,i)=...; k_de.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->de[i]); k_f_tab.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->f[i]); k_df.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->df[i]); ... }`.  src/MOLECULE/dihedral_table.cpp:1113-1119 allocates phi/e/de/f/df/e2/f2 with memory->create (uninitialized), and only the `else if (tabstyle == LINEAR)` branch at :1131-1164 fills de[] and df[]; the SPLINE branch at :1121-1130 fills only e[] (and f[] when !f_unspecified).
failure_scenario: dihedral_style table/kk spline N with a table file: setup_tables reads tablength*ntables uninitialized doubles per table (de, df, and f under NOF). Harmless in the kernel (the spline branch never reads d_de/d_df), but it is an uninitialized read that valgrind/MSan flags, and the double->float narrowing of garbage values is undefined behaviour in a KOKKOS single-precision build.
suggested_fix: Only copy de/df when tabstyle == LINEAR (and f when !tb->f_unspecified), or zero-initialize those arrays in DihedralTable::compute_table().

summary: setup_tables() unconditionally copies tb->de, tb->df and tb->f into device views, but for tabstyle spline those arrays are never filled by DihedralTable::compute_table(), so the copy reads uninitialized heap memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_table_cut_kokkos.cpp:467-474 `for (int i = 0; i < tablength; i++) { ... k_de.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->de[i]); k_f_tab.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->f[i]); k_df.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->df[i]); ... }`.  src/MOLECULE/dihedral_table.cpp:1113-1119 allocates these with memory->create (no initialization) and fills de/df only in the `else if (tabstyle == LINEAR)` branch (:1131-1164).  src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/dihedral_table_cut.cpp:~1295 states it explicitly: "If the user did not specify the forces now, AND the user selected the spline option ... THEN the tb->f array is uninitialized".
failure_scenario: dihedral_style table/cut spline N ... with a NOF table: setup_tables reads ntables*tablength uninitialized doubles (de, df, f). The kernel never uses them in the spline branch, so results are correct, but it is an uninitialized read (valgrind/MSan) and narrowing garbage doubles to float in a single-precision KOKKOS build is undefined behaviour.
suggested_fix: Guard the copies: only fill k_de/k_df when tabstyle == LINEAR and k_f_tab/k_f2 when !tb->f_unspecified, or zero those arrays in DihedralTable::compute_table().

summary: The Kokkos kernel does not apply the minimum-image convention to the three bond vectors, while the CPU base style does.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_spherical_kokkos.cpp:248-252 `for (int d = 0; d < g_dim; ++d) { vb12[d] = x(i2,d) - x(i1,d); vb23[d] = ...; vb34[d] = ...; }` with no remapping.  src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/dihedral_spherical.cpp:111-120 does the same subtraction and then `domain->minimum_image(FLERR, vb12[0], vb12[1], vb12[2]); domain->minimum_image(FLERR, vb23[...]); domain->minimum_image(FLERR, vb34[...]);`
failure_scenario: A configuration in which a dihedral bond vector computed from the stored (ghost) coordinates is longer than half a box length: the CPU style remaps it, the /kk style does not, so the two give different phi/theta and different forces.
suggested_fix: Either replicate the minimum-image remapping in the device kernel (using the domain data already exported to Kokkos, cf. other styles), or document/confirm that ghost coordinates make the remapping a no-op and drop it from the CPU style as well.

summary: The region /kk device kernels call unqualified sqrt()/sin()/cos() instead of the Kokkos:: math functions the package rules require for device code.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/region_block_kokkos.h:273 `contact[n].r = sqrt(delx * delx + dely * dely + delz * delz);` and :319-320 `double sine = sin(angle); double cosine = cos(angle);` inside KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION members; the same appears in region_cone_kokkos.h:85,91,97,122,123, region_cylinder_kokkos.h:85,90,95,119,120, region_ellipsoid_kokkos.h:121,122, region_plane_kokkos.h:104,105, region_prism_kokkos.h:106,107 and region_sphere_kokkos.h:131,155,179,193,229,230.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: "Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels (Kokkos::sqrt, Kokkos::exp, Kokkos::pow, Kokkos::log, ...)"; the dihedral kernels reviewed alongside these files all use Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::sin / Kokkos::cos.
failure_scenario: Compiles today on the CUDA/HIP backends (the global ::sqrt has device overloads there), but it is the documented portability hazard for other backends and is inconsistent with the rest of the package.
suggested_fix: Replace the unqualified sqrt/sin/cos calls in the seven region_*_kokkos.h device functions with Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::sin / Kokkos::cos.

summary: update_box() syncs x to the host BEFORE calling the base class and marks the host modified AFTER it, but the base class updates x on the DEVICE in between (DomainKokkos::x2lamda/lamda2x), so the trailing modified(Host,ALL_MASK) makes the stale pre-deform host coordinates newer than the remapped device coordinates and the next sync to device reverts every atom position.
failure_scenario: `fix deform ... remap x` (the default) together with any rigid fix (rfix is filled with every fix whose rigid_flag is set, src/fix_deform.cpp:693-696) in a KOKKOS GPU run: on every deform step the device receives the coordinates as they were before the affine remap, so atoms are not rescaled with the box, the system immediately develops overlaps/lost atoms and the trajectory is wrong. In a Kokkos debug build (KOKKOS_ENABLE_DEBUG_DUALVIEW_MODIFY_CHECK) it instead aborts with a concurrent host/device modification error.
suggested_fix: Drop the ALL_MASK bracket entirely (Fix::deform() only transforms the fix-owned xcm arrays, not per-atom data -- see src/RIGID/fix_rigid.cpp:1285-1293), or, if a host bracket is really wanted, narrow it to the fields the rigid fixes read and place the sync/modified pair around only the `ifix->deform()` loops rather than around the device x2lamda/lamda2x calls.

summary: The per-type mass array is read on the device without ever syncing atomKK->k_mass, which is only ever marked modify_host(); on a GPU the kernel therefore reads a zero-initialized device view, massinv becomes infinite and the computed timestep collapses to 0.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_dt_reset_kokkos.cpp:62 syncs only `V_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK | TYPE_MASK | RMASS_MASK` -- there is no mask bit for the per-type mass -- and line 71 then does `mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();`, used at line 123 `massinv = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0) / mass[type[i]];` inside the device kernel. `grep -n 'k_mass' src/KOKKOS/fix_dt_reset_kokkos.cpp` yields only that one line: no `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()` anywhere in the file or its header. k_mass is only ever marked host-modified: src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:313-316 (`create_kokkos(k_mass,mass,ntypes+1,...)` followed by `k_mass.modify_host()`) and the four AtomKokkos::set_mass overloads at atom_kokkos.cpp:287,293,299,305. The required idiom is src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();`, also used by compute_temp_kokkos.cpp:46, compute_ke_atom_kokkos.cpp:68, fix_flow_gauss_kokkos.cpp, group_kokkos.h:64 and a dozen others.
failure_scenario: GPU run with a per-type-mass atom style and `fix dt/reset/kk` but no other /kk style that happens to sync k_mass first (e.g. plain `fix nve` without the kk suffix, or `fix nve/limit/kk`, which also never syncs it): the device k_mass view is the zero-filled allocation, so massinv = 1/0 = inf, dtf = sqrt(2*xmax/(ftm2v*sqrt(fsq)*inf)) = 0, dt reduces to 0 and update->dt is set to 0 (or to tmin), stalling the run. With rmass styles the code is unaffected because RMASS_MASK is in the sync list.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();` to FixDtResetKokkos::init() (or immediately before line 71), exactly as fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 does.

summary: The per-type mass array is read on the device without ever syncing atomKK->k_mass, which is only ever marked modify_host(), so on a GPU the kernel reads a zero-initialized device view and every atom's kinetic energy comes out as 0.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_electron_stopping_kokkos.cpp:41 lists `X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | TYPE_MASK | TAG_MASK | MASK_MASK | RMASS_MASK` -- there is no mask bit for the per-type mass -- and line 84 does `d_mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();`, used at line 143 `double massone = (d_rmass.data()) ? ... : static_cast<double>(d_mass(itype));` inside the device kernel. `grep -n 'k_mass' src/KOKKOS/fix_electron_stopping_kokkos.cpp` returns only line 84: no sync anywhere. k_mass is only ever marked host-modified (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:313-316 and the set_mass overloads at 287,293,299,305), so every consumer must sync it itself; the correct idiom is src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();`, and it is followed by compute_temp_kokkos.cpp:46, compute_ke_atom_kokkos.cpp:68, group_kokkos.h:64, fix_flow_gauss_kokkos.cpp etc. The CPU base reads the host array directly: src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_electron_stopping.cpp:172 `double massone = (atom->rmass) ? atom->rmass[i] : atom->mass[itype];`.
failure_scenario: GPU run of `fix electron/stopping/kk` on a per-type-mass atom style (the normal case for the radiation-damage workflows this fix targets) without another /kk style that happens to sync k_mass first: d_mass(itype) reads the zero-filled device allocation, so energy = 0.5*mvv2e*0*v2 = 0, every atom fails the `energy < Ecut` test and NO electronic stopping force is ever applied -- the fix silently does nothing and SeLoss stays 0.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();` in FixElectronStoppingKokkos::init() (or right before line 84), as fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 does.

summary: The table temperature bounds lo and hi are stored in INTEGER Kokkos views in all three table structs, so the double bounds read from the EOS table file are truncated toward zero; every table index and every clamp in energy_lookup/temperature_lookup is then computed from the wrong lower bound.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.h:93,99,105 all declare `typename AT::t_int_1d lo,hi;` / `HAT::t_int_1d lo,hi;`, while the CPU struct is src/DPD-REACT/fix_eos_table_rx.h:44-51 `struct Table { int ninput; double lo, hi; ... }` with src/DPD-REACT/fix_eos_table_rx.cpp:108-109 `tb->lo = tb->rfile[0]; tb->hi = tb->rfile[tb->ninput-1];` -- the first and last TEMPERATURE in the table file. The truncation happens at src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:563-564 `h_table->lo[i] = tb->lo; h_table->hi[i] = tb->hi;` (double -> int). The truncated value is then used for the index arithmetic at fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:348-354 `thetai = MAX(thetai,d_table_const.lo(ispecies)); thetai = MIN(thetai,d_table_const.hi(ispecies)); itable = static_cast<int>((thetai - d_table_const.lo(ispecies)) * d_table_const.invdelta(ispecies));` whereas invdelta is still the correct double (fix_eos_table_rx.cpp:465-466 `tb->delta = (tb->hi - tb->lo)/tlm1`). That this is a copy-paste slip is visible in the parent it was cloned from: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.h:71-92 has `t_int_1d nshiftbits,nmask;` in that slot and keeps the physical quantities as `t_double_1d innersq,invdelta,deltasq6;`.
failure_scenario: An EOS table whose first temperature is not an exact integer -- e.g. lo=0.5, hi=10.5, tablength=1000 so invdelta=99.9: lo is stored as 0 and hi as 10, thetai is clamped to [0,10] instead of [0.5,10.5], and for thetai=5.0 the code reads itable=499 instead of the correct 449, i.e. an energy from a completely different part of the table. At the top of the range itable reaches 999 while d_table_const.de only has tablength-1=999 entries (indices 0..998), so it also reads one element past the end of de. Every `fix eos/table/rx/kk` run with non-integer table bounds gets wrong internal energies/temperatures; the plain `fix eos/table/rx` gets them right.
suggested_fix: Change `lo,hi` to `typename AT::t_kkfloat_1d` / `HAT::t_kkfloat_1d` in all three structs (TableDeviceConst, TableDevice, TableHost) and cast with static_cast<KK_FLOAT> in create_kokkos_tables(), matching what pair_table_kokkos.h does for innersq/invdelta/deltasq6.

summary: temperature_lookup() copies the table bounds into local `int` variables, truncating them a second time and breaking the `if (t1==hi) delta = -delta;` test that tells the secant solver to search downward from the top of the table.
failure_scenario: A table with hi = 10.5: t1 is clamped to 10 and `t1 == hi` is compared against the int 10, so with a starting temperature at or above the table maximum the solver keeps delta positive and steps t2 = 1.001*t1 further outside the table instead of stepping back inside; energy_lookup then re-clamps and f2-f1 collapses, tripping the 'Secant solver did not converge because table bounds were exceeded' warning path and returning the clamped t1 rather than the correct temperature.
suggested_fix: Declare them as `KK_FLOAT lo = d_table_const.lo(0); KK_FLOAT hi = d_table_const.hi(0);` (together with the view type change in the header).

summary: FixEfield::update_efield_variables() evaluates equal- and atom-style variables on the host through the plain atom->x/atom->v pointers, but post_force only ever syncs to the device, so on a GPU the variables are evaluated against stale host coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_efield_kokkos.cpp:83 `atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read);` (execution_space == Device for efield/kk) is the only sync in the routine; line 158 then calls `FixEfield::update_efield_variables();`, which at src/fix_efield.cpp:504-522 runs `input->variable->compute_equal(xvar)` / `input->variable->compute_atom(xvar, igroup, &efield[0][0], 4, 0)`. Variable evaluation goes straight to atom->x / atom->v / any non-KOKKOS compute on the host (there is no atomKK reference anywhere in src/variable.cpp), and auto_sync is 0 for the whole run (verlet_kokkos.cpp:311) with ModifyKokkos::post_force only re-enabling it for fixes that are NOT kokkosable. The rest of the package does this correctly: fix_aveforce_kokkos.cpp:85 `atomKK->sync(Host, ALL_MASK);` immediately before its compute_equal calls at 87-89, fix_addtorque_group_kokkos.cpp:79 the same before 81-83, and fix_damping_cundall_kokkos.cpp:89 `atomKK->sync(Host,ALL_MASK);` before its compute_atom at line 90.
failure_scenario: GPU run of `fix efield/kk` with a position-dependent field, e.g. `variable ez atom 0.5*z` + `fix f all efield/kk 0.0 0.0 v_ez`: atom->x on the host was last refreshed at setup (or at the last dump), so every step the field is computed from the setup-time coordinates and the applied force is wrong; the same applies to `energy`/`potential` atom-style variables and to any equal-style variable that pulls in a non-KOKKOS per-atom compute.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->sync(Host, ALL_MASK);` immediately before the FixEfield::update_efield_variables() call (as fix_aveforce_kokkos.cpp:85 does). The same omission exists in fix_addforce_kokkos.cpp:139-151 and fix_addtorque_atom_kokkos.cpp:123-131, which should be fixed together.

summary: A leftover `|| 1` in the compute_X dispatch makes the condition always true, so the GPU team/scratch code path for compute_X is dead and every GPU run falls back to the serialized parallel_scan range policy.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_acks2_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:343 `if (execution_space == HostKK || 1) { // CPU`. The corresponding H-matrix dispatch 40 lines above is correct: line 303 `if (execution_space == HostKK) { // CPU`, and fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:579 also uses the plain `if (execution_space == HostKK)`. Because of `|| 1` the `else` block at lines 354-376 (FixACKS2ReaxFFKokkosComputeXFunctor team launch, plus its `Kokkos::deep_copy(d_mfill_offset,0)`) can never execute.
failure_scenario: Any GPU run of `fix acks2/reaxff/kk`: compute_X is executed with `Kokkos::parallel_scan(nn, ...)` over a RangePolicy on the device, which serializes the neighbor loop per atom instead of using the team/vector kernel, giving a large slowdown on the X-matrix build. It also means compute_x_team has been shipped untested; note that if it were re-enabled it contains a race, `a_X_diag[i] -= X_val` at line 1156 is executed by all 32 vector lanes of a ThreadVectorRange with a non-atomic accessor when NEIGHFLAG==FULL.
suggested_fix: Drop the `|| 1` so the team path is used on device, and re-verify compute_x_team (in particular make the `a_X_diag[i]` update at line 1156 a per-thread accumulation or an atomic) before enabling it.

summary: The KOKKOS constructor re-creates all of the base class's plain arrays as dual views without first freeing the base allocations, orphaning ~4 MB per MPI rank (12 arrays: g_axis, the four cmap grids, num_crossterm and the six crossterm_* arrays).
evidence: src/MOLECULE/fix_cmap.cpp:94-98 allocates `g_axis`, `cmapgrid`, `d1cmapgrid`, `d2cmapgrid`, `d12cmapgrid` with memory->create, and line 116 `FixCMAP::grow_arrays(atom->nmax)` allocates `num_crossterm` and `crossterm_type`/`crossterm_atom1..5` with memory->grow. src/KOKKOS/fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp:57-61 then calls `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_g_axis,g_axis,...)` etc. and line 82 calls `FixCMAPKokkos::grow_arrays(atom->nmax)` -> `memoryKK->grow_kokkos(...)`, with no `memory->destroy(...)` in between. memory_kokkos.h:69-76 `grow_kokkos` for a 1d array does `array = data.view_host().data();` (the old pointer is simply dropped), and memory_kokkos.h:223-242 for a 2d array only `srealloc`s the row-pointer block, so the base's contiguous data block (the old `array[0]`) is leaked. Compare fix_addforce_kokkos.cpp:125-126 and fix_acks2_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:93-94, which both call `memory->destroy(...)` immediately before handing the pointer to the KOKKOS allocator.
failure_scenario: Any `fix cmap/kk` run leaks 5 grid arrays (~110 KB) plus nmax*(4 + 6*4 + 5*6*8) bytes of per-atom arrays -- about 4.4 MB per rank at nmax = 16384 -- for the lifetime of the process; repeated fix/unfix or `clear` cycles accumulate it, and leak checkers in CI will flag it.
suggested_fix: Add `memory->destroy(g_axis); memory->destroy(cmapgrid); memory->destroy(d1cmapgrid); memory->destroy(d2cmapgrid); memory->destroy(d12cmapgrid);` before line 57 and `memory->destroy(num_crossterm); memory->destroy(crossterm_type); memory->destroy(crossterm_atom1..5);` before the grow_arrays() call at line 82.

summary: The KOKKOS constructor frees the base class's storque array and sets the pointer to nullptr but never allocates the replacement dual view, so `storque` stays null until `atom->nmax > maxatom` first becomes true; the atom-style variable path then dereferences a null pointer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_addtorque_atom_kokkos.cpp:115-116 `memory->destroy(storque); storque = nullptr;` -- no create_kokkos follows. src/GRANULAR/fix_addtorque_atom.cpp:99-100 leaves the base with `maxatom = 1; memory->create(storque, maxatom, 3, ...)`, and the KOKKOS class does not reset `maxatom`. The only allocation site is src/KOKKOS/fix_addtorque_atom_kokkos.cpp:169-174 `if (varflag == ATOM && atom->nmax > maxatom) { ... create_kokkos(k_storque,storque,maxatom,3,...) }`, which is skipped whenever `atom->nmax <= 1`. Line 193 then evaluates `&storque[0][0]`. The two sibling styles do it correctly: fix_addforce_kokkos.cpp:125-127 and fix_setforce_kokkos.cpp:43-44 both call `memory->destroy(sforce)` followed immediately by `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_sforce,sforce,maxatom,...)` in the constructor.
failure_scenario: A rank whose `atom->nmax` is still the 1 set by `AtomVec::grow(1)` in create_box.cpp:274 / atom.cpp:696 (a sub-domain that never owns or ghosts an atom) running `fix addtorque/atom/kk` with an atom-style variable: line 169's guard is false, `storque` is null, and `input->variable->compute_atom(xvar,igroup,&storque[0][0],3,0)` at line 193 dereferences null -> segfault. The plain CPU fix does not crash there because the base allocation survives.
suggested_fix: Follow fix_addforce_kokkos/fix_setforce_kokkos: in the constructor replace the base allocation with `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_storque,storque,maxatom,3,"addtorque/atom:storque"); d_storque = k_storque.view<DeviceType>();` right after `memory->destroy(storque)`.

summary: fix colvars/kk is a pure delegating wrapper (sync to host, call the CPU hook, mark modified) with no device kernel, which the package's FULL PORTS ONLY rule forbids and which names colvars as the example to leave unported.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_colvars_kokkos.cpp:79-93 is the whole implementation: `post_force` does `atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK|F_MASK|TAG_MASK|IMAGE_MASK); FixColvars::post_force(vflag); atomKK->modified(Host,F_MASK);` and `end_of_step` likewise; there is no Kokkos kernel anywhere in the file, and the constructor does not even set `execution_space`. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md, section 'FULL PORTS ONLY (project policy)': 'A /kk variant that just syncs to host, calls the CPU base-class hook, and marks modified is a fake port and is forbidden. ... If a fix's per-atom work genuinely cannot run on-device (host-only variable eval, plain double ** arrays like fix move's xoriginal, external library coupling like colvars), leave it unported rather than shipping a delegating wrapper.'
failure_scenario: No numerical error; the styles colvars/kk, colvars/kk/device and colvars/kk/host advertise GPU residency they do not provide, and each post_force forces a full x/f/tag/image device-to-host transfer. Functionally the syncs cover exactly what FixColvars::post_force (src/COLVARS/fix_colvars.cpp:560-563) and ::end_of_step (708-710) read, and setup() is covered because VerletKokkos::setup only clears auto_sync around modify->setup (verlet_kokkos.cpp:196-198) after everything was kept host-current, so this is a policy issue rather than a correctness one.
suggested_fix: Either delete the style per the stated policy, or add an explicit exemption note in the KOKKOS instructions if the maintainers intend to keep it.

summary: The region test is applied before the energy checks instead of after them, so an atom outside the region whose kinetic energy exceeds the stopping table no longer triggers the 'kinetic energy too high' error that the CPU fix raises.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_electron_stopping_kokkos.cpp:138-152 orders the tests mask -> numneigh -> `if (region && !d_match(i)) return;` -> energy -> `if (energy > d_elstop_ranges(0, table_entries-1)) { error_value = {i, energy}; return; }`. The CPU base does the opposite and says so explicitly: src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_electron_stopping.cpp:165-185 `// Do fast checks first, only then the region check` -- mask (166), numneigh (169), energy vs table max with `error->one(...)` (178-180), and only then `if (region) { if (region->match(...) != 1) continue; }` (182-185).
failure_scenario: An input with `fix electron/stopping ... region <r>` where a fast atom outside region r exceeds the tabulated energy range: the CPU fix aborts with 'kinetic energy too high for atom N', the /kk fix runs on silently. Forces are identical in both cases, so this only changes whether the user is told the table is too short.
suggested_fix: Move the `if (region && !d_match(i)) return;` test to after the `energy > d_elstop_ranges(0, table_entries-1)` check so the two versions raise the same error, or note the intentional difference in a comment.

summary: FixEnforce2DKokkos::setup() unconditionally calls post_force(), dropping the base class's rRESPA branch that zeroes the z force in every stored respa level array, and the style never rejects rRESPA the way its sibling /kk fixes do.
failure_scenario: CPU-only KOKKOS build, `-sf kk`, `run_style respa` with `fix enforce2d`: at setup the per-level force arrays keep whatever f_z they were given (e.g. from a fix langevin or an added force in an inner level), because the level loop that the CPU fix runs is skipped; Respa::sum_flevel_f then re-injects that z component on the first step of a 2d run.
suggested_fix: Either drop the setup() override so the base class version runs (post_force is virtual and will still dispatch to the KOKKOS kernel), or add an init() override that rejects rRESPA like the neighbouring /kk fixes do.

summary: The bounds guard on the crossterm list uses `>` where `>=` is needed, so an index equal to maxcrossterm would be written one element past the end of d_crosstermlist.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp:212 `if (l_ncrosstermlist > maxcrossterm) Kokkos::abort("l_ncrosstermlist > maxcrossterm");` followed at 214-219 by `d_crosstermlist(l_ncrosstermlist,0..5) = ...`. d_crosstermlist is allocated with exactly `maxcrossterm` rows at line 158 (`memoryKK->create_kokkos(d_crosstermlist,maxcrossterm,CMAPMAX,...)`), so the valid range is 0..maxcrossterm-1. The CPU base uses the correct comparison, src/MOLECULE/fix_cmap.cpp:279 `if (ncrosstermlist == maxcrossterm) { maxcrossterm += LISTDELTA; ... }`. Additionally the check runs before the `if(is_final)` branch, where in the non-final scan pass `l_ncrosstermlist` is only a per-thread partial offset, so it does not reliably guard anything.
failure_scenario: A rank whose local crossterm count reaches maxcrossterm (= ncmap) writes six ints past the end of d_crosstermlist without tripping the guard. Reaching that count requires one rank to own every crossterm in the system, so this is a latent rather than routinely-hit overflow.
suggested_fix: Change the comparison to `>=` and move it inside the `if (is_final)` branch so it tests the actual write index.

summary: The device-side minimum_image() applies at most a single box-length wrap per dimension (if/else if), whereas Domain::minimum_image() loops (while) until the separation is inside the half box, so a drag point more than ~1.5 box lengths from an atom gets a different image than the CPU fix.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_drag_kokkos.cpp:142-154 `if (m_xperiodic) { if (dx > m_xprd_half) dx -= m_xprd; else if (dx < -m_xprd_half) dx += m_xprd; }` (and the triclinic branch 155-180 likewise). src/domain.cpp Domain::minimum_image(const std::string&,int,double&,double&,double&) uses `while (fabs(dx) > xprd_half) { ... }` in every branch and additionally raises 'Atoms have moved too far apart ... for minimum image' when fabs(dx) > MAXIMGCOUNT*xprd. The CPU fix calls exactly that function: src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_drag.cpp:124 `domain->minimum_image(FLERR, dx,dy,dz);`.
failure_scenario: `fix drag` with a target point specified well outside the periodic box (e.g. box 0..100 and `fix drag all drag 350 50 50 1.0 0.1`): the CPU fix wraps dx three times and pulls atoms toward the nearest image of the target, the /kk fix wraps once and applies a drag force of the wrong direction/magnitude, so ftotal and the trajectory differ between the two. For a target inside the box the two agree.
suggested_fix: Replace the single conditional wraps with `while` loops (as in bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp/dihedral_table_kokkos.cpp, which have the same shortcut but where the separation is bounded), or document/enforce that the drag point must lie inside the box.

summary: The dynamic_cast to FixRxKokkos<DeviceType> is not checked for failure, so a fix rx whose KOKKOS instantiation does not match this fix's DeviceType leaves rx_fixKK null and init()/setup()/post_integrate() dereference it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:85 `rx_fixKK = dynamic_cast<FixRxKokkos<DeviceType> *>(rx_fix);` with no null test; it is then dereferenced unconditionally whenever rx_flag is set, at lines 121-122, 185-186 and 239-240 (`rx_fixKK->get_k_species_ind_to_atom_prop_ind()`). The base class only guarantees that rx_fix is a FixRX matching the style regex `^rx/kk` (src/DPD-REACT/fix_eos_table_rx.cpp:57-65), which covers both FixRxKokkos<LMPDeviceType> and FixRxKokkos<LMPHostType>. The sibling style shows the intended guard: src/KOKKOS/fix_dpd_energy_kokkos.cpp:35-37 `pairDPDEKK = dynamic_cast<decltype(pairDPDEKK)>(pairDPDE); if (!pairDPDEKK) error->all(FLERR,"Must use pair_style dpd/fdt/energy/kk with fix dpd/energy/kk");`.
failure_scenario: Mixing suffixes on a GPU build, e.g. `fix r all rx/kk/host ...` together with `fix e all eos/table/rx/kk ...` (device): the dynamic_cast between the two different template instantiations fails, rx_fixKK stays null, and the first call to FixEOStableRXKokkos::init() segfaults instead of printing a diagnostic.
suggested_fix: Add `if (rx_flag && !rx_fixKK) error->all(FLERR,"Must use fix rx/kk with the same suffix as fix eos/table/rx/kk");` right after the cast, following fix_dpd_energy_kokkos.cpp:36-37.

summary: FixGravityKokkos::post_force() ignores the 'disable' keyword and applies the gravitational force even when the user asked for it to be disabled.
failure_scenario: 'fix g all gravity/kk 1.0 vector 0 0 -1 disable' (used together with granular pair styles that only extract gvec) applies a full gravitational force on every atom every step instead of none; total energy/trajectory is wrong versus the non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (disable) return;' after the varflag block (before the atomKK->sync call) in FixGravityKokkos::post_force(), matching src/fix_gravity.cpp:276.

summary: FixLangevinKokkos's constructor re-allocates ratio[] and resets every entry to 1.0 after the base constructor already stored the user's 'scale' keyword values, so 'fix langevin/kk ... scale <type> <value>' is silently ignored.
failure_scenario: 'fix f all langevin/kk 300 300 100 12345 scale 2 10.0' damps type-2 atoms with ratio 1.0 instead of 10.0; the /kk run gives a different (wrong) trajectory and temperature from the non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Copy the base-class ratio values into the new dual view instead of overwriting them: save the old ratio pointer before 'delete[] ratio', copy old_ratio[i] into the new array for i=1..ntypes, then modify_host().

summary: FixLangevinKokkos::post_force() calls the non-virtual host-only FixLangevin::omega_thermostat() instead of the device version, with no sync/modified bookkeeping, so 'fix langevin/kk ... omega yes' updates only a stale host torque array while the device kernel omega_thermostat_kokkos() is dead code.
failure_scenario: GPU run with granular particles: 'fix 1 all langevin/kk 300 300 100 4321 omega yes'.  Pair style leaves torque device-current; the host loop reads a stale host torque/omega and writes the host copy, which is never claimed, so the device integrator (fix nve/sphere/kk) never sees the rotational drag or random torque -- the rotational thermostat is silently a no-op (and the host arrays it read are garbage).
suggested_fix: Rename FixLangevinKokkos::omega_thermostat_kokkos() to omega_thermostat() (and declare FixLangevin::omega_thermostat() virtual), so the KOKKOS device kernel is the one invoked from post_force().

summary: The maxpartner-overflow retry loop in pre_exchange_no_newton() re-allocates k_partner/k_valuepartner but never re-assigns d_partner/d_valuepartner, so the retry kernel writes past the end of the old (smaller) device views and all collected history is written into a buffer that is then thrown away.
