failure_scenario: Granular run (pair gran/hooke/history/kk) in which any atom accumulates more than 8 contact partners: the second pass of the loop writes d_partner(i,m)/d_valuepartner(i,...) beyond the old row stride -- corrupting neighbouring rows and running off the end of the allocation for the last atom -- and the freshly grown k_partner is marked device-modified while containing only the truncated first-pass data, so contact history is silently lost across the atom exchange.
suggested_fix: After both grow_kokkos() calls inside the loop, re-assign d_partner = k_partner.template view<DeviceType>(); and d_valuepartner = k_valuepartner.template view<DeviceType>(); (or simply call grow_arrays(atom->nmax), which already does this).

summary: FixNeighHistoryKokkos does not override pack_restart/size_restart/unpack_restart, so restart files are written from stale host mirrors of npartner/partner/valuepartner and restart data is unpacked into page-allocator chunks that no longer alias the dual views.
evidence: FixNeighHistory sets restart_peratom = 1 / restart_global = 1 and registers Atom::RESTART (src/fix_neigh_history.cpp:41-42, :79-80).  src/fix_neigh_history.cpp:900-907 'void FixNeighHistory::write_restart(FILE *fp) { pre_exchange(); ... }' -- the KOKKOS pre_exchange runs on the device and ends with k_npartner/k_partner/k_valuepartner .modify<DeviceType>() (fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:144-147).  FixNeighHistory::pack_restart (src/fix_neigh_history.cpp:916-927) and size_restart (:979-982) then read npartner[i]/partner[i][n]/valuepartner[i][...] -- the host mirrors -- with no k_*.sync_host().  The KOKKOS class (fix_neigh_history_kokkos.h:44-80) declares no pack_restart/unpack_restart, unlike e.g. FixGJFKokkos which overrides both with sync_host()/modify_host() (src/KOKKOS/fix_gjf_kokkos.cpp:495-511).  Worse, FixNeighHistory::unpack_restart (:934-960) does 'partner[nlocal] = ipage_atom->get(npartner[nlocal]);' -- in the KOKKOS build 'partner' is the row-pointer array that memoryKK->grow_kokkos aliases to k_partner's host mirror (fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:298-300), so this repoints a row away from the dual view and the data is dropped at the next grow_arrays().
failure_scenario: 'write_restart' during a granular run with fix neigh/history/kk: the per-atom contact history written to the file is whatever was last on the host (typically the state from the previous host-side exchange, or zeros), and reading that restart back re-creates contacts with wrong or missing shear history, so the restarted run does not reproduce the original trajectory.
suggested_fix: Override pack_restart/size_restart in FixNeighHistoryKokkos with k_npartner/k_partner/k_valuepartner .sync_host() before delegating, and override unpack_restart to write directly into the dual views' host mirrors (then modify_host()) instead of into ipage_atom/dpage_atom chunks.

summary: FixNHKokkos::remap() drops the entire 'isochoric' branch of FixNH::remap(), so 'fix npt/kk ... isochoric <dims>' silently runs as an ordinary NPT and does not conserve the reference volume.
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all npt/kk temp 300 300 100 x 0 0 1000 isochoric yz' -- the y and z box lengths are never rescaled to keep the volume at vol_start, so the /kk run has a monotonically drifting volume and a completely different trajectory/pressure from the identical non-kk run, with no warning.
suggested_fix: Port the isochoric block from src/fix_nh.cpp:1236-1298 into FixNHKokkos::remap(), or (minimally) add 'if (isochoric) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot (yet) use isochoric with fix npt/kk");' in FixNHKokkos::init().

summary: FixNVESphereKokkos ignores the 'update dipole/dlm' option: it always applies the simple cross-product dipole integrator, so 'fix nve/sphere/kk ... update dipole/dlm' silently uses a different (non-symplectic) integrator than the CPU style and never updates omega.
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all nve/sphere/kk update dipole/dlm' on a dipolar sphere system: the run silently uses the plain cross-product update (and never rotates omega), giving a different, less stable trajectory than the identical non-kk run; users following the doc's own example (line 37) get wrong results with no warning.
suggested_fix: Port the DLM branch into the kernel, or add 'if (dlm == DLM) error->all(FLERR,"Fix nve/sphere/kk does not (yet) support update dipole/dlm");' in FixNVESphereKokkos's constructor.

summary: FixNVEAsphereKokkos has no superellipsoid guard: it always reads AtomVecEllipsoid's 'bonus' array and derives the inertia from 'shape', but for superellipsoid particles the CPU style uses 'bonus_super[j].inertia' and 'bonus' is never allocated.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style ellipsoid superellipsoid' + 'fix 1 all nve/asphere/kk': the kernel indexes an unallocated/zero-extent k_bonus view -- out-of-bounds device read (illegal memory access on GPU) or, where the view happens to exist, integration with the wrong (shape-derived instead of stored) principal moments of inertia.
suggested_fix: Add the same guard as fix_nve_asphere_noforce_kokkos.cpp:63-65 to FixNVEAsphereKokkos::init(), or port the bonus_super branch.

summary: FixNVELimitKokkos reads the per-type mass dual view on the device without ever syncing it (there is no MASS_MASK bit and no init() override), so the per-type-mass branch integrates with an uninitialized device mass array.
failure_scenario: GPU build, 'fix 1 all nve/limit/kk 0.1' on a system with per-type masses (no rmass) and no other /kk style that happens to sync k_mass: d_mass holds whatever the freshly allocated device buffer contains (typically zeros), so dtfm = dtf/0 = inf and every velocity becomes NaN on the first half-kick.
suggested_fix: Add an init() override to FixNVELimitKokkos that calls FixNVELimit::init() and then 'atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();', exactly as fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:41-47 does.

summary: zero_force_item() subtracts the mean random force from f only, not from d_flangevin, so with 'zero yes tally yes' the tallied Langevin energy uses an uncorrected force (the CPU version corrects both).
failure_scenario: 'fix f all langevin/kk 300 300 100 999 zero yes tally yes' -- f_f (the cumulative energy transferred to the reservoir, used in ecouple/thermo output and for energy conservation checks) differs from the equivalent non-kk run by the omitted -fsumall*v term at every step.
suggested_fix: In zero_force_item(), also subtract d_fsumall from d_flangevin(i,*) when the tally array is active (add a template flag, mirroring Tp_TALLY in the CPU code).

summary: get_kinetic_energy() reads the per-type mass dual view on the device without calling atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>() first, so it can use a stale (or never-copied) device mass array.
failure_scenario: A 'mass' command (or a data-file read) between runs marks k_mass host-modified; if fix momentum/kk with 'rescale yes' is the first device consumer of the masses, the reduction uses the previous (or zero-filled) device copy, so ekin_old/ekin_new and hence the rescale factor are wrong -- silently, since factor just becomes 1.0 when both are 0.
suggested_fix: Add 'atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();' next to the TYPE_MASK sync in get_kinetic_energy(), matching src/KOKKOS/group_kokkos.h.

summary: FixLangevinKokkos::setup() unconditionally calls post_force(vflag), dropping the r-RESPA branch of the base setup() and without erroring out on respa the way every other KOKKOS fix does.
failure_scenario: 'run_style respa 2 2' plus 'fix f all langevin/kk ...': at setup the Langevin force is added to atom->f without copy_flevel_f/copy_f_flevel, so the outer-level respa force array does not contain it and the first steps of the run use a different force than the non-kk build.
suggested_fix: Either replicate the base setup()'s respa branch, or add the standard 'Cannot (yet) use respa with fix langevin/kk' error in FixLangevinKokkos::init().

summary: post_neighbor()'s kernel writes the masked neighbor index into d_firstflag instead of writing it back into d_neighbors, leaving non-boolean values in the per-neighbor history flag array.
failure_scenario: Today the two ported granular pair styles happen to hide it -- pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:172 and pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:172 both Kokkos::deep_copy(d_firsttouch,0) at the start of every compute(), so the bogus flags are wiped before pre_exchange reads them.  Any pair style that does not re-zero the flags (or any path where pre_exchange follows post_neighbor without an intervening compute) would count every neighbor as a history partner, immediately overflow maxpartner, and store zero-valued history.
suggested_fix: Change the statement to 'd_neighbors(i,jj) = j;' to mirror the CPU's 'jlist[jj] = j;', and explicitly leave d_firstflag(i,jj) at the 0 written by the preceding deep_copy unless history is found.

summary: Neither FixMinimize's nor FixMinimizeKokkos's destructor starts with the mandatory 'if (copymode) return;' guard.
evidence: src/fix_minimize.cpp:37-50 'FixMinimize::~FixMinimize() { atom->delete_callback(id,Atom::GROW); memory->destroy(peratom); if (vectors) {...} }' has no copymode test, and src/KOKKOS/fix_minimize_kokkos.cpp:101-105 'FixMinimizeKokkos::~FixMinimizeKokkos() { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_vectors,vectors); vectors = nullptr; }' has none either.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 1 requires the guard as the first line of every base-class destructor a KOKKOS style inherits.
failure_scenario: Today the class is only used through lambdas that capture views, so copymode is never set and nothing double-frees; the moment anyone passes *this to a parallel_for the copy's destructor would delete_callback() and free k_vectors out from under the live fix.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (copymode) return;' as the first statement of both destructors.

summary: nh_v_press() and nh_v_temp() call temperature->restore_bias_all() rather than restore_bias_all_kk() on a kokkosable temperature compute, forcing a full device->host copy of v twice per timestep.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:578-579 'if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->restore_bias_all();' and the identical line at :733-734, while the matching remove calls at :558 and :716 correctly use remove_bias_all_kk().  Every KOKKOS temperature compute implements restore_bias_all() as 'restore_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK);' (src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_partial_kokkos.cpp:212-216, and the same shape in compute_temp_deform/ramp/com/profile/region_kokkos.cpp), i.e. the non-_kk entry point adds a host copy of the whole velocity array.  All sibling fixes use the _kk form: src/KOKKOS/fix_temp_rescale_kokkos.cpp:162, fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:159, fix_nvt_sllod_kokkos.cpp:386, fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:371.
failure_scenario: GPU run of 'fix 1 all npt/kk temp ... ' with 'fix_modify 1 temp <a temp/partial/kk or temp/profile/kk compute>': every timestep transfers atom->v device->host twice (once from nh_v_press, once from nh_v_temp) for no reason; results are correct but the port loses most of its speedup.
suggested_fix: Change both kokkosable branches to temperature->restore_bias_all_kk().

summary: FixNHKokkos::remap() converts the dilate-group atoms with a host loop (two full x host/device round trips per remap) although DomainKokkos already provides a device x2lamda/lamda2x variant that takes a groupbit.
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all npt/kk ... dilate mygroup' on a GPU: remap() is called twice per timestep and each call copies the whole coordinate array device->host and back twice, so the /kk barostat is slower than the plain CPU one; results are correct.
suggested_fix: Replace both host loops with 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal, dilate_group_bit);' and 'domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal, dilate_group_bit);'.

summary: FixLangevinKokkos::end_of_step() marks V_MASK and k_lv as device-modified although it only reads v and never touches lv.
failure_scenario: Spurious device->host copies of v every step; and if lv were ever registered for atom callbacks (grow_arrays/copy_arrays are currently dead code because fix langevin registers no Atom::GROW callback), a copy_arrays() followed by end_of_step() would hit Kokkos::abort on a GPU build.
suggested_fix: Delete both statements: end_of_step() writes nothing.  Consider removing the vestigial lv/franprev/end_of_step_item code entirely now that the gjf option has been removed from fix langevin.

summary: ~FixPropertyAtomKokkos() calls atomKK->update_property_atom() while the dying fix is still in Modify's fix list, so AtomKokkos::fix_prop_atom[] is rebuilt containing a pointer to the object being destroyed (use-after-free on every later atomKK->sync()/modified()).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_property_atom_kokkos.cpp:63-85: 'FixPropertyAtomKokkos::~FixPropertyAtomKokkos() { ... atomKK->update_property_atom(); }'. src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:162-180: 'void AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() { nprop_atom = 0; ... for (auto &ifix : modify->get_fix_by_style("^property/atom")) { ... ++nprop_atom; prop_atom_fixes.push_back(ifix); } ... fix_prop_atom[n++] = dynamic_cast<FixPropertyAtomKokkos *>(ifix); }'. src/modify.cpp Modify::delete_fix(int ifix): 'delete fix[ifix]; atom->update_callback(ifix); for (int i = ifix + 1; i < nfix; i++) fix[i - 1] = fix[i]; ... nfix--;' -- the entry is removed from fix[] only AFTER the destructor has run, and src/modify.cpp Modify::get_fix_by_style() iterates 'for (int ifix = 0; ifix < nfix; ifix++) if (fix[ifix] && utils::strmatch(fix[ifix]->style, style))', so the fix currently being destroyed still matches. AtomKokkos::sync()/modified() then dereference it: src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp 'for (int n = 0; n < nprop_atom; n++) fix_prop_atom[n]->sync(space, mask);'.
failure_scenario: fix p all property/atom d_foo ; run 100 ; unfix p ; run 100  -> the first atomKK->sync() in the second run calls sync()/modified() on the freed FixPropertyAtomKokkos object (heap use-after-free: crash, or silent corruption of the DualView modify flags).
suggested_fix: Do not rebuild the list from inside the destructor; instead have AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() skip the fix being destroyed (pass 'this' to exclude), or trigger the rebuild from Modify::delete_fix()/Atom::update_callback() after the fix has been removed from modify->fix[].

summary: FixReaxFFBondsKokkos::Output_ReaxFF_Bonds() drops the base class's 'if (filename == "NULL") return;' early exit, so 'fix ... reaxff/bonds/kk N NULL' creates and writes a file literally named NULL instead of suppressing file output.
failure_scenario: fix 1 all reaxff/bonds/kk 10 NULL  (the documented way to enable dump-image bond rendering without a bonds file) -> rank 0 creates a file named 'NULL' in the working directory and writes a full bond table into it every 10 steps.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (filename == "NULL") return;' right after the FindBond_kokkos() call, matching FixReaxFFBonds::Output_ReaxFF_Bonds().

summary: fix reaxff/bonds/kk never fills numobjs/numneigh/neighid, so the inherited FixReaxFFBonds::image() always returns 0 and dump image silently renders no ReaxFF bonds.
evidence: src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_bonds.cpp:377-383: 'int FixReaxFFBonds::image(int *&objs, double **&parms) { ... if (!numobjs) return 0;' and the body reads 'numneigh[i]' / 'neighid[i][jj]'. numobjs is set only in FixReaxFFBonds::FindBond() (src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_bonds.cpp:187 'numobjs = 0;' and :206 'numobjs += nj;'). FixReaxFFBondsKokkos::Output_ReaxFF_Bonds() (src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_bonds_kokkos.cpp:102-137) calls PairReaxFFKokkos::FindBond_kokkos() instead, which fills only device views in the pair style and never touches numobjs/numneigh/neighid; FixReaxFFBondsKokkos does not override image().
failure_scenario: fix 1 all reaxff/bonds/kk 10 NULL  +  dump  d all image ... bonds fix 1 ...  -> the images contain the atoms but no bonds, with no error message; the same input with the non-kk fix draws them.
suggested_fix: Either override image() in FixReaxFFBondsKokkos to build the object list from the pair style's device bond data (syncing it to the host first), or make init() refuse the combination with a clear error when the fix is used as a dump image bond source.

summary: Wrong logical operator in the tmpid skip guard: '(j == 0) && (j < i)' instead of the base class's '(j == 0) || (j < i)', so empty bond slots are no longer skipped and lower-index partners would be processed a second time.
failure_scenario: For the local atom with index i == 0 the sentinel value j == 0 that marks an unused tmpid slot is no longer skipped, so up to MAXSPECBOND(=24) spurious self-pair iterations run per outer pass (currently caught by the following clusterID/x0 equality test, so no wrong numbers today). The guard is also the only protection against double-processing a bond if PairReaxFFKokkos::FindBondSpecies ever stored both directions -- it currently stores only j > i (src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp, TagPairReaxFindBondSpecies: 'if (j < i) continue;'), which is what masks the defect.
suggested_fix: Change '&&' to '||' so the guard matches FixReaxFFSpecies::FindMolecule().

summary: The firstgroup loop-truncation is keyed on igroup but the shift kernel selects atoms with group2bit, so with 'atom_modify first <group>' plus the 'shift <other-group>' keyword the atoms of the shift group beyond nfirst are never displaced.
failure_scenario: atom_modify first mobile ; group mobile ... ; group shiftme ... ; fix 1 mobile recenter INIT INIT INIT shift shiftme  -> only the shiftme atoms that happen to sit in the first nfirst slots of the local atom list are recentered; the rest drift, and the /kk result differs from the non-kk result.
suggested_fix: Drop the firstgroup truncation (loop over atom->nlocal), or make it conditional on group2bit == groupbit.

summary: datamask_read/datamask_modify are narrowed from the Fix defaults (ALL_MASK/ALL_MASK) although the inherited post_integrate() can delete atoms via FixReaxFFSpecies::DeleteSpecies(), which rewrites every per-atom array on the host; only DVECTOR_MASK is marked modified, leaving the device copies of x/v/tag/type/image stale.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_species_kokkos.cpp:94-95: 'datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | Q_MASK | MASK_MASK | DVECTOR_MASK | TYPE_MASK | RMASS_MASK | TAG_MASK; datamask_modify = DVECTOR_MASK;' (src/fix.cpp:110-111 defaults are 'datamask_read = ALL_MASK; datamask_modify = ALL_MASK;'). src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp:266-278 ModifyKokkos::post_integrate() does only 'atomKK->sync(fix->execution_space, fix->datamask_read); ... fix->post_integrate(); ... atomKK->modified(fix->execution_space, fix->datamask_modify);'. FixReaxFFSpecies::post_integrate() -> Output_ReaxFF_Bonds() -> 'if (delflag != NONE && nvalid != -1) DeleteSpecies(Nmole, Nspec);' and DeleteSpecies does 'avec->copy(atom->nlocal - 1, i, 1); atom->nlocal--; ... atom->natoms -= ndel; ... atom->nghost = 0; atom->map_init(); atom->map_set();' (src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_species.cpp). AtomVecKokkos does not override AtomVec::copy() (src/atom_vec.cpp:269), so the compaction is a pure host-side rewrite of every registered per-atom field.
failure_scenario: fix 1 all reaxff/species/kk 1 1 100 species.out delete del.out masslimit 0 50  under -k on -sf kk: after the first deletion step the device still holds the pre-compaction x/v/tag/type/image (and the old nlocal worth of data), so the next device kernel integrates the wrong atoms -- silently wrong trajectories or a crash.
suggested_fix: Leave datamask_read/datamask_modify at ALL_MASK for this (deliberately kokkosable = 0) fix, or at least add every mask that AtomVec::copy() touches and set datamask_modify = ALL_MASK whenever delflag != NONE.

summary: Nothing forces 'fix property/atom' to the /kk variant under KOKKOS, yet AtomKokkos::add_custom() always allocates the custom arrays as Kokkos views; the non-kk FixPropertyAtom::grow_arrays() then calls memory->grow()/realloc() on a pointer that aliases into a Kokkos allocation.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:466-477 (AtomKokkos::add_custom, flag==1 && cols==0): 'dvector = (double **) memory->srealloc(...); this->sync(Device, DVECTOR_MASK); memoryKK->grow_kokkos(k_dvector, dvector, ndvector, nmax, "atom:dvector"); ...' and src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h grow_kokkos() sets 'array[i] = &data.view_host()(i,0)'. src/fix_property_atom.cpp FixPropertyAtom::grow_arrays() then does 'memory->grow(atom->dvector[index[nv]], nmax, "atom:dvector"); memset(&atom->dvector[index[nv]][nmax_old], 0, nbytes);' -- Memory::grow() calls srealloc()/realloc() on that Kokkos-owned pointer. The only guard, src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:162-170 AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() ('if (!ifix->kokkosable) error->all(FLERR, "KOKKOS package requires a Kokkos-enabled version of fix property/atom")'), is reached only from FixPropertyAtomKokkos's own constructor/destructor, so it never runs when every property/atom fix in the run is non-kk. src/lammps.cpp:465 shows suffix_enable is set only by -sf/-suffix, and src/modify.h:108 add_fix() applies the suffix only when suffix_enable is set.
failure_scenario: lmp -k on t 4 -in in.reaxff (no -sf kk) with 'pair_style reaxff/kk' and 'fix 1 all reaxff/species/kk ...': FixReaxFFSpecies::setup() runs modify->add_fix("clusterID_... all property/atom d_... ghost yes"), which resolves to the plain FixPropertyAtom; its post_constructor()->grow_arrays(atom->nmax) reallocs a Kokkos pointer -> glibc 'realloc(): invalid pointer' abort or silent heap corruption. A bare 'fix p all property/atom d_foo' under -k on without -sf kk hits the same path.
suggested_fix: Call AtomKokkos::update_property_atom() (or an equivalent kokkosable check) from AtomKokkos::add_custom(), or have ModifyKokkos force the /kk variant for property/atom regardless of suffix_enable.

summary: pack_exchange_kokkos()/unpack_exchange_kokkos() ignore the ExecutionSpace argument and never mark/sync the exchange buffer (k_buf.modify<DeviceType>() + sync to the requested space), so with 'package kokkos comm/exchange host' on a GPU build the s_hist/t_hist of migrating atoms are packed into the device copy of the buffer while MPI sends the host copy.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1313-1343 'pack_exchange_kokkos(const int &nsend, DAT::tdual_double_2d_lr &k_buf, ..., ExecutionSpace /*space*/) { k_buf.sync<DeviceType>(); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(...TagQEqPackExchange...); ... k_s_hist.template modify<DeviceType>(); ... return nsend*nprev*2; }' -- no 'k_buf.modify<DeviceType>()' and no sync of k_buf; same in unpack_exchange_kokkos (:1362-1387). Every other KOKKOS fix does it, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp (pack_exchange_kokkos) 'k_buf.template modify<DeviceType>(); if (space == HostKK) k_buf.sync_host(); else k_buf.sync_device();', src/KOKKOS/fix_shake_kokkos.cpp and src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp likewise. The caller src/KOKKOS/comm_kokkos.cpp:1373-1375 packs with 'kkbase->pack_exchange_kokkos(count,k_buf_send,...,ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space)' and then sends from 'MPI_Send(k_buf_send.view<DeviceType>().data(),nextrasend,...)' (:1404) where DeviceType is CommKokkos::exchange_device's template parameter -- LMPHostType when exchange_comm_on_host is set (src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:589-591, 'package kokkos comm/exchange host'), while the fix's DeviceType is LMPDeviceType.
failure_scenario: GPU build with GPU-aware MPI, 'package kokkos comm/exchange host', pair_style reaxff/kk + fix qeq/reaxff/kk on >1 MPI rank: on every reneighboring step the charge-history (s_hist/t_hist) of every migrating atom is filled from whatever the host side of comm's send buffer last held, so the CG initial guess for those atoms is garbage (extra iterations, or non-convergence/NaN if the stale bytes are large).
suggested_fix: Add 'k_buf.template modify<DeviceType>(); if (space == HostKK) k_buf.sync_host(); else k_buf.sync_device();' at the end of pack_exchange_kokkos and sync k_buf from the space the data arrived in at the start of unpack_exchange_kokkos, as fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp / fix_shake_kokkos.cpp do.

summary: cg_solve() prints the non-convergence warning unconditionally, ignoring the documented 'nowarn' keyword (maxwarn) that the CPU style honors.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:510-514: 'if (loop >= imax && comm->me == 0) error->warning(FLERR,fmt::format("Fix qeq/reaxff/kk cg_solve convergence failed after {} iterations at step {}: ..."));' vs src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:812-814: 'if ((i >= imax) && maxwarn && (comm->me == 0)) error->warning(FLERR, "Fix qeq/reaxff CG convergence failed after {} iterations at step {}", i,update->ntimestep);'. maxwarn is set by the 'nowarn' keyword (src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:77 'maxwarn = 1;' and :101 'else if (strcmp(arg[iarg],"nowarn") == 0) maxwarn = 0;') and is documented in doc/src/fix_qeq_reaxff.rst:87-92.
failure_scenario: fix 1 all qeq/reaxff/kk 1 0.0 10.0 1e-14 reaxff maxiter 20 nowarn -- the documented use case of forcing a fixed iteration count floods the log with one warning per QEq step instead of being silent.
suggested_fix: Add '&& maxwarn' to the condition, matching FixQEqReaxFF::CG().

summary: cg_solve() returns the fused loop count, so the global scalar of fix qeq/reaxff/kk is half of the value the CPU and OPENMP styles report for the same solve.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:516 'return loop;' feeding :287 'matvecs = cg_solve();', with the inherited src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:475-478 'double FixQEqReaxFF::compute_scalar() { return matvecs/2.0; }'. The CPU style counts both solves: src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:626-628 'matvecs_s = CG(b_s, s); matvecs_t = CG(b_t, t); matvecs = matvecs_s + matvecs_t;', and the OPENMP fused solver does the same, src/OPENMP/fix_qeq_reaxff_omp.cpp:779-802 'matvecs_s = matvecs_t = i; ... return matvecs_s + matvecs_t;'.
failure_scenario: thermo_style custom step f_1 with fix qeq/reaxff vs fix qeq/reaxff/kk on the same input prints ~N and ~N/2 iterations respectively for an identical solve.
suggested_fix: Return 2*loop from cg_solve() (or set matvecs = 2*cg_solve()) so the reported scalar matches the CPU/OPENMP convention.

summary: get_chi_field() is called twice per QEq step (once from allocate_array(), once from pre_force()), and each call forces a device->host sync of x/mask/image plus a full host-side loop over all atoms.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:219 'allocate_array();' inside pre_force(), and allocate_array() ends with :360-364 '// init_storage
  if (efield) get_chi_field();
  Kokkos::parallel_for(...TagQEqZero...);'. pre_force() then repeats it at :265-267 '// init_matvec
  if (efield) get_chi_field();'. Each call is src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1430-1436 'atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK|MASK_MASK|IMAGE_MASK); FixQEqReaxFF::get_chi_field(); k_chi_field.modify_host(); k_chi_field.sync_device();'. The CPU style calls it once per pre_force (src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:622) plus once in init_storage(), which runs only from setup_pre_force().
failure_scenario: fix qeq/reaxff/kk together with fix efield on a GPU: every QEq step performs two full x/mask/image device->host copies and two O(nlocal) host loops instead of one.
suggested_fix: Drop the 'if (efield) get_chi_field();' from allocate_array() (the following TagQEqZero kernel only needs d_chi_field, which pre_force() refills right afterwards), or drop the duplicate call in pre_force().

summary: fix reaxff/bonds/kk inherits FixReaxFFBonds::allocate(), so numneigh/neighid/abo (nmax x MAXREAXBOND) are allocated and grown but never used by the KOKKOS path, and memory_usage() no longer reports them.
evidence: src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_bonds.cpp:68 'allocate();' in the base constructor allocates 'numneigh' (nmax), 'neighid' (nmax x MAXREAXBOND, tagint) and 'abo' (nmax x MAXREAXBOND, double); allocate() is not virtual (src/REAXFF/fix_reaxff_bonds.h:49 'void allocate();') and FixReaxFFBondsKokkos does not override it. src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_bonds_kokkos.cpp:141-152: 'double FixReaxFFBondsKokkos::memory_usage() { bytes = nbuf*sizeof(double); // These are accounted for in PairReaxFFKokkos: //bytes += nmax*sizeof(int); ...' -- the commented-out terms are exactly the arrays the base fix (not the pair style) still owns.
failure_scenario: A 1M-atom reaxff/kk run with fix reaxff/bonds/kk wastes ~1M*MAXREAXBOND*(sizeof(tagint)+sizeof(double)) bytes of host memory that no code reads, and 'info memory' under-reports the fix's footprint.
suggested_fix: Make FixReaxFFBonds::allocate()/destroy() virtual and override them in the KOKKOS class to be no-ops (or keep them and restore the memory_usage terms).

summary: FixQEqReaxFFKokkos::init() syncs q to execution_space (Device) before FixQEqReaxFF::init() reads atom->q and atom->mask on the host, i.e. the sync is in the wrong direction and MASK_MASK is missing.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:100-104: 'void FixQEqReaxFFKokkos<DeviceType>::init() { atomKK->sync(execution_space,Q_MASK); FixQEqReaxFF::init(); ...'. The only per-atom data the base init() touches is on the host: src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:422-427 'double qsum_local = 0.0, qsum = 0.0; for (int i = 0; i < atom->nlocal; i++) { if (atom->mask[i] & groupbit) qsum_local += atom->q[i]; } MPI_Allreduce(...)'. With execution_space == Device, atomKK->sync(Device,Q_MASK) copies host->device (a no-op when the device copy is the fresh one) and leaves the host copy stale.
failure_scenario: Two consecutive run commands with fix qeq/reaxff/kk on a GPU: the first run leaves q modified on the device (fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:537 'atomKK->modified(execution_space,Q_MASK)'); the second run's init() then computes qsum from the pre-run host charges and prints (or fails to print) the 'group is not charge neutral' warning based on stale data.
suggested_fix: Change the call to 'atomKK->sync(Host, Q_MASK|MASK_MASK);' since the base init() reads those arrays on the host.

summary: The H-matrix capacity reduction sums d_numneigh[ii] over the list index ii instead of d_numneigh[d_ilist[ii]], while every consumer of that capacity indexes by d_ilist[ii]; the two agree only because the Kokkos neighbor build happens to set d_ilist(i)==i.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1453-1456: 'void FixQEqReaxFFKokkosNeighborFunctor<DeviceType>::operator()(TagQEqNeighborNumNeigh, const int& ii, bigint& totneigh) const { totneigh += static_cast<bigint>(d_numneigh[ii]); }' -- the result is m_cap_big (:230-231) and sizes d_jlist/d_val (:326-327). Both consumers dereference the ilist first: the CPU scan at :1487-1497 'const int i = d_ilist[ii]; ... const int jnum = d_numneigh[i];' and the GPU team version at :1592-1600 'const int i = d_ilist[ii]; int jnum = d_numneigh[i]; ... totalnbrs += jnum;' whose per-team total is reserved with 'Kokkos::atomic_fetch_add(&d_mfill_offset(), totalnbrs)' (:1618). The CPU base sums the same way as the consumers: src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:374-378 'm = 0; for (ii = 0; ii < nn; ii++) { i = ilist[ii]; m += numneigh[i]; }'. Today src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:593,838,970,1132,1330,1575 all set 'neigh_list.d_ilist(i) = i;', so the two sums are equal and no overrun occurs.
failure_scenario: Latent: if any Kokkos neighbor build ever produces a non-identity or subset d_ilist (e.g. a reordered or partial ilist), the GPU team compute_H reserves more slots than m_cap_big and writes past the end of d_jlist/d_val (out-of-bounds device write, silent corruption).
suggested_fix: Change the functor to 'totneigh += static_cast<bigint>(d_numneigh[d_ilist[ii]]);' so the capacity estimate matches the consumers and the CPU base.

summary: grow_arrays() unconditionally refills the host mirrors of the tied per-atom DualViews from the device copies during a run, which silently discards the base class' host-side bookkeeping whenever the arrays grow on the HOST exchange/borders path of a GPU build.
failure_scenario: GPU build, `fix rigid/small/kk` on the host exchange path -- which init() selects automatically for ellipsoid/line/tri/body atom styles or whenever another per-atom fix (e.g. fix property/atom) lacks device exchange (fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:170-181).  A reneighbor in which comm->exchange() or comm->borders() grows atom->nmax resets bodytag/bodyown/xcmimage/displace to their values from before the migration; pre_neighbor() then pushes that corrupted host state to the device, so migrated atoms keep the body IDs of the atoms that used to occupy their slots.  Result is either the hard error "Rigid body atoms ... missing on proc" from reset_atom2body(), or silently wrong body membership and wrong trajectories.
suggested_fix: Before the grow_kokkos() calls, push the host side to the device (modify_host() + sync<DeviceType>()) whenever the fix is running on the host exchange path -- or, more simply, extend host_holds_bookkeeping to also cover `!(exchange_comm_device && !commKK->exchange_comm_legacy)` so the existing save/restore of the host contents covers a grow during a host exchange too.

summary: In the setup path (setup_pre_force -> solve_reactions(vflag,false)) the KOKKOS version initializes the "Old" species concentrations only for atoms in the fix group, whereas the CPU FixRX initializes them for every local atom.
failure_scenario: `fix rx` applied to a subset group (e.g. `group mobile ...; fix 1 mobile rx ...`).  On the setup step the *Old per-atom properties of atoms outside `mobile` stay at their fix property/atom default (0.0) under /kk, while the CPU run sets them equal to the current concentrations.  Downstream consumers of the Old values (fix eos/table/rx, pair dpd/fdt/energy) then see a spurious concentration change for those atoms and the /kk run diverges from the CPU run.
suggested_fix: Add a separate parallel_for over all nlocal atoms (no groupbit test) that copies d_dvector(atom_ind,i) into d_dvector(atom_ind_old,i) in the setup (ZERO_RATES) path, mirroring fix_rx.cpp:551-558.

summary: On the first run, sort_kokkos() and setup_pre_neighbor() clear the DualView sync state and re-declare the (pre-exchange) host arrays authoritative, discarding the per-atom body bookkeeping that the setup-time DEVICE exchange legitimately moved; the justifying comment ("nothing had pushed the host arrays create_bodies() wrote to the device") is contradicted by pack_exchange_kokkos.
failure_scenario: Two or more MPI ranks, GPU build with the device exchange active, and at least one atom migrating during the setup-time comm->exchange() of the first run (e.g. a data file whose atoms lie outside the box, so domain->pbc() moves them across a proc boundary).  The per-atom bodytag the exchange moved on the device is thrown away and the pre-exchange host array -- indexed by the pre-exchange local atom ordering -- is used instead, so setup_bodies_static() builds the bodies from bodytags belonging to the wrong atoms: either the hard error "Rigid body atoms ... missing on proc" from reset_atom2body(), or silently wrong bodies and inertia tensors.
suggested_fix: On the first run, retire the device claim with sync_host() (which brings the exchange result down to the host) instead of clear_sync_state(), or only clear when the setup-time exchange actually packed nothing.

summary: Dead host-only copies of the ODE solver (rk4, rkf45, rkf45_step, rkf45_h0, rhs, rhs_dense, rhs_sparse) are never called and would dereference device views from host code if they ever were.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:174 (rk4), :587 (rkf45_step), :690 (rkf45_h0), :775 (rkf45), :875 (rhs), :887 (rhs_dense), :921 (rhs_sparse) are plain host member functions.  A grep of the file shows they are only called by each other; the only solver actually used is k_rk4/k_rkf45 from the device kernel (fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1304 and :1308).  rhs_dense reads `d_kineticsData.stoichReactants(jrxn,ispecies)` (line 903) and rhs_sparse reads `this->d_kineticsData.nuk/nu/inu` (lines 931-935) -- these are `ArrayTypes<DeviceType>` views, i.e. GPU memory for the /kk/device instantiation.
failure_scenario: No failure today (dead code), but ~350 lines of unmaintained duplicate solver that segfaults on a GPU build the moment anyone wires it up, and that silently diverges from the device solver if only one of the two copies is fixed.
suggested_fix: Delete the host-only rk4/rkf45/rkf45_step/rkf45_h0/rhs/rhs_dense/rhs_sparse members (and their declarations in fix_rx_kokkos.h:156-188), keeping only the k_* device versions.

summary: Two large `#if 0` blocks hold disabled alternative lambda implementations of the two temperature kernels, plus commented-out member declarations in the header.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1828-1894 (`#if 0` ... `#else` ... `#endif` around a LAMMPS_LAMBDA copy of Tag_FixRxKokkos_firstPairOperator) and :1908-1931 (same for the 2nd pair operator); src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1439 (`//DAT::tdual_int_scalar k_error_flag("pair:error_flag");`), :1199-1219 (`//else {` ... `//}`); src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.h:225-226, :257, :267 commented-out member declarations.  The project code-review rule states that disabled/alternative implementations must be removed entirely.
failure_scenario: Maintenance hazard only: the disabled copies already differ from the live kernels (e.g. the #if 0 copy at line 1877 omits the `NEIGHFLAG==HALF||NEIGHFLAG==HALFTHREAD` guard that the live kernel has at line 1728), so a future reader can be misled into reinstating a wrong version.
suggested_fix: Delete the `#if 0` blocks and the commented-out declarations.

summary: Device kernels call unqualified C library math (pow, exp, sqrt, fabs, fmax, fmin) instead of the Kokkos:: equivalents required by the KOKKOS package rules, inconsistently with line 1093 which does use Kokkos::pow.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1284-1286 inside operator()(Tag_FixRxKokkos_solveSystems...):
        userData.kFor[irxn] = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(static_cast<double>(d_kineticsData.Arr(irxn)) *
                               pow(theta, static_cast<double>(d_kineticsData.nArr(irxn))) *
                               exp(-static_cast<double>(d_kineticsData.Ea(irxn)) / boltz / theta));
and in the KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION helpers: :1040 `pow(...)`, :397/:437/:446/:467-468 (`sqrt`, `fmax`, `fmin`), :509/:520/:524/:536-547 (`fabs`, `sqrt`, `fmax`, `fmin`), :1717-1718 (`sqrt`).  Compare src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1093 which correctly uses `Kokkos::pow`.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos:: math in device kernels.
failure_scenario: Compiles today on CUDA/HIP because ::pow/::exp/::sqrt are provided as device functions, but breaks on backends/toolchains where only the Kokkos:: wrappers are guaranteed, and blocks a future switch of these accumulators to KK_FLOAT.
suggested_fix: Replace the unqualified calls in all KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION bodies with Kokkos::pow/exp/sqrt/fabs/fmax/fmin.

summary: The Langevin device kernel calls the unqualified C library sqrt() instead of Kokkos::sqrt(), which the KOKKOS package rules require for device kernels.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:896-925, inside `Kokkos::parallel_for("fix rigid/small langevin", Range1D(0, nlocal_body), KOKKOS_LAMBDA(const int ibody) {`:
      double gamma2 = sqrt(b.mass) * tsqrt * sqrt(24.0*boltz/tp/dt/mvv2e) / ftm2v;   (:903)
      gamma2 = tsqrt * sqrt(24.0*boltz/tp/dt/mvv2e) / ftm2v;                          (:909)
      tbody[0] = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(b.inertia[0]*gamma1*... + sqrt(b.inertia[0])*gamma2*(rand_gen.drand()-0.5));  (:921, :923, :925)
.github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md requires Kokkos:: math inside device kernels; the rest of this file correctly routes its math through MathExtraKokkos::.
failure_scenario: Compiles on CUDA/HIP today because ::sqrt is provided as a device function, but is not portable to backends/toolchains where only the Kokkos:: wrappers are guaranteed, and blocks a future switch of these accumulators to KK_FLOAT.
suggested_fix: Replace the five in-kernel sqrt() calls with Kokkos::sqrt().

summary: The destructor frees the extended per-atom arrays only when extended/orientflag/dorientflag are still set; because setup_bodies_static() recomputes those flags on every reinit run, a flag that has flipped back to 0 leaves a Kokkos-owned pointer in the base class, which FixRigidSmall::~FixRigidSmall() then passes to memory->destroy().
failure_scenario: A `fix rigid/small/kk` with reinit yes whose bodies contain finite-size particles in run 1 but only point particles in a later run (the finite-size particles were deleted, or their radius set to 0): extended goes 1 -> 0, the destructor skips destroy_kokkos, and FixRigidSmall::~FixRigidSmall() calls memory->destroy() (sfree) on the host mirror of a Kokkos DualView -> heap corruption / crash at the end of the run.
suggested_fix: Guard on the pointers rather than the flags: `if (eflags) memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eflags, eflags);` and likewise for orient/dorient.

summary: min_post_force applies the SHAKE restraint force to the closest-image (possibly ghost) atom index instead of the mapped-back owner, and the following comm->reverse_comm(this) is a no-op, so ghost force contributions are silently dropped while the matching energy/virial are tallied on the owners.
evidence: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:527-544 'const int idx0 = d_closest_list(i, slot0); const int idx1 = d_closest_list(i, slot1); ... a_f(idx0,0) += ...; a_f(idx1,0) -= ...' - no 'idx < nlocal' guard and no map-back.  The CPU original, RIGID/fix_shake.cpp:2842-2870 (FixShake::bond_force), first maps the image index back to the canonical owned index ('i1 = atom->map(atom->tag[i1]); i2 = atom->map(atom->tag[i2]);') and only then applies 'if ((i1 >= 0) && (i1 < nlocal)) f[i1][0] += delx*fbond;'.  The Kokkos code does perform that map-back a few lines later, but only for the energy/virial atom list (fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:553-558 'own0 = AtomKokkos::map_kokkos<...>(d_shake_atom(m,slot0),...); if ((own0 >= 0) && (own0 < nlocal)) atomlist[count++] = own0;').  The 'comm->reverse_comm(this)' at fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:473 cannot recover the ghost forces: FixShake sets only 'comm_forward = 3' (RIGID/fix_shake.cpp:95) and never sets comm_reverse nor overrides pack_reverse_comm/unpack_reverse_comm (grep finds none in fix_shake.cpp/.h or fix_shake_kokkos.cpp/.h), and CommBrick::reverse_comm(Fix*,int) uses 'nsize = fix->comm_reverse' (comm_brick.cpp:1126-1127) which is 0.
failure_scenario: minimize with 'fix shake/kk' on a molecule that straddles a periodic boundary (so domain->closest_image returns a ghost index for a cluster partner owned by the same processor).  The restraint force on the ghost slot is thrown away, while ebond/virial/eatom are still credited to both owners: the reported SHAKE restraint energy and global virial are then twice the force that is actually applied, and the minimizer's forces differ by a factor of two from the plain 'fix shake' run.
suggested_fix: Map idx0/idx1 back through the atom map (as done for own0/own1 at lines 553-558) and guard the force accumulation with '< nlocal', exactly as FixShake::bond_force does; then drop the dead comm->reverse_comm(this) call at line 473 (or add a real pack/unpack_reverse_comm and set comm_reverse).

summary: post_force unconditionally calls k_xoriginal.modify_host() before syncing to the device, which makes the (never-updated) host copy of xoriginal win over the device copy and silently overwrites the reference coordinates that the device-side exchange kernels just rewrote.
evidence: fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:105-106 'k_xoriginal.modify_host(); k_xoriginal.sync<DeviceType>();' - post_force never writes the host side of k_xoriginal (the kernel at :127-145 only reads d_xoriginal).  Meanwhile pack_exchange_kokkos compacts xoriginal on the device ('d_xoriginal(i,0) = d_xoriginal(j,0); ...' at :197-199) and ends with 'k_xoriginal.template modify<DeviceType>();' (:240), and unpack_exchange_kokkos writes the received values on the device (:261-263) and ends with the same modify (:294); neither touches the host mirror.  For the default double-precision build ttransform_kkfloat_1d_3_lr has NEED_TRANSFORM==0 (kokkos_type.h:700), so modify_host() forwards to Kokkos DualView::modify_host(), which sets modified_flags(0) = max(flags)+1, and sync<DeviceType>() -> sync_device_impl() 'if (modified_flags(0) > modified_flags(1)) { deep_copy(d_view, h_view); ... }' (lib/kokkos/containers/src/Kokkos_DualView.hpp:656-668) - a silent host->device copy of the stale array.  The base class writes xoriginal on the host only in copy_arrays/unpack_exchange/unpack_restart, and each of those KOKKOS overrides already calls modify_host() itself (:175, :322, :352), so the extra unconditional modify_host() serves no purpose.
failure_scenario: GPU build, any run with 'fix spring/self/kk' in which atoms migrate between MPI ranks: comm->exchange() runs before post_force in the same step, so on the first reneighboring step post_force copies the pre-exchange host xoriginal (old local ordering, missing the received atoms) onto the device.  Every atom is then tethered to another atom's reference position, giving wrong forces and a wrong spring energy for the rest of the run.  Even in a single-rank run it forces a full nmax*3 host->device copy every timestep.
suggested_fix: Delete the 'k_xoriginal.modify_host();' at line 105 and keep only 'k_xoriginal.sync<DeviceType>();'.

summary: pack_exchange_kokkos writes each migrating atom's shear history into the send buffer at an offset derived from the atom's LOCAL INDEX instead of its slot in the send list, so the bytes actually transmitted are uninitialized memory (and the write can run past the end of the buffer).
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:368-374 'void ...operator()(TagFixWallGranPackExchange, const int &mysend) const { const int i = d_sendlist(mysend); int m = i*size_history; for (int v = 0; v < size_history; v++) d_buf(m++) = static_cast<double>(d_history_one(i,v)); ...' - the offset must be 'mysend*size_history'.  The receiving side proves it: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:418-425 uses 'int m = i*size_history;' with i the RECEIVE SLOT, and src/KOKKOS/comm_kokkos.cpp:1373-1410 sends exactly the first 'nextrasend' doubles of k_buf_send, where nextrasend is this function's return value 'nsend*size_history' (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:410).  comm_kokkos.cpp:1371 only guarantees 'nsend*fix_iextra->maxexchange' doubles of capacity, so writing at d_sendlist(mysend)*size_history (an index up to nlocal*size_history) both scatters the data outside the transmitted window and can overrun the buffer.  The sibling styles index by the send slot: fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:187 'int m = nsend + offset;' with 'd_buf[mysend] = m;', and fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:224 'd_buf(mysend) = ...'.
failure_scenario: multi-processor granular run with 'fix wall/gran/kk hooke/history ...': on the first timestep an atom in contact with the wall migrates to another rank, its tangential shear history arrives as whatever happened to be in buffer slots 0..nsend*3-1, so the frictional force jumps discontinuously; with nlocal*size_history larger than the send buffer it is an out-of-bounds device write (silent corruption or a GPU segfault).
suggested_fix: Change 'int m = i*size_history;' to 'int m = mysend*size_history;' in TagFixWallGranPackExchange.

summary: unpack_exchange_kokkos stores the received shear history at the receive-slot index instead of the destination atom index returned by d_indices, so the history is written onto the wrong atoms and the migrated atoms keep stale history.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:418-426 'int index = d_indices(i); if (index > -1) { int m = i*size_history; for (int v = 0; v < size_history; v++) d_history_one(i,v) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_buf(m++)); }' - the guard reads d_indices(i) but the destination is 'd_history_one(i,v)' rather than 'd_history_one(index,v)'.  Every other KOKKOS fix that implements this hook uses the mapped index: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:276 'd_current_segment(index) = static_cast<int>(d_buf(i));', fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:261-263 'd_xoriginal(index,0) = ...', fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:252-254.  d_indices is filled by AtomVecKokkos::unpack_exchange_kokkos (comm_kokkos.cpp:1358-1359) and gives the local index the i-th received atom was placed at, which is generally != i.
failure_scenario: multi-processor 'fix wall/gran/kk hooke/history' run: after an exchange the received atoms' d_history_one entries are left at whatever the (compacted) local slot held, while the low-numbered local atoms 0..nrecv-1 - which did not migrate - have their tangential displacement history overwritten with other atoms' values.  Friction forces are wrong for both sets of particles and the error accumulates because the history is integrated over time.
suggested_fix: Write 'd_history_one(index,v) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_buf(m++));'.

summary: post_force silently does nothing for pairstyle 'granular' (and for wallstyle 'region'): the if/else chain has no branch and no error for them, so the wall exerts no force at all.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:107-119 'if (pairstyle == HOOKE) error->all(...); else if (pairstyle == HOOKE_HISTORY) { ... } else if (pairstyle == HERTZ_HISTORY) error->all(...);' - there is no branch for the fourth style.  The base class header src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.h:29 declares 'enum { HOOKE, HOOKE_HISTORY, HERTZ_HISTORY, GRANULAR };' so 'fix wall/gran/kk granular ...' (accepted by FixWallGranOld's constructor, src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:81 'else if (strcmp(arg[3],"granular") == 0) pairstyle = GRANULAR;') leaves pairstyle == 3 and falls off the end of the chain.  The file's own shadowing enum at fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:24 'enum{HOOKE,HOOKE_HISTORY,HERTZ_HISTORY,BONDED_HISTORY};' hides this: value 3 is named BONDED_HISTORY there and is never tested.  The same hole exists in the inner chain: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:110-117 dispatches only XPLANE/YPLANE/ZPLANE/ZCYLINDER, so wallstyle REGION (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:379) launches no kernel either.
failure_scenario: 'fix wall/gran/kk granular hertz/material ... tangential mindlin ...' (or any hooke/history wall attached to a region) runs to completion with no error message and zero wall force - particles pass straight through the wall, while the plain 'fix wall/gran' gives the correct granular contact forces.
suggested_fix: Add a final 'else error->all(FLERR, "Fix wall/gran/kk does not yet support ... style");' to both the pairstyle and the wallstyle chain, and rename the third enumerator in fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp to GRANULAR so it matches fix_wall_gran_old.h.

summary: post_force syncs only X and MASK to the host before calling Group::xcm()/Group::mass(), but those routines also read atom->image, atom->type and atom->rmass, whose host copies are stale after DomainKokkos::pbc() marks IMAGE modified on the device - the unwrapped center of mass is then wrong by whole box lengths.
evidence: fix_spring_kokkos.cpp:67 'atomKK->sync(Host, X_MASK | MASK_MASK);' (and the identical line 126 in the COUPLE branch) immediately followed by 'if (group->dynamic[igroup]) masstotal = group->mass(igroup); group->xcm(igroup, masstotal, xcm);' (lines 69-70, 128-131).  src/group.cpp Group::xcm reads 'imageint *image = atom->image; ... domain->unmap(x[i], image[i], unwrap);' plus 'int *type = atom->type; double *mass = atom->mass; double *rmass = atom->rmass;'.  src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:398-430 (DomainKokkos::pbc) runs DomainPBCFunctor on the device over atomKK->k_image and ends with 'atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK|V_MASK|IMAGE_MASK);' - so the host image array is stale until something syncs IMAGE_MASK to the host.  Nothing does inside the run loop: VerletKokkos::run sets 'lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 0;' (verlet_kokkos.cpp:311) and only performs 'atomKK->sync(Host,ALL_MASK)' on output timesteps (verlet_kokkos.cpp:547) and after the loop (:555).  Contrast the CPU FixSpring, which runs entirely on the host with always-current image flags.
failure_scenario: 'fix spring/kk tether' (or couple) on a group whose atoms cross a periodic boundary during the run: on every non-thermo timestep after a pbc remap, domain->unmap uses the pre-remap image flag with the post-remap coordinate, so xcm jumps by one box length, and the spring force k*(r-r0) applied to the whole group is grossly wrong (and espring / f_spring output with it).
suggested_fix: Change both syncs to 'atomKK->sync(Host, X_MASK | MASK_MASK | IMAGE_MASK | TYPE_MASK | RMASS_MASK);' so every array Group::xcm()/Group::mass() touches is current on the host.

summary: The d_b_stats/d_a_stats bond/angle statistics that min_post_force allocates, zeroes and accumulates with atomics every minimization step are never copied to the host, never MPI-reduced and never printed - the work and the per-step device allocation are entirely wasted.
evidence: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:433-446 allocate and zero 'd_b_stats'/'d_a_stats' on every min_post_force call; lines 577-581 and 608-611 accumulate into them with Kokkos::atomic_add/max/min.  'grep -n "[db]_[ba]_stats" src/KOKKOS/fix_shake_kokkos.{cpp,h}' shows no other use: no deep_copy back to the host, no MPI_Allreduce, no output.  The CPU original does the reduce and the printing inline in min_post_force (RIGID/fix_shake.cpp:996-1031).  The Kokkos version instead prints via FixShake::stats() (fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:504-507), which recomputes the statistics from the current coordinates, so the accumulators are pure dead code.  A related inconsistency inside the dead block: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:607-612 updates a_max/a_min only 'if (count > 0)', whereas RIGID/fix_shake.cpp:988-989 updates them unconditionally.
failure_scenario: any 'minimize' with 'fix shake/kk ... output_every > 0': two extra device allocations plus a full atomic scatter per step whose result is discarded.
suggested_fix: Either copy d_b_stats/d_a_stats back to b_count/b_ave/b_max/b_min and reduce+print them as FixShake::min_post_force does, or delete the accumulators and the zeroing kernel and keep only the FixShake::stats() call.

summary: FixShardlowKokkos binds the per-type mass array to a device view but never syncs atomKK->k_mass to the device, so on a GPU build the SSA kernel reads whatever the device copy of mass[] happens to contain.
evidence: fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:214-220 'if (atomKK->rmass) { massPerI = true; masses = atomKK->k_rmass.view<DeviceType>(); } else { massPerI = false; masses = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>(); }' - no 'atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()' anywhere in the file ('grep -n k_mass src/KOKKOS/fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp' returns only that line).  masses is then read inside the device kernel at fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:415 'const KK_FLOAT mass_i = masses(massPerI ? i : itype);' and :465 'const KK_FLOAT mass_j = masses(massPerI ? j : jtype);'.  There is no MASS bit in src/atom_masks.h (only RMASS_MASK, line 34), so the datamask sync at fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:619 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK|V_MASK|TYPE_MASK|RMASS_MASK|UCOND_MASK|UMECH_MASK|DPDTHETA_MASK)' cannot cover it.  Every other KOKKOS style that reads k_mass on the device syncs it explicitly, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 'atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();' and src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_kokkos.cpp:46,54.
failure_scenario: CUDA/HIP build, a dpd/fdt/energy system with per-type masses (no per-atom rmass) and a non-kk integrator (plain 'fix nve', which FixShardlow::setup accepts, src/DPD-REACT/fix_shardlow.cpp:158-165): nothing ever copies mass[] to the device, so massinv_i/massinv_j in ssa_update_dpde are computed from uninitialized device memory and the Shardlow velocity/energy updates are garbage or NaN.
suggested_fix: Add 'atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();' in FixShardlowKokkos::init() (or right before the assignment in pre_neighbor()), matching fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46.

summary: The Kokkos constructor frees the base class's foriginal array but leaves Fix::array_atom pointing at the freed memory (and drops the base's zero-initialization), so any per-atom access to f_ID before the first post_force reads freed memory.
evidence: src/fix_store_force.cpp:36-44 (base constructor) 'nmax = atom->nmax; memory->create(foriginal, nmax, 3, "store/force:foriginal"); array_atom = foriginal; ... for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++) foriginal[i][0] = foriginal[i][1] = foriginal[i][2] = 0.0;' with the comment 'zero the array since dump may access it on timestep 0 / zero the array since a variable may access it before first run'.  src/KOKKOS/fix_store_force_kokkos.cpp:40-42 then does 'memory->destroy(foriginal); foriginal = nullptr; nmax = 0;' without touching array_atom, which still holds the row-pointer block that memory->destroy() just freed.  array_atom is only refreshed later, inside post_force's reallocation branch (fix_store_force_kokkos.cpp:70-76 'array_atom = foriginal;').
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all store/force/kk' followed by any per-atom access before the first setup/run - e.g. 'write_dump all custom out.txt id f_1[1]' or an atom-style variable referencing f_1[1] evaluated by a command before 'run' - dereferences the freed pointer block (use-after-free; garbage values or a segfault), whereas the CPU style deliberately returns zeros.
suggested_fix: In the Kokkos constructor set 'array_atom = nullptr;' after freeing, or better: allocate k_foriginal there with nmax = atom->nmax, zero the host side for nlocal atoms and set array_atom = foriginal, reproducing the base class contract.

summary: FixWallFlowKokkos::init() replaces the base init() instead of calling it, silently dropping the triclinic, rigid-body and box-change compatibility checks that FixWallFlow::init() performs.
evidence: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:57-68 'template <class DeviceType> void FixWallFlowKokkos<DeviceType>::init() { atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read); k_current_segment.template sync<DeviceType>(); d_x = ...; copymode = 1; Kokkos::parallel_for(...TagFixWallFlowInit...); copymode = 0; k_current_segment.template modify<DeviceType>(); }' - there is no 'FixWallFlow::init();' call.  The base version (src/fix_wall_flow.cpp:185-217) does much more than fill current_segment: 'if (domain->triclinic != 0) error->all(FLERR, "Fix wall/flow cannot be used with triclinic simulation box");' plus the loop over modify->get_fix_list() that raises 'Fix wall/flow is not compatible with rigid bodies' (nrigid) and 'Fix wall/flow is not compatible with simulation box size changing along flow direction' (box_change on the flow axis).  Only the last five lines of that function (the current_segment fill) are reproduced by the kernel.  Every other /kk style in this group calls its base init() first (e.g. fix_viscous_kokkos.cpp:112, fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:80, fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:76).
failure_scenario: 'fix wall/flow/kk x ...' combined with 'fix rigid' or with 'fix npt' straining the flow axis, or a 'change_box ... triclinic' issued after the fix was defined: the plain CPU fix stops with a clear error, the /kk variant runs and produces wrong results (the wall coordinates walls.front()/back() were frozen at construction from domain->boxlo/boxhi, so a changing box silently misplaces the walls).
suggested_fix: Call FixWallFlow::init() at the top of FixWallFlowKokkos::init() (its current_segment loop is harmless and is immediately overwritten by the device kernel), or replicate the three checks.

summary: datamask_read omits V_MASK although end_of_step's kernel writes only selected entries of the velocity array and then claims the whole array as device-modified, so a host-side velocity update made earlier in the step is discarded.
evidence: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:38-39 'datamask_read = X_MASK | RMASS_MASK | TYPE_MASK | MASK_MASK; datamask_modify = V_MASK;'.  end_of_step (fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:81-101) only does 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read);' and then binds 'd_v = atomKK->k_v.template view<DeviceType>();' (:85); the kernel writes just three components for the atoms that crossed a wall (fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:156-160 'd_v(atom_i, flowax) = v * direction; ...') and the call ends with 'atomKK->modified(execution_space, datamask_modify);' (:101).  src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp wraps every fix callback with exactly the same pair ('atomKK->sync(fix[i]->execution_space,fix[i]->datamask_read); ... atomKK->modified(fix[i]->execution_space,fix[i]->datamask_modify);'), so nothing else brings v to the device.  Sibling styles that partially overwrite v do sync it first, e.g. fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:145 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,V_MASK|MASK_MASK);' and fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:162.
failure_scenario: any run mixing 'fix wall/flow/kk' with a non-KOKKOS style that writes velocities on the host (a plain 'fix langevin', 'fix momentum', or the exchange_comm_legacy Domain::pbc path, src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:381 'atomKK->modified(Host,X_MASK|V_MASK|MASK_MASK|IMAGE_MASK)'): the device copy of v is never refreshed, the fix marks it as the newest version, and every velocity except those of the few wall-crossing atoms silently reverts to an older state.
suggested_fix: Add V_MASK to datamask_read in the constructor (or call 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, V_MASK)' in end_of_step before binding d_v).

summary: The device hooke/history kernel omits the limit_damping clamp on the normal force, so the 'limit_damping' keyword is silently ignored by fix wall/gran/kk.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:226-227 'KK_FLOAT damp = meff*gamman_kk*vnnr*rsqinv; KK_FLOAT ccel = kn_kk*(radius-r)*rinv - damp;' goes straight on to the tangential terms.  The CPU original has one more line at src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:897-899: 'damp = meff*gamman*vnnr*rsqinv; ccel = kn*(radius-r)*rinv - damp; if (limit_damping && (ccel < 0.0)) ccel = 0.0;'.  limit_damping is a real command-line option parsed at fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:120-123 ('if (strcmp(arg[iarg],"limit_damping") == 0) { limit_damping = 1; iarg += 1; }') and is a plain int member (fix_wall_gran_old.h:72) that the functor copy already carries.  Every other line of the kernel matches hooke_history() exactly.
failure_scenario: 'fix wall/gran/kk hooke/history kn kt gamman gammat xmu 1 limit_damping zplane ...': for fast approaches where the damping term exceeds the elastic term, ccel stays negative and the wall pulls the particle in (and the tangential Coulomb limit fn = xmu*|ccel*r| is computed from the unclamped value), whereas the CPU fix clamps it to zero.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (limit_damping && (ccel < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.0))) ccel = 0.0;' after the ccel assignment in the kernel.

summary: The Kokkos overrides of grow_arrays and copy_arrays handle only history_one and drop the array_atom half, and maxexchange is set to size_history, so the 'contacts' option leaves array_atom never regrown while the inherited pack/unpack_exchange still read and write size_peratom_cols entries of it.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:303-311 'void FixWallGranKokkos<DeviceType>::grow_arrays(int nmax) { if (use_history) { ... memoryKK->grow_kokkos(k_history_one,history_one,nmax,size_history,...); ... } }' and :316-323 copy_arrays likewise only wraps the history part.  The base versions do both: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1567-1573 'if (use_history) memory->grow(history_one,...); if (peratom_flag) { memory->grow(array_atom,nmax,size_peratom_cols,"fix_wall_gran_old:array_atom"); }' and :1579-1588 copy_arrays copies array_atom too.  The KOKKOS pack_exchange/unpack_exchange delegate to the base (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:348, :356), which writes 'size_history + size_peratom_cols' doubles when peratom_flag (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1609-1625), yet the constructor sets 'maxexchange = size_history;' (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:35).  'contacts' is a supported keyword (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:410-412 'peratom_flag = 1; size_peratom_cols = 8;').  On top of that the device kernel never fills array_atom and never calls clear_stored_contacts(), which the CPU post_force does (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:637-639, 713-722).
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all wall/gran/kk hooke/history ... zplane 0 NULL contacts': array_atom is allocated once (in the base constructor at the initial atom->nmax) and never grown, so as soon as atoms are added or nmax grows, copy_arrays/pack_exchange index past the end of it (heap corruption); and even before that, the per-atom contact output is always the stale/zero content the kernel never writes.
suggested_fix: Call FixWallGranOld::grow_arrays()/copy_arrays() for the peratom_flag part from the Kokkos overrides, set maxexchange to size_history + (peratom_flag ? size_peratom_cols : 0), and either fill array_atom in the kernel or reject the 'contacts' keyword in FixWallGranKokkos::init().

summary: The Kokkos thermostats remove/restore the velocity bias with the group-wide Compute::remove_bias_all()/_kk() hooks, but the CPU originals use the per-atom Compute::remove_bias(i,v[i]) - three bias-capable temperature computes implement only the per-atom form, so with 'fix_modify temp' pointing at one of them the /kk fix silently thermostats the biased velocities.
evidence: fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:135-143 and :158-166 'if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->remove_bias_all_kk(); else { ... temperature->remove_bias_all(); ... } }' (the identical pattern is at fix_temp_rescale_kokkos.cpp:138-146/161-169 and fix_temp_csvr_kokkos.cpp:129-137/158-166).  The CPU originals loop per atom: src/fix_temp_berendsen.cpp:183-193 'for (...) if (mask[i] & groupbit) { temperature->remove_bias(i,v[i]); v[i][0] *= lamda; ... temperature->restore_bias(i,v[i]); }' and src/fix_temp_rescale.cpp:183-191, src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_temp_csvr.cpp:48-57 of end_of_step.  src/compute.h:153-159 declares 'virtual void remove_bias_all() {}' / 'virtual void remove_bias_all_kk() {}' as empty base methods, and a scan of every compute that sets tempbias shows three that declare remove_bias(int,double*) but no remove_bias_all(): src/compute_temp_sphere.h:36-39, src/ASPHERE/compute_temp_asphere.h, src/BODY/compute_temp_body.h.  compute temp/sphere/kk (src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_sphere_kokkos.cpp:35 'kokkosable = 1') likewise overrides neither, so both the kk and the non-kk branch above are no-ops for it.
failure_scenario: 'compute ts all temp/sphere ... bias <some bias compute>' plus 'fix_modify 1 temp ts' on a 'fix temp/berendsen/kk' (or temp/rescale/kk, temp/csvr/kk): the bias is never subtracted, so the streaming/rotational component is rescaled together with the thermal one - the thermostat drives the wrong quantity, whereas the plain CPU fix removes the bias per atom.
suggested_fix: Either implement remove_bias_all()/restore_bias_all() (and the _kk variants) in compute temp/sphere, temp/asphere and temp/body, or make the /kk thermostats refuse a temperature compute whose remove_bias_all is the base no-op, as fix temp/csld/kk already does for the whole BIAS case (fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:103-104).

summary: FixShardlow, the base class of the Kokkos style that is copied by value into device functors, has no 'if (copymode) return;' guard as the first line of its destructor.
evidence: src/DPD-REACT/fix_shardlow.cpp:118-122 'FixShardlow::~FixShardlow() { memory->destroy(rand_state); maxRNG = 0; }' - no copymode guard ('grep -n copymode src/DPD-REACT/fix_shardlow.cpp' finds nothing).  FixShardlowKokkos passes '*this' to Kokkos::parallel_for at fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:624,626,660,662, and its own destructor (fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:106-109) also lacks the guard.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 1 requires the guard in every base-class destructor a _kokkos style inherits from.
failure_scenario: today only latent: FixShardlowKokkos::initial_integrate overrides the base version, so the private 'rand_state' the base destructor frees is always nullptr and memory->destroy() is a no-op.  Any future code path that lets the base allocate rand_state (or any new allocation added to ~FixShardlow) becomes a double free when the functor copies are destroyed.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (copymode) return;' as the first line of FixShardlow::~FixShardlow() (and of ~FixShardlowKokkos).

summary: post_force pulls the full coordinate array back to the host every timestep just to compute the group center of mass with the host-only Group::xcm(), which defeats most of the benefit of the device kernel.
evidence: fix_spring_kokkos.cpp:67 and :126 'atomKK->sync(Host, X_MASK | MASK_MASK);' followed by group->xcm(...) on lines 70 and 130-131; the force kernels at :113/:118/:184/:189 then run on the device.  Other KOKKOS fixes that need a group reduction do it with a device parallel_reduce instead (e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp), and .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md warns that forcing a full x transfer every step 'is slower than no /kk at all'.
failure_scenario: any GPU run with 'fix spring/kk': one device->host copy of x (3*nlocal doubles) per timestep, plus (if IMAGE_MASK is added per the sync bug above) the image array too.
suggested_fix: Compute the center of mass (and the dynamic-group mass) with a Kokkos::parallel_reduce over the device views followed by a single MPI_Allreduce, as fix_momentum_kokkos does.

summary: fix temp/csld/kk draws its random velocities from a Kokkos random pool but inherits the base class write_restart/restart, which save and restore only the unused RanMars generator - so a restarted run replays the same random-velocity sequence from the beginning instead of continuing the stream.
evidence: fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:45-49 seeds 'rand_pool(utils::inumeric(FLERR, arg[6], false, lmp) + comm->me)' and the kernel draws from it (fix_temp_csld_kokkos.cpp:211-215 'rand_type rand_gen = rand_pool.get_state(); ... rand_gen.normal() ...').  The class overrides only the constructor, destructor, init(), end_of_step() and temp_scalar() (fix_temp_csld_kokkos.h:42-56), so src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_temp_csld.cpp:294-329 remain in force: write_restart does 'random->get_state(state); MPI_Gather(...)' and restart does 'random->set_state(list+2+comm->me*103)' on the RanMars object that the Kokkos path never advances.  Nothing re-seeds or restores rand_pool, which is reconstructed from arg[6]+comm->me on every read_restart.
failure_scenario: run 10000 steps with 'fix temp/csld/kk', write_restart, read_restart and continue: the thermostat's gaussian velocity draws restart at the head of the same stream the first run used, so the two segments of the trajectory share identical noise, unlike the CPU 'fix temp/csld' whose RanMars state is restored.  (A second, smaller inconsistency: restart() reads 'list+2+comm->me*103' while write_restart strides by PRNGSIZE = 103, so the two agree only by coincidence of that constant.)
suggested_fix: Override write_restart()/restart() to save and restore the Kokkos pool state (or at minimum document in doc/src/fix_temp_csld.rst that the /kk variant does not restore its random-number state).

summary: min_post_force marks x as modified on the device before calling stats(), although the kernel never writes x; this can force a spurious device->host copy of the coordinates or collide with a pending host-side modification.
evidence: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:504-507 'if (update->ntimestep == next_output) { atomKK->modified(execution_space, X_MASK); stats(); }'.  The min_post_force kernel (fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:515-615) only reads d_x and writes d_f; the datamask sync at line 386 is 'atomKK->sync(execution_space, X_MASK | F_MASK)'.  FixShakeKokkos::stats() already does 'atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK)' (fix_shake_kokkos.cpp, stats()), so the modified() call is not needed to get x onto the host.
failure_scenario: a minimization step in which the host copy of x is the current one (host modify flag set) and this call also sets the device modify flag, leaving both sides claimed for k_x.
suggested_fix: Remove the 'atomKK->modified(execution_space, X_MASK);' call; stats() already syncs x to the host.

summary: pack_forward_comm_kokkos and unpack_forward_comm_kokkos launch Kokkos::parallel_for with '*this' as the functor without setting copymode = 1, so the functor copy's destructor is only harmless because post_force() happens to have set copymode earlier.
evidence: fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:2130-2133 'if (pbc_flag) Kokkos::parallel_for(...TagFixShakePackForwardComm<1>...,*this); else Kokkos::parallel_for(...<0>...,*this);' and fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:2178 'Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType, TagFixShakeUnpackForwardComm>(0,n),*this);' - neither is bracketed by 'copymode = 1; ... copymode = 0;'.  Every other parallel_for(*this) in the file does bracket it (lines 262-266, 430-463, 633-740, 1964-1969, 2052-2056), as do the sibling styles (fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:497-501, fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:288-292).  Without the guard the copy's ~FixShakeKokkos would run with copymode == 0 and execute the full teardown, including 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_shake_atom,shake_atom)' which does 'sfree(array)' (KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:272-281) on the row pointers still owned by the original object.
failure_scenario: any future caller that invokes comm->forward_comm(this) outside FixShakeKokkos::post_force() (which sets copymode = 1 at line 633 before the forward comm at line 668) gets a double free of shake_atom/shake_type/closest_list plus a spurious bondtype_findset() pass over all local atoms.
suggested_fix: Set copymode = 1 before and copymode = 0 after the parallel_for in both pack_forward_comm_kokkos and unpack_forward_comm_kokkos.

summary: The exchange hooks of fix wall/gran/kk are missing three of the sync/modify calls their sibling styles perform: no modify<DeviceType>() after pack_exchange_kokkos writes the device history, no sync<DeviceType>() before the unpack kernel, and no sync_host() before the host unpack_exchange.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:386-411 pack_exchange_kokkos does 'k_history_one.template sync<DeviceType>();' and then runs a kernel that WRITES d_history_one (the copylist compaction at :375-380 'd_history_one(i,v) = d_history_one(j,v);'), but never calls 'k_history_one.template modify<DeviceType>();' - compare fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:240 and fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:231 and fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:257, which all do.  fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:431-450 unpack_exchange_kokkos writes the device view and calls modify<DeviceType>() (:449) without a preceding sync<DeviceType>() - compare fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:286 and fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:277.  fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:353-361 unpack_exchange calls 'FixWallGranOld::unpack_exchange(nlocal,buf)' (which writes history_one on the host) and then modify_host() without the 'k_history_one.sync_host();' that its own pack_exchange does at :346 and that fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:318 does.
failure_scenario: a step where atoms leave a rank but none arrive (nrecv == 0 for every dimension): the device-side compaction is never registered, so the DualView still reports both sides in sync, and the next copy_arrays()/unpack_exchange() modify_host() makes the stale host copy authoritative - the compacted shear histories are lost.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_history_one.template modify<DeviceType>();' at the end of pack_exchange_kokkos, 'k_history_one.template sync<DeviceType>();' before the parallel_for in unpack_exchange_kokkos, and 'k_history_one.sync_host();' at the start of unpack_exchange.

summary: unpack_exchange_kokkos writes d_current_segment on the device and marks it device-modified without first syncing it there, so a pending host-side modification of current_segment is dropped for the atoms the kernel does not touch.
evidence: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:279-295: the function binds d_buf/d_indices, launches TagFixWallFlowUnpackExchange (which writes 'd_current_segment(index) = ...' for received atoms only, :276) and ends with 'k_current_segment.template modify<DeviceType>();' - there is no 'k_current_segment.template sync<DeviceType>();'.  Its own pack_exchange_kokkos does perform that sync (fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:237), and both sibling styles built from the same template sync before the unpack kernel: fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:286 'k_xoriginal.template sync<DeviceType>();' and fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:277.  The host side can legitimately be the newer one, because copy_arrays (:187-192) and unpack_exchange (:262-268) both end with k_current_segment.modify_host().
failure_scenario: a legacy host sort (AtomKokkos::sort() falls back to it when any other extra-grow fix lacks sort_device) marks current_segment host-modified via copy_arrays; on the next device exchange in which this rank sends no atoms for a dimension but receives some, pack_exchange_kokkos is skipped (comm_kokkos.cpp:1369 'if (nsend) { ... }') so no sync happens, and unpack_exchange_kokkos then promotes the stale device copy - atoms get the wrong segment and are re-thermostatted spuriously (or not at all) at the next wall crossing.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_current_segment.template sync<DeviceType>();' before the parallel_for in unpack_exchange_kokkos, matching pack_exchange_kokkos and the sibling styles.

summary: The per-element weight read from wjelem is stored in an int instead of a double, truncating any non-integer element weight (and zeroing weights below 1) in both the descriptor and the descriptor-derivative kernels.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:757-758 'const int jelem = t_jelems[ipair]; int weight = t_wjelem[jelem];' (MLIAPSO3SpectrumTag), and the same 'int weight = t_wjelem[jelem];' at lines 893 and 933 (MLIAPSO3SpectrumDXDRTag). t_wjelem is 'float_1d t_wjelem' (src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.h:75), filled from the double array descriptor->wjelem in src/KOKKOS/mliap_descriptor_kokkos.h:36-40. The CPU original declares it double: src/ML-IAP/mliap_so3.cpp:819 'double weight;' with 'weight = wjelem[jelem];' at line 871 (and 952/1005/1063 for spectrum_dxdr), used as 'm_clist_r[tn] = m_clist_r[tn] * weight;' (line 914). The value comes straight from the 'welems' line of the SO3 parameter file, parsed with utils::numeric (src/ML-IAP/mliap_descriptor_so3.cpp:150-155), so it is an arbitrary real number.
failure_scenario: An SO3 parameter file with 'welems 1.0 0.5' (or any non-integer weight): with pair_style mliap/kk the second element's contribution is multiplied by 0 instead of 0.5, so all descriptors, energies and forces involving that element are wrong, while pair_style mliap gives the correct answer. Even 'welems 1.0 1.0' is only correct by luck.
suggested_fix: Change 'int weight' to 'double weight' at lines 758, 893 and 933 (the later 'double(weight)' casts then become no-ops).

summary: MLIAPDummyModelKokkos's destructor decrements the Python unified_interface reference that its base class destructor also decrements, so the object is released twice for a single incref.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:140-145 '~MLIAPDummyModelKokkos() { // manually decrement borrowed reference from Python\n  Py_DECREF(unified_interface); }' -- and the base destructor, which always runs afterwards, does exactly the same: src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:123-127 'MLIAPDummyModel::~MLIAPDummyModel() { Py_DECREF(unified_interface); }'. build_unified takes exactly one reference per object: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:251-255 'model->unified_interface = unified_interface; Py_INCREF(unified_interface); descriptor->unified_interface = unified_interface; Py_INCREF(unified_interface);'. The sibling Kokkos descriptor gets this right and deliberately leaves the DECREF to the base: lines 41-45 '~MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos() { // done in base class\n  // Py_DECREF(unified_interface); }'.
