failure_scenario: 'pair_style mliap/kk unified <module>' followed by redefining pair_style, or simply shutting LAMMPS down: three Py_DECREFs are issued against two Py_INCREFs, dropping the interface object's refcount to zero (or below) while the descriptor still holds a pointer to it -- a use-after-free/abort in CPython, or 'Fatal Python error: deallocating None'-style corruption.
suggested_fix: Delete the Py_DECREF from ~MLIAPDummyModelKokkos() and let MLIAPDummyModel's destructor release the reference, mirroring the descriptor.

summary: The reduction functor stores a raw host pointer to the RegBlockKokkos/RegSphereKokkos object and dereferences it inside the device kernel, which is an illegal memory access on CUDA/HIP unless the build opts into unified memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_region_kokkos.h:96-112 'FixWallRegionKokkos<DeviceType> c; T *regionKK; ... KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator()(const int i, value_type result) const { c.wall_particle(regionKK,i,result); }' -- the fix itself is copied BY VALUE ('c(*c_ptr)') but the region is kept as a pointer, filled in src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:117-122 with the address returned by 'dynamic_cast<RegBlockKokkos<DeviceType>*>(region)', i.e. an ordinary host-heap object created by Domain's region factory. The kernel then does 'regionKK->match_kokkos(...)' (fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:159) and 'regionKK->surface_kokkos(...)' (line 173), which read instance members such as dynamic/openflag/interior/xlo/xhi and the RegionRemapKokkos boxremap (src/KOKKOS/region_block_kokkos.h:68-119, 122-127) from that host address. Every other Kokkos style that needs a region avoids this by calling the region's own match_all_kokkos(), which copies '*this' into the kernel (e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_setforce_kokkos.cpp:85-90, fix_addforce_kokkos.cpp:105-110, compute_temp_region_kokkos.cpp:69-70). UVM is not on by default: cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:58-64 rejects Kokkos_ENABLE_CUDA_UVM and doc/src/Speed_kokkos.rst:439-441 documents Kokkos_ENABLE_IMPL_CUDA_UNIFIED_MEMORY as an opt-in CMake option.
failure_scenario: 'region r block ... ' + 'fix w all wall/region/kk r lj93 1.0 1.0 2.5' on a CUDA or HIP build without Kokkos_ENABLE_IMPL_CUDA_UNIFIED_MEMORY: the first post_force kernel dereferences a host address on the device and the run dies with 'an illegal memory address was encountered' (or, worse, silently reads garbage region geometry and produces wrong wall forces).
suggested_fix: Pass the region object by value into the functor (store 'T regionKK;' copy-constructed from '*regionKK', the way the fix itself is copied) after setting the region's copymode, or restructure so the kernel is launched from inside the region class like match_all_kokkos() does.

summary: The kernel that fills elems iterates over atom->nmax instead of nlocal+nghost, so it reads uninitialized entries of atom->type and uses them to index the element map view, which is only ntypes+1 long.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:186-189 'Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType>(0,nmax), KOKKOS_LAMBDA (int i) { const int itype = type(i); d_elems(i) = map(itype); });' -- the CPU original loops only over the valid atoms, src/ML-IAP/mliap_data.cpp:206-209 'for (int i = 0; i < nall; i++) { const int itype = type[i]; elems[i] = map[itype]; }' with 'int nall = atom->nlocal + atom->nghost;' (line 118). nmax is atom->nmax (set at src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:72-73), so indices in [nall, nmax) hold whatever was last in the type array, or uninitialized memory right after Atom::grow(). The map view is allocated with exactly ntypes+1 entries: src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:159 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_map, map, n+1, "pair_mliap:map");'.
failure_scenario: pair_style mliap/kk immediately after the atom arrays are grown (e.g. the first steps of a run, or after a large migration): type(i) for i >= nlocal+nghost is an arbitrary int, so map(itype) reads outside the ntypes+1 map allocation. With Kokkos bounds checking enabled the run aborts; without it, it is a silent out-of-bounds read (and a segfault if the index is far enough out).
suggested_fix: Launch the kernel over RangePolicy(0, nall) (nlocal+nghost) as the CPU version does, matching the deep_copy that already zeroes the rest of d_elems.

summary: For wallstyle ZCYLINDER with the 'shear' keyword the wall velocity vwall is accumulated with += inside the per-atom loop, so every contacting atom sees a wall velocity contaminated by all previously processed atoms.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:602-608 sets vwall once before the loop ('vwall[0] = vwall[1] = vwall[2] = 0.0; ... else if (wshear) vwall[axis] = vshear;'), then inside the 'for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++)' loop at lines 666-670: 'if (wshear && axis != 2) { vwall[0] += vshear * x[i][1]/delxy; vwall[1] += -vshear * x[i][0]/delxy; vwall[2] = 0.0; }'. vwall is never reset per atom, so the rotational wall velocity of atom i is added on top of the values left by atoms 0..i-1 (and on top of the pre-loop vwall[axis]=vshear).
failure_scenario: fix f all wall/gran/old hooke ... zcylinder 10.0 shear x 1.0 : with N atoms in contact with the cylinder, the effective wall velocity used for atom k is sum over all previous contacting atoms, growing without bound -> wrong tangential/damping forces and unphysical heating.
suggested_fix: Compute the rotational wall velocity into a per-atom local copy (e.g. 'double vwall_local[3] = {0,0,0}; vwall_local[0] = vshear*x[i][1]/delxy; ...') and pass that to the interaction routines instead of mutating the shared vwall array.

summary: atomKK->modified() for X_MASK|V_MASK is called before the reflection kernels run instead of after them, so a host-side sync triggered from inside the wall loop (equal-style wall variable) clears the device-modified flag and the reflections of the remaining walls are never copied back to the host.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_reflect_kokkos.cpp:48-49 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read); atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify);' -- the parallel_for that actually writes x and v is only issued later, at lines 77-79 inside the 'for (int m = 0; m < nwall; m++)' loop, and line 65 evaluates 'input->variable->compute_equal(varindex[m])' between the modified() call and the last kernel. Every other Kokkos fix in the package calls modified() after the kernels, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_setforce_kokkos.cpp:110-145 and src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp:121-129, and the sibling style src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_piston_kokkos.cpp:164-203 does the same.
failure_scenario: 'fix w all wall/reflect/kk xlo 0.0 xhi v_top' where the equal-style variable v_top references a compute or thermo keyword that reads per-atom x on the host: evaluating the variable syncs x device->host and clears k_x's device-modified flag; the subsequent xhi reflection kernel then writes only the device copy, and the following host read (dump, another non-kokkos fix) sees unreflected coordinates.
suggested_fix: Move 'atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify);' to after the wall loop (just before the addstep_compute call).

summary: compute_gradients launches its reduction with the default execution space instead of RangePolicy<DeviceType>, so the mliap/kk/host variant of a GPU build runs the kernel on the GPU over host-space views.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_linear_kokkos.cpp:54 'Kokkos::parallel_reduce(data->nlistatoms, KOKKOS_LAMBDA (int ii, double &update) {' -- the integer form of parallel_reduce uses Kokkos::DefaultExecutionSpace, while the views captured on lines 41-49 come from '.template view<DeviceType>()'. The class is instantiated for both device types (lines 94-97 'template class MLIAPModelLinearKokkos<LMPDeviceType>; #ifdef LMP_KOKKOS_GPU template class MLIAPModelLinearKokkos<LMPHostType>;') and the host variant is reachable through 'PairStyle(mliap/kk/host,PairMLIAPKokkos<LMPHostType>)' (src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.h:22), which builds the model with 'new MLIAPModelLinearKokkos<DeviceType>(lmp,arg[iarg+2])' (src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:180). Every other kernel in this ML-IAP group spells the policy out, e.g. src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:148,154,186,228 and mliap_descriptor_so3_kokkos.cpp:92,205.
failure_scenario: A CUDA-enabled build running 'pair_style mliap/kk/host model linear ... descriptor so3 ...': the reduction is dispatched to Kokkos::Cuda while d_ielems/d_descriptors/d_betas/d_eatoms are HostSpace views, so the kernel dereferences host pointers on the device (illegal memory address, or silently wrong betas/energy).
suggested_fix: Use 'Kokkos::parallel_reduce(Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType>(0,data->nlistatoms), ...)' as the rest of the ML-IAP Kokkos code does.

summary: spectrum_dxdr() grows m_ulist_r/m_ulist_i/m_dYlm_r/m_dYlm_i for a larger atom count but forgets m_dclist, which the same kernel subviews by the identical chunk index.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:807-820 re-creates m_clisttot_r/i, and inside 'if (delta > 0)' re-creates m_ulist_r, m_ulist_i, m_dYlm_r and m_dYlm_i with the new num_of_temp -- m_dclist is absent. The only place m_dclist is allocated is init_arrays (line 244 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(m_dclist, num_of_temp, m_nmax, m_numYlms, 3, ...)'), which is called only from spectrum() (line 679). The DXDR kernel indexes it with the same chunk index as the views that were grown: line 886 'auto dclist = Kokkos::subview(m_dclist,ii_chunk,Kokkos::ALL,Kokkos::ALL,Kokkos::ALL);' with 'int ii_chunk = ii%m_chunk_size;' (line 879). spectrum() is skipped whenever the model is linear and eflag is 0 -- src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:113 'if (model->nonlinearflag || eflag)' and MLIAPModelLinear leaves nonlinearflag = 0 (src/ML-IAP/mliap_model.cpp:39).
failure_scenario: pair_style mliap/kk model linear ... descriptor so3 ...: on a non-thermo timestep (eflag = 0) where list->inum has grown since the last energy step, spectrum_dxdr enlarges m_ulist_r but not m_dclist, and the kernel writes dclist(n,i,k) through a subview whose first index is past the end of m_dclist -- out-of-bounds device writes and corrupted forces (or an abort with Kokkos bounds checking).
suggested_fix: Re-create m_dclist alongside m_ulist_r/m_dYlm_* in the 'if (delta > 0)' block of spectrum_dxdr, or simply call init_arrays(nlocal, ncoefs) at the top of spectrum_dxdr the way spectrum() does.

summary: init() increments roll_history_index / twist_history_index before they are ever assigned when the corresponding history is disabled, reading uninitialized members.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:519-541: roll_history_index is only assigned inside 'if (roll_history) {...}' and twist_history_index only inside 'if (twist_history) {...}', but lines 533-537 do 'if (normal_model == JKR) { tangential_history_index += 1; roll_history_index += 1; twist_history_index += 1; }' and lines 538-541 do the same for MINDLIN_RESCALE unconditionally. Neither index is initialized in the constructor (header src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.h:80-82 declares them plain ints).
failure_scenario: fix wall/gran/old granular jkr ... tangential linear_history ... (no rolling/twisting): roll_history_index and twist_history_index are read while indeterminate; harmless today only because granular() guards their use with roll_model/twist_model, but it is undefined behaviour and trips MemorySanitizer/valgrind.
suggested_fix: Initialize normal_history_index/tangential_history_index/roll_history_index/twist_history_index to 0 in the constructor (or at the top of init()) before the conditional increments.

summary: roll_model and twist_model are left uninitialized when pairstyle is not GRANULAR.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:87-90 initializes 'normal_model = NORMAL_NONE; tangential_model = TANGENTIAL_NONE; damping_model = DAMPING_NONE;' but roll_model/twist_model are assigned only in the GRANULAR branch at line 127 ('roll_model = twist_model = NONE;'). For pairstyle HOOKE/HOOKE_HISTORY/HERTZ_HISTORY they stay indeterminate; the header src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.h:70 declares them without initializer.
failure_scenario: Any derived/accelerated variant or future code that queries roll_model/twist_model outside the GRANULAR branch (e.g. FixWallGranKokkos) reads garbage; with the CPU code path it is currently latent only because granular() is not called.
suggested_fix: Set 'roll_model = ROLL_NONE; twist_model = TWIST_NONE;' next to the other model defaults at line 88 so they are always defined.

summary: array_atom allocated by grow_arrays() when the 'contacts' keyword is used is never freed in the destructor.
evidence: grow_arrays (src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1567-1572) does 'if (peratom_flag) memory->grow(array_atom,nmax,size_peratom_cols,"fix_wall_gran_old:array_atom");' but the destructor (lines 476-491) only frees idregion, history_one and mass_rigid.
failure_scenario: 'fix ... wall/gran/old ... contacts' followed by 'unfix' (or repeated fix/unfix in a loop) leaks nmax*8 doubles per instance.
suggested_fix: Add 'memory->destroy(array_atom);' to ~FixWallGranOld() (after the copymode guard).

summary: The Kokkos random pool is seeded from the base-class member tseed, which is left uninitialized whenever the optional 'temp' keyword is not used.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_piston_kokkos.cpp:35-41 'FixWallPistonKokkos<DeviceType>::FixWallPistonKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp, int narg, char **arg) : FixWallPiston(lmp, narg, arg), ... rand_pool(tseed + comm->me)'. tseed is declared as a plain int in src/SHOCK/fix_wall_piston.h:40 ('int tempflag, tseed;') and is assigned ONLY inside the 'temp' keyword branch of the base constructor (src/SHOCK/fix_wall_piston.cpp:82-99: 'tseed = utils::inumeric(FLERR,arg[iarg+3],false,lmp);'); the constructor initializes tempflag/roughflag/... at lines 44-55 but never tseed. The CPU style avoids the issue because it only constructs RanMars inside that branch (line 96).
failure_scenario: 'fix p all wall/piston/kk zlo pos 0.0 vel 0.5' (no temp keyword): rand_pool is constructed with an indeterminate seed value; the read of the uninitialized tseed is undefined behaviour and is flagged by valgrind/MemorySanitizer. It also unconditionally allocates a full RNG state pool sized by device concurrency even when no thermostat is requested.
suggested_fix: Initialize tseed (e.g. to 0) in the FixWallPiston constructor next to the other defaults, and/or only construct/seed rand_pool when tempflag is set.

summary: grow_neigharrays() declares an unused host mirror of cutsq, producing an unused-variable warning.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:225-227 'auto d_cutsq=k_pairmliap->k_cutsq.template view<DeviceType>(); auto h_cutsq=k_pairmliap->k_cutsq.view_host(); auto d_numneighs = ...' -- h_cutsq is never referenced again in the function; only d_cutsq is used inside the parallel_reduce at line 244.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; -Wunused-variable noise and a hint that a host/device cutsq mix-up was intended here.
suggested_fix: Delete the h_cutsq line.

summary: The 'Loading python model complete' message is printed by every MPI rank because the comm->me == 0 guard of the CPU version was dropped.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:129-130 'model_loaded = 1; utils::logmesg(MLIAPModelKokkos<DeviceType>::lmp, "Loading python model complete.\n");' versus src/ML-IAP/mliap_model_python.cpp:131-132 'model_loaded = 1; if (comm->me == 0) utils::logmesg(lmp, "Loading python model complete.\n");'. The deferred-load message a few lines above (mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:106-107) does keep the guard, so the omission is clearly unintended.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style mliap/kk model mliappy ...' on N MPI ranks prints the line N times into the screen/log output.
suggested_fix: Wrap the logmesg in 'if (MLIAPModelKokkos<DeviceType>::comm->me == 0)' like the CPU version and like the deferred-load branch above it.

summary: The growth test for the 3-D k_dplist_r view compares the total element count against only its first extent, so the view is destroyed and reallocated on essentially every spectrum() call.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:697-701 'totali = (bigint) totaln * ncoefs * 3; if ( totali > (bigint)k_dplist_r.extent(0)) { memoryKK->realloc_kokkos(k_dplist_r, "MLIAP_SO3Kokkos:m_dplist_r", (int)totaln, ncoefs, 3); ... }'. k_dplist_r is 'float_3d' (npairs x ncoefs x 3), so extent(0) is totaln, and the test is 'totaln*ncoefs*3 > totaln_prev', which is true for every realistic ncoefs. The neighbouring tests for the 1-D m_sbes_array (line 684) and m_rip_array (line 691) correctly compare against the flat length.
failure_scenario: Every timestep that computes descriptors frees and re-allocates a npairs*ncoefs*3 double device array, adding an avoidable large allocation/deallocation per step.
suggested_fix: Compare against the actual first extent, e.g. 'if (totaln > (int)k_dplist_r.extent(0) || ncoefs != (int)k_dplist_r.extent(1))'.

summary: compute_forces() unconditionally marks the pair style's per-atom virial dual view host-modified and copies it to the device every step, even when per-atom virial tallying is off.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_descriptor_so3_kokkos.cpp:88-91 'auto d_vatom = data->k_pairmliap->k_vatom.template view<DeviceType>(); Kokkos::View<double[6], DeviceType> virial("virial"); data->k_pairmliap->k_vatom.modify_host(); data->k_pairmliap->k_vatom.template sync<DeviceType>();' -- neither statement is guarded by vflag_atom, unlike the matching write-back at lines 132-135 'if (vflag_atom) { ... modify<DeviceType>(); ... sync_host(); }'. The pair style has already put a zeroed k_vatom on both sides just before (src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:99-108), so the extra host->device copy is redundant even when vflag_atom is set.
failure_scenario: Every timestep copies the whole nmax x 6 vatom array host->device for nothing; on a GPU run without per-atom virial output this is a pure PCIe cost proportional to the atom count.
suggested_fix: Wrap the modify_host()/sync<DeviceType>() pair in 'if (vflag_atom)', or drop it entirely since pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp already leaves both sides zeroed and current.

summary: MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos::set_elements() forgets to set allocated_elements, so the per-element name strings it strdups are never freed.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:122-128 'void MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos<DeviceType>::set_elements(char **elems, int nelems) { nelements = nelems; elements = new char *[nelems]; for (int i = 0; i < nelems; i++) { elements[i] = utils::strdup(elems[i]); } }' versus the CPU original src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:108-114 which ends with 'allocated_elements = 1;'. The base destructor frees the strings only under that flag: src/ML-IAP/mliap_descriptor.cpp:36-40 'if (allocated_elements) for (int i = 0; i < nelements; i++) delete[] elements[i]; delete[] elements;'.
failure_scenario: Every 'pair_style mliap/kk unified ...' leaks nelements strdup'd strings; repeated pair_style redefinition in a long script leaks steadily.
suggested_fix: Add 'allocated_elements = 1;' at the end of MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos::set_elements().

summary: Every FixWall-derived Kokkos style declares V_MASK in datamask_read although none of them reads atom velocities, forcing an unnecessary velocity sync to the device on each wall evaluation.
evidence: 'datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK;' appears identically in src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:33, fix_wall_harmonic_outside_kokkos.cpp:33, fix_wall_lj1043_kokkos.cpp:37, fix_wall_lj126_kokkos.cpp:33, fix_wall_lj93_kokkos.cpp:40, fix_wall_morse_kokkos.cpp:35 and fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:47, and wall_particle() syncs that whole mask ('atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read);', e.g. fix_wall_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:100). The kernels only ever touch d_x, d_f and d_mask (fix_wall_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:101-103,137-158) -- no style in the family reads v.
failure_scenario: On a GPU run where another style has left the velocities host-modified, each wall_particle() call triggers a full nlocal x 3 host-to-device copy of v that is never used; with several walls this repeats per wall per timestep.
suggested_fix: Drop V_MASK from datamask_read in these seven constructors (fix_wall_reflect_kokkos.cpp:36 already lists only what it uses).

summary: set_k_coeffelem() frees the previous coeffelem with memory->destroy(), which would corrupt the heap if it is ever called a second time on a model whose coeffelem is already Kokkos-backed.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_kokkos.h:87-100 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_coeffelem, tmp, model->nelements, model->nparams, ...); ... memory->destroy(model->coeffelem); model->coeffelem = tmp;'. After the first call model->coeffelem is the array produced by create_kokkos, whose row pointers alias Kokkos-owned memory (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:236-241 'array[i] = &data.view_host()(i,0);'), and the matching deallocator only frees the row-pointer block (memory_kokkos.h:272-281 destroy_kokkos, which does sfree(array) but never sfree(array[0])). Memory::destroy for a 2d array frees array[0] as well.
failure_scenario: Today the only callers are one-shot constructor paths (mliap_model_linear_kokkos.cpp:30, mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:81), so it does not fire; a second call (e.g. reloading coefficients for a deferred python model) would free Kokkos-owned memory with sfree() and corrupt the heap.
suggested_fix: Guard the swap, e.g. call memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_coeffelem, model->coeffelem) when k_coeffelem is already allocated, and only use memory->destroy() for the plain array from the first read_coeffs().

summary: Pair-major offsets into the spherical-Bessel and radial-integral arrays are computed in int in three kernels, while the arrays themselves are sized with bigint and the CPU original uses bigint indices.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:581,597 'int ipair = t_ij(ii); ... const int gindex = (ipair - 1) * findex;' (findex = m_Nmax*(m_lmax+1)), line 777 'int gindex = (ipair - 1) * findex;', and lines 659-667 '(ipair - 1) * m_Nmax * (m_lmax + 1) + (bigint) i * (m_lmax + 1) + l' / '(ipair - 1) * m_nmax * (m_lmax + 1) + ...' -- all int products. The CPU version keeps these in bigint: src/ML-IAP/mliap_so3.cpp:703-704 'bigint ipair = 0; bigint gindex;', line 722 'gindex = (ipair - 1) * findex;', lines 795-803. The allocation side already uses bigint (src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:683 'totali = (bigint) totaln * m_Nmax * (m_lmax + 1);'), and the sibling DXDR kernel gets it right at line 912 'bigint gindex = (bigint) (ipair - 1) * findex;', so this is an internal inconsistency.
failure_scenario: npairs * m_Nmax * (lmax+1) above 2^31 wraps to a negative offset and the kernel reads/writes far outside m_sbes_array/m_rip_array. Note the arrays would then be tens of GB, so this is only reachable on very large unified-memory nodes; it is nevertheless a latent 32-bit truncation the CPU code explicitly avoids.
suggested_fix: Declare ipair/gindex as bigint in the MLIAPSO3GetSBESArrayTag, MLIAPSO3GetRipArrayTag and MLIAPSO3SpectrumTag operators, matching line 912.

summary: m_chunk_size is never initialized in the constructor and is only set by init_arrays(), which spectrum_dxdr() does not call, so a first call to spectrum_dxdr() without a preceding spectrum() takes a modulus by an indeterminate value.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.h:84 declares 'int m_chunk_size;' with no initializer and the constructor (src/KOKKOS/mliap_so3_kokkos.cpp:39-55) initializes m_rcut, m_alpha, m_lmax, m_nmax, m_Nmax, m_numYlms, m_init_arrays, m_dfac_l1/l2, m_pfac_l1/l2, m_idxu_count, m_idxy_count and alloc_* but not m_chunk_size. It is assigned only in init_arrays (line 223), which is called only from spectrum() (line 679). spectrum_dxdr() uses it at line 810 ('std::min(nlocal, m_chunk_size)') and its kernel at line 879 ('int ii_chunk = ii%m_chunk_size;') and line 859 ('start += m_chunk_size').
failure_scenario: If compute_forces() ever runs before compute_descriptors() (a linear model on a step with eflag = 0, see pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:113), the chunk loop divides by an indeterminate int -- integer division by zero on the device, or an arbitrary chunk index. In practice the setup step always has eflag = 1, so the field is set before it matters, but nothing enforces that.
suggested_fix: Initialize m_chunk_size in the constructor (and ideally call init_arrays() at the top of spectrum_dxdr() as spectrum() does).

summary: update_pair_energy zeroes the per-atom energy array over nlocal entries although it is allocated with nlistatoms (= list->inum) entries, unlike the CPU version which loops over nlistatoms.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:271-274 'const auto nlocal = data->nlocal; Kokkos::parallel_for(nlocal, KOKKOS_LAMBDA(int ii) { d_eatoms[ii] = 0; });' versus src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:244-245 'const auto nlistatoms = data->nlistatoms; for (int ii = 0; ii < nlistatoms; ii++) data->eatoms[ii] = 0;'. eatoms/k_eatoms is created with nlistatoms entries in src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:101-102 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatoms, eatoms, nlistatoms, "mliap_data:eatoms");'. update_atom_energy (line 381) writes d_eatoms[i] over nlocal for the same reason.
failure_scenario: Any configuration where list->inum is smaller than atom->nlocal (a pair_style hybrid sub-list, or a neighbor list restricted to a subset of the atoms) makes the zeroing kernel write past the end of the eatoms device allocation.
suggested_fix: Loop over data->nlistatoms in the zeroing kernel (and bound update_atom_energy the same way), matching the CPU implementation and the allocation size.

summary: improper hybrid/kk keeps the base-class default centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL although every KOKKOS improper sub-style sets CENTROID_NOTAVAIL, so the cvflag_atom accumulation loop dereferences a null sub-style cvatom pointer.
evidence: ImproperHybridKokkos::ImproperHybridKokkos (src/KOKKOS/improper_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:91-102) never touches centroidstressflag, so it inherits `centroidstressflag = CENTROID_AVAIL;` from Improper::Improper (src/improper.cpp:46). Every KOKKOS improper sub-style does the opposite, e.g. src/KOKKOS/improper_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:50 `centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL;` (same line in improper_class2_kokkos.cpp:48, improper_cossq_kokkos.cpp:50, improper_cvff_kokkos.cpp:50, improper_distance_kokkos.cpp:43, improper_distharm_kokkos.cpp:43, improper_fourier_kokkos.cpp:46, improper_inversion_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:43, improper_ring_kokkos.cpp:45, improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.cpp:43, improper_umbrella_kokkos.cpp:46). Improper::ev_setup (src/improper.cpp:125-127) therefore sets cvflag_atom=1 (and allocates cvatom) for the hybrid but cvflag_atom=0 / vflag_atom=1 for each sub-style, leaving styles[m]->cvatom == nullptr (src/improper.cpp:44). The hybrid then runs `double **cvatom_substyle = styles[m]->cvatom;` and `cvatom[i][j] += cvatom_substyle[i][j];` (src/KOKKOS/improper_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:207-209). The guard in ComputeCentroidStressAtom (src/compute_centroid_stress_atom.cpp:189-191) only inspects force->improper->centroidstressflag, i.e. the hybrid's AVAIL value, so it does not catch this.
failure_scenario: improper_style hybrid/kk harmonic cvff + `compute centroid/stress/atom` (or `compute pressure ... virial` with VIRIAL_CENTROID, e.g. used by fix bocs / compute stress/mop-style consumers): the centroid check passes, cvflag_atom is set for the hybrid, and the first iteration of the accumulation loop segfaults on a null cvatom_substyle.
suggested_fix: Set `centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL;` in the ImproperHybridKokkos constructor (matching the sub-styles), or compute it in init_style() as the max over sub-styles' flags.

summary: The improper cvff/kk device kernel reads the host-only raw pointer `sign[type]` instead of the device view `d_sign[type]`, so on a GPU build it dereferences a host address inside the kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/improper_cvff_kokkos.cpp:278 (inside operator()(TagImproperCvffCompute...) which is KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION): `if (sign[type] == -1) {` / `p = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(2.0) - p;` / `pd = -pd;`. `sign` is the base class member `int *sign, *multiplicity;` (src/MOLECULE/improper_cvff.h:40) allocated with memory->create in ImproperCvff::allocate. The Kokkos mirror exists and is kept in sync but is never used: `DAT::tdual_int_1d k_sign,k_multiplicity;` / `typename AT::t_int_1d d_sign,d_multiplicity;` (src/KOKKOS/improper_cvff_kokkos.h:88,91), filled in coeff()/read_restart() (improper_cvff_kokkos.cpp:388,393,409,414), allocated in allocate() (:366,370) and synced at :92 `k_sign.template sync<DeviceType>();`. Two lines above, the sibling array IS read correctly through its device view: `const int m = d_multiplicity[type];` (:247).
failure_scenario: Any GPU (CUDA/HIP/SYCL, non-UVM) run with `improper_style cvff/kk`: the kernel dereferences a host pointer -> illegal memory access / crash, or silently garbage `sign` values and therefore wrong improper energies and forces for `sign = -1` types. CPU-only Kokkos builds are unaffected, which is why it can pass CI.
suggested_fix: Replace `sign[type]` with `d_sign[type]` in the kernel (matching the `d_multiplicity[type]` usage on line 247).

summary: improper distance/kk drops the five domain->minimum_image() calls that the CPU ImproperDistance::compute applies to every bond vector, so the /kk style computes a different plane normal and different forces whenever a bond vector is longer than half the box.
evidence: CPU src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/improper_distance.cpp:98-125 computes each of the five vectors and immediately folds it: `xab = x[i2][0] - x[i1][0]; ... domain->minimum_image(FLERR, xab,yab,zab);` (also for xac/yac/zac :107, xad/yad/zad :113, xbc/ybc/zbc :119, xbd/ybd/zbd :125). The KOKKOS kernel src/KOKKOS/improper_distance_kokkos.cpp:149-167 computes exactly the same five differences and never folds any of them: `const KK_FLOAT xab = x(i2,0) - x(i1,0); ... const KK_FLOAT zbd = x(i4,2) - x(i2,2);` -- there is no minimum-image code anywhere in the file (`grep -n minimum_image src/KOKKOS/improper_distance_kokkos.cpp` is empty) and domain.h is not even included. The KOKKOS package already has a device-side implementation of this that could be reused: BondHarmonicRestrainKokkos copies domain->xprd/xprd_half/triclinic in compute() (src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:111-121) and calls its own KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION minimum_image() (:191, defined :243-295).
failure_scenario: A periodic cell whose shortest edge is less than twice an improper bond length (small unit cells, or an improper spanning a periodic image), run with improper_style distance vs distance/kk: the CPU style folds e.g. xbd back into the box before forming the plane normal, the /kk style does not, so the normal, the projection da, the energy k*da^2+chi*da^4 and all four forces differ.
suggested_fix: Copy domain->triclinic/xprd/yprd/zprd/*_half into the functor in compute() and add a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION minimum_image() applied to the five difference vectors, mirroring src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:243-295.

summary: improper distharm/kk drops the six domain->minimum_image() calls the CPU ImproperDistHarm::compute applies to its bond vectors, so plane normal, projection and forces differ from the base style when a bond vector exceeds half the box.
evidence: CPU src/YAFF/improper_distharm.cpp:98-131 folds every difference vector: `xab = x[i2][0] - x[i1][0]; ... domain->minimum_image(FLERR, xab,yab,zab);` and likewise for xac (:107), xad (:113), xbc (:119), xbd (:125) and xcd (:131). The KOKKOS kernel src/KOKKOS/improper_distharm_kokkos.cpp:149-167 forms the same differences (`const KK_FLOAT xab = x(i2,0) - x(i1,0); ... const KK_FLOAT zcd = x(i4,2) - x(i3,2);`) with no folding; `grep -n minimum_image src/KOKKOS/improper_distharm_kokkos.cpp` is empty and domain.h is not included. Everything else in the kernel (xna/yna/zna, rna, da = -(xna*xad+...), domega, a, f1..f4 at :188-208) matches CPU :133-169 term for term. src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:111-121 and :243-295 show the device-side minimum_image pattern already used in this package.
failure_scenario: improper_style distharm vs distharm/kk in a periodic cell whose shortest edge is under twice an improper bond length (or an improper wrapped across a boundary): the CPU folds xbc/xcd/xad before building the plane normal and the projection da, the /kk style does not, giving different energy k*(da-chi)^2 and different forces on all four atoms.
suggested_fix: Copy domain->triclinic/xprd/yprd/zprd/*_half into the functor in compute() and apply a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION minimum_image() to the difference vectors, as in src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:243-295.

summary: improper sqdistharm/kk drops the six domain->minimum_image() calls the CPU ImproperSQDistHarm::compute applies to its bond vectors, diverging from the base style when a bond vector exceeds half the box.
evidence: CPU src/YAFF/improper_sqdistharm.cpp:98-131 folds every difference vector (`xab = x[i2][0] - x[i1][0]; ... domain->minimum_image(FLERR, xab,yab,zab);` and the same for xac, xad, xbc, xbd, xcd). The KOKKOS kernel src/KOKKOS/improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.cpp:149-167 forms the identical differences with no folding; `grep -n minimum_image src/KOKKOS/improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.cpp` is empty and domain.h is not included. The rest of the kernel (:169-207: xna/yna/zna, rna, da, da2, eimproper = k*(da2-chi)^2, a = 4*da*k*(da2-chi), f1..f4) matches CPU :133-169 exactly, and a diff of improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.cpp against improper_distharm_kokkos.cpp differs only in those three energy/force lines, so the whole family shares the omission.
failure_scenario: improper_style sqdistharm vs sqdistharm/kk in a periodic cell whose shortest edge is under twice an improper bond length: CPU folds the vectors before building the plane normal and projection, /kk does not, so energies and all four forces differ.
suggested_fix: Add the device-side minimum_image used by src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:243-295 (with domain->triclinic/xprd/*_half copied into the functor in compute()) and apply it to the six difference vectors.

summary: improper umbrella/kk allocates a brand-new Kokkos DualView for the warning flag on every timestep inside compute() instead of once in the constructor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/improper_umbrella_kokkos.cpp:97-103 inside compute(): `// zero warning flag` / `k_warning_flag = DAT::tdual_int_scalar("ImproperUmbrella::warning_flag");` / `d_warning_flag = k_warning_flag.template view<DeviceType>();` ... Every other KOKKOS bonded style creates it once in the constructor, e.g. src/KOKKOS/improper_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:46-48 (in the ctor) and then only does `h_warning_flag() = 0; k_warning_flag.modify_host(); k_warning_flag.sync<DeviceType>();` per step (improper_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:102-104). improper_fourier_kokkos.cpp:99-101 has the same per-step allocation.
failure_scenario: Every MD step with improper_style umbrella/kk performs a device allocation+free (cudaMalloc/cudaFree class of call), which serializes the GPU stream; measurable overhead in improper-dominated runs. No wrong numbers.
suggested_fix: Move the `k_warning_flag = DAT::tdual_int_scalar(...)` / `d_warning_flag` / `h_warning_flag` initialization into the constructor as improper_harmonic_kokkos does, keeping only the zeroing in compute().

summary: improper fourier/kk allocates a brand-new Kokkos DualView for the warning flag on every timestep inside compute() instead of once in the constructor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/improper_fourier_kokkos.cpp:99-105 inside compute(): `// zero warning flag` / `k_warning_flag = DAT::tdual_int_scalar("ImproperFourier::warning_flag");` / `d_warning_flag = k_warning_flag.template view<DeviceType>();` / `h_warning_flag = k_warning_flag.view_host();` / `h_warning_flag() = 0; ...`. The constructor (:36-47) does not create it, unlike every other KOKKOS bonded style: improper_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:46-48 and improper_class2_kokkos.cpp:44-46 create it once in the ctor and only zero it per step. improper_umbrella_kokkos.cpp:97-103 has the same defect.
failure_scenario: Every MD step with improper_style fourier/kk performs a device allocation and free (cudaMalloc/cudaFree class of call) that serializes the GPU stream; overhead only, no wrong numbers.
suggested_fix: Move the k_warning_flag / d_warning_flag / h_warning_flag initialization into the ImproperFourierKokkos constructor and keep only the zero+modify_host+sync in compute().

summary: cutsq_custom is declared as int instead of double, so the trim cutoff squared is truncated to an integer and neighbors are dropped (or all of them dropped when the cutoff is below 1.0).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.h:283 'int nlocal,num_skip,cutsq_custom;'.  It is filled with a floating point value in src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:50 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and compared against a double in :144 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;'.  Every other npair trim class stores it as double: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.h:248 'double cutsq_custom;', src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.h:366 'double cutsq_custom,delta;', src/npair_skip.cpp:68 'double cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom * cutoff_custom;'.
failure_scenario: skip/trim/kk/* list with cutoff_custom = 3.5 -> cutsq_custom = int(12.25) = 12, so neighbor pairs at 3.465 < r <= 3.5 A are silently dropped from the list; with cutoff_custom < 1.0 (e.g. a short-range fix list) cutsq_custom becomes 0 and the list is emptied entirely, zeroing all forces from that sub-style.
suggested_fix: Change the declaration to 'int nlocal,num_skip; double cutsq_custom;'.

summary: build() writes d_ilist on the device but never calls k_list->k_ilist.modify<DeviceType>(), so a later k_ilist.sync_host() is a no-op and consumers read stale host ilist data.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:151 'd_ilist(inum) = i;' (device kernel) and the end of build() at :97-105 has no modify call.  Every other KOKKOS npair build does it: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:360 'list->k_ilist.template modify<DeviceType>();', src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:82, src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:520, src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:84.  Consumers rely on the flag: src/KOKKOS/npair_copy_kokkos.cpp:77 and src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:130 call 'listcopy_kk->k_ilist.sync_host()' before reading view_host(), as does src/KOKKOS/fix_reaxff_species_kokkos.cpp:80.
failure_scenario: A CPU-side list copied or trimmed from a skip/kk/device list (kk2cpu path in NPairCopyKokkos::copy_to_cpu / NPairTrimKokkos::trim_to_cpu), or fix reaxff/species, reads the host mirror of k_ilist, which still contains whatever the last host-side write left (all zeros on the first build) -> wrong atom indices, wrong neighbor lists, likely out-of-bounds firstneigh entries.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_list->k_ilist.template modify<DeviceType>();' at the end of NPairSkipKokkos::build(), as the sibling npair styles do.

summary: NPairTrimKokkos's constructor never sets execution_space, so it keeps the NPair default of Host and the device build syncs x to the host instead of the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:27 'NPairTrimKokkos<DeviceType>::NPairTrimKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : NPair(lmp) {}' - no 'execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space;'.  The base sets 'execution_space = Host;' in src/npair.cpp:44.  The sibling styles do set it: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:33 and src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:28.  It is then used in src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:57 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK);' immediately before the device kernel that reads 'x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>()' (:56, kernel at :94-111).
failure_scenario: With trim/kk/device, whenever x was last modified on the host (host-side comm/exchange/borders, a non-Kokkos fix touching x, read_restart) the device copy of x is never refreshed; the trim kernel computes rsq from stale coordinates and keeps/drops the wrong neighbors, giving wrong forces without any error.  It also forces a pointless device->host copy of x on every build.
suggested_fix: Set 'execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space;' in the NPairTrimKokkos constructor.

summary: xprd_half/yprd_half/zprd_half are stored as int in NeighborKokkosExecute, truncating the half box lengths and corrupting minimum_image_check(), which decides whether special-bond scaling is applied to a pair.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:261 'const int xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' with the matching constructor parameters at :303 'const int & _xprd_half, const int & _yprd_half, const int & _zprd_half'.  They are initialized in src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:206 from 'domain->xprd_half,domain->yprd_half,domain->zprd_half', which are declared 'double xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' in src/domain.h:50.  They are then used in floating point comparisons: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:420-425 'if (xperiodic && fabs(dx) > xprd_half) return 1;', which must match src/domain.h:198-204 exactly.
failure_scenario: Box with xprd = 9.0 -> domain->xprd_half = 4.5 but the functor stores 4.  A 1-4 special-bond partner whose |dx| is 4.2 makes minimum_image_check() return 1 on the KOKKOS path and 0 on the CPU path, so the pair is stored without the special-bond code and the special_lj/special_coul factor is never applied -> wrong energies/forces for molecular systems in small periodic boxes (and every pair in a box shorter than 2 length units, where xprd_half truncates to 0 or 1).
suggested_fix: Change the three members and the three constructor parameters to double.

summary: xprd_half/yprd_half/zprd_half are declared int in NPairSSAKokkosExecute, truncating the half box lengths used by minimum_image_check().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.h:175 'const int xprd_half, yprd_half, zprd_half;' and constructor parameters :237 'const int & _xprd_half, const int & _yprd_half, const int & _zprd_half'; initialized from the doubles 'domain->xprd_half,domain->yprd_half,domain->zprd_half' at src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:428 (src/domain.h:50 declares them double).  Used in a floating point test at src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.h:342-347, which must match src/domain.h:198-204 as used by the CPU build at src/DPD-REACT/npair_half_bin_newton_ssa.cpp:211 and :296.
failure_scenario: Same as the npair_kokkos.h case: in a box whose half-length is not an integer, special-bond pairs whose |dx| falls between trunc(xprd_half) and xprd_half are stored without the special-bond code and lose their special_lj/special_coul scaling, so SSA/DPD runs disagree with the CPU build.
suggested_fix: Change the three members and the matching constructor parameters to double.

summary: PPPMKokkos does not override reset_grid(), so fix balance drives the inherited PPPM::reset_grid(), which dereferences the base-class gc (always nullptr for the KOKKOS style) and calls the non-virtual PPPM::compute_rho_coeff() on the never-allocated rho_coeff/drho_coeff pointers.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h declares its own shadowing members 'Grid3dKokkos<DeviceType> *gc;' (:449) and a non-virtual 'void compute_rho_coeff();' (:486), while the base declares 'class Grid3d *gc;' (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:84) and the NON-virtual 'void compute_rho_coeff();' (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:142).  PPPMKokkos overrides neither reset_grid() nor allocates the base members, and src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:637-668 'void PPPM::reset_grid() { deallocate(); ... allocate(); if (!overlap_allowed && !gc->ghost_adjacent()) ...; compute_gf_denom(); ... compute_rho_coeff(); setup(); }'.  The PPPM constructor leaves both at null ('fft1(nullptr), fft2(nullptr), remap(nullptr), gc(nullptr)' and 'rho1d = rho_coeff = drho1d = drho_coeff = nullptr;'), and PPPMKokkos::allocate() (src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:791-892) only fills the KOKKOS members.  reset_grid() is invoked unconditionally by src/fix_balance.cpp:341 'if (force->kspace) force->kspace->reset_grid();'.
failure_scenario: 'kspace_style pppm/kk' together with 'fix balance ... ' (or any other caller of KSpace::reset_grid): on the first rebalance PPPM::reset_grid() evaluates gc->ghost_adjacent() on a null Grid3d* and then writes rho_coeff[l][m] through a null FFT_SCALAR** -> segmentation fault.
suggested_fix: Add a 'void reset_grid() override;' to PPPMKokkos that repeats the sequence using the KOKKOS members (and make PPPM::compute_rho_coeff() virtual so the KOKKOS version is picked up).

summary: unpack_forward_grid_kokkos's per-atom branch reads the u_brick (per-atom energy) value from d_buf[7*i] without adding unpack_offset, unlike the six virial reads right below it, so the tiled grid comm unpacks the wrong buffer stretch.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:2418 'if (eflag_atom) d_u_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i];' versus :2420-2425 'd_v0_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i+1 + unpack_offset]; ... d_v5_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i+6 + unpack_offset];' and the sibling kernel :2404-2406 'd_vdx_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[3*i   + unpack_offset];'.  unpack_offset is set from the caller at :2379 and the tiled path passes a non-zero value: src/KOKKOS/grid3d_kokkos.cpp:771-773 'offset = nper * recv[m].offset; kspaceKKBase->unpack_forward_grid_kokkos(which,k_buf2,offset,recv[m].nunpack,k_recv_unpacklist,m);'.  The CPU base advances one running index for every field (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp, PPPM::unpack_forward_grid, FORWARD_IK_PERATOM branch: 'if (eflag_atom) esrc[list[i]] = buf[n++];').
failure_scenario: comm_style tiled (Comm::LAYOUT_TILED) with 'kspace_style pppm/kk' and any per-atom energy request (compute pe/atom, dump custom c_pe), on a run with more than one received message: every receive after the first fills its ghost u_brick cells from the beginning of the shared receive buffer instead of its own stretch -> wrong per-atom Coulomb energies (and reads past the end of the buffer for the last receive is avoided only by luck).
suggested_fix: Change the line to 'if (eflag_atom) d_u_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i + unpack_offset];'.

summary: TRIM branch uses cutsq_custom unconditionally and drops the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype], so a trim list whose own request has no custom cutoff (cutoff_custom==0) trims away every neighbor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:55 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and :138/:150 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;'.  The CPU base src/npair_halffull.cpp:127-128 and :140-141 instead do 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  The same fallback exists in src/npair_trim.cpp:89 and src/npair_skip.cpp:108.  cutoff_custom is only nonzero when the request set NeighRequest::cut (src/npair.cpp:96), yet Neighbor::morph_halffull()/morph_copy_trim() set trim=1 purely from 'icut != jcut' (src/neighbor.cpp:1495-1501, 1576-1584) where a request without ->cut gets icut = cutneighmax; a parent list requested with a cutoff LARGER than cutneighmax therefore produces a trimmed child whose own cutoff_custom is 0.
failure_scenario: A fix/compute requests a neighbor list with a cutoff larger than the pair-style cutoff+skin (e.g. fix nonaffine/displacement style requests), so the default-cutoff pair list becomes a halffull/trim child of it with cutoff_custom==0.  On CPU it is trimmed back to cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; with KOKKOS cutsq_custom==0 makes 'rsq > 0.0' true for every pair, so every half list is emptied and all pair forces/energies silently become zero.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU logic: pass the per-type cutneighsq (as a device dual view) into the functor and use 'const double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : d_cutneighsq(itype,jtype);' , or at minimum error out at build time when TRIM is set and cutoff_custom == 0.

summary: The trim test uses cutsq_custom unconditionally, dropping the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype] when the trimmed list's own request carries no custom cutoff.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:113 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;' and :179 (CPU path) with cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom (:38,:59).  The base src/npair_trim.cpp:89-90 does 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  cutoff_custom is 0 unless the request set NeighRequest::cut (src/npair.cpp:96), while Neighbor::morph_copy_trim() sets trim=1 from 'icut != jcut' alone (src/neighbor.cpp:1576-1584), where a request without ->cut uses icut = cutneighmax.
failure_scenario: A list with the default cutoff that gets trimmed from a longer-cutoff parent list (parent requested a cutoff larger than cutneighmax) has cutoff_custom == 0, so cutsq_custom == 0 and 'rsq > 0.0' rejects every neighbor -> empty neighbor lists and zero forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU fallback by passing the per-type cutneighsq into the functor as a device view and using it when cutsq_custom == 0, or refuse to build with an explicit error when TRIM and cutoff_custom == 0.

summary: The TRIM branch drops the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype] when the skip list's own request has no custom cutoff.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:50 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and :144 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;' vs src/npair_skip.cpp:108-109 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  Note src/neighbor.cpp:1244-1252 clears ->cut for skip requests ('skip lists inherit the cutoff of the parent they skip from'), so cutoff_custom is 0 for exactly the skip lists this class builds.
failure_scenario: A skip/trim/kk/* list whose request had its ->cut flag cleared by morph_unique() has cutoff_custom == 0, so every neighbor fails 'rsq > 0.0' and the sub-style's neighbor list is empty; the CPU build of the same input trims to the per-type neighbor cutoffs instead.
suggested_fix: Use the same '(cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]' rule, with cutneighsq mirrored into a device view.

summary: PPPMKokkos::init() never implements the 'kspace_modify slab auto' iteration, so slab_volfactor stays at its 1.0 initial value and the EW3DC slab correction is applied to a box with no inserted vacuum.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:221-252 runs only the plain 'while (order >= minorder)' loop with no reference to slab_auto, while the CPU base wraps it in the auto-volfactor loop: src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:295-298 'const bool slab_auto_enabled = (slabflag == 1 && slab_auto); if (slab_auto_enabled) slab_volfactor = auto_slab_volfactor(accuracy, two_charge_force, g_ewald, xprd, yprd, zprd, error);' and :354-360 which re-derives it after adjust_gewald() until converged.  'kspace_modify slab auto' is accepted for any pppmflag style and sets 'slabflag = 1; slab_auto = 1; slab_volfactor = 1.0;' (src/kspace.cpp:527-530); nothing in PPPMKokkos rejects it.
failure_scenario: 'kspace_style pppm/kk' plus 'kspace_modify slab auto': slab_volfactor remains 1.0, so zprd_slab == zprd, Grid3d::set_zfactor(1.0) inserts no vacuum, and slabcorr() adds the EW3DC dipole correction for a slab geometry that was never extended -> silently wrong energies and z forces (the identical CPU input picks a volfactor of typically 3).
suggested_fix: Either port the slab_auto convergence loop from PPPM::init() into PPPMKokkos::init(), or explicitly error out in PPPMKokkos::init() when (slabflag == 1 && slab_auto).

summary: deallocate() nulls fft1 twice and never nulls fft2, leaving fft2 a dangling pointer after the FFT3dKokkos object is deleted.
failure_scenario: Any path that calls deallocate() twice without an intervening allocate() double-frees fft2: e.g. PPPMKokkos::init() calls deallocate() at :212 and error->all()s at :254/:256 before reaching allocate() at :272, after which the destructor (:127) calls deallocate() again -> delete of an already freed FFT3dKokkos.
suggested_fix: Replace the second 'fft1 = nullptr;' with 'fft2 = nullptr;'.

summary: The device find_M kernel drops the CPU check that the two atoms found at tag+1 and tag+2 actually have the TIP4P hydrogen type, so a mis-ordered molecule silently produces a wrong M site instead of an error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_tip4p_kokkos.cpp:113-122 'int iH1 = AtomKokkos::map_kokkos<DeviceType>(d_tag(i)+1,map_style,k_map_array,k_map_hash); int iH2 = ...(d_tag(i)+2,...); if (iH1 < 0 || iH2 < 0) { k_tip4p_flag...() = 1; ... return; } iH1 = closest_image(i,iH1); iH2 = closest_image(i,iH2);' - only the -1 case is caught.  The CPU base checks both conditions: src/KSPACE/pppm_tip4p.cpp, PPPMTIP4P::find_M(): 'if (iH1 == -1 || iH2 == -1) error->one(FLERR,"TIP4P hydrogen is missing"); if (atom->type[iH1] != typeH || atom->type[iH2] != typeH) error->one(FLERR,"TIP4P hydrogen has incorrect atom type");'.  The same check is present in every other TIP4P implementation (pair_lj_cut_tip4p_long.cpp, pppm_tip4p.cpp).
failure_scenario: A data file whose water molecules are not stored as consecutive O,H,H IDs (e.g. O,H,O,H,... or an ID gap after the O) makes tag+1/tag+2 resolve to non-hydrogen atoms: 'kspace_style pppm/tip4p' aborts with 'TIP4P hydrogen has incorrect atom type', while 'pppm/tip4p/kk' places the M site relative to those unrelated atoms and returns silently wrong long-range energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (d_type(iH1) != typeH_kk || d_type(iH2) != typeH_kk) { k_tip4p_flag...() = 2; ... return; }' after the map lookups and report the corresponding error on the host, mirroring the base class.

summary: trim_to_cpu reads atom->x (the host mirror) without syncing X_MASK to the host, so coordinates can be stale when the parent Kokkos list was built on the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:130-132 'listcopy_kk->k_ilist.sync_host(); double** x = atom->x;' - k_ilist is synced but nothing calls atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK), while the distances at :174-177 are computed from that host x.  Compare trim_to_kokkos at :56-57 which does sync x (albeit to the wrong space, see the execution_space finding).
failure_scenario: A non-Kokkos style requesting a trimmed copy of a device-built Kokkos list (kk2cpu + trim) gets its neighbor pairs filtered with host coordinates from the previous device->host sync, so pairs are wrongly kept or dropped after any device-side integration step.
suggested_fix: Call 'atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK);' at the top of NPairTrimKokkos::trim_to_cpu() before taking atom->x.

summary: For triclinic boxes compute() converts x to lamda coordinates through DomainKokkos, which always runs on the device and marks X_MASK modified on Device, so the pppm/kk/host instantiation keeps reading the un-converted host coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:590 'x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();' and :620 'domain->x2lamda(atomKK->nlocal);' with no atomKK->sync afterwards.  DomainKokkos::x2lamda(int n) (src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:672-685) does 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view_device(); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<LMPDeviceType, TagDomain_x2lamda>(0,n),*this); ... atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK);' - always LMPDeviceType.  src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h:18 registers 'KSpaceStyle(pppm/kk/host,PPPMKokkos<LMPHostType>);', whose kernels then read the host mirror.
failure_scenario: GPU build, triclinic box, 'kspace_style pppm/kk/host': particle_map()/make_rho()/fieldforce_ik() index the grid with Cartesian coordinates while boxlo has been set to domain->boxlo_lamda (:616-618), so every atom maps to a nonsense grid point -> 'Out of range atoms - cannot compute PPPM' or badly wrong long-range forces.
suggested_fix: Call 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK);' after domain->x2lamda() (and again after domain->lamda2x()), or refuse triclinic for the host instantiation.

summary: For NEWTON builds the ghost atoms of the parent full list are looped over and list->gnum is set from the parent, whereas the CPU base restricts both to the newtoff case.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:61-62 'int inum_full = list->listfull->inum; if (list->ghost) inum_full += list->listfull->gnum;' and :79-80 'list->inum = k_list_full->inum; list->gnum = k_list_full->gnum;'.  src/npair_halffull.cpp:72-73 guards the same addition with 'if (!NEWTON)' and :155-157 sets 'list->inum = inum; if (!NEWTON) if (list->ghost) list->gnum = list->listfull->gnum;'.  The CPU header src/npair_halffull.h registers no NP_NEWTON|NP_GHOST halffull style at all, while npair_halffull_kokkos.h:101-149 does.
failure_scenario: A half+ghost neighbor list with newton on built by KOKKOS (halffull/newton/ghost/kk/*) fills half-list entries for ghost i atoms using the newton 'above and to the right' tie-break, which double counts (owner of the ghost stores the same pair) and reports gnum != 0 to consumers that assume newton ghost lists are empty.
suggested_fix: Either guard the ghost extension and gnum assignment with '!NEWTON' as the CPU version does, or remove the NP_NEWTON|NP_GHOST halffull KOKKOS style registrations if that combination is not supported.

summary: The KOKKOS skip build ignores list->molskip entirely and unconditionally dereferences list->iskip / list->ijskip, which are left as null pointers for molecular skip lists.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:75-79 'k_iskip.view_host()(itype) = list->iskip[itype]; ... k_ijskip.view_host()(itype,jtype) = list->ijskip[itype][jtype];' and the kernel at :122 'if (!d_iskip(itype))' / :137 'if (d_ijskip(itype,type(j))) continue;'.  src/neigh_list.cpp:159-171 only allocates iskip/ijskip when '!molskip'.  The CPU base src/npair_skip.cpp:51,78,98-100 reads 'int molskip = list->molskip;' and applies 'if (!molskip && iskip[itype]) continue;' plus the INTRA/INTER molecule tests; the INTEL variant does the same (src/INTEL/npair_skip_intel.cpp:117,149-151).
failure_scenario: pair_style hybrid/molecular (the only setter, src/pair_hybrid_molecular.cpp:48,51) with a KOKKOS sub-style produces a skip list with molskip != 0 and iskip == ijskip == nullptr; NPairSkipKokkos::build() dereferences the null pointers at :76/:78 -> segmentation fault (and even if they were allocated the intra/inter-molecular filtering would be missing).
suggested_fix: Port the molskip logic (sync MOLECULE_MASK, pass atom->molecule into the functor, apply the INTRA/INTER tests) and skip the iskip/ijskip fill when list->molskip is set; alternatively error out for molskip lists in the KOKKOS skip builder.

summary: list->inum is derived by indexing the last work item of the last phase with index h_ssa_phaseLen(...)-1, which is -1 when that phase ended up with no non-empty work items.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:470-471 'data.neigh_list.inum = h_ssa_itemLoc(ssa_phaseCt-1,h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1)-1) + h_ssa_itemLen(ssa_phaseCt-1,h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1)-1);'.  d_ssa_phaseLen(workPhase) is overwritten by the device kernel with the COMPACTED work-item count at :652-653 'if (firstTry) { d_ssa_phaseLen(workPhase) = workItem; ... }', where workItem is only incremented when 'inum > inum_start' (:632-636), so it is 0 for a phase in which no atom got a neighbor.  The CPU base accumulates inum directly instead: src/DPD-REACT/npair_half_bin_newton_ssa.cpp:112 'int inum = 0;' ... :244 'list->inum = inum;'.
failure_scenario: An MPI rank whose subdomain holds no local atoms (or whose last work phase has no atom with neighbors) makes h_ssa_phaseLen(ssa_phaseCt-1) == 0, so the code reads d_ssa_itemLoc/itemLen at column -1: out-of-bounds device read and a garbage list->inum that downstream SSA kernels then loop over.
suggested_fix: Guard the expression (use 0 when the phase length is 0), or better, have the kernel reduce the total inum explicitly the way the CPU builder accumulates it.

summary: AtomNeighbors for the destination half list is constructed with d_numneigh(i), which is the not-yet-written (stale/uninitialized) half-list neighbor count.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:107-108 'const AtomNeighbors neighbors_i = AtomNeighbors(&d_neighbors(i,0),d_numneigh(i), &d_neighbors(i,1)-&d_neighbors(i,0));' - d_numneigh(i) is only assigned at :157 'd_numneigh(i) = n;', and d_numneigh is freshly allocated without initialization in src/KOKKOS/neigh_list_kokkos.cpp:46.
failure_scenario: Reads uninitialized device memory on the first build (harmless today because AtomNeighbors::num_neighs is never read here, but it trips memory checkers and would silently break if the member were ever used).
suggested_fix: Pass 0 (or the parent count d_numneigh_full(i)) instead of d_numneigh(i), or build the AtomNeighbors object after the count is known.

summary: deallocate() passes the plain device Views to memoryKK->destroy_kokkos() instead of the DualViews the buffers were created from, so k_density_fft/k_work1/k_work2 keep holding their allocations.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:906-908 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_density_fft,density_fft); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_work1,work1); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_work2,work2);' whereas allocate() created them through the DualViews: :835-842 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_density_fft,density_fft,nfft_both,...); d_density_fft = k_density_fft.view<DeviceType>(); ... memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_work1,work1,2*nfft_both,...);'.  destroy_kokkos only does 'data = TYPE(); array = nullptr;' (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:83-88), so the DualView reference keeps the memory alive until the next create_kokkos overwrites it.
failure_scenario: On PPPMKokkos::init() (which calls deallocate() at :212 and allocate() at :272) the old grid-sized FFT work arrays are still referenced by k_work1/k_work2/k_density_fft while the new ones are allocated -> transient doubling of the FFT buffer footprint; on a memory-tight GPU this is an out-of-memory abort where the CPU build succeeds.
suggested_fix: Pass the DualViews: 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_density_fft,density_fft);' etc., and reset the derived device views to empty.

summary: k_eatom/k_vatom are destroyed and re-created on every compute() call whenever per-atom energy/virial is requested, instead of only when the existing view is too small.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:576-585 'if (eflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"pair:eatom"); d_eatom = k_eatom.view<DeviceType>(); }' with no size test.  Every other KOKKOS style guards it, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp 'if (k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { destroy; create; ... } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);', and the CPU base only reallocates when 'atom->nmax > maxeatom' (src/kspace.cpp, KSpace::ev_setup).
failure_scenario: A run with 'compute pe/atom' or 'compute stress/atom' and 'kspace_style pppm/kk' performs two device allocations plus two frees (each an implicit fence) per timestep, which on a GPU costs far more than the kernels themselves.
suggested_fix: Reallocate only when 'k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom' and otherwise Kokkos::deep_copy the view to zero.

summary: d_inum is only written by the thread handling ii == num_skip-1, so when num_skip is 0 the previous build's inum is reused for list->inum.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:157-160 'if (final) { if (ii == num_skip-1) d_inum() = inum; }' - with num_skip == 0 the RangePolicy(0,0) runs no iterations, yet :94-97 still reads d_inum into list->inum.  The CPU base src/npair_skip.cpp:62,122 starts from 'int inum = 0;' and always assigns 'list->inum = inum;'.
failure_scenario: A processor whose parent skip list becomes empty (all atoms migrated away) keeps the stale, larger inum from the previous build; consumers then iterate d_ilist beyond the valid range.
suggested_fix: Deep-copy 0 into d_inum before the parallel_scan, or set list->inum = 0 explicitly when num_skip == 0.

summary: The GPU team kernels stage atom tags through a double shared-memory buffer, so tagint values lose precision in LAMMPS_BIGBIG builds and the newton/triclinic (itag+jtag)%2 tie-break can pick the wrong owner.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:665 'other_x[MY_II + 4 * atoms_per_bin] = itag;' and :779 'const tagint jtag = other_x[m + 4 * atoms_per_bin];' (same pattern at :1389/:1507 in build_ItemSizeGPU), where other_x is 'double* other_x' (:634, :1354).  The flat kernel reads the tags exactly: :532 'const tagint jtag = tag(j);'.  With -DLAMMPS_BIGBIG tagint is int64_t (src/lmptype.h) and values above 2^53 are not representable in a double.
failure_scenario: A LAMMPS_BIGBIG run with atom IDs above 2^53 rounds jtag, so 'if (itag > jtag)' and the '(itag+jtag) % 2' parity test can differ between the two owners of an owned/ghost pair -> the pair is either stored twice or not at all in a half/newton/triclinic list.
suggested_fix: Store tags in a separate tagint-typed slice of the shared-memory block (or read tag(j) directly in the tie-break) instead of round-tripping them through double.

summary: The team kernels return from a subset of the block when mbins is not a multiple of BINS_PER_TEAM, so the later __syncthreads_count()/team_barrier() calls are reached by only part of the block.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:630-632 'const int ibin = dev.league_rank()*BINS_PER_TEAM+MY_BIN; if (ibin >= mbins) return;' where MY_BIN = dev.team_rank()/atoms_per_bin varies within the team (BINS_PER_TEAM == factor == 2 whenever atoms_per_bin < 64, see :264).  The block-wide synchronizations at :671 'int test = (__syncthreads_count(i >= 0 && i < nlocal) == 0);' and :737/:760/:833 'dev.team_barrier();' are then executed by only the MY_BIN==0 half of the block.  Same shape at :992 and :1352.
failure_scenario: An odd mbins with atoms_per_bin < 64 leaves the MY_BIN==1 threads exited before the barriers; the collective is formally undefined and __syncthreads_count returns a partial count, which can make the surviving threads take the early-return branch and skip building neighbor lists for that bin.
suggested_fix: Replace the early return with a predicate that keeps all threads participating in the barriers (e.g. set a local 'valid' flag and guard the body with it), or size the league so every team's bins are in range.

summary: The Kokkos RNG pool is seeded in the constructor's member-initializer list from `seed`, which is an uninitialized PairBrownian member at that point (it is only parsed in settings()), so the user's seed is ignored and an indeterminate value is used.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pair_brownian_kokkos.cpp:49-51:
  PairBrownianKokkos<DeviceType>::PairBrownianKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : PairBrownian(lmp),
                                                                    rand_pool(seed + comm->me)
src/COLLOID/pair_brownian.cpp:46-51 -- the base constructor sets only `single_enable` and `random`; it never initializes `seed` (declared as a bare `int seed;` at src/COLLOID/pair_brownian.h:51).  `seed` is first assigned in PairBrownian::settings (src/COLLOID/pair_brownian.cpp:368), which runs AFTER the constructor.  grep shows `rand_pool` is never re-initialized: the only other uses in the file are get_state() (:278) and free_state() (:476).
Every other KOKKOS PAIR style with an RNG re-initializes the pool in init_style() once seed is known, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_ext_kokkos.cpp:83-90 `rand_pool = decltype(rand_pool)(seed + comm->me, unique_token.size());` (the fix styles can use the member-init list because Fix constructors parse the seed in the base constructor).
failure_scenario: `pair_style brownian/kk mu 1 1 rin rout T 5813` -- the 5813 seed never reaches the device RNG; the stream is whatever the uninitialized memory held, so runs are not reproducible and changing the seed changes nothing. Reading the indeterminate int is also UB.
suggested_fix: Default-construct rand_pool and (re)initialize it in init_style() after PairBrownian::init_style(), e.g. `rand_pool = decltype(rand_pool)(seed + comm->me, unique_token.size());`, mirroring pair_dpd_ext_kokkos.cpp:83-90.

summary: compute() calls ev_init(eflag,vflag,0) (alloc = 0) but the style never allocates eatom/k_eatom, so with eflag_atom set `Pair::eatom` stays nullptr and compute pe/atom dereferences a null pointer.
failure_scenario: `pair_style brownian/kk ...` plus `compute 1 all pe/atom` (or any dump/compute that sets ENERGY_ATOM) -> segmentation fault on the first invocation of the compute.
suggested_fix: Either call `ev_init(eflag,vflag)` (alloc = 1) so the base allocates and zeroes eatom, or add a k_eatom dual view allocated under `if (eflag_atom)` like every other KOKKOS pair style.

summary: The DSF self-energy is computed on the host from `atom->q[i]`, but compute() only syncs q to the DEVICE (`atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read)`); on a GPU build the host q array is stale after every device-side exchange/sort, so eng_coul and eatom get self-energies from the wrong charges.
failure_scenario: GPU run `-k on g 1 -sf kk` with `pair_style born/coul/dsf/kk` on >1 MPI rank: after the first reneighbor, atoms have migrated and the host atom->q[0..nlocal) still holds the previous step's charges (and the previous nlocal), so the sum of q_i^2 -- and therefore the reported Coulomb energy -- is wrong; the per-atom energies are wrong even on 1 rank as soon as atom sorting permutes d_q.
suggested_fix: Move the self-energy into the device kernel using the `q` device view (as pair_coul_dsf_kokkos does), or at minimum call `atomKK->sync(Host,Q_MASK)` before the host loops and iterate over the neighbor list's ilist rather than 0..nlocal.

summary: Same defect as pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos: the DSF self-energy is summed on the host from `atom->q[i]` while compute() only syncs q to the device, so on a GPU build the charges are stale after any device-side exchange or atom sort.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank GPU run with `pair_style born/coul/dsf/cs/kk`: after the first atom migration the host q array no longer matches the current local atoms, so the self-energy contribution to eng_coul (and to eatom) uses the wrong charges.
suggested_fix: Compute the self-energy inside the device kernel from the `q` device view (pattern of pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:228-236), or sync Q_MASK to the host first and loop over list->ilist.

summary: The Wolf self-energy is summed on the host from `atom->q[i]` while compute() only syncs q to the device, so on a GPU build the charges are stale after any device-side exchange or atom sort.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank GPU run with `pair_style born/coul/wolf/kk`: after the first atom migration, the host q[0..nlocal) holds the previous step's atoms, so the self-energy in eng_coul is wrong; per-atom energies are wrong even on one rank once atom sorting permutes d_q.
suggested_fix: Move the self-energy into the device kernel using the `q` device view, or sync Q_MASK to the host before the loop and iterate over list->ilist.

summary: Same defect as pair_born_coul_wolf_kokkos: the Wolf self-energy is summed on the host from `atom->q[i]` while compute() only syncs q to the device, so the charges are stale on a GPU build after any device-side exchange or atom sort.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank GPU run with `pair_style born/coul/wolf/cs/kk`: the self-energy term of eng_coul is computed from the previous step's host charges after atoms migrate.
suggested_fix: Compute the self-energy in the device kernel from the `q` device view (cf. pair_coul_wolf_cs_kokkos.cpp:239-243), or sync Q_MASK to the host and loop over list->ilist.

summary: PairBondValKokkos::settings() replaces the base class argument check with `narg > 3` and then hard-codes `PairBondVal::settings(2,arg)`, so too-few arguments are never rejected and arg[1] is read out of bounds, while a bogus 3rd argument is silently ignored.
failure_scenario: `pair_style bondval/kk 6.0` (narg==1) passes narg=2 to the base, which dereferences arg[1] -- a stale/dangling pointer left in Input::arg from a previous command -> garbage cut_global or a segfault. `pair_style bondval/kk 6.0 4.0 junk` (narg==3) is accepted and `junk` silently ignored, whereas the CPU style errors out.
suggested_fix: Check `if (narg != 2) utils::missing_cmd_args(FLERR, "pair_style bondval", error);` (or simply forward narg unchanged: `PairBondVal::settings(narg,arg);`).

summary: PairBondValVecKokkos::settings() replaces the base argument check with `narg > 3` and hard-codes `PairBondValVec::settings(2,arg)`, so too-few arguments are never rejected and arg[1] is read out of bounds, while a bogus 3rd argument is silently ignored.
failure_scenario: `pair_style bondval/vec/kk 6.0` (narg==1) makes the base read arg[1], a stale pointer left over in Input::arg -> garbage cut_global or a segfault; `pair_style bondval/vec/kk 6.0 4.0 extra` is accepted with `extra` silently ignored while the CPU style errors.
suggested_fix: Forward narg unchanged (`PairBondValVec::settings(narg,arg);`) or validate `narg != 2` with utils::missing_cmd_args().

summary: With neighflag FULL the kernel never applies the equal-and-opposite force/torque to atom j, so each pair is evaluated twice with INDEPENDENT random numbers and the stochastic pair force is no longer antisymmetric -- momentum is not conserved; the DPD KOKKOS styles reject FULL for exactly this reason.
failure_scenario: `package kokkos neigh full` (which forces newton off, kokkos.cpp:857-860) with `pair_style brownian/kk`: total linear momentum random-walks away instead of being conserved, and the pair virial is built from two different random forces for the same pair.
suggested_fix: Reject FULL (and newton off) in PairBrownianKokkos::init_style() with an explicit error, as pair_dpd_ext_kokkos does, or drop FULL from EnabledNeighFlags.

summary: None of the 13 KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION declarations in this header carry the required `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` comment.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pair_bondval_kokkos.h:67-108 and 118-121 declare e.g.
  KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION
  void operator()(TagPairBondValPackForwardComm, const int&) const;
with no preceding `// NOLINTNEXTLINE`.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md 'Common mistakes' lists 'Missing `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` before a `KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION` (required to suppress linter warnings in LAMMPS)'.  Every other pair style header in the group (e.g. pair_adp_kokkos.h:68-69, pair_beck_kokkos.h:48-49) has it; only pair_bondval_kokkos.h and pair_bondval_vec_kokkos.h are missing it among the pair styles.
failure_scenario: clang-tidy/lint runs emit warnings for these declarations.
suggested_fix: Add `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` immediately before each `KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION` line.

summary: Two commented-out debugging printf() calls left in the device kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_bondval_vec_kokkos.cpp:601: `  //printf("i: %d, d_Di(i,0): %f, d_Di(i,1): %f, d_Di(i,2): %f\n", i, d_Di(i,0), d_Di(i,1), d_Di(i,2));` and :605: `    //printf("i: %d, phi: %f", i, phi);`.  The project review rules state that commented-out code added for debugging must be removed entirely, and that printf() must not appear in new code.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; a code-review/style rule violation that would be flagged on the PR.
suggested_fix: Delete both commented-out printf lines.

summary: None of the 13 KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION declarations in this header carry the required `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` comment.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pair_bondval_vec_kokkos.h declares e.g. (lines 122-125)
    KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION
    params_bvv() {cut=0;cutsq=0;...};
with no preceding `// NOLINTNEXTLINE`.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md 'Common mistakes' requires it; pair_adp_kokkos.h:68 and pair_beck_kokkos.h:48 show the expected form.  Among all src/KOKKOS/*.h only pair_bondval_kokkos.h and pair_bondval_vec_kokkos.h (plus bond_quartic_exp, fix_nve_asphere, fix_rigid_small, math_extra) lack it.
failure_scenario: clang-tidy/lint warnings on these declarations.
suggested_fix: Add `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` before each `KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION`.

summary: For special-bonded pairs the CPU core/shell style rescales the WHOLE pair force (Coulomb and Born) by 1/(rsq+EPS_EWALD_SQR), but the KOKKOS split into compute_fcoul/compute_fpair applies that rescaling only to the Coulomb part, leaving the Born part scaled by 1/rsq.
evidence:
src/CORESHELL/pair_born_coul_long_cs.cpp:113-126 sets `r2inv = 1.0/(rsq + EPS_EWALD_SQR);` inside the `factor_coul < 1.0` branch, and that same r2inv is then used for the Born term at :154 `r6inv = r2inv*r2inv*r2inv;` / :157 and for the combined scaling at :160 `fpair = (forcecoul + factor_lj*forceborn) * r2inv;`.
src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp:264 `return forcecoul / (rsq_cs + static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(EPS_EWALD_SQR));` (Coulomb only), while :185-215 compute_fpair uses `rsq = rsq_in + EPSILON; r2inv = 1.0/rsq; ... return forceborn*r2inv;` with no EPS_EWALD_SQR, and pair_kokkos.h:245-248 just adds the two contributions.
failure_scenario: A special-bonded (factor_coul < 1) core/shell pair that is also inside cut_lj gets a Born force differing from the CPU style by a relative 1e-12/rsq; visible as a small mismatch in a tight force-style regression comparison against the CPU reference.
suggested_fix: Either apply the EPS_EWALD_SQR-corrected inverse-square scaling to the Born term too (e.g. pass factor_coul into compute_fpair), or document the intentional deviation.

summary: The core/shell EPSILON=1e-20 guard overflows in a single-precision KOKKOS build: r6inv = (1/EPSILON)^3 becomes inf in float, so a coincident core/shell pair produces NaN forces instead of a value the zero special-bond factor can cancel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_cs_kokkos.cpp:37 `static constexpr double EPSILON = 1.0e-20;`, :185 `const KK_FLOAT rsq = rsq_in + static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(EPSILON);`, :187-196 `r2inv = 1.0/rsq; r6inv = r2inv*r2inv*r2inv; ... forceborn = born1*r*rexp - born2*r6inv + born3*r2inv*r6inv;`.  With LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE / SINGLE_DOUBLE (kokkos_type.h:400-408 make KK_FLOAT = float) and rsq_in == 0: r2inv = 1e20f, r2inv*r2inv already overflows float (max 3.4e38) to inf, so forceborn = -inf + inf = NaN and `factor_lj*NaN` stays NaN even for factor_lj == 0.  In the CPU style (src/CORESHELL/pair_born_coul_dsf_cs.cpp:104-124) everything is double and 1e60/1e80 stay finite, so the special-bond factor cancels them.  Same shape in pair_born_coul_wolf_cs_kokkos.cpp:190 and (pre-existing) pair_lj_cut_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp:200.
failure_scenario: Single/mixed-precision KOKKOS build, core/shell model where a shell starts exactly on its core (r == 0, the case EPSILON exists for) -> NaN pair forces on that pair.
suggested_fix: Do the EPSILON-guarded arithmetic in double (or use a larger, float-safe EPSILON such as 1e-12) in the CS kernels.

summary: init_one() fills only the (i,j) element of the self-allocated k_cut_ljsq/k_cut_coulsq dual views, leaving (j,i) at zero, so with more than MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS (12) atom types every pair with itype>jtype loses its entire Coulomb interaction.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_kokkos.cpp:181-184 allocates standalone views 'k_cut_ljsq = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d("pair:cut_ljsq",n+1,n+1);' / 'k_cut_coulsq = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d(...)' (NOT aliased to any host array), and :230/:232 write only 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...' / 'k_cut_coulsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...' while init_one is only called with i<=j (src/pair.cpp:284-288).  The functor uses these for the non-stack path: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:245-249 'if (rsq < (STACKPARAMS?c.m_cut_ljsq[itype][jtype]:c.d_cut_ljsq(itype,jtype)))' and 'if (rsq < (STACKPARAMS?c.m_cut_coulsq[itype][jtype]:c.d_cut_coulsq(itype,jtype)))', and pair_kokkos.h:955/969 select STACKPARAMS=false when 'fpair->atom->ntypes > MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS' (=12, kokkos_type.h:44).  Sibling styles do it correctly, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_soft_kokkos.cpp:232-234 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(j,i) = ...'.
