failure_scenario: pair_style coul/cut/kk with 13 or more atom types: for a neighbor pair with itype=5, jtype=3 the test 'rsq < d_cut_coulsq(5,3)' compares against 0, compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul are never called, and the Coulomb force and energy of that pair are silently zero (roughly half of all cross-type interactions).
suggested_fix: Write both elements in init_one, i.e. 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutone*cutone;' and the same for k_cut_coulsq.

summary: init_one() fills only the (i,j) element of the self-allocated k_cut_ljsq/k_cut_coulsq dual views, leaving (j,i) at zero, so with more than 12 atom types every pair with itype>jtype loses its entire Coulomb interaction.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_debye_kokkos.cpp:204-207 allocates standalone views 'k_cut_ljsq = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d("pair:cut_ljsq",n+1,n+1);' and 'k_cut_coulsq = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d(...)', and :253/:255 write only 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...' / 'k_cut_coulsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...'; init_one is only invoked with i<=j (src/pair.cpp:284-288).  src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:245-249 tests 'rsq < c.d_cut_ljsq(itype,jtype)' and 'rsq < c.d_cut_coulsq(itype,jtype)' on the STACKPARAMS=false path, selected when atom->ntypes > MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS (pair_kokkos.h:955/969, kokkos_type.h:44 '#define MAX_TYPES_STACKPARAMS 12').  Compare src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_soft_kokkos.cpp:232-234 which correctly assigns both (i,j) and (j,i).
failure_scenario: pair_style coul/debye/kk with 13 or more atom types: for a neighbor pair with itype=7, jtype=2 the cutoff test compares rsq against 0, so compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul are skipped and the screened Coulomb force and energy of that pair are silently zero.
suggested_fix: Assign both elements: 'k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cut_ljsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutone*cutone;' and the same for k_cut_coulsq.

summary: Special-bonds handling diverges from the CPU style: the KOKKOS kernel multiplies the whole damped DSF prefactor by factor_coul instead of subtracting (1-factor_coul)*prefactor, so excluded/scaled pairs get the wrong Coulomb force and energy.
evidence: src/pair_coul_dsf.cpp:108-114 'prefactor = qqrd2e * qtmp * q[j] / r; ... forcecoul = prefactor * (erfcc / r + 2.0 * alpha / MY_PIS * erfcd + r * f_shift) * r; if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0 - factor_coul) * prefactor;' and :127-128 'ecoul = prefactor * (erfcc - r * e_shift - rsq * f_shift); if (factor_coul < 1.0) ecoul -= (1.0 - factor_coul) * prefactor;' (PairCoulDSF::single, src/pair_coul_dsf.cpp:295-299, uses the same convention).  src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:260 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = factor_coul * qqrd2e*qtmp*q[j]/r;' and :264-265/:281 compute forcecoul and ecoul from that prefactor with NO '(1-factor_coul)*prefactor' subtraction.  The correctly ported sibling src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:212-213 and :261-262 does 'forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' / 'ecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;'.
failure_scenario: Any molecular system run with pair_style coul/dsf/kk and special_bonds coul 0.0 0.0 0.0: for every 1-2/1-3/1-4 pair inside cut_coul the CPU adds prefactor*(X-1) (the DSF damping/shift remainder, X = erfcc + 2*alpha*r*erfcd/MY_PIS + r*r*f_shift) while the /kk style adds exactly 0, so forces and eng_coul differ from the CPU reference.
suggested_fix: Drop factor_coul from the prefactor and add 'if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' / the same for ecoul, mirroring src/pair_coul_dsf.cpp:114 and :128 (src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:223,248 carries the identical defect against src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:137-143).

summary: The per-type-pair scale[i][j] prefactor of the CPU style is missing everywhere in the KOKKOS port, so 'fix adapt ... pair coul/long scale ...' is silently ignored with coul/long/kk.
evidence: src/KSPACE/pair_coul_long.cpp:121 'prefactor = qqrd2e * scale[itype][jtype] * qtmp * q[j] / r;', :131 'forcecoul = scale[itype][jtype] * qtmp * q[j] * table;', :134 and :155 all apply scale, and PairCoulLong::extract (:379-381) exposes it to fix adapt.  In src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_long_kokkos.cpp the corresponding lines :192 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = qqrd2e * qtmp*q[j]*rinv;', :178 'KK_FLOAT forcecoul = qtmp*q[j] * table;', :220 and :233 have no scale factor; 'grep -n scale src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_long_kokkos.{cpp,h}' returns nothing and params_coul (pair_coul_long_kokkos.h:48-56) holds only cut_coulsq.
failure_scenario: pair_style coul/long/kk plus 'fix adapt 1 pair coul/long scale 1 1 v_ramp': the CPU run ramps the Coulomb interaction, the /kk run keeps scale=1 forever and produces a different trajectory with no warning.
suggested_fix: Add a 'scale' member to params_coul, fill it in init_one from scale[i][j], and multiply prefactor/forcecoul/ecoul by it in both the table and the non-table branch (same fix needed in pair_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp).

summary: The per-type-pair scale[i][j] prefactor of the CPU core/shell style is missing in the KOKKOS port, so 'fix adapt ... pair coul/long/cs scale ...' has no effect with coul/long/cs/kk.
evidence: src/CORESHELL/pair_coul_long_cs.cpp:107 'prefactor = qqrd2e * scale[itype][jtype] * qtmp*q[j];', :138 'forcecoul = scale[itype][jtype] * qtmp*q[j] * table;', :141 and :162 all apply scale (inherited PairCoulLong::extract exposes it to fix adapt).  'grep -n scale src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_long_cs_kokkos.{cpp,h}' returns no hits; compute_fcoul (:229, :244) and compute_ecoul (:294) build prefactor as 'qqrd2e * qtmp*q[j] / reps' with no scale, and params_coul (pair_coul_long_cs_kokkos.h:48-55) stores only cut_coulsq.
failure_scenario: pair_style coul/long/cs/kk with 'fix adapt ... pair coul/long/cs scale ...': the scaling factor is silently ignored and the /kk run diverges from the CPU run.
suggested_fix: Store scale[i][j] in params_coul (filled in init_one) and multiply it into prefactor/forcecoul/ecoul in both branches, as the CPU style does.

summary: Commented-out code left in compute_fpair().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_buck6d_coul_gauss_dsf_kokkos.cpp:192 '    // ebuck6d *= sme;  // not needed for force path'
failure_scenario: none (cosmetic); LAMMPS review rules require removal of commented-out code
suggested_fix: Delete the commented-out statement.

summary: For special-bonded (factor_coul<1) core/shell pairs the Buckingham term is evaluated with 1/(rsq+EPSILON) instead of the CPU style's 1/(rsq+EPS_EWALD_SQR), so the vdW force/energy of such a pair differs from the CPU reference.
evidence: src/CORESHELL/pair_buck_coul_long_cs.cpp:105 'rsq += EPSILON;' then 124 'r2inv = 1.0/(rsq + EPS_EWALD_SQR);' inside the factor_coul<1 branch, and 150-156 use that r2inv for r6inv, forcebuck AND fpair.  src/KOKKOS/pair_buck_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp:194 'const KK_FLOAT rsq = rsq_in + static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(EPSILON);' (compute_fpair) and 221 the same in compute_evdwl always use EPSILON=1e-20, never EPS_EWALD_SQR=1e-12; the EPS_EWALD_SQR correction is applied only inside compute_fcoul (line 286 'return forcecoul / (rsq_cs + EPS_EWALD_SQR);').
failure_scenario: pair_style buck/coul/long/cs/kk with a core/shell pair at r -> 0 that has special_coul<1 but special_lj != 0: the CPU caps r2inv at 1e12 while the KOKKOS style uses 1e20, so r6inv differs by 24 orders of magnitude; for ordinary separations the difference is ~1e-12 relative.
suggested_fix: Pass the same effective r2inv to the vdW terms, e.g. add EPS_EWALD_SQR (not EPSILON) in compute_fpair/compute_evdwl when factor_coul<1, mirroring the CPU r2inv reassignment.

summary: compute() never sets copymode = 1 around the pair_compute<> call, unlike every other pair style in the package.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_cut_kokkos.cpp:106-113 goes straight from 'qqrd2e = ...' to 'EV_FLOAT ev = pair_compute<PairCoulCutKokkos<DeviceType>,void >(this,...)' with no 'copymode = 1;' / 'copymode = 0;'; compare src/KOKKOS/pair_buck_coul_cut_kokkos.cpp:121-151.  Same omission in pair_coul_debye_kokkos.cpp, pair_coul_cut_soft_kokkos.cpp and pair_coul_long_soft_kokkos.cpp.
failure_scenario: Currently benign because ~PairComputeFunctor (src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:103) sets c.copymode = 1 on its own copy before destruction; but any future code path that copies the style outside the functor would double-free the Kokkos/host arrays.
suggested_fix: Add 'copymode = 1;' before the pair_compute<> call and 'copymode = 0;' at the end of compute(), matching the rest of the package.

summary: The 'Overlapping small/large' and 'Overlapping large/large' fatal checks of the CPU style are dropped, so overlapping colloids silently produce Inf/NaN forces instead of aborting.
evidence: src/COLLOID/pair_colloid.cpp:151-152 'if (rsq <= K[1]) error->one(FLERR,"Overlapping small/large in pair colloid");' and :190-191 'if (r <= K[1]) error->one(FLERR,"Overlapping large/large in pair colloid");'. src/KOKKOS/pair_colloid_kokkos.cpp:159-208 (compute_fpair SMALL_LARGE/LARGE_LARGE branches) contain no equivalent check; K3/K0 go to zero and the result is Inf/NaN.
failure_scenario: pair_style colloid/kk with two large colloids that come into contact: the CPU run stops with a clear error, the /kk run keeps integrating NaN forces and silently corrupts the trajectory.
suggested_fix: Accumulate an overlap flag in the kernel (e.g. a device scalar reduced with the EV_FLOAT or a separate parallel_reduce) and call error->one() on the host after the kernel, as other KOKKOS styles do for kernel-detected errors.

summary: The parallel (longitudinal) dissipative force in pair dpd/ext/tstat/kk has the wrong sign - the leading minus of the CPU expression is missing, turning the drag term into an energy-pumping anti-drag.
failure_scenario: Any run with `pair_style dpd/ext/tstat` under `-sf kk`: the longitudinal friction becomes negative friction, so relative radial velocities are amplified instead of damped every step; the thermostat no longer holds the target temperature and the system heats up and typically blows up (lost atoms), while the pure-CPU style is stable.
suggested_fix: Change line 302 to `fpair = -params(itype,jtype).gamma*wdPar*wdPar*dot*rinv;` (keeping the following `fpair *= factor_dpd;`).

summary: During a temperature ramp (t_start != t_stop) pair dpd/ext/tstat/kk updates only the parallel noise amplitude sigma and never the perpendicular one sigmaT, so the transverse random force stays at the initial temperature.
failure_scenario: `pair_style dpd/ext/tstat 1.0 5.0 <cut> <seed>` under -sf kk: the transverse dissipation grows with the ramped gammaT-based drag while the transverse noise amplitude stays at T=1.0, breaking the fluctuation-dissipation balance; the perpendicular degrees of freedom equilibrate to the wrong (starting) temperature.
suggested_fix: Also set `k_params.view_host()(i,j).sigmaT = k_params.view_host()(j,i).sigmaT = sqrt(2.0*boltz*temperature*gammaT[i][j]);` inside the same loop.

summary: Per-atom energy (eatom) is always zero for pair dpd/kk on timesteps where per-atom energy is requested but global energy is not, because evdwl is computed only under `eflag_global` instead of `eflag_either`.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:370-379 `if (EVFLAG && eflag_global) { evdwl = 0.5*params(itype,jtype).a0*params(itype,jtype).cut*wd*wd; evdwl *= factor_dpd; ev.evdwl += ...; }` followed by `if (EVFLAG && (eflag_atom || vflag_either)) this->template ev_tally<NEIGHFLAG>(ev,i,j,evdwl,fpair,...)`; evdwl is declared `KK_FLOAT evdwl = 0;` at line 316 and never assigned when eflag_global==0. The CPU base src/DPD-BASIC/pair_dpd.cpp:154-163 guards with `if (eflag)` (i.e. eflag_either): `if (eflag) { evdwl = 0.5*a0[itype][jtype]*cut[itype][jtype]*wd*wd; evdwl *= factor_dpd; } if (evflag) ev_tally(i,j,nlocal,newton_pair,evdwl,0.0,fpair,delx,dely,delz);`. The identical mistake is repeated in the team-policy kernel at line 488.
failure_scenario: Run pair_style dpd/kk with `compute pe/atom` dumped every N steps while no global-energy compute matches that timestep (Integrate::ev_set then yields eflag = ENERGY_ATOM only, eflag_global = 0). eatom[] comes out all zeros instead of the DPD conservative energy.
suggested_fix: Change the guard at lines 370 and 488 to `if (EVFLAG && eflag_either)` (computing evdwl) and keep `if (eflag_global) ev.evdwl += evdwl;` as a separate inner test.

summary: The KOKKOS EAM styles ignore the per-type-pair scale[][] factor that the CPU PairEAM applies to force, pair energy and embedding energy, so `fix adapt ... pair eam* scale ...` silently has no effect under -sf kk.
evidence: There is no reference to `scale` anywhere in src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.cpp or .h (grep -n scale finds only the copyright banner). CPU base src/MANYBODY/pair_eam.cpp applies it in three places: line 295 `fpair = -scale[itype][jtype]*psip*recip;` vs KOKKOS pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:815 `const KK_FLOAT fpair = -psip*recip;`; line 306 `if (eflag) evdwl = scale[itype][jtype]*phi;` vs pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:829/1059 which tally bare `phi`; and line 361 `phi *= scale[type[i]][type[i]];` in compute_embedding() vs pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:649-650/725-726/934-935 which tally the unscaled embedding phi. PairEAM::extract() (pair_eam.cpp:1679) still hands the scale array to fix adapt, and fix_adapt.cpp:428-432 resolves the /kk-suffixed style, so the fix writes values nobody reads. doc/src/fix_adapt.rst:191 documents `pair eam, eam/alloy, eam/fs ... scale ... type pairs`. The /omp (OPENMP/pair_eam_omp.cpp:236,310,321) and /opt (OPT/pair_eam_opt.cpp:284,366,377) variants do apply it.
failure_scenario: `pair_style eam/alloy/kk` + `fix adapt 1 pair eam/alloy scale 1 1 v_lambda` (thermodynamic integration): forces and energies are computed with scale==1 for the whole run, so the free-energy integration result is wrong, with no error or warning.
suggested_fix: Add a device-resident scale table (e.g. a DualView filled in an init_one() override, like the other /kk styles do for their params) and multiply fpair, the pair phi and the embedding phi by it, matching pair_eam.cpp:295, 306 and 361.

summary: pair dpd/kk reads atom->tag on the device in its team kernel but never syncs TAG_MASK, so the device tag view can be stale.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:173 `atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | TYPE_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK);` (no TAG_MASK) and line 179 `tag = atomKK->k_tag.view<DeviceType>();`. The team kernel then reads it at lines 426 `const tagint itag = tag(i);` and 447 `const tagint jtag = tag(j);` and feeds both into the SARU random-number hash at line 467. datamask_read is EMPTY_MASK (line 97) so VerletKokkos's sync at verlet_kokkos.cpp:438 is a no-op as well.
failure_scenario: Any host-side update of atom->tag (e.g. `reset_atoms id`, tag_extend after atom creation, a host-side atom sort) leaves the device tag view stale; the SARU-seeded random forces are then computed from wrong tags, giving a silently different (and non-reproducible) DPD noise realization.
suggested_fix: Add TAG_MASK to the sync mask in compute() (and to datamask_read), or only assign/use `tag` on the code path that needs it after an explicit `atomKK->sync(execution_space,TAG_MASK)`.

summary: PairEAMKokkos::array2spline() overrides the base without ever allocating the host frho_spline/rhor_spline/z2r_spline arrays, yet the style inherits atomic_energy_enable=1, so PairEAM::compute_atomic_energy() dereferences null pointers when fix sgcmc uses it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:384-418 `void PairEAMKokkos<DeviceType>::array2spline() { rdr = 1.0/dr; rdrho = 1.0/drho; ... }` builds only the Kokkos DualViews and never calls PairEAM::array2spline(), which is the only place the host arrays are created (src/MANYBODY/pair_eam.cpp: `memory->create(frho_spline,nfrho,nrho+1,7,"pair:frho"); memory->create(rhor_spline,...); memory->create(z2r_spline,...)`); they stay at the nullptr set in PairEAM's constructor (pair_eam.cpp:67-69). The KOKKOS constructor (pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:44-51) clears respa_enable and single_enable but leaves atomic_energy_enable at the 1 set by PairEAM::PairEAM (pair_eam.cpp:42). PairEAM::compute_atomic_energy (pair_eam.cpp:410,415,424) does `coeff = z2r_spline[type2z2r[jtype][itype]][m];`, `coeff = rhor_spline[...][m];` and `coeff = frho_spline[type2frho[itype]][m];`. src/MC/fix_sgcmc.cpp:259 only checks `if (!force->pair->atomic_energy_enable) error->all(...)` and then calls it at lines 1040-1062.
failure_scenario: `pair_style eam/alloy/kk` (or eam/kk, eam/fs/kk, eam/he/kk) together with `fix sgcmc ... ` in atomic-energy mode: the guard passes and the first swap attempt dereferences a null z2r_spline -> segmentation fault. The same nullptr also makes PairEAM::single() unusable, though single_enable=0 hides that.
suggested_fix: Set `atomic_energy_enable = 0;` in the PairEAMKokkos constructor, or have array2spline() call PairEAM::array2spline() first so the host spline tables exist.

summary: datamask_read/datamask_modify are set to EMPTY_MASK instead of the arrays the style actually reads and writes, violating the KOKKOS package rule and disabling the integrator-level sync/modify.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:97-98 `datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK; datamask_modify = EMPTY_MASK;` while compute() at line 173 syncs `X_MASK|V_MASK|F_MASK|TYPE_MASK|ENERGY_MASK|VIRIAL_MASK` and line 278 marks `F_MASK|ENERGY_MASK|VIRIAL_MASK` modified. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md: "declare datamask_read / datamask_modify ... exactly the per-atom arrays the style reads and writes". Compare pair_dpd_ext_kokkos.cpp:98-99 and pair_dpd_fdt_energy_kokkos.cpp which declare real masks.
failure_scenario: Callers that rely on pair->datamask_read/modify (VerletKokkos::host_force_styles at verlet_kokkos.cpp, dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:119-121, min_kokkos) get an empty mask; e.g. in the host/device overlap path datamask_read_host stays 0 so nothing is staged into the pinned host buffer for a dpd/kk/host run.
suggested_fix: Set datamask_read = X_MASK|V_MASK|F_MASK|TYPE_MASK|TAG_MASK|ENERGY_MASK|VIRIAL_MASK and datamask_modify = F_MASK|ENERGY_MASK|VIRIAL_MASK in the constructor.

summary: The HIP TeamPolicy variant of EAM kernel C calls the unqualified `sqrt` in device code instead of `Kokkos::sqrt`, unlike every other square root in the file.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:1005 `const KK_FLOAT r = sqrt(rsq);` inside `operator()(TagPairEAMKernelC<...>, const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type&, EV_FLOAT&)`. The equivalent RangePolicy kernel uses `Kokkos::sqrt` (line 776 `const KK_FLOAT r = Kokkos::sqrt(rsq);`), as do lines 602, 696 and 901. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: "Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ... never std::".
failure_scenario: Under LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE the unqualified overload can bind to the double version and silently widen/narrow; on toolchains where <cmath>'s sqrt is not visible as a device function the HIP build fails to compile.
suggested_fix: Change line 1005 to `const KK_FLOAT r = Kokkos::sqrt(rsq);`.

summary: The KOKKOS EAM styles drop the CPU style's 'per-atom density exceeded rhomax' warning, so a user gets no notice that the embedding table was linearly extrapolated.
evidence: CPU src/MANYBODY/pair_eam.cpp:316-324 tracks beyond_rhomax in compute_embedding() (line 359 `if (!HE) beyond_rhomax = 1;`) and does `MPI_Allreduce(&beyond_rhomax,&exceeded_rhomax,1,MPI_INT,MPI_SUM,world); if (exceeded_rhomax) ... error->warning(FLERR,"A per-atom density exceeded rhomax of EAM potential table - a linear extrapolation to the energy was made");`. src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.cpp performs the same extrapolation at lines 647-648, 723-724 and 932-933 (`else if (d_rho[i] > rhomax_kk) phi += d_fp[i] * (d_rho[i]-rhomax_kk);`) but never sets or reduces any flag, and compute() (lines 201-318) has no corresponding warning.
failure_scenario: An EAM run under -sf kk in which atoms come close enough to exceed rhomax produces extrapolated energies identical to the CPU run but without the diagnostic warning, so the user does not learn the table was exceeded.
suggested_fix: Reduce a beyond_rhomax flag out of kernel B/AB (e.g. an extra int in the reduction or a small device flag view) and issue the same MPI_Allreduce + warning as pair_eam.cpp:316-324.

summary: pair dpd/kk uses two different random-number generators depending on whether energy/virial is tallied on the timestep, so the noise realization (and hence the trajectory) depends on the thermo/dump interval when autotuning is enabled.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:229-240: `if (evflag) Kokkos::parallel_reduce(RangePolicy<...TagDPDKokkos<HALF,1>>...)` -> the range kernel draws `randnum = rand_gen.normal()` (line 349, Kokkos Random pool / RanMars), `else { if (tuner) { ... TeamPolicy<...TagDPDKokkos<HALF,0>> ... } }` -> the team kernel draws `saru(tag1, tag2, timestep, seed, randnum)` (line 467), a uniform SARU hash. The two kernels therefore consume different RNG streams for the same physics.
failure_scenario: With `package kokkos ... ` autotuning enabled and neighflag HALF, changing the thermo output frequency changes which kernel runs on which step and therefore changes the DPD random forces and the trajectory.
suggested_fix: Use one RNG scheme in both kernels (preferably the tag/timestep-based SARU in both, which is also decomposition-independent).

summary: pair gran/hooke/kk ignores fix rigid body masses when computing the effective mass meff, silently producing different damping forces than the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.cpp:280 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass);' uses only rmass[i]/rmass[j] (lines 211,243). The CPU base src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke.cpp:111-120 does 'mi = rmass[i]; mj = rmass[j]; if (fix_rigid) { if (mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = mass_rigid[i]; if (mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = mass_rigid[j]; } meff = mi*mj/(mi+mj);' and pair_gran_hooke.cpp:19-33 refreshes/communicates mass_rigid every reneighboring. 'grep -n fix_rigid src/KOKKOS/pair_gran*' returns nothing, and PairGranHooke::init_style (via PairGranHookeHistory::init_style, src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:42-52) still sets fix_rigid without any /kk error check. doc/src/pair_gran.rst:201-203 documents the rigid-body mass substitution as part of the model.
failure_scenario: Granular input with 'fix rigid' (or rigid/small) plus 'pair_style gran/hooke/kk': the velocity-damping term meff*gamman*vnnr and the friction cap meff*gammat*vrel use the individual particle mass instead of the body mass -> different trajectories than the identical non-kk run, with no warning.
suggested_fix: Port the mass_rigid lookup (a device DualView filled from fix_rigid->extract plus a forward comm) into the Kokkos kernels, or at minimum error out in PairGranHooke*Kokkos::init_style when fix_rigid is non-null.

summary: pair gran/hooke/history/kk ignores fix rigid body masses when computing the effective mass meff, silently diverging from the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:350 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass);' (imass/jmass are plain rmass, lines 274 and 306). CPU base src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:133-142 'mi = rmass[i]; mj = rmass[j]; if (fix_rigid) { if (mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = mass_rigid[i]; if (mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = mass_rigid[j]; } meff = mi*mj/(mi+mj);' plus the mass_rigid refresh/forward comm at pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:25-41. 'grep -n fix_rigid src/KOKKOS/pair_gran*' finds nothing, and the /kk init_style (line 63-93) adds no guard.
failure_scenario: Granular input combining 'fix rigid' with 'pair_style gran/hooke/history/kk' -> the normal damping and Coulomb friction cap use the single-particle mass rather than the body mass, giving silently different forces than the identical non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Port the mass_rigid array to a device DualView (filled from fix_rigid->extract plus a forward comm each reneighbor) or error out in init_style when fix_rigid is set.

summary: pair gran/hertz/history/kk ignores fix rigid body masses when computing the effective mass meff, silently diverging from the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:350 'KK_FLOAT meff = imass*jmass / (imass+jmass);' with imass/jmass taken straight from rmass (lines 274, 306). CPU base src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hertz_history.cpp:176-183 (identical block to pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:133-142) does 'mi = rmass[i]; mj = rmass[j]; if (fix_rigid) { if (mass_rigid[i] > 0.0) mi = mass_rigid[i]; if (mass_rigid[j] > 0.0) mj = mass_rigid[j]; }' after refreshing and forward-communicating mass_rigid. No fix_rigid/mass_rigid reference exists anywhere under src/KOKKOS.

summary: gran/hooke/kk stores the special_bonds lj factors into the base class's int special_lj[4], truncating fractional factors to 0 or 1.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.cpp:125-128 'special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ...' with src/pair.h:247 'int special_lj[4];    // copied from force->special_lj for Kokkos' -- PairGranHookeKokkos declares no KK_FLOAT special_lj of its own (see src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.h:63-96), unlike e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_gauss_cut_kokkos.h:89 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];'. The kernel then does src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_kokkos.cpp:234 'KK_FLOAT factor_lj = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(special_lj[sbmask(j)]);' and line 237 'if (factor_lj == 0) continue;'. The CPU base uses the true doubles: src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke.cpp:45 'double *special_lj = force->special_lj;'.
failure_scenario: Granular run with bonded particles and 'special_bonds lj 0.5 1.0 1.0': the CPU style scales the 1-2 granular contact force by 0.5, while gran/hooke/kk truncates 0.5 to 0 and skips those pairs entirely (factor_lj == 0 -> continue).
suggested_fix: Declare a 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];' member in the three KOKKOS granular pair style headers (shadowing Pair::special_lj as the other KOKKOS pair styles do), or change Pair::special_lj to double.

summary: gran/hooke/history/kk stores special_bonds lj factors in the base class int special_lj[4], truncating fractional factors to 0/1.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:142-145 'special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ...' with src/pair.h:247 'int special_lj[4];' -- the /kk header (src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.h:66-104) declares no KK_FLOAT special_lj shadow, unlike the other KOKKOS pair styles (e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lennard_mdf_kokkos.h:89). Kernel use: line 297 'KK_FLOAT factor_lj = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(special_lj[sbmask(j)]);' and line 300 'if (factor_lj == 0) continue;'. CPU: src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hooke_history.cpp:53 'double *special_lj = force->special_lj;'.
failure_scenario: 'special_bonds lj 0.5 1 1' with gran/hooke/history/kk: 1-2 contacts are dropped entirely (0.5 truncates to 0) instead of being scaled by 0.5, changing forces and the stored shear history.
suggested_fix: Add 'KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];' to the three KOKKOS granular pair style headers so the double factors survive, or widen Pair::special_lj to double.

summary: d_neighbors_touch / d_numneigh_touch are allocated every time the neighbor list is resized but are never read or written anywhere, wasting a full neighbor-list-sized device allocation.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:160-164 'if (d_numneigh.extent(0) != d_numneigh_touch.extent(0)) d_numneigh_touch = typename AT::t_int_1d(...); if (d_neighbors.extent(0) != d_neighbors_touch.extent(0) || ...) d_neighbors_touch = typename AT::t_neighbors_2d("pair:neighbors_touch",d_neighbors.extent(0),d_neighbors.extent(1));'. Declared at src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.h:90-91. 'grep -rn "d_neighbors_touch|d_numneigh_touch" src/KOKKOS/*' matches only those declaration and allocation lines (and the identical block in pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:160-164) -- no kernel ever touches them. t_neighbors_2d is tdual_int_2d_dl (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1282-1283), so the allocation duplicates the entire int neighbor list.
failure_scenario: Any gran/hooke/history/kk or gran/hertz/history/kk run allocates a second array of nmax*maxneighs ints on the GPU that is never used; on a large granular run this can be hundreds of MB of wasted device memory and can trigger an out-of-memory abort.
suggested_fix: Delete the two members and their allocation block from both granular history KOKKOS pair styles.

summary: gran/hertz/history/kk stores special_bonds lj factors in the base class int special_lj[4], truncating fractional factors to 0/1.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:142-145 'special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ...' assigns doubles into src/pair.h:247 'int special_lj[4];'; the /kk header src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.h:66-104 declares no KK_FLOAT shadow. Kernel: line 297 'KK_FLOAT factor_lj = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(special_lj[sbmask(j)]);', line 300 'if (factor_lj == 0) continue;'. CPU uses the true doubles (src/GRANULAR/pair_gran_hertz_history.cpp, 'double *special_lj = force->special_lj;').

summary: atoms_per_team can become 0 (integer division by zero on the next line) when 'package kokkos threads/per/atom' or 'pair/team/size' is given an unfortunate value; neither is range-checked.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:926-953: 'if (fpair->lmp->kokkos->threads_per_atom_set) vectorsize = fpair->lmp->kokkos->threads_per_atom; ... vectorsize = MIN(vectorsize,max_vectorsize); ... if (fpair->lmp->kokkos->pair_team_size_set) teamsize_max = fpair->lmp->kokkos->pair_team_size; atoms_per_team = teamsize_max/vectorsize;' followed by line 953 'const int num_teams = inum / atoms_per_team + (inum % atoms_per_team ? 1 : 0);'. The 'if (vectorsize == 0) vectorsize = 1;' guard at line 917 only protects the GetMaxNeighs result, not the later user override. src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:696-706 parses 'threads/per/atom' and 'pair/team/size' with utils::inumeric and no bounds check; KokkosLMP::newton_check (kokkos.cpp:857-870) only checks that neigh/thread is on.
failure_scenario: 'package kokkos neigh/thread on threads/per/atom 0' -> vectorsize 0 -> teamsize_max/0; or 'package kokkos neigh/thread on pair/team/size 8 threads/per/atom 32' -> atoms_per_team = 0 -> inum/0. Either way an integer divide-by-zero (SIGFPE) instead of a clear error message.
suggested_fix: Validate threads_per_atom (>=1) and pair_team_size (>=1) when parsing the package kokkos options, and clamp atoms_per_team to at least 1 in pair_compute_neighlist.

summary: PairHybridScaledKokkos::settings() drops the CPU guard that rejects INTEL/GPU/OMP accelerator sub-styles, so hybrid/scaled/kk silently accepts sub-styles whose force accumulation is incompatible with its clear/scale/restore scheme.
evidence: diff of the two settings() bodies shows the /kk copy is missing src/pair_hybrid_scaled.cpp:388-391 (missing right after 'compute_tally[nstyles] = 1;' at src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_scaled_kokkos.cpp:562) 'if ((styles[nstyles]->suffix_flag & (Suffix::INTEL | Suffix::GPU | Suffix::OMP)) != 0) error->all(FLERR, "Pair style hybrid/scaled does not support accelerator styles");' -- it is the only substantive difference besides the function name. The scheme in src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_scaled_kokkos.cpp:340-384 zeroes atom->f/atom->torque before every sub-style and reads them back right after that sub-style's compute(), which a GPU style (whose forces are added later by FixGPU::post_force) or an OMP style with thread-private force buffers does not satisfy.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style hybrid/scaled/kk 1.0 lj/cut/gpu 10.0 0.5 coul/cut/gpu 10.0' is accepted; the GPU sub-style's forces are added in FixGPU::post_force after the hybrid already snapshotted and restored f, so the scale factors are not applied and the forces are wrong -- the CPU hybrid/scaled refuses the same input.
suggested_fix: Copy the suffix_flag check from src/pair_hybrid_scaled.cpp into PairHybridScaledKokkos::settings() (KOKKOS sub-styles are unaffected since Suffix::KOKKOS is not in the mask).

summary: k_cutsq is marked host-modified only once inside allocate(), so cutoff values written to cutsq[][] by Pair::init() on a later run are never copied to the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:1656-1658 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_cutsq,cutsq,ntypes+1,ntypes+1,"pair:cutsq"); d_cutsq = k_cutsq.template view<DeviceType>(); k_cutsq.modify_host();' is the ONLY modify_host() on k_cutsq in the file ('grep -n "k_cutsq" src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp' -> lines 81, 153, 1656-1658). The only sync is compute() line 153 'k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>();', which is a no-op once the dirty flag has been cleared. PairExp6rxKokkos does not override init_one (see src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.h:90-94), unlike every other KOKKOS pair style in this package (e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_gauss_cut_kokkos.cpp:338-339 'k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = ...; k_cutsq.modify_host();'), while src/pair.cpp Pair::init() rewrites cutsq[i][j] = cut*cut on the host before every run and src/DPD-REACT/pair_exp6_rx.cpp:722-728 lets pair_coeff set a per-pair cutoff.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style exp6/rx/kk 10.0 ...' / 'pair_coeff * * ... none 10.0' / 'run 100' / 'pair_coeff * * ... none 6.0' / 'run 100': the second run's kernels still test rsq against the old 10.0 cutoff (d_cutsq is stale) and also use the stale rCut in the shifted-potential terms, silently giving wrong energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Override init_one() in PairExp6rxKokkos to call PairExp6rx::init_one() and then k_cutsq.modify_host(), or simply call k_cutsq.modify_host() unconditionally in init_style()/setup() before the sync in compute().

summary: pair gauss/kk silently drops the documented 'occupancy' pvector output (nextra set to 0), so a compute pair gauss on the /kk style yields no vector instead of the occupancy count.
failure_scenario: Input using 'pair_style gauss/kk', 'compute gauss all pair gauss', 'variable occ equal c_gauss[1]' -> compute has no vector, so the variable errors out (or silently no data), while the identical non-kk input reports the occupancy.
suggested_fix: Either compute the occupancy count on device (an extra reduction member in EV_FLOAT or a separate parallel_reduce) or, at minimum, print a one-time warning in init_style and document the limitation in doc/src/pair_gauss.rst.

summary: The invalid-neighbor-list fallback uses printf() and then returns silently instead of raising a LAMMPS error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:858-865 'EV_FLOAT pair_compute_neighlist (PairStyle* fpair, std::enable_if_t<!((NEIGHFLAG&PairStyle::EnabledNeighFlags) != 0), ...> list) { EV_FLOAT ev; (void) fpair; (void) list; printf("ERROR: calling pair_compute with invalid neighbor list style: requested %i  available %i \n",NEIGHFLAG,PairStyle::EnabledNeighFlags); return ev; }'. .github/copilot-instructions.md forbids printf()/fprintf(screen,...) in favour of utils::logmesg()/error->all().
failure_scenario: A pair style requested with a neighbor list variant it does not support prints an unformatted message on every MPI rank and then computes zero forces silently instead of aborting.
suggested_fix: Replace the printf with fpair->error->all(FLERR, ...) (or utils::logmesg) so the run stops with a proper LAMMPS error message.

summary: PairHybridOverlayKokkos::coeff is a stale copy of PairHybridOverlay::coeff and still carries the old, less specific error message for an unknown sub-style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_overlay_kokkos.cpp:61-64 'if (m == nstyles) { if (strcmp(arg[2],"none") == 0) none = 1; else error->all(FLERR,"Pair coeff for hybrid has invalid style: {}", arg[2]); }' vs src/pair_hybrid_overlay.cpp:62-65 'if (strcmp(arg[2],"none") == 0) none = 1; else error->all(FLERR,"Expected hybrid sub-style instead of {} in pair_coeff command", arg[2]);'. A diff of the two coeff() bodies shows this is their only difference, so the /kk copy has simply drifted.
failure_scenario: A typo in a pair_coeff sub-style name produces a different (older) error message under hybrid/overlay/kk than under hybrid/overlay, and any future fix to the CPU coeff() will silently miss the KOKKOS copy.
suggested_fix: Sync the error message with src/pair_hybrid_overlay.cpp, or better, factor the shared logic so the KOKKOS overlay style does not duplicate coeff().

summary: single() and born_matrix() index scaleidx/atomvar with the loop counter m instead of the sub-style index map[itype][jtype][m], so the atom-style-scale branch is chosen from the wrong sub-style's data.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_scaled_kokkos.cpp:654-663 'double scale = scaleval[map[itype][jtype][m]]; esum += scale * pstyle->single(...); if (scaleidx[m] < 0 || atomvar[m] < 0) { fforce += scale * fone; } else { update_atomscale(m); ... }' -- note scaleval uses map[itype][jtype][m] while scaleidx/atomvar/update_atomscale use the bare m. Same pattern at lines 738-748 in born_matrix(). (The CPU original src/pair_hybrid_scaled.cpp:263-276 has the identical mistake, so this is a faithfully copied bug rather than a KOKKOS-only one.)
failure_scenario: hybrid/scaled with more than one sub-style where the sub-style order and the per-type-pair map order differ: 'pair_write' or a tally compute that calls single() picks the wrong scale mode, applying a constant scale where an atom-style variable was meant (or the reverse, evaluating the wrong variable).
suggested_fix: Hoist 'const int ms = map[itype][jtype][m];' and use scaleval[ms], scaleidx[ms], atomvar[ms] and update_atomscale(ms) throughout both loops; fix the CPU original the same way.

summary: Roughly 690 lines of unreachable code follow an unconditional return in each of the two compute operator() overloads.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:399-412 is a block that dispatches to vectorized_operator<...> for all four (Site1EqSite2 x OneType) cases and ends with 'return;' at line 411; lines 414-753 (the whole original scalar kernel, including the a_f(i)/a_uCG[i] writeback at 748-752) can never execute. The same shape repeats at lines 772-785 ('return;' at 784) leaving lines 787-1133 dead. The dead copies still reference MathSpecialKokkos::powint (lines 581-1150) whereas the live vectorized_operator uses the local __powint<12> helper, so the two have already diverged.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect today, but the dead kernels look like the authoritative implementation: a future fix applied there (as the powint/__powint divergence shows already happened in reverse) would silently have no effect on results.
suggested_fix: Delete lines 414-753 and 787-1133 so each operator() only contains the vectorized_operator dispatch.

summary: A misspelled guard macro (KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_simd, lowercase) permanently disables one of the three omp simd reduction pragmas in getMixingWeightsVect.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:2117 '#ifdef KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_simd' followed by '#pragma omp simd reduction(+:errorFlag1)', whereas the other two sites spell it correctly: line 1273 '#ifdef KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_SIMD' and line 2354 '#ifdef KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_SIMD'. Only those three occurrences exist in src/.
failure_scenario: The nTotal/fractionOFA reduction loop in the CPU-only (non-GPU) mixing-weight path is never vectorized; a silent performance loss only.
suggested_fix: Change the guard at line 2117 to KOKKOS_ENABLE_PRAGMA_SIMD.

summary: The helper __powint uses a reserved double-underscore identifier and falls off the end of a non-void function when the compiler cannot fold the if.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:1138-1151 'template<int n> KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION KK_FLOAT __powint(const KK_FLOAT& x, const int) { static_assert(n == 12, ...); if (n == 12) { KK_FLOAT x3 = x*x*x; return x3*x3*x3*x3; } }' -- no return outside the if, and identifiers beginning with two underscores are reserved to the implementation in any scope (C++ [lex.name]).
failure_scenario: -Wreturn-type warnings (errors under -Werror) and a possible clash with a compiler/CUDA internal name; the unused second 'const int' parameter also makes call sites read as if the exponent were a runtime value.
suggested_fix: Rename it (e.g. powint12 in an anonymous namespace), drop the unused int parameter, and return the value unconditionally.

summary: The kernel writes the device side of FixNeighHistoryKokkos::k_firstflag/k_firstvalue but never calls modify<DeviceType>() on those DualViews.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_gran_hooke_history_kokkos.cpp:166-172 syncs and takes views ('fix_historyKK->k_firstflag.template sync<DeviceType>(); ... Kokkos::deep_copy(d_firsttouch,0);') and the kernel then writes them (lines 313-315 'd_firstshear(i,3*jj) = 0;', line 319 'd_firsttouch(i,jj) = 1;', lines 415-417). No 'k_firstflag.modify<DeviceType>()' / 'k_firstvalue.modify<DeviceType>()' appears afterwards, unlike src/KOKKOS/fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:237-238 which does exactly that after its own kernel. Same omission in pair_gran_hertz_history_kokkos.cpp:166-172.
failure_scenario: Currently masked because post_neighbor() leaves the DualView marked device-modified, so subsequent sync<Device> calls are no-ops; but any future host-side write or sync_host() of the history arrays between two pair computes would silently discard the shear history updated on device.
suggested_fix: Add 'fix_historyKK->k_firstflag.template modify<DeviceType>(); fix_historyKK->k_firstvalue.template modify<DeviceType>();' after the parallel_for in both granular history KOKKOS pair styles.

summary: single()/born_matrix() call update_atomscale() which writes into the host scratch array atomscale and into k_atomscale, but both are only ever allocated inside compute().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_hybrid_scaled_kokkos.cpp:298-303 allocates them only under 'if (atomscaleflag && (atom->nmax > nmaxatomscale))' inside compute(); update_atomscale (lines 211-223) does 'input->variable->compute_atom(atomvar[m], igroupall, atomscale, 1, 0); auto h_atomscale = k_atomscale.view_host(); for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; ++i) h_atomscale(i) = atomscale[i];' with no allocation check, and single() (line 663) / born_matrix() (line 743) call it directly. The constructor leaves atomscale nullptr (line 37) and k_atomscale default-constructed (extent 0).
failure_scenario: 'pair_write' or a pair tally compute invoking single() on a hybrid/scaled/kk whose scale factor is an atom-style variable, before compute() has run with that variable active -> compute_atom writes through a null pointer and h_atomscale(i) writes past a zero-extent view.
suggested_fix: Move the atomscale/k_atomscale allocation into update_atomscale() (grow to atom->nmax on entry) so every caller is safe.

summary: special_coul is applied by scaling the whole damped-shifted-force Coulomb term by factor_coul instead of subtracting (1-factor_coul)*prefactor as the CPU style does, so forces and Coulomb energies on special-bonded pairs are wrong.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:223-229 compute_fcoul: 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = factor_coul * qqrd2e * qtmp * q(j);' ... 'return prefactor * (erfcc/r + 2.0*alpha_kk/MY_PIS * erfcd + r*f_shift_kk) * r2inv;' and :248-253 compute_ecoul: 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = factor_coul * qqrd2e * qtmp * q(j);' ... 'return prefactor * (erfcc - r*e_shift_kk - rsq*f_shift_kk) / r;'. CPU base src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:137-143 'prefactor = qqrd2e*qtmp*q[j]/r; forcecoul = prefactor * (erfcc/r + 2.0*alpha/MY_PIS * erfcd + r*f_shift) * r; if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' and :164-165 'ecoul = prefactor * (erfcc - r*e_shift - rsq*f_shift); if (factor_coul < 1.0) ecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;'. Algebraically CPU gives A*S - (1-fc)*A/r while the kokkos style gives fc*A*S (A = qqrd2e*qi*qj, S = erfcc/r + 2a/sqrt(pi)*erfcd + r*f_shift); they agree only when factor_coul == 1. The correctly ported sibling src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:205-215 and :258-262 uses the CPU form.
failure_scenario: Any molecular system with special_bonds coul != 1.0 (the LAMMPS default 0.0 0.0 0.0) run with 'pair_style lj/cut/coul/dsf/kk': every 1-2/1-3/1-4 pair inside cut_coul gets a Coulomb force and energy different from pair_style lj/cut/coul/dsf, e.g. with factor_coul = 0 the kk style returns exactly 0 while the CPU style returns -A*(S-1/r).
suggested_fix: Set prefactor = qqrd2e*qtmp*q(j)/r (no factor_coul), form forcecoul/ecoul as in the CPU style and then apply 'if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' (same for ecoul), mirroring pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp. The same defect is in src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:260-266 and should be fixed together.

summary: The DSF self-energy is added only to the global eng_coul and never to the per-atom energy array, so eatom/compute pe/atom is missing the self term that the CPU style tallies.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:129-133 'for (int ii = 0; ii < inum; ii ++) { double qtmp = atom->q[ii]; eng_coul += -(e_shift/2.0 + alpha/MY_PIS) * qtmp*qtmp*static_cast<double>(qqrd2e); }' -- there is no corresponding d_eatom/eatom update anywhere in the file (the only eatom handling is the sync at :151-154). CPU base src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:110-112 'if (eflag) { double e_self = -(e_shift/2.0 + alpha/MY_PIS) * qtmp*qtmp*qqrd2e; ev_tally(i,i,nlocal,0,0.0,e_self,0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0); }', and Pair::ev_tally with i==j and newton_pair==0 adds 0.5*e_self twice, i.e. the full e_self, to eatom[i]. The correctly ported sibling src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:145-153 does 'if (eflag_atom) { ... for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++) eatom[i] += -(e_shift/2.0 + alpha/MY_PIS) * qisq * force->qqrd2e; }'.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style lj/cut/coul/dsf/kk' + 'compute pe/atom' (or a dump with c_pe): the sum over per-atom energies does not equal the reported global potential energy and differs from the CPU style by -(e_shift/2 + alpha/sqrt(pi))*qqrd2e*sum(q_i^2), which for a charged system is a large fraction of the Coulomb energy.
suggested_fix: After 'k_eatom.sync_host()' add a loop that adds the per-atom self-energy to eatom[i] for i < nlocal, guarded by eflag_atom, exactly as pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp does.

summary: The host-side self-energy loop reads the host charge array atom->q without ever calling atomKK->sync(Host,Q_MASK), so on a GPU build it reads charges that are stale after the device-side atom exchange/sort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:96 only does 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read)' (execution_space is Device for the /kk and /kk/device variants), and then :131 reads the host raw pointer 'double qtmp = atom->q[ii];'. atom->q is the host mirror of atomKK->k_q (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_charge_kokkos.cpp:73 'memoryKK->grow_kokkos(atomKK->k_q,atomKK->q,nmax,"atom:q")'). Both AtomVecKokkos::unpack_exchange_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:2852 'atomKK->modified(space,datamask_exchange);') and AtomVecChargeKokkos::sort_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_charge_kokkos.cpp:122-134, Sorter.sort(...,d_q) then 'atomKK->modified(Device, ALL_MASK & ~F_MASK)') mark q modified on the device, and nothing in the /kk force path syncs it back to the host.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank GPU run where atoms migrate: after comm->exchange() the host q array still holds the previous step's atom set and count, so the self-energy sum uses wrong charges (and reads past the previously valid nlocal entries), corrupting the reported Coulomb energy.
suggested_fix: Either call atomKK->sync(Host,Q_MASK) before the loop, or (better) compute the self-energy in a Kokkos parallel_reduce over the device view q, adding to ev.ecoul / d_eatom.

summary: The self-energy loop is not guarded by eflag and indexes the charge array with the neighbor-list slot ii instead of list->ilist[ii], and it uses list->inum instead of nlocal.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:127-133 'int inum = list->inum; for (int ii = 0; ii < inum; ii ++) { //int i = list->ilist[ii];\n  double qtmp = atom->q[ii]; eng_coul += ...; }' -- the correct index line is commented out. CPU base src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:110 wraps the self term in 'if (eflag)' and uses qtmp = q[i] with i = ilist[ii]. The sibling src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:119-123 loops 'for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++)'.
failure_scenario: Currently benign because NPairKokkos sets d_ilist(i)=i and inum=nlocal (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:593,:356), and eng_coul is reset by ev_init on every eflag_global step; but the unconditional accumulation dirties eng_coul on non-energy steps and the ii indexing silently breaks if a future neighbor build ever produces a non-identity ilist.
suggested_fix: Guard the loop with 'if (eflag)' (splitting the eflag_global and eflag_atom contributions), and loop 'for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++)' as pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp does.

summary: Dead DualView members k_cut_ljsq and k_cut_coulsq are declared but never allocated, filled, modified or synced anywhere in the style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_charmm_coul_charmm_implicit_kokkos.h:98 'DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d k_cut_ljsq;' and :100 'DAT::tdual_kkfloat_2d k_cut_coulsq;'. grep for k_cut_ljsq/k_cut_coulsq over pair_lj_charmm_coul_charmm_implicit_kokkos.{cpp,h} returns only these two declarations. The device views actually used, d_cut_ljsq/d_cut_coulsq, are created directly in allocate() (pair_lj_charmm_coul_charmm_implicit_kokkos.cpp:298-300) and filled by Kokkos::deep_copy in init_style() (:413-415). The sibling style pair_lj_charmm_coul_charmm_kokkos.h has no such members.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; a reader can mistake them for the buffers backing d_cut_ljsq/d_cut_coulsq and add a sync/modify call against the wrong (empty) view.
suggested_fix: Delete the two unused declarations.

summary: The total force (fx/fy/fz), its accumulation onto i and j, and the torque accumulation are all computed INSIDE the `if (rsq < cut_coulsq_ij)` block, so for any pair with cut_coul <= r < cut_lj the LJ force is computed but silently discarded, while the LJ energy is still tallied.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut_kokkos.cpp:320 opens `if (rsq < cut_coulsq_ij) {` and line 434 closes it (`} // cutsq_coulsq_ij`); lines 400-421 -- `KK_FLOAT fq = factor_coul*qqrd2e; fx = fq*forcecoulx + delx*forcelj; ... fx_i += fx; ... a_f(j,0) -= fx;` -- sit inside that block, while `forcelj` is computed at lines 303-306 under the separate `if (rsq < cut_ljsq_ij)`. The CPU style src/DIPOLE/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut.cpp closes the coul block at line 203 and only THEN does `fq = factor_coul*qqrd2e; fx = fq*forcecoulx + delx*forcelj;` (lines 215-218) and the f/torque accumulation (lines 222-236). The same defect is repeated in the team kernel: block opened at line 561, closed at line 669, with fx/fy/fz assigned at lines 642-644 inside it while `fx` is initialised to 0 at line 517 and accumulated at line 674 outside.
failure_scenario: `pair_style lj/cut/dipole/cut/kk 10.0 6.0` (cut_lj 10, cut_coul 6, both legal; cutsq = max(cut_lj,cut_coul)^2 per src/DIPOLE/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut.cpp init_one): every pair with 6 <= r < 10 contributes its LJ energy to eng_vdwl but zero force and zero virial, so forces do not match the energy, energy is not conserved, and results differ from the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Move the `fq`/`fx`/`fy`/`fz` computation, the i- and j-side force and torque accumulation out of the `if (rsq < cut_coulsq_ij)` block (to just before the ev_tally_xyz call), exactly as the CPU style does, in both the range and the team kernel.

summary: evdwl and ecoul are only evaluated when eflag_global is set, so when only per-atom energy is requested (eflag_atom without eflag_global) ev_tally_xyz receives epair = 0 and all per-atom pair energies come out zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut_kokkos.cpp:307 `if (eflag_global) { evdwl = ...; ev.evdwl += ...; }` and line 423 `if (EVFLAG && eflag_global) { ecoul = ...; ev.ecoul += ...; }`, while line 436-437 `if (EVFLAG && (eflag_atom || vflag_either)) ev_tally_xyz<...>(ev, i, j, ecoul+evdwl, ...)` uses those variables (initialised to 0 at lines 285-286). The CPU style src/DIPOLE/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut.cpp:238 guards the same computation with `if (eflag)` (i.e. eflag_either), and src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:180 and 264 likewise use `c.eflag_either`. Repeated at lines 548 and 658 in the team kernel.
failure_scenario: `compute pe/atom` dumped on a timestep on which no global energy is needed (Verlet::ev_set gives eflag = ENERGY_ATOM only, eflag_global = 0): every atom's pair energy is reported as 0.0 instead of its real value.
suggested_fix: Change both guards to `eflag_either` (keeping the ev.evdwl / ev.ecoul reduction updates themselves under eflag_global).

summary: The Wolf self-energy is accumulated in a host loop over atom->q[i] although only the DEVICE copy of q was synced, so a device-side sort or a device-side charge update leaves the host charges stale and the self-energy (and per-atom eatom) wrong.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_wolf_kokkos.cpp:88 `atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read);` (execution_space = Device for the /kk and /kk/device variants) is the only sync, then lines 119-123 `for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++) { double qisq = atom->q[i]*atom->q[i]; eng_coul += ...; }` and lines 148-152 `eatom[i] += ...` read the HOST array atom->q. src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_charge_kokkos.cpp:124-134 (sort_kokkos) sorts d_q on the device and then calls `atomKK->modified(Device, ALL_MASK & ~F_MASK)` (Q_MASK included), leaving the host mirror stale; src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:537 likewise does `atomKK->modified(execution_space,Q_MASK)`.
failure_scenario: GPU run with the default atom sorting: after AtomKokkos::sort_device() the host q array holds the pre-sort permutation, so eatom[i] gets another atom's self-energy (per-atom energies wrong); with any /kk fix that updates charges on the device (fix qeq/*) the total eng_coul self-term is computed from stale charges and the global Coulomb energy is wrong.
suggested_fix: Either add `atomKK->sync(Host,Q_MASK);` before the host loops (and keep the loops off the critical path), or better, compute the self-energy in a Kokkos kernel over d_q so the term stays device-resident.

summary: In the team kernel the per-atom force/torque update after the ThreadVectorRange reduction is not wrapped in Kokkos::single(Kokkos::PerThread(team),...), so every vector lane executes the read-modify-write on f(i,*) and torque(i,*).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut_kokkos.cpp:501 `Kokkos::parallel_reduce(Kokkos::ThreadVectorRange(team, jnum), [&](...){...}, fx_i, fy_i, fz_i, torquex_i, torquey_i, torquez_i);` is followed at lines 684-689 by bare `a_f(i,0) += fx_i; ... a_torque(i,2) += torquez_i;`. The canonical pattern in src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:354-358 wraps exactly this update: `Kokkos::single(Kokkos::PerThread(team), [&] () { a_f(i,0) += fsum.x; ... });` (and pair_kokkos.h:309-314 for the ZEROFLAG store).
failure_scenario: GPU run with `-k on ... -pk kokkos neigh full` plus the autotuner enabled and newton off (the only path that selects the team policy, lines 188-200): with vectorsize > 1 and independent thread scheduling the non-atomic `f(i,0) += fx_i` from the lanes of a warp can interleave, giving forces that are a multiple of the correct value on some atoms.
suggested_fix: Wrap the six post-reduction accumulations in `Kokkos::single(Kokkos::PerThread(team), [&] () { ... });` as pair_kokkos.h does.

summary: compute() never sets copymode = 1 around the pair_compute<> call, unlike every other KOKKOS pair style; the style-copy double-free is only avoided by the PairComputeFunctor destructor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_soft_kokkos.cpp:114-144 goes straight from `// loop over neighbors of my atoms` to `EV_FLOAT ev = pair_compute<...>(this,...)` with no `copymode = 1;`/`copymode = 0;` pair, whereas e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp:107 and src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_kokkos.cpp:125 set `copymode = 1;` before the call and reset it at the end. Safety today rests entirely on src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:103 `~PairComputeFunctor() {c.copymode = 1; list.copymode = 1;};`.
failure_scenario: Any future code path that copies the style object outside PairComputeFunctor (or an added Kokkos kernel taking *this) would run the copy's destructor with copymode == 0 and free k_eatom/k_vatom/k_cutsq/k_cut_ljsq that the original still owns.
suggested_fix: Add `copymode = 1;` before the pair_compute<> call and `copymode = 0;` at the end of compute(), matching the other lj/cut/* Kokkos styles.

summary: For a special-bonded pair the CPU core/shell style rescales r2inv with EPS_EWALD_SQR and uses that rescaled r2inv for the LJ force/energy as well; the Kokkos compute_fpair/compute_evdwl only add EPSILON, so the LJ term diverges from the CPU style at very small separations.
evidence: src/CORESHELL/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_cs.cpp:126 sets `r2inv = 1.0/(rsq + EPS_EWALD_SQR);` inside the `factor_coul < 1.0` branch, and lines 153-157 then use exactly that r2inv for `r6inv = r2inv*r2inv*r2inv; forcelj = r6inv*(lj1*r6inv - lj2);` and `fpair = (forcecoul + factor_lj*forcelj) * r2inv`. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp:200-210 instead always uses `const KK_FLOAT rsq = rsq_in + EPSILON; const KK_FLOAT r2inv = 1.0/rsq;` (EPSILON = 1e-20, EPS_EWALD_SQR = 1e-12) and the same in compute_evdwl at lines 296-299.
failure_scenario: A core/shell pair at r ~ 0 with a non-zero special_lj factor: CPU evaluates r6inv from 1/(rsq+1e-12) while the Kokkos style evaluates it from 1/(rsq+1e-20), producing LJ forces/energies that differ by ~24 orders of magnitude (and overflow to inf/NaN under a KK_FLOAT=float build).
suggested_fix: Pass factor_coul into the LJ helpers (or precompute) so compute_fpair/compute_evdwl use 1/(rsq+EPS_EWALD_SQR) when factor_coul < 1.0 and rsq < cut_coulsq, matching the CPU style.

summary: compute_fpair multiplies the LJ derivative by rshift instead of dividing by it, so the pair force is wrong by a factor rshift^2 -- faithfully copied from the CPU style, which has the same expression (pre-existing upstream defect, not a port regression).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_expand_sphere_kokkos.cpp:154 `return r6inv*(lj1*r6inv - lj2) * rshift / r;` mirrors src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_expand_sphere.cpp:61 `fpair = factor_lj * forcelj * rshift / r;` (and single() at the same file). With lj1 = 48*eps*sigma^12 and lj2 = 24*eps*sigma^6 (init_one), forcelj = r6inv*(lj1*r6inv-lj2) equals rshift * (-dE/drshift), so the scalar multiplying del must be forcelj/(rshift*r) -- which is exactly what the sibling style src/pair_lj_expand.cpp:? does: `fpair = factor_lj * forcelj / rshift / r;` (and src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_expand_kokkos.cpp:158 `return forcelj/rshift/r;`).
failure_scenario: pair_style lj/expand/sphere (with or without /kk): the force on every pair is scaled by rshift^2 relative to the analytic gradient of the tallied energy, so forces do not match the energy and energy is not conserved; the discrepancy vanishes only at rshift = 1.
suggested_fix: If confirmed upstream, change both the CPU style and the Kokkos kernel to `forcelj / rshift / r` (matching lj/expand); the YAML reference fixtures were generated from the current code, so they must be regenerated together with the fix.

summary: The per-atom virial array k_vatom is sized and size-checked with `maxeatom` instead of `maxvatom`, so when per-atom stress is requested without per-atom energy the array is never allocated and v_tally writes out of bounds / through a null pointer.
failure_scenario: `pair_style mliap/kk ...` plus `compute s all stress/atom NULL` and a dump of it, with no per-atom energy compute: eflag_atom stays 0 so maxeatom stays 0, the `extent(0) < maxeatom` test is 0 < 0 (false), k_vatom/vatom are never allocated, and the first v_tally dereferences a null `vatom` (host path) or writes past a zero-extent view (device path) - segfault or silent memory corruption.
suggested_fix: Use `maxvatom` in both the extent comparison and the create_kokkos call (and fix the "pair:eatom" memory label to "pair:vatom").

summary: d_scale is declared as an integer view (AT::t_int_2d) but holds the MEAM `scale` factor, which is a double; every scale value is truncated to an integer on the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.h:108 `typename AT::t_int_2d d_scale;` (and the same type in src/KOKKOS/meam_kokkos.h:65 and its meam_dens_final/meam_force signatures). It is filled in src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.cpp:299-310 from the CPU `double **scale`: `MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_scale,"pair:scale",n+1,n+1); ... h_scale(i,j) = scale[i][j];`. The CPU base declares `double **scale` (src/MEAM/pair_meam.h) and uses it as a double: src/MEAM/meam_dens_final.cpp:34 `scaleii = scale[type[i]][type[i]];`, src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:92 `scaleij = scale[type[i]][type[j]];`.
failure_scenario: `fix adapt ... pair meam scale 1 1 v_ramp` with a scale that ramps 0->1: on the device every value below 1.0 truncates to 0 (energies/forces zeroed) and 1.5 truncates to 1, so pair meam/kk gives completely different energies from pair meam.
suggested_fix: Change d_scale to a floating-point view (`typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d`) in pair_meam_kokkos.h, meam_kokkos.h and the meam_dens_final/meam_force signatures.

summary: d_scale is copied to the device only inside coeff(), so later host-side changes to `scale` (fix adapt, and PairMEAM::init_one's symmetrization) never reach the device, and the lower triangle is copied from uninitialized memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.cpp:296-310 is the only place d_scale is written; it runs from coeff(). src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:303-312 sets `scale[i][j] = 1.0` only for `j >= i`, and the j<i entries are first written in init_one (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:353-354 `scale[j][i] = scale[i][j];`), which runs after coeff and is not overridden by PairMEAMKokkos - so the `for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++) h_scale(i,j) = scale[i][j];` loop reads memory->create'd but never-initialized doubles for j<i. `scale` is also exposed for run-time modification via PairMEAM::extract (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:898 `if (strcmp(str,"scale")==0) return (void *) scale;`) and `fix adapt pair meam scale` is a documented feature (doc/src/fix_adapt.rst), but nothing re-uploads d_scale after fix adapt writes it.
failure_scenario: `fix adapt 1 pair meam scale 1 1 v_lambda` in a run with pair_style meam/kk: the host scale array changes every step but the device keeps the value captured at pair_coeff time, so the /kk run reproduces the unscaled potential while the CPU run scales it.
suggested_fix: Refresh d_scale from `scale` at the start of compute() (or in init_one/init_style), and initialize the whole scale array symmetrically before copying.

summary: The KOKKOS MEAM force kernel indexes the scale factor with (type[i],type[i]) instead of (type[i],type[j]), leaves eatom unscaled, and never applies scaleij to dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm as the CPU library does.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h:187-194: `KK_FLOAT scaleij = d_scale(type[i], type[i]); KK_FLOAT phi_sc = phi * scaleij; if (eflag_global) ev.evdwl += phi_sc*sij; if (eflag_atom) { a_eatom[i] += 0.5*phi*sij; a_eatom[j] += 0.5*phi*sij; }`. CPU src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:92 `scaleij = scale[type[i]][type[j]];` and :115-119 `double phi_sc = phi * scaleij; ... eatom[i] = eatom[i] + 0.5 * phi_sc * sij; eatom[j] = eatom[j] + 0.5 * phi_sc * sij;`. CPU :622-628 additionally does `if (!isone(scaleij)) { dUdrij *= scaleij; dUdsij *= scaleij; dUdrijm[0..2] *= scaleij; }` - there is no corresponding code in src/KOKKOS/meam_force_kokkos.h (grep for scaleij finds only lines 187-188; dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm at lines 692-714 are used unscaled).
failure_scenario: Any run using a non-unit MEAM scale factor (fix adapt pair meam scale, or an off-diagonal scale): forces from pair meam/kk are unscaled while pair meam scales them, and per-atom energies differ even for the diagonal case.
suggested_fix: Use `d_scale(type[i], type[j])`, apply scaleij to the eatom contributions, and add the missing `dUdrij/dUdsij/dUdrijm *= scaleij` block to mirror src/MEAM/meam_force.cpp:622-628.

summary: compute_evdwl for pair_style morse/kk omits the energy offset, so `pair_modify shift yes` has no effect and the pair energy differs from the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.cpp:165-178 reads only r0/d0/alpha and returns `d0 * dexp * ( dexp - static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(2.0) );` - `offset` is never fetched from m_params/params even though it is stored there (src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.cpp:238 `k_params.view_host()(i,j).offset = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(offset[i][j]);` and declared at src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.h:54). The CPU base src/pair_morse.cpp:119 computes `evdwl = d0[itype][jtype] * (dexp * dexp - 2.0 * dexp) - offset[itype][jtype];`. Sibling KOKKOS styles do subtract it, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_smooth_linear_kokkos.cpp and src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_smooth_kokkos.cpp:175.
failure_scenario: `pair_style morse 10.0` with `pair_modify shift yes`: pair morse/kk reports an unshifted pair energy (evdwl and per-atom energy differ from pair morse by offset*npairs), while forces are unaffected.
suggested_fix: Fetch `offset` from m_params/params in compute_evdwl and subtract it, mirroring src/pair_morse.cpp:119.

summary: The per-atom self-energy term is tallied into the global energy with a 0.5 factor when newton_pair is off, whereas the CPU base adds the full value; with `neigh full` (which forces newton off) the /kk global vdW energy is exactly half the CPU value.
failure_scenario: `package kokkos neigh full` (or plain `newton off`) with `pair_style multi/lucy/rx linear 1000`: thermo `epair`/`evdwl` is half of what the non-kk run and the `neigh half`+`newton on` kk run report.
suggested_fix: Drop the NEWTON_PAIR conditional and always add the full `evdwl` (this term is a per-local-atom self energy, not a pair term), matching Pair::ev_tally(0,0,...) in both newton modes.

summary: The Gaussian-charge Coulomb correction is only evaluated when rsq < cut_coulsq (the pair_kokkos COUL_FLAG gate), whereas the CPU base evaluates it whenever rsq < cut_ljsq[i][j], so the correction is silently dropped for pairs with cut_coul <= r < cut_lj[i][j].
evidence: src/YAFF/pair_lj_switch3_coulgauss_long.cpp:160-177 computes forcecoul2/erfc2/prefactor2 inside `if (rsq < cut_ljsq[itype][jtype])` with NO cut_coulsq condition, and lines 189-190 add `ecoul += prefactor2*erfc2*factor_coul;` inside the same cut_ljsq test; line 208 `fpair = (forcecoul + factor_coul*forcecoul2 + factor_lj*forcelj) * r2inv;`. In the KOKKOS port the correction lives in compute_fcoul (src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_switch3_coulgauss_long_kokkos.cpp:226-232) and compute_ecoul (line 301-306), and src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:247-248 / 269-273 only call compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul when `rsq < d_cut_coulsq(itype,jtype)`. cut_lj[i][j] may legally exceed cut_coul: src/YAFF/pair_lj_switch3_coulgauss_long.cpp:363 `double cut = MAX(cut_lj[i][j],cut_coul+2.0*qdist);` and coeff() accepts a per-pair cut_lj (arg[5]).
failure_scenario: `pair_style lj/switch3/coulgauss/long 8.0 6.0 2.0` (cut_lj_global 8, cut_coul 6) or any pair_coeff with an explicit per-pair LJ cutoff larger than cut_coul: for pairs at 6.0 <= r < 8.0 the /kk variant omits the -qqrd2e*qi*qj*erfc(gamma*r)/r force and energy term that the CPU style adds, giving different forces and different Coulomb energy from the non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Move the Gaussian correction out of the cut_coulsq-gated compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul, e.g. evaluate it in compute_fpair/compute_evdwl (which are gated by cut_ljsq), or make d_cut_coulsq(i,j) = max(cut_coulsq, cut_ljsq[i][j]) while keeping the Ewald part internally gated by cut_coulsq.

summary: Same defect as the lj/switch3 sibling: the Gaussian-charge Coulomb correction sits inside compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul, which pair_kokkos only calls when rsq < cut_coulsq, while the CPU base applies it whenever rsq < cut_ljsq[i][j].
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_mm3_switch3_coulgauss_long_kokkos.cpp:228-234 (`if (rsq < cut_ljsq_val && lj2_val > 0.0) { ... forcecoul += factor_coul*prefactor2*(erfc2+EWALD_F*rrij*expn2); }`) and :305-310 for the energy, both reachable only through src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:247-248/269-273 which gate on `rsq < d_cut_coulsq(itype,jtype)`. The CPU base src/YAFF/pair_mm3_switch3_coulgauss_long.cpp computes forcecoul2/erfc2/prefactor2 inside `if (rsq < cut_ljsq[itype][jtype])` (lines 83-103 of compute()) with no cut_coulsq test, and adds `ecoul += prefactor2*erfc2*factor_coul;` under the same cut_ljsq test (line 116); fpair at line 133 is `(forcecoul + factor_coul*forcecoul2 + factor_lj*forcelj)*r2inv`. cut_lj[i][j] may exceed cut_coul (init_one: `double cut = MAX(cut_lj[i][j],cut_coul+2.0*qdist);`, and pair_coeff takes an optional per-pair LJ cutoff).
failure_scenario: `pair_style mm3/switch3/coulgauss/long 10.0 8.0 3.0` (cut_lj 10, cut_coul 8): pairs at 8 <= r < 10 lose the -qqrd2e*qi*qj*erfc(gamma*r)/r Gaussian correction in both force and Coulomb energy relative to the non-kk run.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the Gaussian correction in compute_fpair/compute_evdwl (which are gated by cut_ljsq), or set d_cut_coulsq(i,j)/m_cut_coulsq[i][j] to max(cut_coulsq, cut_ljsq[i][j]) and gate the Ewald part on cut_coulsq inside compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul.

summary: update_table is set only in the constructor, so a pair_coeff issued after the first run adds a table on the host that is never uploaded, leaving the device table arrays too small / stale.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp:68 `update_table = 1;` (constructor) is the only place the flag is raised, and :952 `update_table = 0;` at the end of create_kokkos_tables(); the coeff() override at :97-104 never sets it. The sibling table styles avoid this by overriding compute_table: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:508-512 `void PairTableKokkos<DeviceType>::compute_table(Table *tb) { update_table = 1; PairTable::compute_table(tb); }` (same in src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:1294-1298); PairMultiLucyRX::compute_table is non-virtual (src/DPD-REACT/pair_multi_lucy_rx.h:75) so the flag must be set in coeff() instead.
failure_scenario: A script that does `pair_coeff ... ; run 100 ; pair_coeff ... (second table) ; run 100`: ntables becomes 2 and tabindex points at index 1, but d_table_const.innersq/e/f still have extent 1 and d_table_const.tabindex still holds the old values, so the kernel reads out of bounds on the device.
suggested_fix: Set `update_table = 1;` in PairMultiLucyRXKokkos::coeff() after calling PairMultiLucyRX::coeff().

summary: pace/extrapolation/kk scales the pair forces with scale(itype,itype) while the CPU base scales them with scale[itype][jtype], so a non-uniform 'scale' (fix adapt) gives different forces on the KOKKOS path.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp:1429 (TagPairPACEComputeDerivative) 'const KK_FLOAT scale = d_scale(itype,itype);' and :1692-1694 'f_ij(ii, jj, 0) = scale * f_ji[0] + ...'. The CPU base src/ML-PACE/pair_pace_extrapolation.cpp:251-253 uses the OFF-DIAGONAL element: 'fij[0] = scale[itype][jtype] * neighbours_forces(jj, 0);' (only the energy at :276 uses scale[itype][itype]). scale is user-settable per type pair through extract() (src/ML-PACE/pair_pace_extrapolation.cpp:482) i.e. 'fix adapt ... pair pace/extrapolation scale I J v_x'.
failure_scenario: pair_style pace/extrapolation with 'fix adapt pair pace/extrapolation scale 1 2 v_s' and s != scale(1,1): the /kk forces between type-1 and type-2 atoms are scaled by scale(1,1) instead of scale(1,2), giving different (and non-conservative) forces than the non-KOKKOS run.
suggested_fix: In TagPairPACEComputeDerivative read the neighbor's LAMMPS type and use d_scale(itype,jtype) for f_ij, keeping d_scale(itype,itype) for the energy tally, matching the base class.

summary: nm/cut/coul/long/kk silently ignores the tabulated Coulomb path (ncoultablebits / pair_modify table), so it does not reproduce the CPU style's numbers; it is the only KOKKOS coul/long style lacking the CoulLongTable specialisation.
evidence: KOKKOS compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul (src/KOKKOS/pair_nm_cut_coul_long_kokkos.cpp:190-208, 243-260) always evaluate the erfc polynomial and never consult rtable/ftable/ctable/etable; compute() dispatches with Specialisation=void (line 124: 'ev = pair_compute<PairNMCutCoulLongKokkos<DeviceType>,void>'). The CPU base src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_nm_cut_coul_long.cpp:134-157 branches on 'if (!ncoultablebits || rsq <= tabinnersq)' and otherwise interpolates the tables, and init_style (same file, line 316) still calls init_tables(cut_coul,nullptr). Every other KOKKOS coul/long style (pair_lj_cut_coul_long_kokkos.cpp, pair_born_coul_long_kokkos.cpp, pair_coul_long_kokkos.cpp, ...) instantiates pair_compute<...,CoulLongTable<1>> and implements the table branch.
failure_scenario: Default settings (ncoultablebits=12): running the same input with 'pair_style nm/cut/coul/long' vs '.../kk' gives Coulomb forces/energies that differ by the table interpolation error (~1e-6 relative), and the tables allocated by init_tables() are dead memory.
suggested_fix: Add the CoulLongTable<1>/<0> specialisation branch to compute_fcoul/compute_ecoul and dispatch pair_compute with CoulLongTable<ncoultablebits?1:0> as in pair_lj_cut_coul_long_kokkos.cpp, or at minimum force ncoultablebits=0 in the KOKKOS init_style so CPU and GPU agree.

summary: d_num_ms_combs is allocated, only partially filled (rank-1 entries left uninitialized) and never read by any kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:647 allocates it, :699 fills it only for rank>1 functions ('h_num_ms_combs(mu, idx_func_through) = func->num_ms_combs;'), :724 deep-copies it; grep over pair_pace_kokkos.{cpp,h} shows no read other than memory_usage() at :3341. Identical dead array in pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp:333/394/426.
failure_scenario: No wrong results; wasted device memory and an uninitialized-mirror read if a future change starts using it.
suggested_fix: Drop d_num_ms_combs (and its mirror/deep_copy) from both PACE KOKKOS styles.

summary: The Accelerator Variants line for pair_style pedone lists the variants out of alphabetical order (*pedone/omp* before *pedone/kk*).
evidence: doc/src/pair_pedone.rst:8 'Accelerator Variants: *pedone/omp*, *pedone/kk*'. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md documentation checklist item 3 requires 'Add *<name>/kk* to the Accelerator Variants: line, ordered alphabetically'; doc/src/pair_nm.rst:17,22,27,32 do it correctly ('*nm/cut/kk*, *nm/cut/omp*').
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; inconsistent documentation ordering relative to every other accelerated style.
suggested_fix: Swap to 'Accelerator Variants: *pedone/kk*, *pedone/omp*'.

summary: The per-atom core-repulsion factor is written into corerep_factor[] indexed by the neighbor-list position (chunk_offset+i) instead of by the atom index d_ilist[chunk_offset+i], unlike the CPU base which indexes by the atom i.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:1223-1225: 'for (int i = 0; i < chunk_size; i++) corerep_factor[chunk_offset+i] = h_corerep(i);' while every kernel resolves the atom as 'const int i = d_ilist[ii + chunk_offset];' (e.g. compute_fs_one, line 2178). The CPU base src/ML-PACE/pair_pace.cpp:201-202 does 'i = list->ilist[ii]; ... corerep_factor[i] = 1 - aceimpl->ace->ace_fcut;'. Same pattern in src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp:811-821 for extrapolation_grade_gamma and corerep_factor.
failure_scenario: Whenever the KOKKOS neighbor list's ilist is not the identity permutation of 0..nlocal-1, 'compute pace/atom' (corerep factor / gamma grade) reports the values attached to the wrong atoms.
suggested_fix: Copy d_ilist to the host once per chunk and write corerep_factor[h_ilist(chunk_offset+i)] = h_corerep(i) (likewise for extrapolation_grade_gamma), matching the base class.

summary: The hard-core (core-repulsion) part of the pair force is added to f_ij without the 'scale' prefactor in both pace/kk and pace/extrapolation/kk, whereas the CPU base multiplies the complete neighbours_forces (which includes that term) by scale.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:2856-2859 'const KK_FLOAT fpair = dF_drho_core(ii) * dcr(ii,jj); f_ij(ii, jj, 0) = scale * f_ji[0] + fpair * r_hat[0];' (and the ZBL term at :2865-2867 'f_ij(ii, jj, 0) += dF_dfcut(ii) * r_hat[0];' is also unscaled); identical code at src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp:1691-1702. The CPU base src/ML-PACE/pair_pace.cpp:212-214 applies the factor to the whole per-neighbor force: 'fij[0] = scale[itype][itype] * aceimpl->ace->neighbours_forces(jj, 0);'.
failure_scenario: With 'fix adapt pair pace scale * * v_s' and s != 1 on a potential that has a hard-core repulsion / ZBL inner cutoff, the /kk run scales only the basis part of the force while the CPU run scales everything, so the two diverge and the /kk forces are inconsistent with the (fully scaled) energy.
suggested_fix: Multiply the core-repulsion and dF_dfcut contributions by 'scale' as well: f_ij = scale * (f_ji + fpair*r_hat [+ dF_dfcut*r_hat]).

summary: Integer division by zero (SIGFPE) in divideInterval() when a rank has no local atoms (list->inum == 0).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:254-256: 'nAtomBlocks = calculateNumberOfIntervals(inum, atomBlockSize); if (nAtomBlocks > 100) nAtomBlocks = 100; divideInterval(atomBlocks, inum, nAtomBlocks);'.  calculateNumberOfIntervals (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:475-483) returns 'M = N/intervalSize' = 0 for N==0 and does not bump it because 'N % intervalSize != 0' is false.  divideInterval (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:461-472) then executes 'int intervalSize = N / M;' and 'int remainder = N % M;' with M==0.  The CPU base never reaches this code: PairPOD::compute() uses the blockMode==0 branch (src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:187-233) and the block code (pair_pod.cpp:236-239) is dead.
failure_scenario: Any MPI rank whose subdomain momentarily contains no local atoms (dilute system, strong load imbalance, or simply more ranks than atoms) -> list->inum == 0 -> integer division by zero -> SIGFPE / undefined behavior at the first force evaluation.
suggested_fix: Return early from compute() when inum == 0 (after ev_init and the per-atom array setup), or clamp nAtomBlocks to at least 1 in calculateNumberOfIntervals().

summary: In the non-shielded vdW branch the derivative term is multiplied by rij instead of divided by it, giving a vdW force wrong by a factor r^2 for force fields with vdw_type == 2.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1256-1260 (analytic kernel, 'else' == no shielding): 'exp2 = exp(0.5*alpha*(1.0-rij/r_vdw)); exp1 = exp2*exp2; etmp = epsilon*(exp1-2.0*exp2); evdwl = Tap*etmp; fvdwl = dTap*etmp-Tap*epsilon*(alpha/r_vdw)*(exp1-exp2)*rij;'.  The CPU reference src/REAXFF/reaxff_nonbonded.cpp:164-165 has 'CEvd = dTap * e_vdW - Tap * twbp->D * (twbp->alpha / twbp->r_vdW) * (exp1 - exp2) / r_ij;' and the table generator inside this same KOKKOS file, PairReaxFFKokkos::LR_vdW_Coulomb (pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:669-670), also divides: 'lr->CEvd = dTap * twbp->D * (exp1 - 2.0 * exp2) - Tap * twbp->D * (twbp->alpha / twbp->r_vdW) * (exp1 - exp2) / r_ij;'.  Note dTap here is already dTap/dr divided by r (pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1228-1233 adds d_tap[1]/rij), so the second term must carry the same 1/r.
failure_scenario: Any ReaxFF force field whose ffield header sets vdW type 2 (inner wall, no shielding) run with pair_style reaxff/kk and control->tabulate == 0: the vdW force term is scaled by r^2 instead of 1/r (a factor r^2 at r~3 A is ~10x too large and of the wrong r-dependence), so trajectories, forces and pressure differ from pair_style reaxff; energies stay correct, which makes it hard to notice.
suggested_fix: Change '*rij' to '/rij' at pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1260 to match reaxff_nonbonded.cpp:165.
