summary: TagPairReaxZero unconditionally writes d_hb_num(n), but that view is only allocated when cut_hbsq > 0, so a run with hbond_cutoff 0 dereferences a null view.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1592-1599 'void PairReaxFFKokkos<DeviceType>::operator()(TagPairReaxZero, const int &n) const { d_total_bo(n) = 0; d_CdDelta(n) = 0; d_bo_num(n) = 0; d_hb_num(n) = 0; ... }' - no guard.  allocate_array() only creates it conditionally: ':1530-1533 if (cut_hbsq > 0.0) { MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_hb_num,"reaxff/kk:hb_num",nmax); MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_hb_list,...); }'.  Every other use is guarded (:1629, :1764, :1851, :1900, :3327 behind 'if (cut_hbsq > 0.0)' at :1024).  cut_hbsq is set from the control file at :360 'cut_hbsq = api->control->hbond_cut * api->control->hbond_cut;' and the CPU style explicitly supports hbond_cut == 0 (src/REAXFF/pair_reaxff.cpp:133, reaxff_forces.cpp:51, reaxff_init_md.cpp:56 all test 'if (control->hbond_cut > 0)').
failure_scenario: A control file containing 'hbond_cutoff 0.0' (the documented way to switch H-bonds off) with pair_style reaxff/kk -> d_hb_num is a default-constructed View whose data pointer is null -> segfault (host) or illegal memory access (GPU) in the very first TagPairReaxZero launch.
suggested_fix: Guard the write: 'if (cut_hbsq > 0.0) d_hb_num(n) = 0;' (or always allocate d_hb_num with size nmax).

summary: Only the two-body slice of the base-descriptor array bd is zeroed; the d3/d4/d33/d34/d44 slices are left stale when their Nij guards fail (the zeroing calls are commented out), whereas the CPU code zeroes all Ni*Mdesc entries.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:1415 'set_array_to_zero(d2, Ni*nl2);' is the only zeroing; :1436 '//set_array_to_zero(d3, Ni*nl3);' and :1445 '//set_array_to_zero(d4, Ni*nl4);' are commented out and there is no zeroing at all for d33/d34/d44.  The CPU counterpart starts with a full wipe: src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:1797 'for (int i=0; i<Ni*Mdesc; i++) bd1[i] = 0.0;' and EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 does the same (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1207 'for (int i=0; i<Mdesc; i++) bd[i] = 0.0;').
failure_scenario: A block whose total pair count drops to Nij<=1 (e.g. a 2-atom dimer stretched beyond rcut after a step where it was bonded): d3/d4/d33/d34/d44 keep the values written on the previous step/block and are multiplied by the POD coefficients in blockatom_base_coefficients -> wrong energy and forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Restore an unconditional 'set_array_to_zero(bd, Ni*Mdesc)' at the top of blockatom_base_descriptors().

summary: 'neighflag' is read in compute() but never initialized on host execution, because init_style() returns early before assigning it.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.h:50 declares 'int neighflag;' and the constructor (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:47-67) never initializes it.  init_style() (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:89-96) does 'if (host_flag) { ...; PairPOD::init_style(); return; }' and only the non-host path reaches ':101 neighflag = lmp->kokkos->neighflag;'.  compute() then reads it at :192 'if (neighflag == FULL) no_virial_fdotr_compute = 1;'.  host_flag is 1 for every CPU-only KOKKOS build (:66 'host_flag = (execution_space == HostKK);' with LMPDeviceType == LMPHostType) and for the pod/kk/host variant.  Contrast pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:774 where neighflag is assigned before any early return that can skip it.
failure_scenario: Serial/OpenMP KOKKOS build running 'pair_style pod/kk': the uninitialized int happens to hold 1 (FULL == 1, kokkos_type.h:27) -> no_virial_fdotr_compute is silently switched on mid-run, changing which virial path Pair::ev_setup selects; otherwise plain undefined behaviour flagged by sanitizers.
suggested_fix: Initialize neighflag in the constructor (e.g. 'neighflag = lmp->kokkos->neighflag;' or HALF) and/or set it before the host_flag early return in init_style().

summary: thb_cutsq is hardcoded to 1e-5 instead of taken from api->control->thb_cutsq, so the control-file keyword 'thb_cutoff_sq' is silently ignored by reaxff/kk.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:365-366 'thb_cut = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(api->control->thb_cut); thb_cutsq = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.000010); //thb_cut*thb_cut;'.  src/REAXFF/reaxff_control.cpp:101-102 reads it from the control file ('} else if (keyword == "thb_cutoff_sq") { control->thb_cutsq = values.next_double();') and the CPU kernel uses it: src/REAXFF/reaxff_valence_angles.cpp:222 '(bo_ij->BO * bo_jk->BO > control->thb_cutsq)'.  The KOKKOS angular screening uses the hardcoded value at pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2574 'if (bo_ij <= thb_cut || bo_ik <= thb_cut || bo_ij * bo_ik <= thb_cutsq) continue;'.
failure_scenario: A control file with a non-default 'thb_cutoff_sq' (e.g. 0.001 to speed up the valence-angle loop): pair_style reaxff uses it, pair_style reaxff/kk keeps 1e-5, so the two include different sets of valence angles and give different energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Set thb_cutsq = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(api->control->thb_cutsq); in setup().

summary: TagPairReaxFindBondSpecies writes d_tmpid/d_tmpbo before checking the MAXSPECBOND bound and keeps writing past the end of the row for every further bond, since the error is only reported after the whole kernel finishes.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4400-4407 'if (bo_tmp >= 0.10) { d_tmpid(i,nj) = j; d_tmpbo(i,nj) = bo_tmp; nj++; if (nj > MAXSPECBOND) k_error_flag.view<DeviceType>()() = 1; }' - the views are created with second extent MAXSPECBOND (:4350-4351 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_tmpid,tmpid,nmax,MAXSPECBOND,...)'), so index nj == MAXSPECBOND is already out of range and the guard fires only afterwards.  The error is not acted on until FindBondSpecies() returns (:4374-4375).  The CPU base has the same off-by-one (src/REAXFF/pair_reaxff.cpp:786-791) but calls error->all() immediately, so at most one element is overwritten there.
failure_scenario: With 'fix reaxff/species' on a structure where some atom has 25 or more bonds with BO >= 0.10 (MAXSPECBOND is 24, reaxff_defs.h:54): the kernel writes d_tmpid(i,24), d_tmpid(i,25), ... , silently corrupting the next atoms' rows (and running past the allocation for the last atom) before the run is finally aborted with 'Increase MAXSPECBOND'.
suggested_fix: Test the bound before writing: 'if (nj >= MAXSPECBOND) { k_error_flag...() = 1; break; } d_tmpid(i,nj) = j; ...'.

summary: The three-/four-body descriptor guards use the per-BLOCK pair count Nij instead of the per-ATOM neighbor count used by the reference EAPOD implementation, so atoms with 0/1/2 neighbours get non-zero 3-/4-body descriptors in pod/kk but zero in pair_style pod.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:1421 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nij>1))', :1443 'if ((nl4 > 0) && (Nij>2))', :1452/:1460/:1468 'Nij>3/4/5' - here Nij is the TOTAL number of (i,j) pairs of the whole atom block (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:274 'nij = NeighborCount(numij, rcutsq, gi1, ni);' over up to atomBlockSize=2048 atoms).  The reference used by pair_style pod is EAPOD::peratomenergyforce2 (src/ML-POD/eapod.cpp:1248-1284) where the identical guards 'if ((nl3 > 0) && (Nj>1))', 'if ((nl4 > 0) && (Nj>2))', 'Nj>3/4/5' use Nj = number of neighbours of the SINGLE atom i (called from src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:216 with the per-atom nij).
failure_scenario: An atom with exactly one neighbour inside rcut (gas-phase molecule, evaporated atom, dimer scan): pair_style pod leaves its d3 block zero, pod/kk computes d3 = sum pc3*sumU*sumU != 0 -> different energy and force for that atom.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the guards per atom (numij(i+1)-numij(i)) inside the kernels, or at minimum document/verify that the block-level guard reproduces EAPOD; the safest is to zero the descriptor of atoms with fewer neighbours than the guard requires.

summary: PairReaxFFKokkos::Init_Lookup_Tables() builds the spline tables for every LAMMPS type pair without checking map[i] == -1, so an unmapped (NULL) type indexes reax_param.tbp[-1]; Deallocate_Lookup_Tables() conversely skips those pairs and leaks their arrays.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:509-531 'for (i = 1; i <= num_atom_types; ++i) { for (j = i; j <= num_atom_types; ++j) { ... LR_vdW_Coulomb(i, j, r * dr, &(LR[i][j].y[r])); ...' - no 'if (map[i] == -1) continue;', while LR_vdW_Coulomb dereferences ':626 twbp = &(api->system->reax_param.tbp[map[i]][map[j]]);'.  Both the init_md() copy loop (:426-429 'if (map[i] == -1) continue;') and Deallocate_Lookup_Tables (:591 'if ((map[i] == -1) || (map[j] == -1)) continue;') do guard on map.  The CPU reference src/REAXFF/reaxff_lookup.cpp:195-198 restricts the loops to types actually present ('if (aggregated[i])') and sets LR[i][j].n = 0 otherwise (:255).
failure_scenario: 'pair_coeff * * ffield.reax NULL C H' (a NULL type, common with hybrid or with fixed/wall particles) plus 'tabulate' enabled in the control file -> tbp[-1][...] is read out of bounds inside LR_vdW_Coulomb -> garbage table values or a segfault; even without a crash the six spline arrays of every unmapped pair are never freed.
suggested_fix: Skip unmapped types in Init_Lookup_Tables (set LR[i][j].n = 0 for them) and drop the map[] guard from Deallocate_Lookup_Tables so that whatever was allocated is freed.

summary: PairPOD::~PairPOD() lacks the mandatory 'if (copymode) return;' guard required of every base class a KOKKOS style inherits from.
evidence: src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:107-159 starts directly with 'memory->destroy(rij);' - no copymode check - while PairPODKokkos sets copymode = 1 during compute (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:208) and its own destructor does have the guard (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:76).  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 1 requires the guard in the base-class destructor.
failure_scenario: Any future functor that captures the pair object by value (the standard KOKKOS pattern) would run ~PairPOD on the copy and free the original's memory -> double free / GPU crash.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (copymode) return;' as the first line of PairPOD::~PairPOD().

summary: Error message in pod/kk names the wrong pair style ('pair pace/kk'), copied from pair_pace_kokkos.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:107-108: 'if (neighflag == FULL) error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair pace/kk");' - identical text to pair_pace_kokkos.cpp:780-781 which legitimately refers to pace.
failure_scenario: A user running pod/kk with 'package kokkos neigh full' is told to fix a pace setting.
suggested_fix: Change the message to name pod/kk.

summary: Unconditional Kokkos::fence() plus std::chrono timestamps around every kernel, even though the timing output is never used (timing flag is always 0).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:63 'timing = 0;' and nothing ever sets it; comptime[] is accumulated at :277, :284, :291, :306, :1403, :1412, :1419, :1426, :1433, :1440, :1449, :1457, :1465, :1473, :1618, :1630, :1653, :1660 but never printed.  Each accumulation is preceded by an unconditional 'Kokkos::fence()' (:275, :282, :289, :304, :1401, :1410, :1417, :1424, :1431, :1438, :1447, :1455, :1463, :1471, :1617, :1628, :1651, :1658), which serialises the device queue ~18 times per atom block.
failure_scenario: Every timestep pays a full device fence per kernel; on a GPU this removes all kernel overlap and adds host-device round trips for no benefit.
suggested_fix: Guard the fences and chrono calls with 'if (timing)' (or delete the instrumentation).

summary: The host_flag branch allocates three fresh Kokkos views (d_numneigh, d_ilist, d_neighbors) on every single timestep instead of reusing them.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:221-229: 'd_numneigh = typename AT::t_int_1d("pair_pod:numneigh",inum); ... d_ilist = typename AT::t_int_1d("pair_pod:ilist",inum); ... MemoryKokkos::realloc_kokkos(d_neighbors,"neighlist:neighbors",inum,maxn);' inside compute().  Because host_flag is 1 for every CPU-only KOKKOS build, this is the default path there.
failure_scenario: Large CPU KOKKOS runs pay an inum*maxneigh allocation, zero-fill and copy of the whole neighbor list every step.
suggested_fix: Only (re)allocate when inum or maxn grows, as the rest of the style does with grow_atoms()/grow_pairs().

summary: Device kernels call the unqualified C library math functions instead of the Kokkos:: overloads required by the KOKKOS coding rules.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:632 'double dij = sqrt(...)', :643 'double y5 = sqrt(y4);', :644 'double y6 = exp(-1.0/y5);', :648/:651 'exp(-1.0)', :659-:672 'exp(-alpha...)', :678 'sqrt(2.0/(l_rmax))', :681/:689/:697 'sin(a*x0)', :684/:692/:700 'cos(...)', :754 'double dij = sqrt(xx + yy + zz);' - all inside KOKKOS_LAMBDA bodies.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::exp / Kokkos::sin / Kokkos::cos in device kernels.
failure_scenario: Portability: back ends that do not pull the C math functions into device scope (and future Kokkos versions) fail to compile or silently fall back to double precision.
suggested_fix: Prefix the calls with Kokkos::.

summary: k_scale/d_scale are allocated but never filled or read, and 'using MathSpecial::powint' is unused; k_cutsq is modified on the host but never synced (it is also never read on device).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:145-146 allocate k_scale/d_scale; grep shows no other use of d_scale in the file.  :120-121 set and modify_host() k_cutsq but there is no matching 'k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>()' and d_cutsq is never referenced in a kernel.  :40 'using MathSpecial::powint;' with no call site.
failure_scenario: No functional impact today, but the unsynced k_cutsq is a trap for anyone who later adds a device read of d_cutsq.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused scale views and powint using-declaration; if d_cutsq is kept, add the sync after modify_host().

summary: PairSNAPKokkosHost declares its virtual overrides without the 'override' specifier, unlike the sibling PairSNAPKokkosDevice.
evidence: pair_snap_kokkos.h:559-563 (Device) 'void coeff(int, char**) override; void init_style() override; double init_one(int, int) override; void compute(int, int) override; double memory_usage() override;' versus :578-582 (Host) 'void coeff(int, char**); void init_style(); double init_one(int, int); void compute(int, int); double memory_usage();'.
failure_scenario: If a Pair base-class signature ever changes, the Host wrapper silently stops overriding and the base implementation is called instead of the KOKKOS one - the compiler cannot warn without 'override'.
suggested_fix: Add 'override' to the five PairSNAPKokkosHost declarations.

summary: TagPairReaxBondOrder2 writes d_CdDelta[j] for its neighbours j, which is a redundant benign data race with the thread that owns atom j (and with the already-executed zeroing kernel).
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2205-2211 'd_Cdbo(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_Cdbopi(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_Cdbopi2(i,j_index) = 0.0; d_CdDelta[j] = 0.0; } d_CdDelta[i] = 0.0;' - d_CdDelta[j] belongs to another thread's atom.  d_CdDelta was already zeroed for all nmax entries by TagPairReaxZero (:1594 'd_CdDelta(n) = 0;') which runs earlier in compute() (:855).
failure_scenario: Both threads store 0.0 so the value is correct, but it is a concurrent unsynchronised write that thread sanitizers and Kokkos debug tooling flag, and it hides the fact that the write is dead.
suggested_fix: Delete the 'd_CdDelta[j] = 0.0;' (and the redundant 'd_CdDelta[i] = 0.0;') lines - TagPairReaxZero already covers them.

summary: v_tally3_atom() is dead code that would race if it were ever used, because it writes d_vatom directly instead of through the scatter/atomic view.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:4026-4050 defines PairReaxFFKokkos<DeviceType>::v_tally3_atom(...) with ':4047-4049 if (vflag_atom) { for (int n = 0; n < 6; n++) d_vatom(i,n) += v[n]; }' - a plain non-atomic read-modify-write, unlike v_tally/v_tally3/v_tally4 which all go through ScatterViewHelper (:3934-3935, :3952-3953, :4013-4014).  grep over the file shows no call site (the only occurrences are the declaration pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:437 and this definition).
failure_scenario: No effect today; if anyone wires it up, per-atom virials would be silently corrupted under HALFTHREAD/GPU.
suggested_fix: Remove v_tally3_atom (declaration and definition), or convert it to the ScatterView pattern and template it on NEIGHFLAG like the other tally helpers.

summary: Inner loop counters shadow the pack-decoded atom indices j and k in ComputeAngularPreprocessed, making the kernel very easy to break.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:2740-2741 'const int j = pack.i1; const int k = pack.i2;' then :2769 'for (int j = 0; j < 3; j++) fitmp[j] = 0.0;' and :2783 'for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) fjtmp[k] = 0.0;'.  The loop variables shadow the atom indices; the code is correct only because the uses at :2771-2773 and :2785-2787 are outside the loop scope.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers today, but any edit that moves a use of j or k inside one of those loops silently reads a component index instead of an atom index.
suggested_fix: Rename the loop counters (e.g. 'for (int d = 0; d < 3; d++)') as the rest of the kernel does.

summary: TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh is declared with an operator() but is never defined nor dispatched.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:52 'struct TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh{};' and :169-171 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator()(TagPairReaxComputeLJCoulombShortNeigh, const int&) const;'.  grep for 'ShortNeigh' over src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp returns no hits, so there is neither a definition nor a parallel_for using it.
failure_scenario: None - dead declaration only; it misleads readers into thinking a short-neighbor-list path exists.
suggested_fix: Delete the tag struct and the operator() declaration.

summary: The Kokkos neighbour screening drops the base class' 'rsq > 1e-20' guard, so a coincident pair produces a division by zero (NaN energies/forces).
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:553 'if (rsq < l_rcutsq) count++;' and :605 'if (rsq >= l_rcutsq) return;' versus src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:388 'if (rsq < rcutsq && rsq > 1e-20) {' (also pair_pod.cpp:416 and :451).  radialbasis then divides by dij (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:633-635 'dr1 = xij1/dij;') and angularbasis divides by dij3 (:760).
failure_scenario: Two atoms at identical coordinates (overlapping insertion, fix deposit failure, zero-temperature start from a bad structure) enter the pair list -> dij == 0 -> NaN propagates into all forces and energies instead of the pair being skipped as in the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Add the '&& rsq > 1e-20' condition to both the NeighborCount and NeighborList screening tests so the two styles select the same pairs.

summary: Fixed-size stack array 'double tm[10]' in the multi-element radialangularsum kernel overflows when the POD model has more than 10 elements.
evidence: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:849-858: 'double tm[10]; for (int j=0; j<l_nelements; j++) tm[j] = 0; ... tm[tn] += ...; for (int j=0; j<l_nelements; j++) l_sumU(j + kmi) = ...' with no bound on l_nelements.  (The CPU code has the same 'double sum[10]' at src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:995, and nothing in EAPOD limits nelements.)
failure_scenario: A POD potential fitted for 11 or more elements -> out-of-bounds stack writes inside a device kernel -> silent corruption or crash.
suggested_fix: Add an explicit check in coeff()/copy_from_pod_class() that nelements <= 10, or size the scratch from nelements via team scratch memory.

summary: snap_dispatch_fused_deidrj_all() sets the policy LaunchBounds from team_size_compute_fused_deidrj but launches with team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, so the compiler is told a larger maximum block size than is ever used.
evidence: pair_snap_kokkos.h:273 'SnapAoSoATeamPolicy<DeviceType, team_size_compute_fused_deidrj, TagPairSNAPComputeFusedDeidrjAll> policy_fused_deidrj_all(n_teams_div, team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, vector_length);' - the second template argument feeds LaunchBounds (:183-184 'Kokkos::LaunchBounds<vector_length * num_teams>') while the runtime team size is team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all, which is strictly smaller (e.g. 2 vs 4 for HIP, :107-108, and 2 vs 4 / 1 vs 2 for CUDA, :143-144).
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers, but the kernel is compiled for twice the block size it is launched with, so the register budget per thread (and hence occupancy/performance) is worse than intended.
suggested_fix: Use team_size_compute_fused_deidrj_all as the LaunchBounds template argument for this dispatch.

summary: compute() reuses a single EV_FLOAT_REAX 'ev' across all kernel dispatches and unconditionally does 'ev_all += ev' after each section, so a section that ran parallel_for (no reduction) adds the previous section's reduction result a second time.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:775 'EV_FLOAT_REAX ev; EV_FLOAT_REAX ev_all;' then :918-932 'if (eflag_either) parallel_reduce(...ComputeBond1<HALF,1>...,*this,ev); else parallel_for(...ComputeBond1<HALF,0>...,*this); ev_all += ev;' - in the else branch ev still holds the LJ/Coulomb reduction from :809-816.  The same shape appears at :941/:948 (Multi2, guarded by eflag_either), :992/:998, :1011/:1017, :1030/:1036 (guarded by evflag) and :1056/:1065 (Bond2, guarded by vflag_either).
failure_scenario: Benign today only because the custom ev_setup (:4100-4105) forces vflag_global = 0 for the VIRIAL_FDOTR path that reaxff always takes, so ev.v[] is never filled, and evdwl/ecoul are guarded by eflag_global which implies eflag_either.  Any future change that writes ev.evdwl/ev.ecoul/ev.v in ComputeHydrogen, ComputeTorsion or ComputeLJCoulomb outside those guards silently double counts the energy or virial.
suggested_fix: Reset ev (ev = EV_FLOAT_REAX();) before each section, or move 'ev_all += ev;' inside the reduction branch.

summary: The neighbor-index blocking buffer stores the neighbor index in an unsigned short, truncating for atoms with more than 65535 neighbours in the nonbonded list.
evidence: pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:118 'using blocking_t = unsigned short int;'; pair_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1633 'blocking_t selected_jj[blocksize];' and :1653 'selected_jj[nnz] = jj_current;' where jj_current runs to jnum-1 = d_numneigh[i]-1 (:1621).  Same at :1768/:1789.
failure_scenario: A very large nonb_cut or a pathologically dense system giving an atom >65535 entries in its half neighbor list: the stored index wraps and the wrong neighbor is used for the bond-order list, producing wrong bonds and forces with no diagnostic.
suggested_fix: Use int for selected_jj, or add a check that d_numneigh[i] fits in blocking_t.

summary: pair table/kk stores the special_lj weights into the inherited `int Pair::special_lj[4]`, truncating fractional special-bond factors (0.5 -> 0), so 1-2/1-3/1-4 pair interactions are silently dropped.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:124-127 `special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ... special_lj[3] = force->special_lj[3];`. PairTableKokkos (src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.h) declares NO special_lj member and src/pair_table.h has none either, so the name resolves to src/pair.h:247 `int special_lj[4];    // copied from force->special_lj for Kokkos` (force->special_lj is `double[4]`, src/force.h:116). Every other KOKKOS pair style shadows it with its own `KK_FLOAT special_lj[4]` (e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_soft_kokkos.h:89, src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.h:90). The functor then reads it: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:181 `evdwl = factor_lj * c.template compute_evdwl<...>` with `factor_lj = c.special_lj[j >> SBBITS & 3]`.
failure_scenario: `special_bonds lj 0.0 0.0 0.5` + `pair_style table/kk linear N`: force->special_lj[3]=0.5 is stored as int 0, so all 1-4 tabulated pair interactions get factor 0 instead of 0.5 -> wrong forces and energies, silently. The CPU pair_style table gives 0.5. Any non-integer weight (0.5, 0.8333, ...) is affected.
suggested_fix: Declare `KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];` as a member of PairTableKokkos (as every other KOKKOS pair style does), or change src/pair.h:247 to `double special_lj[4];`.

summary: On steps with eflag==0 && vflag==0, pair table/rx/kk writes uCG/uCGnew on the device but marks only F_MASK modified, so the device updates are silently discarded by the next host sync.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:670-671 `if (eflag || vflag) atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify); else atomKK->modified(execution_space,F_MASK);` while the kernel writes uCG/uCGnew unconditionally: lines 527-531 `uCG_i += 0.5*evdwlOld; if (do_half) uCG(j) += ...; uCGnew_i += 0.5*evdwl; ...` and lines 546-547 `uCG(i) += uCG_i; uCGnew(i) += uCGnew_i;` (no EVFLAG guard). The two sibling RX pair styles get it right: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:151-152 and src/KOKKOS/pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp:238-239 both keep `UCG_MASK | UCGNEW_MASK` in the `else` branch.
failure_scenario: A normal MD step (no thermo/dump output, eflag=vflag=0) with `pair_style table/rx/kk` + `fix eos/table/rx/kk`: the fix does `atomKK->sync(Host,UCG_MASK|UCGNEW_MASK)` (src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:290) which is a no-op because the dual view was never marked device-modified, then `modified(Host,...)` (line 292) and `sync(execution_space,...)` (line 294) copy the stale host values back over the device -> the pair style's uCG/uCGnew contributions are lost and the internal-energy/reaction integration is wrong on every non-output step.
suggested_fix: Change the else branch to `atomKK->modified(execution_space, F_MASK | UCG_MASK | UCGNEW_MASK);`, matching pair_exp6_rx_kokkos and pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.

summary: The special-bond LJ weights are stored in a `Few<int,4>`, truncating fractional special_bonds factors (0.5 -> 0) and dropping those pair interactions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:679-683 `Few<int, 4> special_lj_local; special_lj_local[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ... special_lj_local[3] = force->special_lj[3];` (force->special_lj is `double[4]`, src/force.h:116). The functor signature keeps the int type (line 425 `Few<int, 4> const& special_lj`, line 570) and line 477 reads it: `const KK_FLOAT factor_lj = special_lj[sbmask(j)];`. The CPU base uses the double array directly: src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:94 `double *special_lj = force->special_lj;` and line 144 `factor_lj = special_lj[sbmask(j)];`.
failure_scenario: `special_bonds lj 0.0 0.0 0.5` with `pair_style table/rx/kk`: 1-4 pairs get factor_lj = int(0.5) = 0 instead of 0.5, so those tabulated interactions (force, energy and the uCG/uCGnew contributions, all of which are multiplied by factor_lj) vanish. Silent wrong answer vs. the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Change `Few<int, 4>` to `Few<KK_FLOAT, 4>` (or `Few<double,4>`) in the local variable at line 679 and in the `compute_item`/`compute_all_items` signatures (lines 425, 570).

summary: pair snap/kk never strips the special-bond bits from the neighbor index (`j &= NEIGHMASK` is missing), so in a molecular system it dereferences out-of-range atom indices.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:554 `T_INT j = d_neighbors(i,jj);` then `x(j,0)`, `type(j)` (lines 555-559); again at 581 `T_INT j = d_neighbors(i,jj);` with `snaKK.inside(ii,offset) = j;` (line 591); and in the CPU path at 634 and 653. `grep -n NEIGHMASK src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h` returns nothing, while the CPU base does mask: src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:142-143 `j = jlist[jj]; j &= NEIGHMASK;` (also at 315-316), and sibling KOKKOS manybody styles do too (src/KOKKOS/pair_sw_kokkos.cpp:233-234, src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:350-351). The KOKKOS neighbor build really does set those bits: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:500 and :726 `neighbors_i(n++) = j ^ (which << SBBITS);` for `molecular != Atom::ATOMIC`.
failure_scenario: A molecular system (atom_style full/molecular) where Neighbor::init sets special_flag=2 - which src/neighbor.cpp:557-558 does for EVERY special weight as soon as a kspace_style is defined - run with `pair_style hybrid/overlay snap/kk ... coul/long/kk` : neighbor entries for 1-2/1-3/1-4 pairs carry the SBBITS, so snap/kk reads x/type at index j|(which<<30), i.e. far past the end of the per-atom views -> garbage rij/type, wrong forces or a segfault; the stored `snaKK.inside` index is then used for `a_f(j,*) -= fij[*]` (line 1382) writing out of bounds.
suggested_fix: Add `j &= NEIGHMASK;` immediately after every `d_neighbors(i,jj)` read in TagPairSNAPComputeNeigh and TagPairSNAPComputeNeighCPU (lines 554, 581, 634, 653).

summary: PairTableKokkos::settings() releases the cutsq/tabindex dual views but never frees the aliased legacy row-pointer arrays, leaking them and leaving `cutsq`/`tabindex` dangling and non-null.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:469-477 `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); d_table_const.tabindex = d_table->tabindex = typename AT::t_int_2d_lr(); h_table->tabindex = HAT::t_int_2d_lr(); d_table_const.cutsq = d_table->cutsq = typename AT::t_double_2d_lr(); h_table->cutsq = HAT::t_double_2d_lr(); }`. The arrays were made by `memoryKK->create_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,h_table->cutsq,cutsq,nt,nt,...)` (line 420), which `smalloc`s an `n1`-entry row-pointer array (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:186-196) that only `destroy_kokkos(TYPE&, value_type**&)` (memory_kokkos.h:297-306) frees and nulls. The CPU base does it properly: src/pair_table.cpp settings() `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); memory->destroy(cutsq); memory->destroy(tabindex); }`.
failure_scenario: Repeated `pair_style table/kk ...` commands in one input leak the row-pointer arrays each time and leave `cutsq`/`tabindex` pointing at freed view memory; any read of `cutsq[i][j]` before the next `allocate()` is use-after-free.
suggested_fix: Replace the manual view resets with `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,cutsq);` and `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->tabindex,tabindex);` (then also reset the host mirrors), matching the destructor at lines 62-63.

summary: PairTableRXKokkos::settings() releases the cutsq/tabindex dual views without freeing the aliased legacy row-pointer arrays, leaking them and leaving `cutsq`/`tabindex` dangling.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:1038-1047 `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); d_table_const.tabindex = d_table->tabindex = typename ArrayTypes<DeviceType>::t_int_2d_lr(); h_table->tabindex = ...; d_table_const.cutsq = d_table->cutsq = ...; h_table->cutsq = ...; allocated = 0; }`. Those arrays came from `memoryKK->create_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,h_table->cutsq,cutsq,nt,nt,...)` (line 985), which smallocs an nt-entry row-pointer array (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:186-196) freed only by `destroy_kokkos(TYPE&, value_type**&)`. The CPU base frees them: src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:286-290 `memory->destroy(setflag); memory->destroy(cutsq); memory->destroy(tabindex);`.
failure_scenario: Repeated `pair_style table/rx/kk ...` commands leak the row-pointer arrays and leave `cutsq`/`tabindex` non-null but pointing into released view memory.
suggested_fix: Use `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,cutsq);` and `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->tabindex,tabindex);` instead of the manual view resets.

summary: The fused ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij() (the only bij derivative actually used by tersoff/kk) still contains the pre-2022 buggy extra 0.5 factor in the second term, so the bond-order prefactor differs from the CPU style and from the file's own unfused ters_dbij().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:836-838 `prefactor = param.beta * (factor * (1.0 - 0.5*(1.0 + 0.5/(prm_ijk_pn)) * tmp_pow_neg_prm_ijk_pn));` versus the corrected unfused version in the same file, lines 802-807: `return param.beta * (factor * /* error in negligible 2nd term fixed 2/21/2022 */ /* (1.0 - 0.5*(1.0 + 1.0/(2.0*param.powern)) * */ (1.0 - (1.0 + 0.5/(param.powern)) * Kokkos::pow(tmp,-param.powern)));` and the CPU base src/MANYBODY/pair_tersoff.cpp ters_bij_d(): `return param->beta * (-0.5*pow(tmp,-1.5) * (1.0 - (1.0 + 1.0/(2.0*param->powern)) * pow(tmp,-param->powern)));`. Line 436 `ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij(d_params(iparam_ij),bo_ij,bij,prefactor);` is the call site; ters_dbij()/ters_bij_k() are dead code in this file. The sibling KOKKOS styles use the correct unfused form (pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:484, pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:441, pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp:446).
failure_scenario: Any tersoff/kk configuration where beta*zeta falls in the (c2, c1] branch (roughly 2*n*1e-16 < (beta*zeta)^-n < 2*n*1e-8) gets a three-body prefactor that is wrong by ~half of the correction term (~1e-8 relative), so tersoff/kk forces do not match pair_style tersoff bit-for-bit in that branch.
suggested_fix: Drop the extra `0.5*` so the fused branch reads `(1.0 - (1.0 + 0.5/prm_ijk_pn) * tmp_pow_neg_prm_ijk_pn)`, matching ters_dbij() and the CPU base.

summary: TagPairSNAPPreUi looks up the atom type with the chunk-relative index instead of the real atom index, so with chunking (inum > chunksize) it initializes ulisttot with the wrong element for chem-SNAP potentials.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:711-718 `const int iatom = iatom_mod + iatom_div * vector_length; if (iatom >= chunk_size) return; int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);` (same in the two other PreUi overloads, lines 724-731 and 736-744). Every other kernel in the same file converts first: e.g. line 534 `const int i = d_ilist[ii + chunk_offset];`, lines 986-988, 999-1001, 1012-1014, 1035-1037, 1048-1050, 1061-1063, 1365. `chunk_offset` is advanced by `chunk_offset += chunk_size;` (line 388) inside the chunking loop (line 191), and the KOKKOS neighbor build sets `d_ilist(i) = i` (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:593 etc.), so `type(iatom)` is the type of atom `iatom` rather than of atom `iatom + chunk_offset`. `ielem` selects the diagonal element block in SNAKokkos::pre_ui (src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h: `if (ma == mb && (!chem_flag || ielem == jelem || wselfall_flag)) { re_part = wself; }`).
failure_scenario: A chemflag SNAP potential (`chemflag 1`, wselfall off) with more than `chunksize` (default 32768, src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:636) local atoms per MPI rank: for every chunk after the first, `wself` is placed in the element block of the wrong atom, giving wrong bispectrum components, energies and forces. Silent - results simply differ from pair_style snap and from a smaller-chunksize run.
suggested_fix: In all three TagPairSNAPPreUi overloads, replace `type(iatom)` with `type(d_ilist[iatom + chunk_offset])`, matching TagPairSNAPComputeBetaLinear.

summary: pair sw/kk ignores the `threebody off` setting and always executes the O(jnum^2) three-body loop (results stay correct only because read_file zeroes lambda).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_sw_kokkos.cpp:418-422 `// there is no support for skipping threebody loops (yet) / bool tmp_threebody = skip_threebody_flag; skip_threebody_flag = false; PairSW::init_style(); skip_threebody_flag = tmp_threebody;` and compute() (lines 322-370) runs the jj/kk loop unconditionally, whereas src/MANYBODY/pair_sw.cpp:170-174 sets `jnumm1 = 0` when skip_threebody_flag. Numbers remain right only because src/MANYBODY/pair_sw.cpp:439 `if (skip_threebody_flag) params[nparams].lambda = 0;`.
failure_scenario: `pair_style sw/kk threebody off` runs the full three-body double loop with lambda=0, so sw/kk is several times slower than the CPU style for the same (two-body only) result.
suggested_fix: Guard the three-body loop with `if (!skip_threebody_flag)` (pass the flag into the functor), or at least skip the jj/kk loop when all lambda are zero.

summary: getMixingWeights asserts `isite1 >= 0` / `isite2 >= 0`, which is false for the legal `1fluid` setting (OneFluidValue == -1), so debug builds abort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:90-93 `assert(isite1 >= 0); assert(isite1 < nspecies); assert(isite2 >= 0); assert(isite2 < nspecies);` but line 50 `#define OneFluidValue (-1)` and lines 94/103/113 explicitly handle `isOneFluid(isite1)`; isite1/isite2 are set to OneFluidValue at lines 1161/1171 when the pair_coeff site name is "1fluid". The CPU base (src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:504-593) has no such assertion.
failure_scenario: `pair_coeff 1 1 table file.table ENTRY 1fluid 1fluid` in a build without NDEBUG (any Debug/RelWithDebInfo-without-NDEBUG build, host or CUDA) aborts inside the kernel at the first timestep.
suggested_fix: Drop the two lower-bound asserts, or relax them to `assert(isOneFluid(isite1) || (isite1 >= 0 && isite1 < nspecies));`.

summary: Dead device helpers left behind after the fusing rewrite: ters_bij_k, ters_dbij, ters_fa_k, ters_dfa, ters_dthbj, ters_dthbk and v_tally3_atom are never called.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp defines ters_bij_k (780), ters_dbij (797), ters_fa_k (737), ters_dfa (749), ters_dthbj (938), ters_dthbk (1001), v_tally3_atom (1162); grep for call sites in the file yields only the fused `ters_fa_k_and_ters_dfa` (435), `ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij` (436) and `ters_fc_k_and_ters_dfc` (507). They are exactly the copies that drifted out of sync with the fused versions (see the ters_dbij finding).
failure_scenario: No runtime effect, but the duplicated formulas are what let the fused/unfused divergence go unnoticed.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused helpers (or make the fused versions call them) so there is a single copy of each formula.

summary: Error message names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk") in the tersoff/mod/c/kk (and mod, zbl) variants.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp:120-121 `if (neighflag == FULL) error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` - identical copy-pasted text in pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:121 and pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:134.
failure_scenario: A user running `pair_style tersoff/mod/c/kk` with `package kokkos neigh full` is told to fix `pair tersoff/kk`, a style that is not in their input.
suggested_fix: Use the real style name in each variant's message (tersoff/mod/c/kk, tersoff/mod/kk, tersoff/zbl/kk).

summary: Global vdW energy is accumulated under `if (eflag)` rather than `if (eflag_global)`, so eng_vdwl is polluted on steps that request only per-atom energy.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:177 `if (eflag) eng_vdwl += static_cast<double>(ev.evdwl);` while line 178 correctly uses `if (vflag_global)`. src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:180-183 accumulates `ev.evdwl` whenever `c.eflag_either` is set (i.e. also for eflag==2/atom-only), and Pair::ev_setup only zeroes eng_vdwl when eflag_global is set.
failure_scenario: A step where only `compute pe/atom` is invoked (eflag==2, eflag_global==0) adds the full pair energy into eng_vdwl without ever resetting it; any consumer reading Pair::eng_vdwl before the next eflag_global step sees a doubled/stale value.
suggested_fix: Use `if (eflag_global) eng_vdwl += ...` as the other 59 KOKKOS pair styles do.

summary: Global vdW energy is accumulated under `if (eflag)` rather than `if (eflag_global)`, polluting eng_vdwl on per-atom-energy-only steps.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:810 `if (eflag) eng_vdwl += static_cast<double>(ev.evdwl);` while line 811 uses `if (vflag_global)`. `ev.evdwl` is accumulated unconditionally in the kernel (line 534) and Pair::ev_setup only zeroes eng_vdwl when eflag_global is set.
failure_scenario: A step where only `compute pe/atom` runs (eflag==2, eflag_global==0) adds the whole pair energy into eng_vdwl without a reset.
suggested_fix: Use `if (eflag_global) eng_vdwl += ...`.

summary: The neighbor screening drops the CPU base's `rsq > 1e-20` guard, so a neighbor exactly on top of atom i enters the SNAP kernels with r == 0.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:562 `if (rsq >= rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype)) { jtype = -1; }` and line 642/662 `if (rsq < rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype))`, versus src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:151 `if (rsq < cutsq[itype][jtype]&&rsq>1e-20) {`. The same guard is present in every CPU ML-SNAP style (compute_sna_atom.cpp:417, compute_snad_atom.cpp:318, compute_snap.cpp:400, compute_snav_atom.cpp:314, pair_snap.cpp:324).
failure_scenario: Two coincident atoms (or a self-image in a box smaller than the cutoff) yield r = 0; the CPU style skips the pair, snap/kk divides by zero in compute_cayley_klein / compute_ui and produces NaN forces for the whole configuration.
suggested_fix: Add the `&& rsq > 1e-20` condition to the cutoff test in both TagPairSNAPComputeNeigh and TagPairSNAPComputeNeighCPU.

summary: PairUF3Kokkos::single() gates on `r < d_cutsq(itype,jtype)`, comparing a distance against a SQUARED cutoff, and runs the knot search before the gate, so calls with r past the cutoff walk off the end of d_n2b_knot and evaluate the spline with a bogus index.
failure_scenario: `pair_style uf3 2` (single_enable stays 1, see src/ML-UF3/pair_uf3.cpp:122-125) plus `pair_write 1 1 500 r 0.5 8.0 out.txt`: for every r >= cut the while-loop indexes d_n2b_knot past its last knot (extent max_num_knots_2b), reading out of bounds and/or looping until it happens to find a larger value, then constants_2b(...) is read at that bogus start_index; uf3/kk returns garbage (or crashes) where plain uf3 returns 0.
suggested_fix: Move the knot search inside the guard and compare rsq against d_cutsq (or r against cut[itype][jtype]), exactly as PairUF3::single does.

summary: TagPairVashishtaComputeFullB indexes the short 3-body neighbor list with the loop counter `jj` (a slot index inside i's own list) instead of the neighbor atom id `j`, so the kernel walks the neighbor list of an unrelated atom when adding the leg force on i.
failure_scenario: `pair_style vashishta/kk` with `-pk kokkos neigh full` (the default on a GPU build): FullA supplies only the centre-atom part of each 3-body term and FullB is supposed to add the leg force on i from triplets centred on its neighbours j. With the wrong index, FullB evaluates threebody() for triplets (j; i, k) where k comes from an unrelated atom's list, so rsq2 = |x(k)-x(j)|^2 is arbitrary; the resulting forces are wrong and non-conservative (and can be enormous when |x(k)-x(j)| happens to fall just outside r0, where exp(gamma/(r-r0)) blows up).
suggested_fix: Use `d_numneigh_short_3body[j]` and `d_neighbors_short_3body(j,kk)`. Note the same code is present in stanmoore1/lammps develop, so this looks like a latent upstream defect (the FULL path is not exercised by the CPU-only CI, which runs neighflag=HALF).

summary: PairYLZKokkos reads the ellipsoid bonus (quaternion) array on device but leaves BONUS_MASK out of datamask_read, so atomKK->sync() never brings k_bonus to the device and stale quaternions are used.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_ylz_kokkos.cpp:52 `datamask_read = X_MASK | F_MASK | TORQUE_MASK | TYPE_MASK | ELLIPSOID_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK;` (no BONUS_MASK), line 95 `atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read);`, line 106 `bonus = avecKK->k_bonus.view<DeviceType>();` and the kernel dereferences `bonus(ibnum).quat` at lines 228 and 269. src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:908/921 shows k_bonus is only synced when `mask & BONUS_MASK`. Every other KOKKOS style that reads bonus data includes it: compute_erotate_asphere_kokkos.cpp:35 `datamask_read = ... | ELLIPSOID_MASK | BONUS_MASK;`, fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:618 `atomKK->sync(execution_space,BONUS_MASK|TORQUE_MASK|ANGMOM_MASK|ELLIPSOID_MASK);`, fix_nve_asphere_kokkos.cpp:64/84.
failure_scenario: GPU build: any host-side update of the bonus array marks it host-modified without a matching device sync -- e.g. AtomVecEllipsoidKokkos::unpack_border_bonus / unpack_comm_bonus (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:307/364/440 `atomKK->modified(HostKK,datamask_bonus);`) when comm runs on the host, or a non-KOKKOS asphere integrator. pair ylz/kk then evaluates quat_to_mat() on stale (or never-uploaded) ghost quaternions and returns wrong forces and torques with no error. Invisible on CPU-only builds where host and device share memory.
suggested_fix: Add BONUS_MASK to datamask_read in the PairYLZKokkos constructor (and to datamask_modify only if the style ever wrote bonus data, which it does not).

summary: The KOKKOS M-site pre-kernel drops the CPU styles' check that the two atoms found by tag+1/tag+2 really are of type typeH, so a mis-ordered water topology silently produces wrong M sites instead of an error.
failure_scenario: A data file where an O atom's tag+1 / tag+2 are not its two H atoms (e.g. water mixed with other molecules, or ions numbered between the water atoms): tip4p/cut and tip4p/long abort with a clear error, tip4p/cut/kk and tip4p/long/kk build M sites from the wrong atoms and silently return wrong forces and energies.
suggested_fix: In the TagPairTIP4PNewsite kernel, also set d_hneigh(i,0) = -1 (or a separate error flag) when type(iH1) != m_typeH || type(iH2) != m_typeH, and report the distinct 'incorrect atom type' error from finalize().

summary: PairUF3Kokkos::single() does not scale the returned force by factor_lj, so special-bond scaled pairs get an unscaled force while the energy is scaled.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:1648 `fforce = static_cast<double>(dnconstants_2b(interaction_id, start_index - 1, 0));` ... line 1659 `return factor_lj * value;` -- the CPU base src/ML-UF3/pair_uf3.cpp:1857 does `fforce = factor_lj * force_2b;` before `return factor_lj * value;` (line 1878).
failure_scenario: Any caller of single() with factor_lj != 1 (special_bonds scaling, e.g. `compute group/group` style callers or a tabulation over bonded pairs) gets fforce too large by 1/factor_lj from uf3/kk while plain uf3 returns the scaled value.
suggested_fix: Multiply the accumulated fforce by factor_lj, matching PairUF3::single.

summary: In TagPairVashishtaComputeFullB the cheap threebodyj() variant is chosen on vflag_atom alone, so when eflag_atom is on but vflag_atom is off the three-body energy is never computed and ev_tally3_atom() adds a hard zero to d_eatom.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pair_vashishta_kokkos.cpp:480 `KK_FLOAT evdwl = 0.0;` ... 525-530 `if (vflag_atom)
          threebody(d_params[jiparam],...,eflag,evdwl);
        else
          threebodyj(d_params[jiparam],...,fj);` (threebodyj, line 744, has no eng argument and never writes evdwl) ... 536-537 `if (EVFLAG)
          if (vflag_atom || eflag_atom) ev_tally3_atom(ev,i,evdwl,0.0,fj,fk,delr1,delr2);`, and ev_tally3_atom (line 953) does `epairthird = THIRD*(evdwl+ecoul); d_eatom[i] += epairthird;`. In the FULL path ev_tally3 only credits the centre atom (`if (NEIGHFLAG != FULL)` guards j and k at lines 892-895), so the two leg thirds must come from FullB.
failure_scenario: `pair_style vashishta/kk` + `-pk kokkos neigh full` + `compute pe/atom` without any per-atom stress: every atom gets only the 1/3 of each three-body energy for triplets it centres, losing the 2/3 it should receive as a leg; the per-atom energies no longer sum to the (correct) global eng_vdwl.
suggested_fix: Select threebody() when `vflag_atom || eflag_atom` (and keep threebodyj() only for the no-tally case), or give threebodyj an energy output.

summary: All UF3 spline coefficient/knot views are hardcoded to LMPDeviceType instead of the class's DeviceType template parameter, yet they are read from KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION kernels that are instantiated for LMPHostType as well (uf3/kk/host).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.h:88-108 declares e.g. `Kokkos::View<KK_FLOAT **, LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> d_coefficients_2b;`, `Kokkos::View<int **, LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> map2b;`, `Kokkos::View<KK_FLOAT **[16], LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> constants_2b;` (and 10 more). These are read in the device kernels: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:560 `int interaction_id = map2b(itype, jtype);` and 562/573 inside `twobody()`, and 619/636/647 inside `threebody()`, which run under `Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType,...>` (lines 796/800). src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:1664-1666 explicitly instantiates `PairUF3Kokkos<LMPHostType>` under LMP_KOKKOS_GPU. This is the same defect class the KOKKOS rules describe for `DAT::` per-atom views (.github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 3).
failure_scenario: On a CUDA/HIP build, `pair_style uf3/kk/host` (or `-k on ... -sf kk` with the host back end selected) runs the kernels on the host while these views live in device memory: Kokkos' memory-space access check aborts at the first `map2b(itype,jtype)`. On a CPU-only build both spaces coincide, so the defect is invisible.
suggested_fix: Change the memory space of these views (and d_cut_3b_list) from LMPDeviceType to the class template parameter DeviceType, as the neighbor-short views at lines 179-180 already do.

summary: Error message in PairTersoffMODKokkos::init_style names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk" instead of tersoff/mod/kk), a copy-paste leftover from pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:120-121 `if (neighflag == FULL)\n    error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` -- identical string to src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:134-135.
failure_scenario: User runs `pair_style tersoff/mod/kk` with `-pk kokkos neigh full`; the error names a style they are not using, sending them to the wrong input line.
suggested_fix: Change the string to name tersoff/mod/kk (and check the same copy in pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp / pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp).

summary: Device kernel calls the host math function pow() unqualified instead of Kokkos::pow(), violating KOKKOS rule 4 (all other math in the same block uses Kokkos::).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:406-407 `const KK_FLOAT a_ij = (static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.8854)*global_a_0) /\n        static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(pow(d_params(iparam_ij).Z_i,0.23) + pow(d_params(iparam_ij).Z_j,0.23));` inside KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION tersoff_zbl_compute; contrast line 405 `Kokkos::pow(global_e,...)` and lines 411-416 which all use Kokkos::exp. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos:: math in device kernels.
failure_scenario: Compiling tersoff/zbl/kk for a backend whose device math library does not provide an unqualified ::pow overload (SYCL/HIP variants) fails to compile or silently falls back to the host implementation.
suggested_fix: Replace both calls with Kokkos::pow(...); better still, precompute a_ij and premult once per param in setup_params instead of per pair.

summary: Error message in PairTersoffZBLKokkos::init_style names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk" instead of tersoff/zbl/kk).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:133-134 `if (neighflag == FULL)\n    error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` -- copy-paste from src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:134-135.
failure_scenario: User runs pair_style tersoff/zbl/kk with `-pk kokkos neigh full` and gets an error naming a style not in the input.
suggested_fix: Name the actual style in the message.

summary: The KOKKOS ylz kernel silently skips atoms that are not ellipsoids, dropping the CPU style's "All atoms for pair style ylz must be ellipsoids" error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_ylz_kokkos.cpp:219-220 `const int ibnum = d_ellipsoid(i);\n  if (ibnum < 0) return;   // skip non-ellipsoid atoms` and 247-248 `const int jbnum = d_ellipsoid(j);\n    if (jbnum < 0) continue;`. The CPU base counts these (src/ASPHERE/pair_ylz.cpp:124-127 and 150-153 `++flag; continue;`) and aborts after the loop (lines 202-204 `MPI_Allreduce(&flag,&flag_all,...); if (flag_all) error->all(FLERR, "All atoms for pair style ylz must be ellipsoids");`).
failure_scenario: A system mixing point particles and ellipsoids: pair_style ylz errors out and tells the user what is wrong; pair_style ylz/kk silently omits every interaction involving a point particle and reports plausible-looking but wrong energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Set a device flag when a non-ellipsoid atom is skipped, MPI_Allreduce it after the kernel and raise the same error message.

summary: `kokkosable = 1;` is commented out in the PairUF3Kokkos constructor, so VerletKokkos treats uf3/kk as a non-KOKKOS pair style and turns on auto_sync for the whole pair compute.
failure_scenario: Every uf3/kk step forces a full host/device round trip of x/f/energy/virial through auto_sync, negating the point of the port; also src/force.cpp:208's kokkosable sanity check is bypassed.
suggested_fix: Uncomment `kokkosable = 1;` (and verify the style really keeps its data device-resident) or document why it must stay off.

summary: Local `eng` is left uninitialized when eflag==0 but is still passed to ev_tally() when only vflag_either is set.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:422-440: `KK_FLOAT frep, eng;` ... `if (eflag)\n      eng = (1.0 - fermi_k(...)) * eng_z + fermi_k(...) * eng_t;` ... `if (vflag_either || eflag_atom) this->template ev_tally<NEIGHFLAG>(ev,i,j,eng,frep,delx,dely,delz);`. The equivalent code in pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:386 computes `eng` unconditionally.
failure_scenario: `compute pressure` without any energy output: EVFLAG=1, eflag=0, vflag_global=1 -> ev_tally is called with an indeterminate `eng`. ev_tally only reads epair under `if (eflag_atom)` (which implies eflag), so no wrong numbers today, but the read of an indeterminate value is fragile and warns under -Wmaybe-uninitialized.
suggested_fix: Initialize `KK_FLOAT eng = 0.0;` (or compute it unconditionally as tersoff/mod does).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly)
summary: map_one() sets the hash dual view's modified_host flag, and the next device-side map_clear()/map_set_device() calls modify_device() while that flag is still set, which dual_hash_type turns into an unconditional Kokkos::abort("Concurrent modification of host and device hashes").
evidence: atom_map_kokkos.cpp:396-404 map_one hash branch: sync_host(); insert; k_map_hash.modify_host(). atom_map_kokkos.cpp:139-147 map_clear hash branch with atom_map_legacy==0: view_device().clear(); k_map_hash.modify_device(). atom_map_kokkos.cpp:54-66 map_init(check=0) with !recreate and atom_map_legacy==0 calls map_clear(). atom_map_kokkos.cpp:272 map_set_device ends with k_map_hash.modify_device(). kokkos_type.h:650-662 modify_device()/modify_host() abort when both flags are set; only sync_host()/sync_device() clear a flag. kokkos.cpp:355 sets atom_map_legacy = 0 whenever ngpus > 0. special.cpp:658-746 does map_clear(); map_one() x N; map_init(0); map_set().
failure_scenario: GPU run (default package kokkos atom/map device) with atom_modify map hash (or auto-selected hash for > 1M tags) on any molecular system: Special::build() -> map_clear [modify_device] -> map_one [sync_host clears device flag, sets host flag] -> map_init(0) [hash not grown -> map_clear -> modify_device with host flag set] -> abort. Same sequence in FixShake rendezvous and in Special::onefive_build/fix_bond_create paths.
suggested_fix: In the device branches of map_clear() and map_set_device(), release the host state before claiming the device (e.g. add a clear_sync_state()/reset to dual_hash_type, or call sync_device() first), mirroring k_map_array.clear_sync_state() at line 131.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly)
summary: Every non-KOKKOS compute keeps Compute's default datamask_modify = ALL_MASK (compute.cpp:98), so each setup() marks every per-atom array host-modified and forces a full host->device upload on the next device consumer even though Compute::setup() is read-only for essentially all computes.
evidence: modify_kokkos.cpp:60-67; compute.cpp:97-98 datamask_read = datamask_modify = ALL_MASK; compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.cpp:41-47 documents the same cost (issue #5080) and works around it only for that one compute.
failure_scenario: Any -k on g 1 run with one plain (non-/kk) compute defined: at every run setup, one extra full transform+upload of x/v/f/tag/type/mask/image/... after the setup loop. Correct results, wasted transfer.
suggested_fix: For !kokkosable computes, sync for datamask_read but skip the modified() claim (or claim EMPTY_MASK), matching what setup() actually writes.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by rules_D)
summary: NPair style halffull/newton/tri/trim/skip/kk/device is registered with the orthogonal class NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTrimDevice (TRI=0) although its mask carries NP_TRI and the triclinic alias NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimDevice declared on line 219 is left unused.
evidence: npair_halffull_kokkos.h:219-223 vs the host sibling at 225-229 (which correctly uses NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimHost) and the non-skip triclinic entry at 207-211. npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:112-129 uses TRI to select the delta-based comparison that is required for triclinic ghost coordinates.
failure_scenario: Triclinic box, newton on, a pair style needing a trimmed half-from-full list plus a skip list (e.g. pair hybrid sub-style) on a GPU: exact-coordinate tie-breaking on epsilon-shifted ghost coordinates double-counts or drops pairs -> wrong forces/energies.
suggested_fix: Use NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimDevice on line 221. Also rename the mislabeled orthogonal ghost entry at line 262 (halffull/newton/tri/trim/ghost/kk/device -> halffull/newton/trim/ghost/kk/device), which duplicates the key of the real triclinic entry at 288 (cosmetic: selection is by mask).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 06)
summary: map_set_device() reallocates k_sametag BEFORE the map_init(0) call that can invoke map_delete() and destroy it, so with MAP_HASH a hash regrow leaves the kernel writing sametag into a destroyed zero-extent view; the comment in the code even says the reallocation must come after map_init().
evidence: atom_map_kokkos.cpp:173-192 (sametag realloc at 178-182, then 'possible reallocation of sametag must come after map_init()' comment and map_init(0) at 184-192). CPU src/atom_map.cpp does map_init(0) first, then the sametag realloc. map_set_host() (atom_map_kokkos.cpp:290-294 region) has the correct order.
failure_scenario: Device atom map + hash map: when nlocal+nghost on a rank grows past map_nhash, map_init(0) recreates the map via map_delete() (destroys k_sametag, max_same=0); the subsequent parallel_for writes d_sametag(i) into a zero-extent view -> out-of-bounds device write / bounds-check abort, and sametag stays nullptr for later host users.
suggested_fix: Move the 'if (nall > max_same) {...}' block below the MAP_HASH map_init(0) block, as in src/atom_map.cpp and map_set_host().

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 06)
summary: CommTiledKokkos::forward_comm_device(): in the generic (non x-only, non ghost-velocity) branch the sendself case packs the self buffer but never unpacks it, so ghost atoms a rank sends to itself never receive forward-communicated data.
evidence: comm_tiled_kokkos.cpp:233-237 'if (sendself[iswap]) { ...; n = atomKK->avecKK->pack_comm_kokkos(...); }' with no unpack; the ghost_velocity branch at 195-200 does pack_comm_vel_kokkos followed by unpack_comm_vel_kokkos, and CPU src/comm_tiled.cpp CommTiled::forward_comm() does pack_comm + unpack_comm for self. 'n' is assigned and unused.
failure_scenario: comm_style tiled with device forward comm on a GPU and an atom style whose forward comm is not x-only (dipole, spin, dpd) or any style in a single/mixed-precision build (NEED_TRANSFORM): with periodic boundaries and a rank that is its own neighbor, self ghosts keep stale values for the whole reneighbor interval -> silently wrong forces.
suggested_fix: Add atomKK->avecKK->unpack_comm_kokkos(recvnum[iswap][nrecv],firstrecv[iswap][nrecv],k_buf_send) after the pack in the sendself block.

summary: Sign error in the parallel dissipative force: KOKKOS has fpair = gamma*wdPar^2*dot*rinv (then *= factor_dpd), the CPU style has fpair = -factor_dpd*gamma*wdPar^2*dot*rinv. The drag term becomes an anti-drag that pumps energy into the system.

Note the sibling pair_dpd_ext_kokkos.cpp:301 uses 'fpair -= ...' which is correct there because a conservative term was accumulated first; the tstat variant has no conservative term so it needs the explicit minus.

summary: Temperature-ramp block updates only params.sigma; the CPU style updates sigma AND sigmaT. The perpendicular random force stays at the initial temperature for the whole ramp.

summary: UPSTREAM CPU DEFECT, faithfully mirrored by the KOKKOS port. The pair force is formed as 'forcelj * rshift / r' where the analytic gradient of the tallied energy requires 'forcelj / rshift / r', so every force is off by a factor rshift^2 and does not match the energy. The sibling style lj/expand gets it right.
verified_by: orchestrator. With lj1=48*eps*sigma^12, lj2=24*eps*sigma^6 (pair_lj_expand_sphere.cpp:266-267) and r6inv=1/rshift^6, forcelj = -rshift*dE/drshift, so the scalar multiplying del must be forcelj/(rshift*r). src/pair_lj_expand.cpp:115 and :409 use exactly 'forcelj / rshift / r' for the identical energy form, while src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_expand_sphere.cpp:122 (compute) and :396 (single) use 'forcelj * rshift / r'. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_expand_sphere_kokkos.cpp:154 copies the base, and src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_expand_kokkos.cpp:158 copies the correct one. NOTE: the force-style YAML fixtures for lj/expand/sphere were generated from the current code and must be regenerated with the fix.
