summary: DynamicalMatrixKokkos::setup() shadows the non-virtual DynamicalMatrix::setup(), so the KOKKOS version is never executed and the command runs the plain CPU setup path.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.h:35 declares `void setup();` with no `override` (only command(), update_force(), force_clear() are override). src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h:23 declares `void setup();` NON-virtual (contrast with lines 37-39 `virtual void update_force(); virtual void force_clear(); virtual void openfile(...)`). The only callers are src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.cpp:169 and :177 inside DynamicalMatrix::command(), which statically binds to DynamicalMatrix::setup(). src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:79-83 `void DynamicalMatrixKokkos::command(...) { atomKK->sync(...); DynamicalMatrix::command(narg, arg); }` -> base command -> base setup. DynamicalMatrixKokkos::setup() (dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:91-133) is therefore dead code; its `lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;` (line 93), the `pair_compute_flag` sync/compute/modified block (lines 117-123) and `lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 0;` (line 126) never run.
failure_scenario: `dynamical_matrix all regular 0.000001 file dynmat.dat` with -k on -sf kk: DynamicalMatrix::setup() runs instead, so auto_sync is never enabled around domain->pbc()/reset_box()/image_check()/box_too_small_check()/neighbor->build(1), which read the legacy host x/image arrays; on a GPU run those can be stale relative to the device copy, giving wrong ghost/image handling and hence a wrong dynamical matrix (and the KOKKOS-specific pair sync block is silently skipped).
suggested_fix: Declare `virtual void setup();` in src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h:23 and mark the KOKKOS one `void setup() override;`, or have DynamicalMatrixKokkos::command() do the setup itself instead of delegating to DynamicalMatrix::command().

summary: ThirdOrderKokkos::setup() shadows the non-virtual ThirdOrder::setup(), so the KOKKOS version is never executed.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/third_order_kokkos.h declares `void setup();` without `override`; src/PHONON/third_order.h:23 declares `void setup();` NON-virtual while lines 37-39 declare `virtual void update_force(); virtual void force_clear(); virtual void openfile(...)`. Callers are src/PHONON/third_order.cpp:186 and :194 inside ThirdOrder::command(); src/KOKKOS/third_order_kokkos.cpp:79-83 ThirdOrderKokkos::command() just syncs and calls ThirdOrder::command(narg,arg). ThirdOrderKokkos::setup() (third_order_kokkos.cpp:91-135) with `lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;` (line 93), the pair_compute_flag sync/compute/modified block (lines 117-123) and `auto_sync = 0` (line 126) is dead code.
failure_scenario: `third_order all ... ` run with -k on -sf kk: the CPU ThirdOrder::setup() runs, auto_sync is never enabled around the host-side domain/comm/neighbor block, so host x/image data can be stale on a GPU run and the third-order force constants come out wrong.
suggested_fix: Make ThirdOrder::setup() virtual in src/PHONON/third_order.h:23 and add `override` to the KOKKOS declaration (same fix as dynamical_matrix).

summary: FixWallGranKokkos::post_force() sets copymode = 1 and then takes an error->all() exit for the hooke / hertz/history wall styles, so copymode is never reset to 0 and every later destructor of the fix silently skips atom->delete_callback().
failure_scenario: Exception-enabled build (liblammps / the Python module, LAMMPS_EXCEPTIONS=on): `fix 1 all wall/gran/kk hooke 200000.0 NULL 50.0 NULL 0.5 0 zplane 0.0 NULL` then `run 1` -> post_force throws with copymode==1. The caller catches the exception and issues `unfix 1` (or any later fix/atom_style change): Modify::delete_fix destroys the fix, the destructors early-return, so the Atom GROW/RESTART callbacks for this fix are never removed and history_one/mass_rigid leak. The next atom->grow() dispatches grow_arrays() through the stale callback entry -> use-after-free / crash.
suggested_fix: Move both error->all() checks above `copymode = 1` (they only depend on pairstyle, which is fixed at construction), or reset copymode = 0 before erroring.

summary: FixShardlow::~FixShardlow() lacks the mandatory `if (copymode) return;` guard although FixShardlowKokkos is copied by value into Kokkos functors.
failure_scenario: Today the KOKKOS variant keeps the base `rand_state` pointer at nullptr (it uses the device view d_rand_state, fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:592), so memory->destroy() is a no-op and nothing crashes. The moment any code path lets the base allocate rand_state (e.g. a future host fallback calling FixShardlow::initial_integrate, which grows it at fix_shardlow.cpp:532), the functor copy's destructor frees the original's array -> double free / use-after-free in the next `fix shardlow` step with pair dpd/fdt/energy.
suggested_fix: Add `if (copymode) return;` as the first statement of FixShardlow::~FixShardlow().

summary: Several KOKKOS styles set copymode = 1 and then call error->all()/error->one() before resetting it to 0, so on an exception-enabled build the style is left with copymode == 1 and its destructors free nothing (memory leak).
failure_scenario: liblammps/Python (LAMMPS_EXCEPTIONS=on): a run that trips e.g. "Bad FENE bond" or "requires 'newton on'" throws out of compute(); the caller catches it and later closes LAMMPS. Every destructor in the style's chain sees copymode == 1 and returns immediately, so eatom/vatom, the style's dual views and Pair/Bond::id/style allocations are all leaked. Repeated catch-and-retry loops (a common Python driver pattern) leak on every failure.
suggested_fix: Hoist the input-validation error->all() checks above the `copymode = 1` line (they do not depend on the kernel), and for genuinely in-kernel failures set copymode = 0 before calling error->one()/error->all().

summary: PairPOD::~PairPOD() has no `if (copymode) return;` guard although PairPODKokkos derives from it and sets copymode = 1 around its kernels.
evidence: src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:107-157: `PairPOD::~PairPOD() { memory->destroy(rij); ... memory->destroy(elemindex); delete fastpodptr; if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); memory->destroy(cutsq); } }` -- no guard. src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.h:33 `class PairPODKokkos : public PairPOD`; src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:74-80 `~PairPODKokkos() { if (copymode) return; ... }` and :208 `copymode = 1;` show the style is meant to be copy-safe. src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:131-137 `PairPODKokkos::coeff()` calls `PairPOD::coeff(narg,arg)`, which allocates fastpodptr and (via PairPOD::allocate, called from pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:163) setflag/cutsq, so the base really does own memory. Contrast the guarded base destructors src/pair.cpp:138, src/fix.cpp:120, src/ML-SNAP/... .
failure_scenario: Not reachable today: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp uses only KOKKOS_LAMBDA with local shadow views and never passes *this to a kernel nor uses pair_compute<>/PairComputeFunctor, so no copy of the style is ever destroyed. It becomes a double free (fastpodptr deleted twice, setflag/cutsq freed twice) the moment anyone converts a kernel to the usual `*this` functor form, which the existing `copymode = 1` at line 208 already advertises as safe.
suggested_fix: Add `if (copymode) return;` as the first statement of PairPOD::~PairPOD().

summary: Host-only std::isnan() is called inside the KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION device routine temperature_lookup(), violating the rule that device kernels must use Kokkos:: math.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:381-436 is `template<class DeviceType> KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void FixEOStableRXKokkos<DeviceType>::temperature_lookup(int id, KK_FLOAT ui, KK_FLOAT &thetai) const`.  Line 420: `if (std::isnan(f1) || std::isnan(f2)) k_error_flag.template view<DeviceType>()() = 2;` and line 436: `if (std::isnan(f1) || std::isnan(f2) || std::isnan(ui) || std::isnan(thetai) || std::isnan(t1) || std::isnan(t2))`.  The very same function already uses the portable form on lines 418 and 427 (`if (Kokkos::fabs(f2-f1) < ...)`, `if (Kokkos::fabs(temp-t2) < tolerance)`), so the std:: calls are leftovers.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ... never std:: -- std::pow and friends fail to compile for GPU targets.'  These are the only std:: math calls inside a device function anywhere in src/KOKKOS (all other std::isnan/std::isinf hits, e.g. pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:290-543, are in host-side coefficient setup).
failure_scenario: Building the KOKKOS package with DPD-REACT for a CUDA/HIP backend: nvcc/hipcc reject the call to the host-only std::isnan from __device__ code (or silently fall back to the host overload), so `pair_style ... / fix eos/table/rx ... /kk` does not build for GPU.
suggested_fix: Replace every std::isnan(...) in this device routine with Kokkos::isnan(...) (or the `x != x` idiom), matching the Kokkos::fabs() already used two lines above.

summary: Debug fprintf(stdout,...) calls sit inside a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION device kernel (guarded by #ifdef DEBUG_SSA_BUILD_LOCALS), which is host-only I/O and cannot compile for a GPU backend.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:524-527 `template<class DeviceType> KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void NPairSSAKokkosExecute<DeviceType>::build_locals_onePhase(const bool firstTry, int workPhase) const`.  Inside that device function, lines 618-630: `#ifdef DEBUG_SSA_BUILD_LOCALS ... fprintf(stdout, "Leng%03d workphase (%2d,%3d,%3d): len  = %4d, but ssa_itemLen = %4d%s\n" ,me ,workPhase ...);` and again lines 640-650 `fprintf(stdout, "Phas%03d phase %3d used %6d inums, ...");`.  These are the only stdio calls inside any device kernel in src/KOKKOS.  Project rules: no fprintf(screen/logfile) in new code (use utils::logmesg), and device kernels may not call host-only functions.
failure_scenario: Anyone who defines DEBUG_SSA_BUILD_LOCALS to debug the SSA neighbor build gets a compile error on a CUDA/HIP build (fprintf is a __host__ function called from __device__ code), so the debug aid only works for host-only builds.
suggested_fix: Replace the fprintf calls with Kokkos-safe printf() (usable in device code) or delete the dormant debug block entirely.

summary: fix wall/flow/kk lists V_MASK only in datamask_modify, never in datamask_read, so the device copy of v is never synced before the kernel partially overwrites it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:38-39 `datamask_read = X_MASK | RMASS_MASK | TYPE_MASK | MASK_MASK;` / `datamask_modify = V_MASK;`.  end_of_step() at line 81 does only `atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read);` (no V_MASK), then line 85 `d_v = atomKK->k_v.template view<DeviceType>();` and the kernel writes it in generate_velocity_kk() lines 156-160 (`d_v(atom_i, flowax) = ...`, `d_v(atom_i,(flowax+1)%3) = ...`, `d_v(atom_i,(flowax+2)%3) = ...`) for the subset of atoms that crossed a wall, and finally line 101 `atomKK->modified(execution_space, datamask_modify);` marks the whole device v newer than host.
failure_scenario: GPU run where v was last written on the host (a non-KOKKOS fix/compute, `velocity` command, or a host-side exchange/borders which does atomKK->modified(Host, datamask_exchange) including V_MASK in comm_kokkos.cpp:1043/1483): end_of_step syncs only x/rmass/type/mask to the device, the kernel rewrites v only for wall-crossing atoms in the stale device buffer, then modified(Device,V_MASK) makes that stale buffer authoritative -- every other atom's velocity silently reverts to an older value.
suggested_fix: Add V_MASK to datamask_read in the constructor (line 38), i.e. `datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | RMASS_MASK | TYPE_MASK | MASK_MASK;`.

summary: fix wall/region/kk reads atom radius on the device for the colloid wall style but RADIUS_MASK is not in datamask_read, so the device radius array is never synced.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:47 `datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK;`.  post_force() line 78 syncs only `datamask_read`, then line 98 `if (style == COLLOID) d_radius = atomKK->k_radius.template view<DeviceType>();`.  The kernel reads it at line 164 `tooclose = d_radius(i);` and line 195 `else if (style == COLLOID) engKK = colloid(r,d_radius(i),fwallKK);`.  No other sync in this file covers RADIUS_MASK (only sync call is line 78).  Compare the base FixWallRegion::post_force in src/fix_wall_region.cpp which uses the host `atom->radius` directly.
failure_scenario: `fix wall/region ... colloid ... /kk` on a GPU: radius is filled on the host by read_data/`set diameter`/a non-kk fix and is only copied to the device by an explicit RADIUS_MASK sync.  Without it d_radius contains zeros (or stale values), so `tooclose` is 0 and the colloid wall energy/force uses a wrong particle radius -- wrong forces, and the 'Particle outside surface of region used in fix wall/region' check no longer fires.
suggested_fix: Add RADIUS_MASK to datamask_read (at least when style == COLLOID), e.g. in the constructor after parsing style, or sync it explicitly in post_force before assigning d_radius.

summary: fix nve/limit/kk uses atomKK->k_mass on the device without ever syncing the DualView, so per-type masses are read from an uninitialised (zero) device buffer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_limit_kokkos.cpp:93-101 `auto d_mass = atomKK->k_mass.template view<DeviceType>();` ... `const KK_FLOAT dtfm = l_dtf / d_mass[d_type[i]];` and the same in final_integrate() at lines 167-175.  `grep -n 'k_mass' fix_nve_limit_kokkos.cpp` shows NO `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()`/`sync_device()` anywhere in the file, and the class overrides only initial_integrate()/final_integrate() (fix_nve_limit_kokkos.h:34-36), so no init() runs a sync either.  atom->mass lives in a DualView that is only ever written on the host: AtomKokkos::allocate_type_arrays (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:313-316) and every AtomKokkos::set_mass overload (atom_kokkos.cpp:287,293,299,305) call `k_mass.modify_host()` and nothing else.  There is no MASS_MASK in src/atom_masks.h, so `atomKK->sync(execution_space, ...)` can never carry it.  The correct idiom is FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46: `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();`.
failure_scenario: GPU build, `fix nve/limit/kk` as the only integrator (no fix nve/kk, fix nvt/kk, ... in the input) and per-type masses (no per-atom rmass): the device half of k_mass is the Kokkos default zero-initialised allocation, so `dtfm = dtf/0` is +inf and all velocities/positions become inf/NaN on the first timestep.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: pair_style dpd/kk reads the per-atom tag inside the kernel (SARU RNG seed) but never syncs TAG_MASK to the execution space.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:97-98 `datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK; datamask_modify = EMPTY_MASK;` so VerletKokkos syncs nothing for this style.  compute() line 173 does `atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | TYPE_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK);` -- TAG_MASK is absent -- and line 179 assigns `tag = atomKK->k_tag.view<DeviceType>();`.  The kernel reads it: line 426 `const tagint itag = tag(i);` and line 447 `const tagint jtag = tag(j);`, feeding line 467 `saru(tag1, tag2, timestep, seed, randnum);`.  Every other array the kernel touches (x, v, f, type) is in the line 173 sync list.
failure_scenario: Any host-side write of atom->tag during a GPU run (`reset_atoms id`, a non-KOKKOS fix, `create_atoms` mid-run) leaves the device tag array stale until the next border comm (atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:1560 syncs datamask_border).  The SARU seed is then built from stale tag pairs, so the dissipative/random DPD forces are wrong and pairwise momentum conservation (which relies on i and j drawing the same random number) is broken.
suggested_fix: Add TAG_MASK to the sync list in PairDPDKokkos::compute() (line 173), matching the other arrays the kernel reads.

summary: fix shake/kk reads per-type masses from atomKK->k_mass on the device but never syncs that DualView to the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:638-639 and 864-865 `d_rmass = atomKK->k_rmass.view<DeviceType>(); d_mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();`, used in the kernels at lines 908 (`dtfsq_kk / mass[type[i]]`), 972-973, 1098-1100, 1292-1295, 1545-1546 (`1.0/d_mass[d_type[i0]]`).  The file syncs many of its own DualViews (lines 192-193, 227-228, 255, 387-393) but `grep -n 'k_mass' fix_shake_kokkos.cpp` shows no `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()`.  k_mass is host-only-written (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:287-316, `modify_host()` only) and is not covered by any bit in src/atom_masks.h, so `atomKK->sync(execution_space,...)` cannot bring it over; cf. the required idiom in src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46.
failure_scenario: GPU run whose only k_mass sync came from another style: it works by accident.  Remove/replace that style (e.g. integrate with a non-KOKKOS-synced integrator, or run `fix shake` inside a minimisation) and d_mass is all zeros, so every SHAKE inverse mass is 1/0 = inf and constrained bond lengths blow up.  Any `mass` command issued between two runs also invalidates the device copy (modify_host) and nothing re-syncs it here.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: fix gravity/kk reads per-type mass on the device without syncing atomKK->k_mass.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_gravity_kokkos.cpp:66-69 `if (atomKK->rmass) rmass = ...; else mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();` and the kernel at line 113 `KK_FLOAT massone = mass[type[i]];`.  The only sync in the whole file is `atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read)` at line 61, and no mask bit exists for mass (src/atom_masks.h has no MASS_MASK); `grep -n 'k_mass' fix_gravity_kokkos.cpp` shows no `sync<DeviceType>()`.  Compare src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46, which does `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` in init().
failure_scenario: GPU run with per-type masses where no other KOKKOS style has synced k_mass (or where a `mass` command after the last sync re-marked the host copy newer): d_mass is zero/stale, so the gravitational force `massone*xacc` is zero (or wrong) and the reported gravitational potential energy is wrong.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: fix momentum/kk computes the group mass on the device from atomKK->k_mass without syncing the DualView.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp:70-77 `atomKK->sync(execution_space, TYPE_MASK); ... typename AT::t_kkfloat_1d_randomread mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>(); ... update += static_cast<double>(mass(type(i)) * ...)`.  TYPE_MASK is synced but there is no mask bit for mass and no `atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()` anywhere in the file (all four sync calls are lines 60,70,88,143).  k_mass is written host-side only, with `modify_host()` (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:287-316).

suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: fix dt/reset/kk divides by a per-type mass read from an unsynced atomKK->k_mass device view.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_dt_reset_kokkos.cpp:62 syncs only `V_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK | TYPE_MASK | RMASS_MASK`, then line 68-71 `if (atomKK->rmass) rmass = ...; else mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();`, and the kernel does `massinv = 1.0 / mass[type[i]];` (operator()(TagFixDtResetMass), fix_dt_reset_kokkos.cpp:123).  init() (line 49-55) only calls FixDtReset::init() and the respa check; there is no `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()` in the file.  No MASS_MASK exists in src/atom_masks.h.

suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: fix electron/stopping/kk reads per-type mass on the device without syncing atomKK->k_mass.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_electron_stopping_kokkos.cpp:84-85 `d_mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>(); d_rmass = atomKK->k_rmass.view<DeviceType>();` and line 143 `double massone = (d_rmass.data()) ? ... : static_cast<double>(d_mass(itype));`.  The file carefully syncs its own DualViews (k_elstop_ranges line 51, k_match line 102) and the per-atom masks (line 72 `atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read)`), but never `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()`; mass has no mask bit (src/atom_masks.h) and is host-modified only (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:287-316).

suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: fix shardlow/kk binds its `masses` device view to atomKK->k_mass without syncing the DualView to the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:214-219 `if (atomKK->rmass) { massPerI = true; masses = atomKK->k_rmass.view<DeviceType>(); } else { ... masses = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>(); }`, used at lines 270, 314, 415, 465 (`const double mass_i = masses(massPerI ? i : itype);`).  The file syncs many other DualViews (k_pairDPDE->k_cutsq line 139, np_ssa->k_ssa_* lines 574-580, k_params line 616) and the per-atom masks (lines 619, 658), but never `atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()`; there is no MASS_MASK in src/atom_masks.h.

suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: pair multi/lucy/rx/kk marks k_cutsq host-modified only once, inside allocate(), so a later Pair::init() that recomputes cutsq (after a new pair_coeff) never reaches the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp:967-969 (allocate()): `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_cutsq,cutsq,nt,nt,"pair:cutsq"); d_cutsq = k_cutsq.template view<DeviceType>(); k_cutsq.modify_host();`.  That is the ONLY `k_cutsq.modify*` in the file (`grep -n 'k_cutsq' pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp`), and the style does not override init_one (only PairMultiLucyRX::init_one, src/DPD-REACT/pair_multi_lucy_rx.cpp:469-478, exists).  The device copy is read every step: compute_style() line 182 `k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>();` and the kernels use `d_cutsq(itype,jtype)` at lines 328, 355, 387, 431, 586-587.  Pair::init() fills the host `cutsq[i][j]` (which aliases k_cutsq's host view) from init_one on every run setup, but only allocate() -- called once, from coeff() when !allocated -- ever sets the host-modified flag.  Contrast the standard KOKKOS idiom, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp:262, where `k_cutsq.modify_host()` sits in init_one() and therefore re-fires on every Pair::init().
failure_scenario: `pair_coeff 1 1 tab.txt ENTRY_A` / run / `pair_coeff 1 1 tab.txt ENTRY_B` where ENTRY_B has a different tabulated cutoff, then run again on a GPU: Pair::init() writes the new cutsq on the host, but the host-modified flag was consumed by the first compute's sync, so `k_cutsq.sync<DeviceType>()` is a no-op and the kernel keeps using ENTRY_A's cutoff -- silently wrong forces and energies in the second run.
suggested_fix: Override init_one() in PairMultiLucyRXKokkos to call the base version and then `k_cutsq.modify_host()` (or add the modify_host() to a per-run hook such as init_style()), instead of relying on the one-time flag set in allocate().

summary: FixLangevinKokkos::end_of_step claims device writes (atomKK->modified(V_MASK) and k_lv.modify<DeviceType>()) that the launched kernel never performs.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:757-766: `atomKK->sync(execution_space,V_MASK | MASK_MASK); k_flangevin.template sync<DeviceType>(); if (tallyflag) { FixLangevinKokkosTallyEnergyFunctor<DeviceType> tally_functor(this); Kokkos::parallel_reduce(nlocal,tally_functor,energy_onestep); } atomKK->modified(execution_space,V_MASK); k_lv.template modify<DeviceType>();`.  The only kernel launched is TallyEnergyFunctor, whose body is compute_energy_item() (line 728), a pure reduction that writes nothing.  end_of_step_item()/end_of_step_rmass_item() (lines 774, 794), the only functions that write `v` and `d_lv`, are reached solely through FixLangevinKokkosEndOfStepFunctor (fix_langevin_kokkos.h:260-275) which is never instantiated anywhere in the .cpp.  The CPU base FixLangevin::end_of_step (src/fix_langevin.cpp) likewise only accumulates `energy_onestep`.
failure_scenario: The bogus `k_lv.modify<DeviceType>()` makes the never-written device buffer authoritative; the next FixLangevinKokkos::copy_arrays (line 820) starts with `k_lv.sync_host()`, which then overwrites the host `lv` array with that untouched device buffer.  The redundant `atomKK->modified(execution_space,V_MASK)` additionally forces a full velocity copy back every step.
suggested_fix: Drop both claims from end_of_step(), or instantiate FixLangevinKokkosEndOfStepFunctor if the half-step-velocity swap is actually meant to run; also remove the dead end_of_step_item()/end_of_step_rmass_item()/functor if it is not.

summary: FixRxKokkos::odeDiagnostics reads the host mirror of atom->mask without syncing MASK_MASK to the host.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1583 `HAT::t_int_1d h_mask = atomKK->k_mask.view_host();` and line 1592 `if (h_mask(j) & groupbit) {`, with no `atomKK->sync(Host,MASK_MASK)` anywhere in odeDiagnostics (the function spans lines 1505-1662).  FixRxKokkos declares `datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK` so ModifyKokkos does not sync anything for it either; every other host-side read in this file is preceded by an explicit sync.
failure_scenario: GPU run where the group mask was last written on the device (e.g. `group ... dynamic` handled by a KOKKOS fix, or a device-side border/exchange): the ODE diagnostics loop selects the wrong atoms, so the reported per-group ODE step/function-call statistics are wrong.  Diagnostics only, no effect on the trajectory.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->sync(Host,MASK_MASK);` before line 1583.

summary: fix qeq/reaxff/kk declares X_MASK in datamask_modify although it never writes atom positions, and omits the Q_MASK it does write.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:64-65 `datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | Q_MASK | MASK_MASK | TYPE_MASK | TAG_MASK; datamask_modify = X_MASK;`, and line 307 `atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify);`.  The style only reads x (`x(i,0)` etc. at lines 742-744 and in the neighbor kernels); the array it actually writes is q (line 1002 `q(i) = ...`), which is claimed separately at line 537 `atomKK->modified(execution_space,Q_MASK);`. It is a datamask/actual-access mismatch, the exact thing the KOKKOS rules require to agree, and it hides the fact that Q_MASK is missing from the declaration.

summary: The KOKKOS fix wall/* styles list V_MASK in datamask_read although none of them reads or writes velocities.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_lj93_kokkos.cpp declares `datamask_read = X_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK | V_MASK;` while FixWallLJ93Kokkos::wall_particle (lines 145-178) binds only `d_x = atomKK->k_x...` (151), `d_f = atomKK->k_f...` (152) and `d_mask = atomKK->k_mask...` (153) and the kernel touches nothing else.  The identical unused V_MASK appears in src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_lj126_kokkos.cpp (kernel at 138-171), fix_wall_lj1043_kokkos.cpp (159-192), fix_wall_morse_kokkos.cpp (140-173), fix_wall_harmonic_kokkos.cpp (95-128), fix_wall_harmonic_outside_kokkos.cpp (89-122) and fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:47.

suggested_fix: Remove V_MASK from datamask_read in these seven wall fixes.

summary: pair exp6/rx/kk sets the k_cutsq host-modified flag only in allocate(), so cutsq changes made by a later Pair::init() are never pushed to the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:1656-1658 (allocate()): `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_cutsq,cutsq,ntypes+1,ntypes+1,"pair:cutsq"); d_cutsq = k_cutsq.template view<DeviceType>(); k_cutsq.modify_host();` -- the only `modify` on k_cutsq in the file.  The device copy is consumed every step: compute() line 153 `k_cutsq.template sync<DeviceType>();` and kernels at lines 497, 502, 504, 873, 878, 880, 1206, 1256.  There is no init_one() override (`grep -n '::init_one' pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp` is empty), so nothing re-claims the host write that Pair::init() performs on `cutsq[i][j]` at every run setup.  The robust idiom is the one used by the other pair styles, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp:262, where modify_host() is called from init_one().
failure_scenario: Any command sequence that changes the pair cutoff between runs without re-running allocate() (a new pair_coeff / pair_modify that alters init_one's return value) leaves d_cutsq at the old value on a GPU, so the interaction range used on the device no longer matches the host bookkeeping.
suggested_fix: Add an init_one() override that calls PairExp6rx::init_one() and then `k_cutsq.modify_host()`, so the host write done by Pair::init() is claimed on every run setup.

summary: NPair style halffull/newton/tri/trim/skip/kk/device is registered with the NON-triclinic class NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTrimDevice (TRI=0) instead of the triclinic NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimDevice (TRI=1) declared on the line right above it.
failure_scenario: KOKKOS device run in a triclinic box (e.g. 'change_box all triclinic' or a restart with tilt) with newton on, a pair style that needs a half list built from a full list (halffull), a trimmed sub-cutoff request and a skip list (hybrid pair style / subset neighbor request).  The TRI=0 exact-coordinate branch is used for local/ghost pairs, so epsilon-level coordinate shifts introduced by the orthog->lambda->orthog transform make some i/j ghost pairs be counted twice and others dropped -> silently wrong forces/energies, non-reproducible between runs.
suggested_fix: Change line 221 to name NPairKokkosHalffullNewtonTriTrimDevice (matching the alias on line 219 and the host entry on line 227).

summary: NPair style key on line 262 is misspelled 'halffull/newton/tri/trim/ghost/kk/device' for an ORTHOGONAL (TRI=0, no NP_TRI) entry, duplicating the key of the genuine triclinic entry on line 288.
failure_scenario: An orthogonal-box KOKKOS device run using a trimmed halffull ghost list prints 'pair build: halffull/newton/tri/trim/ghost/kk/device' in the neighbor list info, telling the user a triclinic build style is in use when it is not -- and makes the two entries indistinguishable when debugging.
suggested_fix: Rename the key on line 262 to halffull/newton/trim/ghost/kk/device to match its host sibling on line 268 and its NP_ORTHO-only mask.

summary: The 'accelerated styles' line of the atom_style doc page lists only 7 of the 12 atom styles that the KOKKOS package actually provides -- dipole/kk, dpd/kk, ellipsoid/kk, hybrid/kk and sphere/kk are missing.
evidence:
doc/src/atom_style.rst:33:

  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_atomic_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(atomic/kk,...)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_bond_kokkos.h:16 AtomStyle(bond/kk,...)

doc/utils/check-styles.py does not check atom styles at all (it only checks command, compute, fix, pair, bond, angle, dihedral, improper, kspace and dump lists, see doc/utils/check-styles.py:316-332), so CI does not catch this.  For comparison, doc/src/region.rst:6 does list all 7 region /kk variants and doc/src/min_style.rst lists all 4 minimizer ones.
failure_scenario: A user reading the atom_style page concludes that 'atom_style sphere' or 'atom_style hybrid' has no KOKKOS variant and either avoids the KOKKOS package for granular/hybrid runs or is surprised when -suffix kk silently selects sphere/kk.
suggested_fix: Extend the list on doc/src/atom_style.rst:33 to *angle/kk*, *atomic/kk*, *bond/kk*, *charge/kk*, *dipole/kk*, *dpd/kk*, *ellipsoid/kk*, *full/kk*, *hybrid/kk*, *molecular/kk*, *sphere/kk*, *spin/kk*.

summary: The KOKKOS integrate style verlet/kk is completely undocumented: doc/src/run_style.rst has no verlet/kk in its style list, no '.. index:: run_style verlet/kk', no 'Accelerator Variant' line and no '.. include:: accel_styles.rst'.
failure_scenario: A KOKKOS user who wants to select the integrator explicitly (e.g. 'run_style verlet/kk' when not using -suffix kk) finds no documentation that the style exists or what it does differently; conversely a reader of run_style.rst believes the KOKKOS package does not accelerate the integrator at all.
suggested_fix: Add *verlet/kk* to the style list on doc/src/run_style.rst:13, add '.. index:: run_style verlet/kk', an 'Accelerator Variant: *verlet/kk*' line after the title and '.. include:: accel_styles.rst' near the end of the page.

summary: Unterminated reStructuredText emphasis on the kspace_style style list: '*pppm/tip4p/kk' is missing its closing asterisk, so the KOKKOS variant is not rendered as a style name.
evidence:
doc/src/kspace_style.rst:53 (excerpt):
  ... or *pppm/disp/tip4p/omp* or *pppm/tip4p/kk or *pppm/tip4p/omp* or *pppm/dielectic* ...
Every other entry on that line is delimited by a pair of asterisks; here the closing '*' after 'pppm/tip4p/kk' is missing, so Sphinx pairs the opening '*' of '*pppm/tip4p/kk' with the opening '*' of '*pppm/tip4p/omp*' and emphasises the text 'pppm/tip4p/kk or ' instead.  The style itself is real: src/KOKKOS/pppm_tip4p_kokkos.h registers KSpaceStyle(pppm/tip4p/kk,...) and doc/src/kspace_style.rst:28 has '.. index:: kspace_style pppm/tip4p/kk'.  (The same line also has an unmarked 'ewald/gpu' and a 'pppm/dielectic' typo for 'pppm/dielectric'.)
failure_scenario: The rendered kspace_style page shows a mangled style list around pppm/tip4p/kk, so a user searching the page for the KOKKOS TIP4P PPPM variant does not find it formatted like the other styles.
suggested_fix: Close the emphasis: '*pppm/tip4p/kk*'; while there, fix 'ewald/gpu' -> '*ewald/gpu*' and 'pppm/dielectic' -> '*pppm/dielectric*'.

The action() function itself is now uninstall-only -- src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:12-16:
  action () {
    if (test $mode = 0) then
      rm -f ../$1
    fi
  }
and src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:751-753 makes install/update abort:
  if (test $1 = 1 || test $1 = 2) then
    echo "The KOKKOS package no longer supports the legacy build system. Please build LAMMPS with CMake instead."
    exit 1
so the missing lines cannot break an install; they only mean the uninstall sweep is incomplete.  All 45 styles were added after the legacy install branch was deleted, so no src/ copy of them can exist today -- hence low severity.  (The two remaining rule-1 scan hits, src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:746-747 for mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx and mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx, are false positives: both .pyx files exist, as do their src/ML-IAP dependencies.)

summary: KOKKOS npair style keys order their name tokens differently from the CPU npair styles they mirror, so 40 KOKKOS npair keys have no identically named CPU counterpart and the 'pair build:' info line is not comparable between a CPU and a KOKKOS run.
evidence:
Token order differs systematically (KOKKOS first, CPU second):
  half/bin/newtoff/size/kk/*   (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:102)  vs  half/size/bin/newtoff  (src/npair_bin.h:44)
  half/bin/newton/size/kk/*    (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:97)   vs  half/size/bin/newton   (src/npair_bin.h:49)
  half/bin/newtoff/ghost/kk/*  (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.h:82)   vs  half/bin/ghost/newtoff (src/npair_bin_ghost.h:22)
  halffull/newton/trim/kk/*    (src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.h)  vs  halffull/trim/newton (src/npair_halffull.h:89)
  halffull/newton/tri/trim/kk/*                                  vs  halffull/trim/newton/tri (src/npair_halffull.h:95)
  skip/trim/ghost/kk/*         (src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.h)  vs  skip/ghost/trim        (src/npair_skip.h:45)
Full list of the 40 affected keys in progress_rules_D/rule4d.json.  This is cosmetic rather than functional because NPair styles are internal: Neighbor::choose_pair() selects by bitmask, and the registered name is only used for the 'pair build:' line printed by Neighbor (src/neighbor.cpp:1952).
failure_scenario: A developer diffing the neighbor-list info block of a CPU run against a KOKKOS run (a standard way to check that -suffix kk selected an equivalent build style) sees names that do not correspond and cannot tell whether the same request was satisfied; grep-based tooling keyed on the CPU names finds no KOKKOS match.
suggested_fix: Rename the KOKKOS npair keys to the CPU token order (half/size/bin/newtoff, halffull/trim/newton, skip/ghost/trim, ...) so each KOKKOS key is its CPU counterpart plus the /kk/{host,device} suffix; the masks and classes need no change.

summary: pair_kokkos.h dereferences Atom and Force members but includes neither atom.h nor force.h (nor pulls them in transitively), so it compiles only because every including .cpp happens to include them first.
failure_scenario: Any new translation unit that includes pair_kokkos.h (or includes it before atom.h/force.h) and instantiates one of these templates fails to compile with 'invalid use of incomplete type class LAMMPS_NS::Atom'; a header reordering by clang-format/IWYU in an existing pair style .cpp can trigger the same break.
suggested_fix: Add #include "atom.h" and #include "force.h" to the include block at the top of src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h.

summary: The include guard of compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.h is named after a different, renamed-away style (LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_BONDS_KOKKOS_H), and pair_reaxff_kokkos.h still carries the pre-rename LMP_PAIR_REAXC_KOKKOS_H guard.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.h:26-27:
  #ifndef LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_BONDS_KOKKOS_H
  #define LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_BONDS_KOKKOS_H
whereas the CPU parent src/REAXFF/compute_reaxff_atom.h:24-25 correctly uses
  #ifndef LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_ATOM_H
  #define LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_ATOM_H
and src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:23:
  #ifndef LMP_PAIR_REAXC_KOKKOS_H
while the CPU parent src/REAXFF/pair_reaxff.h:31 uses LMP_PAIR_REAXFF_H ('reax/c' was renamed to 'reaxff').
A scan of every .h in src/ (progress_rules_D/rule6b.py plus a tree-wide duplicate scan) finds NO duplicate guard macro today, so nothing is currently miscompiled.  (The other name deviations found -- fftdata_kokkos.h:17 LMP_FFT_DATA_KOKKOS_H, fix_addforce_kokkos.h:23 LMP_FIX_ADD_FORCE_KOKKOS_H, fix_dpd_energy_kokkos.h:23 LMP_FIX_DPDE_KOKKOS_H, kokkos_type.h:15 LMP_LMPTYPE_KOKKOS_H, meam_kokkos.h:14 LMP_MEAMKOKKOS_H, min_linesearch_kokkos.h:15 LMP_MIN_LSRCH_KOKKOS_H -- mostly mirror the CPU header's own guard name and are benign.)
failure_scenario: If a compute_reaxff_bonds_kokkos.h is ever re-added under its historical name (it existed before the reaxff rename) and both headers end up in one translation unit, the second one is silently skipped and its class is undefined; the wrong names also defeat grep-based tooling that maps guard macros to files.
suggested_fix: Rename the guards to LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_ATOM_KOKKOS_H and LMP_PAIR_REAXFF_KOKKOS_H.

summary: Twelve headers in src/KOKKOS have no include guard at all, and four more use guard macros without the project's LMP_ prefix.
evidence:
No #ifndef/#define guard anywhere in the file (progress_rules_D/rule6b.py -> rule6_guards.json):
  src/KOKKOS/transpose_helper_kokkos.h  (opens namespace LAMMPS_NS at line 21 right after #include "kokkos_type.h" on line 19)
  src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h

  src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h
  src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h
  src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h

Non-LMP_-prefixed guards: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.h:15 KOKKOS_LMP_H, src/KOKKOS/kokkos_base.h:15 KOKKOS_BASE_H, src/KOKKOS/kokkos_few.h:2 KOKKOS_FEW_H, src/KOKKOS/rand_pool_wrap_kokkos.h:15 RAND_POOL_WRAP_H -- the KOKKOS_* ones sit in the macro namespace the Kokkos library itself uses.
Each unguarded file currently has exactly one includer (transpose_helper_kokkos.h <- npair_kokkos.cpp:25; pack_kokkos.h <- remap_kokkos.cpp:20; the *_impl.h and meam_*_kokkos.h files <- sna_kokkos.h / pair_snap_kokkos.cpp / compute_sna_grid*_kokkos.cpp / meam_impl_kokkos.h, itself reached only from the guarded meam_kokkos.h:275), so nothing breaks today.

summary: The KOKKOS package citation string contains a non-ASCII EN DASH (U+2013) in the BibTeX page range, violating the project's 7-bit US-ASCII rule for a string that is written verbatim to the user's log.cite file.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:66-75:
  static const char cite_kokkos_package[] =
    "KOKKOS package: https://doi.org/10.1145/3731599.3767498\n\n"
    "@inproceedings{Johansson25,\n"
    ...
    " pages = {1217-1232},\n"      <- the dash here is actually U+2013 (bytes e2 80 93)
  }
and src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:518:
  if (lmp->citeme) lmp->citeme->add(cite_kokkos_package);
so the byte sequence is emitted into log.cite.  Detected with `LC_ALL=C grep -n '[^ -~\t]' src/KOKKOS/*` (progress_rules_D/rule7_nonascii.out); the project rule is stated in .github/copilot-instructions.md ('7-bit US-ASCII everywhere (sources, docs, scripts); Unicode is forbidden').  Note `cd src && make check` does NOT catch this: src/Makefile:435 runs only check-whitespace, check-permissions, check-homepage, check-errordocs, check-fmtlib and check-docs, and doc/Makefile's char_check scans only doc/src.
failure_scenario: A user's log.cite contains a UTF-8 en dash; BibTeX/BibLaTeX runs in a plain 8-bit-Latin pipeline render it as garbage ('1217â€“1232'), and any downstream tool that assumes ASCII input on the LAMMPS sources (the stated security policy) flags the file.
suggested_fix: Replace the U+2013 with a plain ASCII hyphen (or the BibTeX page-range idiom '1217--1232').

summary: Five non-ASCII characters (RIGHTWARDS ARROW U+2192, EM DASH U+2014, RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK U+2019) appear in source comments in three KOKKOS files, violating the project's ASCII-only rule.
evidence:
`LC_ALL=C grep -n '[^ -~\t]' src/KOKKOS/*` (progress_rules_D/rule7_nonascii.out) reports, besides the citation string in kokkos.cpp:74:
  src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:237  // Host exchange path: flush device->host so the base-class      (U+2192 at column 38)
  src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:688    copy_body_device();  // push host body[] -> d_body            (U+2192 at column 46)
  src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:692  // data to the device - just mark the device side as authoritative and (U+2014 at column 27)
  src/KOKKOS/fix_gjf_kokkos.cpp:132  // vhalf mode: copy lv -> v at start of step (all but the first step)   (U+2192 at column 26)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:726  // if atom J has bonus data, reset J's bonus.ilocal to loc I      (U+2019 at column 41)
The rule is stated in .github/copilot-instructions.md ('7-bit US-ASCII everywhere ... Unicode is forbidden (security policy)').  `cd src && make check-whitespace check-permissions` passes cleanly, so nothing in the build or CI flags these.
failure_scenario: Compilers and editors on non-UTF-8 locales mangle the comments; the files violate the stated ASCII-only security policy, and a future ASCII CI gate over src/ would fail on the KOKKOS package.
suggested_fix: Replace U+2192 with '->', U+2014 with ' -- ', and U+2019 with a plain apostrophe.
